Flag API tokens used from multiple IPs within short time window. Correlate token usage with process execution of suspicious binaries. Alert on dataset write operations (create/push) by tokens with read-only permissions in their historical baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell or Command-Line Invocation of Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify delivery/execution mechanism in truncated body, but malware of this sophistication typically requires script execution or lateral movement. Pipeline should have generated execution-phase detection for scripting interpreter use, but generated no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell or cmd.exe spawning a child process named 'MicrosoftSystem64' or unsigned binary from temp directories. Flag ScriptBlockLogging entries containing hex-encoded or obfuscated payload downloads. Correlate with unsigned DLL loading or suspicious module injection into legitimate Windows processes immediately preceding malware execution.

suggestion.title: Large Volume Data Staging Before Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 'data' (per title) implies prior collection/compression/staging. Pipeline should have generated file-system activity detection for large file creation, compression, or enumeration but generated no collection-phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file enumeration or access to high-value data directories (Documents, Downloads, sensitive shares) by 'MicrosoftSystem64' process or unsigned parent process. Alert on compression tool execution (7z.exe, rar.exe, WinRAR) spawned by malware. Monitor for file creation in staging directories (AppData\Local\Temp, %TEMP%) immediately preceding network activity to HuggingFace infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Initial Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes GREYVIBE as a named threat actor targeting Ukraine. No kill chain was reconstructed and no initial access detection was generated. This is the first step of any attack and must be surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails or documents targeting Ukrainian organizations with GREYVIBE indicators. Establish baselines for unusual attachment types, sender spoofing patterns, or URLs matching known GREYVIBE C2 infrastructure. Alert on successful opens/executions of suspicious attachments in Ukrainian sectors.

suggestion.title: AI-Powered Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'AI-Powered' attacks. No execution-phase technique coverage is present in the kill chain. AI-enhanced malware often uses obfuscation, behavioral variation, or polymorphic payloads requiring detection of execution anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process execution with suspicious command-line patterns or living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) that may indicate polymorphic or obfuscated payload execution. Flag PowerShell/cmd.exe with unusual parameter encoding or base64 payloads. Monitor for process hollowing or code injection as alternate execution paths.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: No C2 detection use case. Threat actor infrastructure, domain registration patterns, or network beacons are standard operational signatures missing entirely from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to domains registered with patterns matching GREYVIBE historical C2 infrastructure. Watch for abnormal DNS query patterns (algorithmic generation, high-entropy subdomains, unusual TLDs). Detect HTTP/HTTPS traffic to suspicious domains from Ukrainian networks using behavioral fingerprinting.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement in Ukrainian Networks
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates Ukraine targeting; no lateral movement detection. Ukrainian critical infrastructure and government networks would be natural post-compromise targets, requiring detection of credential reuse, Kerberos abuse, or share enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual SMB/RDP connections from compromised Ukrainian endpoints to administrative shares or critical systems. Detect pass-the-hash or pass-the-ticket patterns. Flag Kerberos ticket requests with suspicious service principal names targeting domain infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Ukraine Sector
suggestion.rationale: No exfiltration-phase coverage. Strategic attacks on Ukraine typically aim for intelligence collection or disruptive data theft. Absence of detection for bulk data transfer is a critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data volumes leaving Ukrainian government/military networks to external IPs. Detect compression/archiving of sensitive directories before transfer. Flag uploads to cloud storage services or unusual FTP/SFTP traffic with foreign destinations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation by Name Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'typosquatted npm packages used to target cloud and CI/CD credentials'—typosquatting relies on package name similarity (homoglyphs, single-char swaps). Zero use cases generated despite this being the initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm install/yarn add commands installing packages with names matching known typosquatting patterns (edit distance <2 from popular packages, common misspellings). Correlate package name entropy and age-since-publish with installation urgency in CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential File Access from npm Postinstall
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: packages 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets'—npm postinstall scripts execute with ambient environment access. No use case captures credential enumeration during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node/npm process spawning for file-read syscalls against credential paths (.aws/credentials, .kube/config, .env, GCP application-default-credentials, Azure managed-identity endpoints). Alert if reads occur outside normal build-artifact validation windows.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code and Eval Execution in npm Package Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm payloads hide credential-stealing logic via obfuscation (eval, base64, webpack plugins). Article title implies sophisticated packaging but pipeline missed defense-evasion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan postinstall script content and extracted tarballs for eval(), Function() constructors, base64 payloads, and minified code >50% entropy. Flag packages with obfuscation but no declared build/transpilation steps in package.json.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via HTTP/S from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: packages designed to 'steal... secrets' and exfiltrate to attacker infrastructure. Zero exfiltration use cases despite being the attack payoff.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from node processes during npm install phases contacting non-CDN domains, especially with POST payloads containing base64/zlib-compressed data or credential patterns (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, KUBECONFIG content).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Package Installation in CI/CD Runners
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'CI/CD secrets' as target. Malicious packages installed in automated build environments have high privilege to exfiltrate production credentials. No CI/CD-specific detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Tag npm install activity originating from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines runners. Alert if installing packages with typosquatting signatures or first-seen-in-last-7-days age. Cross-reference with dependency-lock files (package-lock.json, yarn.lock) for unauthorized additions.

suggestion.title: AWS/Azure Credential API Calls from npm Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'AWS' and cloud secrets. Malicious packages call credential APIs (AssumeRole, GetCallerIdentity, ListAccessKeys, Get-AzAccessToken). No technique-specific detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail/Defender for credential enumeration APIs (AssumeRole, GetCallerIdentity, ListAccessKeys, ListBuckets, GetItem on secrets tables) triggered by JavaScript/Node.js runtime without corresponding CI job or deployment authorization. Alert on unusual IAM role assumption patterns from npm package contexts.

suggestion.title: VS Code Remote-SSH Arbitrary Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'VS Code Remote-SSH RCE'—pipeline missed the core exploitation event. Attackers execute code on developer machine via compromised Remote-SSH extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned by code-server.exe or remote-ssh processes. Monitor for process injection or extension execution with suspicious command-line arguments, especially network connections or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: SSH Private Key Exfiltration from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Pivot From Developer Machines to Cloud Servers'—attackers must extract cloud/SSH credentials from compromised dev box. Pipeline missed credential harvesting phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads on ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, .aws/credentials, .gcp/keys, and .azure/tokens from non-standard processes. Detect copies to /tmp or exfiltration to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloud Lateral Movement via Compromised Developer Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Pivot...to Cloud Servers'—pipeline failed to detect lateral movement phase where stolen credentials authenticate to cloud infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to AWS/Azure/GCP from source IPs or user contexts previously associated only with dev machines. Alert on logins outside business hours or from geographic anomalies. Correlate timing with local SSH key read events.

suggestion.title: Remote-SSH Session Tunneling and Port Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Remote-SSH extension creates reverse-tunnel attack surface. Pipeline missed persistence/C2 channel established through SSH tunnels post-RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH daemon logs for new public keys added to authorized_keys on developer machines and cloud servers. Detect port-forwarding flags (-R, -L) in SSH connections. Alert on persistent SSH tunnels from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VS Code Extension Installation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers may backdoor Remote-SSH or inject malicious extensions for persistence. Pipeline did not surface extension tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.vscode/extensions for unauthorized installs or modifications, especially unsigned extensions. Track extension.js execution from non-standard paths. Alert on network requests from code-server to untrusted registries.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Enumeration from Compromised Dev Machine
suggestion.rationale: After gaining initial RCE, attackers enumerate cloud permissions before pivot. Article's 'pivot' phase requires discovery. Pipeline missed reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cloud CLI tools (aws, gcloud, az) with enumeration flags (sts get-caller-identity, account get-id, etc.) from developer machines. Monitor for service-level access attempts (S3 list-buckets, Storage list-containers).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Privilege Escalation via sudo Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attacks on sudo' and 'Privilege escalation in the container' as explicit attack vectors enabling container escape and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo invocation patterns in container processes, especially NOPASSWD entries or sudoedit abuse. Detect unauthorized read/modification of /etc/sudoers. Flag privilege transitions to root without corresponding audit logging.

suggestion.title: Cleartext Credentials in Process Command Line
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Passing passwords via command arguments' as a distinct misconfiguration enabling credential compromise in containers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events exposing plaintext credentials in cmdline: regex on --password, -p, --secret, --token patterns. Monitor environment variable exposure via ps or /proc/*/environ access.

suggestion.title: Default Credentials Exploitation in Container Services
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Use of default passwords' as a primary attack surface in containerized infrastructure, enabling account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts using canonical default credentials (root:root, admin:admin, postgres:postgres). Monitor container service logs for successful login with default account names.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Inter-Container Network Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'access neighboring containers' as attacker objective post-compromise, establishing container-to-container lateral movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes in containers communicating with other container networks or reaching Docker daemon socket (127.0.0.1:2375). Detect network scanning within container CIDR ranges.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Insecure File Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'Insecure file permissions' and 'Lack of integrity checks' enabling container escape—the ultimate post-exploitation objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing files outside container root (host mounts, shared volumes). Monitor for exploitation of world-writable mounted paths, Docker socket manipulation, or kernel module loading attempts from within container context.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Vulnerable Base Image Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies base image repositories (Docker Hub) containing 'outdated and vulnerable software versions' whose 'reliability cannot be guaranteed' as attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container image pulls/deployments with known vulnerable package versions. Alert on use of unpatched base image tags (e.g., ubuntu:14.04, centos:6) or images flagged in vulnerability databases.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Targeting World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly cite 'phishing' as attack vector. Description identifies 'ransomware groups, state-aligned actors' targeting 'critical infrastructure'—phishing is primary initial access for both threat classes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with World Cup/FIFA-themed subjects, credential-harvest forms, or suspicious attachments sent to ticketing platforms, stadium operators, or broadcast networks. Correlate sender domain reputation, external forwarding rules, and recipient group membership to identify targeting breadth.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted World Cup Domains - Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly include 'typosquatting'. High-profile sporting event creates surge in phishing via lookalike domains (fifa2026.com vs fifa2026official.com, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to domains one character edit-distance from known World Cup official domains. Alert on certificate issuance for typosquatted domains <30 days old. Flag user clicks from internal network to these domains within 48 hours of phishing email delivery.

suggestion.title: Malicious QR Codes in Phishing - Embedded Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'QR Codes' as attack surface. QR codes in World Cup phishing circumvent URL-filtering and create deniability for attackers (image-based payload).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect QR codes in emails/documents sent to World Cup organizations; decode and check if target URLs are newly registered, bulletproof-hosted, or redirect through shortened links. Alert on QR clicks that immediately trigger credential prompts or file downloads.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Post-Encryption - Destructive Impact
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly include 'wiper'. Combined with 'state-aligned actors' and 'critical infrastructure' context, wiper payloads are deployed post-dwell in destructive campaigns (MBR overwrites, VSS deletion, file destruction).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file deletion/overwrite operations, vssadmin delete commands, cipher /w overwrites, DiskPart MBR writes, and fsutil usn deletejournal sequences. Correlate with failed RDP login attempts and lateral movement 2-3 days prior; flag as pre-wipe reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Command & Control - State-Aligned Exfiltration Prep
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'ransomware groups' and 'state-aligned actors' targeting World Cup infrastructure. C2 communications precede encryption by days to weeks; early detection enables intervention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from World Cup critical infrastructure (ticketing, broadcast, stadium ops networks) to newly registered IPs, bulletproof hosters, or known ransomware/wiper C2 IOC feeds. Flag anomalous DNS queries to uncategorized TLDs or suspicious subdomain patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Staging Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: State-aligned actors targeting critical infrastructure typically exfiltrate sensitive data (attendee lists, broadcast schedules, security protocols) before destructive payload. World Cup infrastructure is high-value espionage target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers from World Cup ticketing/ops networks to external IPs over TLS on non-standard ports or via cloud storage APIs. Correlate with sensitive file access (attendance DBs, schedules, access control lists) and check for data staging in world-writable directories before exfil.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states BTMOB 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is a core privilege-escalation vector specific to Android malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected requests to enable Accessibility Services from non-system apps, followed by rapid permission elevation. Track apps that spawn accessibility-related processes without explicit user approval in the current session. Flag any app requesting accessibility access that is not in a curated whitelist of known legitimate accessibility apps.

suggestion.title: Phishing-Driven APK Installation via Fake Google Play
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' This is the primary delivery vector for BTMOB.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users visiting domains that closely resemble 'play.google.com' but are hosted on attacker infrastructure. Monitor for APK downloads from non-official app stores or HTTP-only sites. Correlate phishing link clicks (from email or SMS) with subsequent APK download attempts within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: BTMOB Malware Post-Installation Capability Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names BTMOB as an active Android RAT with specific capabilities: 'stealing specific data, intercepting financial transactions, capturing screenshots, and remote control capabilities.' Detection must trigger on post-install behavioral execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-installation, monitor for rapid permission requests (especially Accessibility, SMS, Contacts, Camera), screenshot/screen record syscalls, financial app interactions, and data exfiltration attempts to suspicious domains. Correlate accessibility service enablement with subsequent screen capture or keystroke monitoring activity.

suggestion.title: MaaS Platform Subscription and Builder Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article details BTMOB's business model: '$700 monthly subscription, or $5,000 for a lifetime license' conducted 'in private Telegram channels.' Defensive detection should monitor for builder activity and infrastructure sign-ups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor private Telegram channels for builder registration, key exchanges, and payload generation requests. Identify command-and-control domains associated with BTMOB through DNS passive data and NetFlow. Flag any organization-internal IPs/users connecting to known BTMOB C2 infrastructure or accessing the clearnet advertised BTMOB site.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'intercepting financial transactions' as a key capability. This implies monitoring of financial apps and credential harvesting distinct from generic data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APKs that hook into or intercept traffic from banking apps or payment processors. Monitor for keystroke logging, clipboard monitoring, or overlay attacks targeting financial apps. Correlate screen-capture activity with access to banking/payment app windows. Flag apps with simultaneous access to financial apps plus network exfiltration plus accessibility services.

suggestion.title: Malware Family Lineage Tracking: SpySolr to BTMOB Evolution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'BTMOB appears to be an evolution of the SpySolr malware family.' Tracking malware lineages enables proactive detection of variants and attribution of related campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build detection rules that trigger on structural or behavioral overlap between BTMOB and SpySolr samples. Monitor threat feeds (ANYRUN, Cyble) for new variant reports. Establish baseline IoC sets for both families and alert on any samples matching either family's signatures, permissions requests, or callback infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access' and company 'identified unauthorized activity involving an employee's account' on April 14. This was the confirmed detection point; pipeline generated zero UC for initial account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful employee account login from geographically impossible locations, new device fingerprints, or non-standard login hours within 24-48 hours of security awareness reports. Cross-reference with email gateway logs for phishing-adjacent campaigns. Monitor for immediate subsequent access to sensitive systems post-login.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer PII Database Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 5.9M+ customer records stolen including 'names, dates of birth, email addresses, genders' from 'Mariner Society loyalty program.' No UC captures anomalous bulk access to customer tables or PII exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline query access patterns to customer databases and flag accounts executing 5-10x normal row counts or accessing multiple customer PII columns in single queries. Alert on unusual export formats (CSV, JSON) of loyalty program data. Monitor database backup/snapshot creation from compromised account context.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Data Exfiltration via Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers stole 'terabytes of internal corporate data' and '8.7 million records' over 8-day window (April 14-22). Pipeline missed detection UC for sustained anomalous egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained high-volume outbound data transfers (10GB+ in single session or 100GB+ over 8 days) from compromised employee account during off-hours. Correlate with file access logs showing enumeration of internal directories. Flag if destination IPs/domains are not whitelisted business partners.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to IT System Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms attacker 'gain[ed] access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system' as the entry point. No detection UC for monitoring unauthorized system access or IT infrastructure probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised employee accounts for access to infrastructure management tools, VPN systems, or administrative consoles not typically accessed by that user role. Alert on any successful authentication to IT admin systems or cloud console logins from the compromised account within hours of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Gogs Authenticated User RCE Execution via Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code' — the core attack vector is code execution post-authentication. No detection for process spawning from the Gogs application context was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes spawned by Gogs application (gogs.exe, gogs daemon) with parent-child relationship anomalies: unexpected command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), script interpreters (python.exe, node.exe), or LOLBins (certutil, wmic). Baseline legitimate Gogs process trees and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Gogs API Endpoint Activity from Non-Whitelist IPs Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes authenticated user exploitation. Detection should correlate successful authentication to Gogs with anomalous subsequent API activity — no UC addresses this transition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when Gogs login event (HTTP 200/302 to /user/login or equivalent) is followed within 60 seconds by POST/PUT to repo, webhook, or admin endpoints from the same source IP, especially if IP is not in known developer/CI infrastructure whitelist.

suggestion.title: Gogs File Write or Upload Activity with Execution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: RCE via authenticated user typically involves file upload or injection to achieve code execution. Article does not specify mechanism, but upload/write + exec pattern is standard. No UC covers file staging on the Gogs host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to Gogs-sensitive paths (plugins directory, templates, hooks) followed within 300 seconds by process creation from the web app context. Look for temp file creation + immediate execution from web service account.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Account Privilege Elevation or Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved under authenticated context, attacker may escalate within the Gogs host or move laterally. Article acknowledges 'execute arbitrary code' but does not bound to the Gogs process. No post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs-spawned processes that attempt token impersonation, create new local accounts, modify sudoers, or establish network connections outside expected Gogs backend communication range.

suggestion.title: Unusual Gogs Web Configuration or Webhook Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated user' — attacker may persist via webhook or configuration changes (e.g., deployment hook pointing to attacker infrastructure). No detection for repo/system configuration drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to Gogs config files, webhook creation with external URLs, or addition of SSH keys to the gitea/gogs system user. Correlate with unauthorized authentication events.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious npm Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Operation DangerousPassword where 'Attackers exploited the lead maintainer's compromised credentials to publish malicious versions of the [axios] library that injected trojanized code into affected systems'. No detection UC generated despite npm being high-value attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installations and updates for axios; alert on version mismatches between official npm registry and local package-lock.json. Detect execution of node_modules/.bin scripts following axios updates, especially injection of HTTP request hooks or network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti VPN Appliance Exploitation: PhiliKit Implant Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'PhiliKit, a new implant that we assess to be part of UNC5221's SPAWN toolset targeting Ivanti VPN appliances'. No initial-access UC despite explicit threat actor and tool targeting specific known-vulnerable device class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti VPN appliance logs for exploitation attempts matching CVE-2024-21887, CVE-2024-21888 (or newer VOS authentication bypass signatures). Detect POST requests to /authenticate or /system endpoints with abnormal parameter encoding. Alert on successful authentication from unexpected ASNs or without prior legitimate RADIUS/LDAP events.

suggestion.title: Bootkit-style Wiper Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies unattributed cluster MoKhargosh as deploying 'bootkit-style wiper' with destructive potential. No persistence or impact UC despite explicit malware class that modifies boot sector and destroys data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes opening \\Device\\PhysicalDrive or \\Device\\HarddiskVolume for direct write access; monitor bootsector modification via WMI Win32_PhysicalMedia or DiskPart commands. Detect MBR/VBR rewrites and subsequent calls to shutdown or restart commands without legitimate administrative context.

suggestion.title: Developer Targeting via Social Engineering: Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'invested in long-term relationship building' and 'continued targeting developers and the cryptocurrency ecosystem with social engineering schemes'. No credential-access UC despite explicit social engineering vector against high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email for targeted spear-phishing with developer-focused lures (job offers, code review requests, security audits). Alert on credential validation failures followed by successful logins from new geographies within 24 hours. Detect browser extension installations via Chrome Web Store immediately post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Deployment Post-Compromise: Rook Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Article documents Andariel 'attempted to spread Rook ransomware within an engineering company' after initial compromise. No impact UC despite explicit destructive tool and named ransomware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Rook ransomware process signatures (command-line patterns for /ras flag, registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, bulk file encryption with .rook extension). Detect rapid file modification across shared network drives and shadow-copy deletion via vssadmin or wmic.

suggestion.title: TigerRAT Lateral Movement: Andariel Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Andariel in South Korea, where the group deployed TigerRAT' within engineering/nuclear-adjacent infrastructure. No command-and-control or lateral-movement UC despite named RAT family being used in ongoing campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TigerRAT command-and-control traffic patterns: HTTP POST requests with unusual User-Agent strings to legitimate-looking domains (masquerading as Windows Update or security software). Detect process execution of known TigerRAT loaders and memory-injection patterns targeting winlogon.exe or explorer.exe.

suggestion.title: Detection of Typosquatted FIFA Domain Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actors 'rely on minor spelling changes that users are likely to miss, such as fiffa[.]com' and use 'alternative top-level domains (e.g., .org, .xyz, .live, .sale)'. These are named attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for FIFA-related domain variations with minor spelling deviations (fiffa, fifa-*) or hosted on non-standard TLDs (.xyz, .live, .sale). Flag matches against threat-intel feeds of known phishing infrastructure and correlate with user clicks on World Cup-related content.

suggestion.title: Detection of Fake FIFA Employment Portal Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific employment phishing infrastructure: 'fake employment portals like "jobs-fifa[.]com" or "fifa-hiring[.]com"' designed to collect credentials and personal data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to known fake FIFA employment domains (jobs-fifa.*, fifa-hiring.*). Alert on authentication attempts against these portals. Monitor for form field patterns requesting PII (SSN, passport, banking details). Baseline legitimate FIFA careers portal traffic and flag anomalous domain variants.

suggestion.title: Detection of Malvertising Campaign - World Cup Themed Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp' and explicitly recommends users 'Avoid sponsored search ads'. Named distribution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor clicks on World Cup / 2026 World Cup-themed paid search ads that resolve to non-fifa.com domains. Correlate ad-click timestamps with subsequent visits to credential-harvesting sites. Alert on redirects from advertising networks to known phishing infrastructure. Flag unusual landing pages for merchandise, streaming, or tickets.

suggestion.title: Detection of Payment Data Harvesting via Fraudulent Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article states fraudulent sites 'collect from visitors various types of data, including...banking/payment details, which could be used to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft, or run financial scams'. Payment collection is core attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests containing payment card patterns (BIN, expiry, CVV) or banking credentials sent to non-official FIFA domains. Monitor for multi-field form submissions requesting name, address, phone, email, and payment details in sequence. Alert on exfiltration of harvested data to command-and-control infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detection of Fake FIFA Ticket Portal Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'a Chinese threat actor tracked as Ghost Stadium' operating 'more than 300 phishing sites, clones of the real FIFA portal, for premium ticket fraud' and 'sell fake tickets and hospitality packages'. Named infrastructure and fraud vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for payment transactions to FIFA-related domains that are not fifa.com or official ticketing partners. Alert on refund requests or chargebacks for World Cup tickets within 48 hours of purchase. Detect SSL certificate mismatches (fake certs mimicking FIFA). Correlate transaction IPs against known Ghost Stadium infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detection of Malicious Domain Registration - World Cup Infrastructure Takedown Prevention
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hundreds of phishing sites' using 'typosquatted' FIFA domains and 'alternative top-level domains'. Early detection of malicious registrations enables proactive takedowns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WHOIS/DNS registration feeds for FIFA-related domain registrations using non-standard TLDs (.xyz, .live, .sale, .org). Flag bulk registrations by single registrars, privacy-protected registrations with World Cup keywords, or domains registered weeks before June 2026 World Cup. Correlate against threat-intel feeds for Ghost Stadium infrastructure patterns.

suggestion.title: PowerShell RAT Collection and Exfiltration - LegionRelay Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents LegionRelay performing 'file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup' — core MITRE techniques requiring detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell processes spawning children for credential/file enumeration (Get-Content, dir, Invoke-WebRequest to exfiltration hosts), screenshot APIs (System.Drawing.Bitmap), RDP setup (netsh advfirewall, New-ItemProperty for RDP registry). Flag combinations of file enum + screenshot + credential access within short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Fake Cloudflare Verification Prompt - Command Injection via Browser
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PhantomClick: 'fake Cloudflare verification prompts' trick victims into running 'self-infecting commands' — direct pivot from browser social engineering to command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser navigation to typosquatted or known-phishing Cloudflare-lookalike domains with immediate PowerShell/CMD execution (cmd.exe /c, powershell -NoP -W Hidden). Alert on processes spawned from browser context downloading/executing payloads or establishing C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Delivery via Cloud Sharing Links
suggestion.rationale: PhantomMail campaign uses 'Google Drive and 4sync links' delivering 'malicious ZIP/RAR archives' — initial access vector combining social engineering + artifact delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads from Google Drive share links or 4sync.io followed by archive extraction from %TEMP% or Desktop. Flag execution of files extracted from archives (double-extension patterns, EXE/DLL launched from archive temp folders, explorer.exe spawning suspicious processes from extracted content).

suggestion.title: Android Spyware Intelligence Collection - FallSpy Behavior
suggestion.rationale: FallSpy malware 'designed purely for collecting intelligence' targeting 'contact lists, call logs, device and network information, location data, media files, and SIM information' — persistent collection on Android devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android apps (distributed via PrincessClub fake dating sites and Nebo military sites) requesting bulk Contacts, CallLog, Location, and MediaStore permissions. Flag rapid ContentProvider queries post-installation or suspicious process access to sensitive data stores (Telegram, WhatsApp databases). Correlate with network exfiltration to non-standard ports/protocols.

suggestion.title: WebRTC-based Audio/Video Capture and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes GreyVibe added 'WebRTC-based live calls that could capture the victim's audio/video' on PrincessClub/Nebo campaigns — novel C2/exfiltration channel over WebRTC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript WebRTC peer connections from suspicious domains (fake dating/military sites) with audio/video codec negotiation. Alert on microphone/camera permission grants to web-based content + WebRTC ICE candidate exchange to attacker STUN/TURN servers. Flag browser processes launched with --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled flags indicative of automated WebRTC data streams.

suggestion.title: Fake Ukrainian Government/Emergency Entity Impersonation Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Lures 'impersonated Ukrainian government, emergency, telecom, and energy entities' with 'AI-generated' content — persistent brand/entity spoofing requiring infrastructure-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations and SSL certificates impersonating Ukrainian government (.gov.ua spoofs, Cyrillic homoglyphs), emergency services (ДСНС), telcos (Kyivstar, Vodafone UA), and energy companies (DTEK). Flag newly registered domains with brand keywords, sender spoofing of official government addresses, and correlation with attachment/link-click events from spear-phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Fake Job Recruiter Phishing to macOS User
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets cryptocurrency firms via 'fake recruiter lures' — this is T1598 reconnaissance and T1566 phishing delivery. Pipeline generated zero social-engineering detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails from recently-created domains posing as recruiters for crypto/finance companies, particularly those requesting credentials, requesting execution of attachments, or linking to credential-harvesting pages.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Recruiter Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'macOS malware' payload from fake recruiter. Pipeline produced no execution-phase detection despite this being core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious macOS process execution (shell interpreters, Swift interpreters, osascript) spawned from recently-downloaded artifacts, particularly those executed by browser or mail processes, or script execution with obfuscated arguments.

suggestion.title: macOS Credential Access via Fake Recruiter Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Fake recruiter lures targeting crypto firms typically harvest credentials (GitHub tokens, SSH keys, browser-stored credentials). Article mentions social engineering but pipeline generated no credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious credential-access patterns on macOS targets that opened suspicious recruiter emails: keychain access queries, SSH key exports, GitHub CLI token reads, or browser credential store access in short time windows post-email delivery.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JINX-0164 C2 Communication from macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies JINX-0164 as the threat actor. Pipeline should have generated threat-actor-specific C2 detection. Malware payloads require command & control coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline macOS network traffic from crypto-industry targets; alert on new or uncommon outbound connections to unusual domains/IPs from JINX-0164 known infrastructure or patterns consistent with obfuscated C2 (unusual DNS query patterns, suspicious HTTP User-Agents, encrypted tunnels).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Compromise: macOS to Windows via Shared Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Cryptocurrency firms often operate mixed-OS environments. Once macOS malware harvests credentials, pipeline should flag lateral-movement detection for cross-platform credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows logons using credentials first harvested or exposed on compromised macOS systems (cross-reference macOS infection timeline); or SMB connections from macOS systems using harvested Windows credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Researcher Account Suspension / Removal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal'. Pipeline ignored a direct threat actor action (platform enforcement or account takeover). Expected detection: sudden account deactivation, permission revocation, repository access loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk account suspensions targeting researchers, changes to researcher org membership, or API token revocations tied to disclosure activity. Flag patterns where multiple researchers on same project lose access simultaneously.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Disclosure Timeline Enforcement / Suppression
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Microsoft Slams Public Zero-Day Disclosures'—indicates policy enforcement or suppression campaign against coordinated responsible-disclosure. Pipeline should have mapped this to defense-evasion or impact actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid policy changes to disclosure timelines, DMCA takedowns targeting researcher disclosures, or automated account enforcement correlated with zero-day announcement dates. Cross-reference GitHub suspension logs with public CVE/disclosure announcements.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Repository Access / Permissions Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Removed researcher account implies prior access to repos; 'researcher' role suggests access to Microsoft security-sensitive projects. Pipeline should flag unauthorized access removal or repository restriction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass permission revocations on repos tagged 'security', 'vulnerability', or 'research'. Correlate GitHub org permission changes with account suspension events. Flag if revoked accounts had forking or cloning activity in days preceding removal.

suggestion.title: Security Researcher Targeting / Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: The removal of a researcher's account in response to zero-day disclosure suggests either platform enforcement or account compromise by threat actor with anti-disclosure motive. Pipeline should surface researcher identity enumeration or targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous sign-in activity on researcher accounts (new GEOs, failed MFA challenges, API token creation) within 72 hours pre/post disclosure. Flag if account suspension immediately follows high-profile CVE advisory. Monitor for targeted phishing campaigns against security researchers.

suggestion.title: Responsible Disclosure Policy Violation / Timing Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: Microsoft's public criticism of disclosure timing vs. responsible-disclosure SLA. Pipeline ignored the policy/timeline attack vector. Expected detection: deviation from standard CVSS-to-public-disclosure windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline disclosure timelines for CVEs by severity. Alert when Microsoft or peer vendor publicly disputes researcher's disclosure timing, or when accounts are suspended within 14 days of CVE publication. Cross-index suspension dates with public disclosure announcements.

suggestion.title: Gogs Default Configuration Audit: Open Registration Enabled
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false)' and 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance.' This is the entry point enabling all downstream exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Gogs instances for configuration flags; alert if DISABLE_REGISTRATION is false or missing (default-enabled). Cross-reference with Shadowserver/Shodan data to identify internet-facing instances. Monitor Gogs startup logs or API config endpoints for registration policy changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Creation by Newly-Registered Gogs User
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the exploit prerequisite: 'Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner.' Attacker accounts created minutes before repo creation are an abuse pattern distinct from legitimate user workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository creation within 24 hours of account creation. Flag bulk repository creation by single users. Correlate repo ownership with account source IP; cross-reference with VPN/proxy intelligence if available. Establish baseline: legitimate users typically wait days before creating first repo.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Strategy Enabled on Recently-Created Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This configuration change is the attacker's setup for command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs repository settings audit logs for rebase merge strategy activation. Flag when enabled on repositories created within the past week, especially by low-tenure accounts. Look for rapid enable-disable-enable cycles suggesting testing or evasion.

suggestion.title: Git Rebase Command Injection via Malicious Branch Name (--exec Flag Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the core exploit: 'inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the "Rebase before merging" merge operation' using malicious branch names. Successful injection results in arbitrary command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log full command lines for all git rebase invocations spawned by Gogs service. Alert on git rebase with --exec, --run, or -x flags. Flag branch names beginning with '--' or containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $, backtick). Correlate with suspicious pull request metadata from Gogs audit logs.

suggestion.title: Gogs Server Process Spawning Unexpected Child Processes (RCE Execution Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation allows attackers to 'execute arbitrary code remotely as the Gogs server process user' and can 'compromise the server, read every repository.' Child process spawning by Gogs (normally stateless) is a strong RCE signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Gogs child processes (typically none or only internal git commands). Alert on shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe), interpreters (python, perl), or tools (curl, wget, nc) spawned from Gogs process context. Flag processes with working directories inside Gogs repository paths. Monitor for process parent=Gogs with suspicious environment variables.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential and Repository Content Exfiltration from Gogs Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' and 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos).' Post-RCE reconnaissance and data collection are high-fidelity indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file reads/copies from Gogs config directories (.ssh, .gnupg, data/), database files, and secret stores by unexpected processes. Alert on archive/compression tools (tar, zip, 7z) invoked from Gogs context. Detect execution of password cracking utilities (hashcat, john, rockyou) spawned as Gogs children. Monitor for exfiltration patterns (curl/wget to external IPs, SMB/NFS copies).

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL. Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' Clear T1218 execution method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate executables (especially setup/installer binaries) loading DLLs from same directory or non-standard paths. Correlate archive extraction events with immediate execution of legitimately-signed EXEs that subsequently load unsigned or suspicious DLL modules.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and tags reference 'Miner, XMRig.' Primary payload is CPU-intensive mining malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of cryptocurrency mining processes (XMRig, SilentCryptoMiner) or processes with sustained high CPU usage establishing connections to known mining pool domains. Monitor for process command-line arguments containing pool addresses and wallet identifiers.

suggestion.title: RAT Module Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents 'Watchdog RAT agent' section and notes 'RAT module' as campaign addition. RAT provides remote code execution and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child processes spawned from DLL-injected legitimate executables. Detect registry or scheduled task creation from RunDLL32 contexts. Flag suspicious outbound connections from processes with mismatched parent executable names.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Download and Extraction Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes distribution via 'ZIP archive with the following contents: legitimate executable alongside malicious DLL.' Archive downloaded from 'urush1bar4[.]online.' Specific file pairing pattern is highly suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archives downloaded from newly-registered or suspicious domains that contain both a signed executable and a DLL file. Flag extraction patterns where EXE + DLL are extracted to same directory and EXE is subsequently executed within seconds.

suggestion.title: Fake Plugin Update Phishing via Streaming Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update.' Also mentions 'fake browser crash page' variant. User-facing social engineering targeting piracy site visitors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/JavaScript popups claiming software updates from streaming/media domains, especially .ru and .top TLDs. Flag when update prompts reference non-standard plugin versions or redirect to domains unrelated to the claimed software vendor. Correlate with malicious archive downloads.

suggestion.title: Process Injection from Archive-Extracted Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process' and 'executing code within its context.' DLL injection for stealth and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned DLL loads into legitimate processes originating from temporary/download directories. Monitor for process creation events where parent is a recently-extracted executable and child is a system process with unexpected command-line arguments or environment variables.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Unauthenticated or Privileged API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw.' Exploitation of EMS (management server) typically involves HTTP/REST API abuse, unauthorized configuration changes, or direct code execution via unpatched endpoint. Pipeline missed the initial access foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS for anomalous API requests (POST/PUT to /api/* endpoints) from unexpected source IPs, especially those without valid API tokens or with failed authentication followed by success. Alert on EMS process spawning child processes or making unexpected outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution Post-EMS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Deploy Credential Stealer.' Pipeline did not surface detection for stealer execution, memory injection patterns, or lsass/SAM registry access that follows credential-theft implants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential stealer signatures: suspicious child processes from msiexec.exe or rundll32, access to lsass.exe without legitimate SYSTEM context, registry reads to HKLM\SECURITY\SAM or browser credential stores, and unusual handle operations on WinLogon processes.

suggestion.title: Persistence via FortiClient Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: EMS compromises typically result in persistent agent modifications or remote code execution baked into client updates. Article does not explicitly cover this, but it is standard follow-on after EMS pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient installation and update directories (%ProgramFiles%\Fortinet\FortiClient) for unsigned binary modifications, non-standard scheduled tasks added during/after EMS communication, and unexpected GPO pushes from EMS to enrolled endpoints.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via EMS-Managed Credential Distribution
suggestion.rationale: EMS typically manages VPN profiles and stored credentials for client deployment. A compromised EMS can exfiltrate or redistribute credentials for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for mass credential file reads from FortiClient configuration stores (%APPDATA%\Fortinet\Fortisslvpn\profiles, %APPDATA%\Fortinet\SslvpnClient), followed by outbound RDP or SMB connections from previously non-interactive hosts.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration via FortiClient Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Compromised EMS often weaponizes the existing VPN tunnel infrastructure to hide command-and-control traffic. Pipeline did not isolate C2 domains or IP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient UDP 443 and TCP 443 traffic for volume anomalies and non-standard certificate subjects. Flag outbound connections from FortiClient.exe to newly registered domains or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate with process memory injection events.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: The stealer must transmit stolen credentials; pipeline failed to suggest detections for exfiltration channels or data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume credential-sized data transfers (100 bytes–10 MB) from infected endpoint to attacker-controlled IP/domain, especially over HTTP (unencrypted) or to hosting providers known for bulletproof hosting. Cross-reference file creation of .txt, .csv, .json containing plaintext credentials on staging paths.

suggestion.title: MDM Agent Tampering or Termination
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'What MDM can't protect' implies discussion of MDM evasion or circumvention techniques on developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process termination of MDM agents, modifications to MDM daemon configs, or elevated commands disabling device management services. Elevated proc execution targeting mobdevmgr, Intune agent, or similar is high-fidelity indicator.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Installation via Alternative Package Managers
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines use npm, pip, cargo, etc. Article likely identifies package supply chain as an MDM gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager execution with suspicious flags (--registry, --offline, --no-verify) or from unexpected working directories. Flag installations from personal/attacker-controlled registries outside corporate artifact repositories.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Material Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines store SSH keys, API tokens, .env secrets. These are high-value targets and outside MDM's typical scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, .git-credentials, and secret manager directories by non-developer processes. Flag exfiltration attempts of these paths over network or to removable media.

suggestion.title: Git Configuration or Repository Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines rely on git for code management. Compromised git configs or repositories can enable code injection or IP theft undetected by MDM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git operations that modify remote URLs to attacker infrastructure, force-push to erase history, or clone internal repositories to external hosts. Monitor for credential-bearing git commands (git clone with hardcoded PAT).

suggestion.title: Browser Profile or Developer Tool Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Developer tools (IDE configs, browser profiles, git remotes) contain authentication tokens and settings. MDM typically does not encrypt or monitor these at the process level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk read access to browser profiles, IDE settings directories, or shell history by suspicious processes. Monitor for compression or staging of these files prior to exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Entra Account Access Post-Vishing Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' No detection mapped to this initial access vector or the Entra compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra sign-in events from compromised employee accounts showing atypical patterns post-vishing: successful logins from unusual geographies/IP ranges after a burst of failed auth attempts, combined with MFA bypass indicators or step-up authentication bypass. Correlate with employee communication metadata if available.

suggestion.title: Bulk Salesforce Data Export by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'stole 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' No use case for detecting mass record access or bulk export operations from Salesforce.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk API calls or report generation operations querying >100k records from a single account in short time windows. Alert on unusual export methods (API bulk retrieval, report scheduling, data loader usage) from non-service accounts, especially those showing no historical precedent.

suggestion.title: Cross-Cloud SaaS Lateral Movement via Entra Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Entra account was used to access Salesforce, indicating credential reuse across cloud platforms. Article states: 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra sign-in anomalies with spike in Salesforce authentication events from same account within minutes/hours. suggestion.title: DDoS-as-a-Service Platform Access Detection

Flag actors accessing dark-web-advertised infrastructure mentioning 'panel', 'API access', 'monthly plans', or 'reseller programs'.

suggestion.title: Aisuru Botnet C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes 15.72 Tbps Azure attack (October 2025) to Aisuru botnet. No use case targets Aisuru-specific command-and-control patterns or known infrastructure.

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Execution via API or Web Panel
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes DaaS execution: 'access to a web panel, choose a target, select a duration, and rely on someone else's botnet'. No detection captures API calls or panel activity initiating attacks.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Bypass Technique Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions DaaS services advertising 'bypasses for Cloudflare-related protections' in both 2023 and 2026 datasets. No detection rule targets bypass indicators or evasion IOCs.

Flag sudden geographically diverse traffic spikes and packet composition consistent with botnet aggregation (size variation, TTL anomalies, synchronized callback patterns).

suggestion.title: Fake Adobe Domain Access Detection

Alert on email clicks to these domains within 15 minutes of phishing message receipt.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Process Execution from Suspicious Context

suggestion.title: Masquerade Domain Registration - Adobe Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages' — detection should identify newly registered domains masquerading as Adobe services.

Flag domains with Adobe-similar names (adobe-doc.tk, adobedocumentcloud.ga) registered by new or bulletproof registrars.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Download from Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Delivery mechanism described as 'Deliver ScreenConnect Malware' via fake pages — users likely download installers; detection should flag .exe/.msi downloads from non-Adobe domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable downloads to user-writable paths (Desktop, Downloads, %TEMP%) originating from HTTP requests to fake Adobe domains. Include obfuscated variants and legitimate-looking ScreenConnect installer names hosted on non-ConnectWise infrastructure.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Software C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Post-delivery execution requires operator control — ScreenConnect maintains persistent outbound connections for C2.

Flag connections to known ScreenConnect relay infrastructure or unusual geographic destinations. Monitor for DNS queries to .relay.screenconnect.com subdomains.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Adobe Lookalike Link
suggestion.rationale: Entry point: 'Hackers Use Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages' implies phishing campaign delivery; detection should identify emails with links to fake Adobe infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Update Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'Fake Video Player Updates' as the delivery vector. Pipeline should flag non-standard update mechanisms, unsigned update packages, or updates from non-canonical sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for video player processes (e.g., VLC, WMP, custom media apps) initiating HTTP/HTTPS downloads of executable files from suspicious domains or executing unsigned binaries. Flag update requests to non-official update servers or CDNs not associated with the video player vendor.

suggestion.title: Video Player Process Lateral Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions RAT and miner deployment; these require child process spawning or DLL injection from the video player process, not typical legitimate behavior.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Pool Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Miner' malware. Pipeline should detect mining pool connections (Stratum protocol, mining domain patterns, high-entropy traffic to mining pools).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections from video player or child processes to known cryptomining pools (e.g., mining.xmrpool.com, Stratum protocol on ports 3333, 4444, 9999). Monitor for sustained, high-volume connections to single destinations with minimal data transfer variance (characteristic of mining traffic).

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies RAT malware as payload. Pipeline should detect C2 callback patterns: DNS queries to suspicious domains, HTTP POST callbacks with encoded payloads, or reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from video player process to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Detect DNS queries for newly-registered domains from video player or child processes. Flag reverse shell indicators (nc.exe, PowerShell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Auto-Start Registry or Startup Folder
suggestion.rationale: For RAT and miner to survive reboot, malware must establish persistence. Article does not explicitly mention mechanism, but it is implied by 'Deploy' language suggesting installation, not one-shot execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or equivalent startup locations from video player process context. Monitor for suspicious .lnk or .vbs files appearing in Startup folders with timestamps coinciding with fake update execution.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Persistence and C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'HelloDoor' is part of Kimsuky's expanded arsenal; no detection use case generated for identifying its deployment, persistence mechanisms, or C2 communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HelloDoor establishes persistence and communicates over HTTP/HTTPS. Monitor for HelloDoor process creation, startup registry modifications, and unexpected HTTP/S outbound connections from non-browser processes to known or suspected C2 domains.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnels Tunnel Abuse for Remote Access and C2
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'VS Code Tunnels' as attack vector; represents abuse of legitimate development tool for C2, a critical gap for living-off-the-land detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 'code' or 'Code' process with tunnel-related command-line arguments (--tunnel, tunnel.cppTools, etc.) establishing external network connections. Alert on VSCode usage by non-developer accounts or tunnel initialization to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy HTTP Traffic Interception and Credential Capture
suggestion.rationale: Title introduces HTTPSpy as new tool in Kimsuky arsenal; no use case for detecting HTTP traffic interception, man-in-the-middle activity, or credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Threat Actor Infrastructure and Tool Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article names Kimsuky as threat actor but pipeline produced no detection for actor-specific TTPs, tool signatures, or behavioral patterns. Missing foundational actor-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish Kimsuky-specific IOC baselines (tool hashes, behavior patterns). Monitor for HelloDoor execution, HTTPSpy spawning, and VS Code tunnel setup. Correlate with spear-phishing or watering-hole indicators tied to Kimsuky campaigns.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Development Tool Network Behavior
suggestion.rationale: VS Code, HelloDoor, and HTTPSpy represent living-off-the-land and tool abuse; pipeline missed broader detection pattern for dev tools used outside development context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor development tools (VSCode, code.exe, code-server) for unexpected outbound network connections, non-standard parent processes, or execution by non-developer accounts. Flag tunnel-related or proxy-like activity from these tools.

suggestion.title: Fake Codex UI Authentication Attempts

Correlate logon failures to subsequent legitimate Codex API calls from anomalous source IPs.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Token Exfiltration via Fake Codex
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states tokens are stolen; detection must identify when harvested credentials are exfiltrated to attacker C2 or used for unauthorized API calls.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes token theft, but no use case for detecting when stolen credentials are weaponized post-compromise.

Cross-reference stolen token patterns with known C2 infrastructure ASNs.

suggestion.title: Codex Local Repository Modification
suggestion.rationale: Fake UI likely involves local malware or configuration changes; detection should identify tampering with legitimate Codex installation files or config paths.

suggestion.title: NuGet Package Installation from Untrusted Source

Flag installations to development and build environments. Correlate against whitelist of approved packages and versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credential Access from .NET Assembly

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Banking Credentials via HTTP/HTTPS

Monitor for DGA-like DNS queries or connections to newly-registered domains with banking-related keywords.

suggestion.title: Typosquat Package Detection in NuGet Repository

Flag packages with 0 or very low download counts from new publishers claiming to publish banking infrastructure tools.

suggestion.title: Assembly Injection or Reflection-Based Code Execution in .NET

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Suspicious Certificate in Installer Execution

suggestion.title: RVTools Installer Execution from Suspicious Location

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when RVTools.exe or setup processes execute from %TEMP%, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, or other user-writable paths. Baseline legitimate RVTools deployment directories and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: SmartScreen Reputation Bypass or Suppression
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions SmartScreen bypass via certificate abuse — pipeline should detect when installed software evades or triggers SmartScreen warnings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for files that pass code-signing validation (legitimate cert) but lack SmartScreen reputation data, or are marked as 'unknown publisher' despite valid signature. Track Sectigo-signed binaries executing for the first time.

suggestion.title: Certificate-Signed Payload with Unexpected Network Egress

suggestion.title: Installer Payload Extraction to Hidden or System Directories
suggestion.rationale: Malicious installer likely extracts secondary payload — pipeline should detect suspicious file-drop patterns from legitimate-looking parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RVTools or trusted installer processes creating files in System32, AppData\Roaming hidden folders, or ProgramData with non-standard extensions. Detect parent-child relationships: installer → suspicious executable/DLL.

suggestion.title: Spoofed or Abused Sectigo Certificate Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Sectigo cert abuse suggests either certificate was stolen/misused or signature validation logic bypassed — pipeline should alert on certificate inconsistencies.

suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'Steal Banking Credentials' but pipeline did not generate credential-theft detection use cases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by package install scripts (e.g., npm postinstall, .NET build tasks) that enumerate credential storage paths (browser Local State, Windows Credential Manager, cloud CLI config directories), access HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SAM or environment variables containing secrets (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_*, token patterns).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Cloud Credential Access from Package Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes launched from package managers (npm, NuGet) that access cloud provider credential files (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure/tokens, GCP config paths), enumerate environment variables for *KEY* or *TOKEN*, or make authentication calls to AWS STS, Azure Identity Service, or GCP credential endpoints.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration from Package Execution Context

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Poisoning with Credential Harvester Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' but no use case specific to npm supply-chain compromise

suggestion.title: Sicoob Banking Customer Credential Targeted Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Sicoob as target; no use case specifically for detecting harvesting patterns targeting Brazilian banking customers or Sicoob-related credential stores
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for package code or spawned processes targeting Portuguese-language browser credential storage, Sicoob banking URLs in browser cache, or credential patterns matching Brazilian banking formats (CPF/CNPJ embedded in stolen data). suggestion.title: MicrosoftSystem64 Process Execution Detection

suggestion.title: Suspicious HuggingFace Dataset Upload or API Calls

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Stealthy Process / Unsigned/Living-off-the-Land Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly marks the malware as 'stealthy' — a direct signal that it uses defense evasion (LOLBins, code injection, DLL side-loading, etc.). No evasion-focused detection was proposed.

suggestion.title: Masquerading: Process Name / Path Spoofing (System64 vs System32)
suggestion.rationale: Malware name 'MicrosoftSystem64' strongly suggests impersonation of legitimate Microsoft Windows system directories. No masquerading detection rule was generated despite obvious naming deception.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping & Lateral Movement (Ukraine Targets)
suggestion.rationale: Russian APT campaigns against Ukraine infrastructure routinely include credential theft and lateral spread. Pipeline extracted zero credential-access or lateral-movement techniques despite 'cyberattack' framing suggesting multi-stage operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LSASS access, credential manager queries, mimikatz/sekurlsa execution signatures, RDP connection spraying, and SMB enumeration from Ukraine-based hosts. Correlate failed/successful login counts across domains and flag administrative account compromise.

suggestion.title: Automated Malware Execution via Script/Macro Delivery
suggestion.rationale: High-severity attack on geopolitical targets typically uses Office macros, PowerShell, or scripting. Pipeline extracted no execution-phase techniques despite article describing an active campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office document macro execution, suspicious PowerShell (WinRM, Base64 encoding, encoded commands), script interpreter spawns from unusual parents (explorer.exe, winword.exe), and obfuscated VBA/JavaScript execution.

suggestion.title: Impact Phase: Critical Infrastructure Disruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article tags as [CRIT] and targets Ukraine—strong implication of destructive/disruptive intent. Pipeline failed to generate any impact-phase detections (ransomware, wiping, DDoS, data exfiltration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file deletion patterns, MBR/partition table writes, system shutdown commands, and network share encryption/encryption tool signatures. Alert on infrastructure-spanning file locks and simultaneous high-volume data access across critical assets.

suggestion.title: npm Package Typosquat Installation - Name Edit Distance Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on 'typosquatted npm packages'—core attack vector. Pipeline missed detection of package installs where requested name differs from installed name by 1-3 character edits (transposition, homoglyphs, missing chars).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install command lines and .npmrc activity. Flag when Levenshtein distance between requested package name (from CLI arg or package.json) and actually-installed package exceeds 0 but is <3. Cross-reference installed package against official npm registry metadata to confirm typosquat provenance.

suggestion.title: Suspicious post-install Script Enumerates Environment Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets'. Typosquatted packages execute code during install (post-install hooks). Pipeline must detect post-install scripts reading AWS_*, AZURE_*, GCP_*, CI_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, DATABASE_URL environment variables or ~/.aws/~/.ssh filesystem paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned during npm install (node, node_modules/.bin/* executables). Alert when subprocess calls printenv, env, or reads shell environment in context of post-install script. Flag file reads to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config, $GITHUB_TOKEN, or similar secret storage locations.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Secrets via HTTPS POST from npm Context
suggestion.rationale: Stolen secrets must exit the system. Article's 'steal' verb implies network exfiltration. Pipeline should detect HTTPS requests with credential-shaped payloads (base64, JWT tokens, AWS key format) originating from npm-spawned processes to non-whitelisted domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline npm process network behavior (allow legitimate registry calls to registry.npmjs.org, github.com). Alert on outbound HTTPS POST/PUT from node/npm processes to non-whitelisted IPs/domains within 1-10 minutes of suspicious package install. Inspect request bodies/headers for base64-encoded credentials, JWT patterns, or AWS-key-like strings.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package with Empty or Mismatched Repository Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatted packages lack legitimate project history. Pipeline should surface indicators in npm registry metadata: newly-created author accounts, packages claiming to mirror popular libraries but with missing source repository links, zero GitHub stars/forks, or completely absent repository URLs in package.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package against npm registry API.
