Alert on temporal clustering suggesting automated discovery. Baseline the co-occurrence frequency of unrelated low-severity CVEs; flag anomalous combinations.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Vulnerable Code Injection at Scale
suggestion.rationale: Article: '65–70% of production code is now generated by AI, and nearly half of it contains exploitable vulnerabilities.' Repositories with bulk AI-authored code are higher-risk targets for in-the-wild exploitation of newly-introduced flaws.
log_sources: scanner results correlated with code provenance
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repositories with high commit volume from AI coding assistants (detectable via commit metadata, tool attribution) combined with same-day security scanner hits on those new files. Compare vulnerability density in AI-generated vs. human-authored code; alert on outliers above baseline.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Remediation Activity: Distinguish from Malicious Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes mass remediation: 'Snyk is now detecting six vulnerabilities for every one remediated.' Large-scale dependency version changes via agents are legitimate, but same pattern enables supply chain attacks. Detection must distinguish remediation (upgrades off vulnerable versions) from downgrade attacks.
log_sources: git commit diffs to manifest files
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline bulk dependency version changes per repository (expected from scanning/remediation campaigns). Alert on downgrades to known-vulnerable versions or pins to unmaintained releases. Correlate with Snyk/public advisory release dates; remediation activity clusters near advisory dates, malicious downgrades don't.

suggestion.title: Remediation Agent Context Manipulation: Malicious Scan Result Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes agents receiving Snyk scan results as context to drive fixes: 'Snyk scans and injects the right context into your LLM.' Attacker could craft malicious scan payloads to influence generated fixes, inserting hidden code paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor remediation agent inputs for anomalous scan payloads: oversized contexts, nested/encoded vulnerability descriptions inconsistent with known CVE formats, or syntax suggesting prompt injection. Compare generated fixes against expected remediation scope; flag fixes that introduce new dependencies or code execution outside the vulnerability scope.

suggestion.title: Prototype chain abuse: Buffer.__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ in vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC explicitly chains 'Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")' — this is the *actual exploitation code*. No hunt directly detects this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node/nodejs process where command line or script body contains consecutive references to Buffer, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, and __proto__ in same statement. This pattern is exploitation-specific and virtually absent in legitimate code.

suggestion.title: vm2/NodeVM instantiation + shell child process (correlated time-window)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker must instantiate 'new VM()' then run PoC. Pipeline should correlate vm2/NodeVM keywords in parent command line with shell spawning within 30s window, not as separate hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe processes with 'vm2', 'NodeVM', 'require("vm2")', or 'new VM(' in command line, then alert if child cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawns within 30 seconds. 30s window constrains FP from unrelated processes.

suggestion.title: PoC command markers in node-spawned shells (high-fidelity)
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC includes 'echo pwned' and other escape-proof markers. Current UC_8_3 bundles this with other signals; deserves standalone high-confidence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alert (not baselining) on cmd.exe or powershell.exe child of node.exe where command line contains 'echo pwned', 'require("child_process")', 'child_process.exec', 'execSync', or 'spawnSync'. These are vm2-escape PoC signatures with near-zero legitimate use.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 import + process execution (code-path correlation)
suggestion.rationale: Article doesn't show how PoC is *delivered* to vm2 (HTTP POST, file write, repl input). Add behavioral hunt for vm2 loading + child process creation without antecedent legitimate NodeVM setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe process containing vm2 module load followed within 10 seconds by creation of child process (any shell or script interpreter). Baseline out build/test environments. Flag anomalous process parent (web service, message queue processor) running vm2 code.

suggestion.title: vm2 patch bypass detection — nesting:true with undefined require
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the exploitation vector: 'The check uses strict equality (`options.require === false`), which is trivially bypassed by omitting the `require` option entirely. When `require` is not specified, `options.require` is `undefined`, not `false`.' No current UC detects this precondition. Should monitor for vm2 NodeVM instantiation with nesting enabled and require property absent or explicitly undefined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vm2 NodeVM object construction where nesting=true and require is either absent from options or explicitly set to undefined/null. Pattern match on new NodeVM({nesting: true}) or new NodeVM({nesting: true, require: undefined}). This represents direct exploitation of the CVE-2023-37903 patch bypass.

suggestion.title: Child process module access from vm2 sandbox — privilege escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation achieves 'full RCE' via sandbox escape. The exploitation mechanism is accessing child_process module within the vm2 context, which is explicitly listed in UC_6_2 as a telltale command pattern. This represents the actual privilege escalation/escape step that should be detected before OS command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within Node.js application context, detect require() or import statements accessing 'child_process' module, or direct calls to spawn/exec/execSync when vm2 module is present in the same process ancestry. Look for module resolution attempts against child_process from within a sandboxed context indicator (vm2 config in same code block).

suggestion.title: vm2 library version inventory with vulnerable range alerting
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_3 only detects presence of vm2. Article specifies vulnerability exists in version <=3.11.3 ('Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3)'). Asset hunts should parse package.json or npm metadata to extract version and flag specifically vulnerable ranges, not just presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse vm2 package.json files to extract version string and alert when version <= 3.11.3 (vulnerable to CVE-2026-47137). Distinguish between patched and unpatched installations. Correlate with application criticality to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: vm2 package with version validation (<=3.11.3) in package-lock/yarn.lock
suggestion.rationale: UC_7_1 detects the presence of vm2 via package.json on disk but does NOT validate the vulnerable version constraint mentioned in the article summary '(<=3.11.3)'. Presence alone generates FPs for patched instances. Article explicitly states 'vm2 <=3.11.3', but detection does not enforce this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for vm2 presence in lock files where version string matches regex <=3\.11\.[0-3] or legacy 3\.9\.x versions. Correlate with npm_audit logs or package manager telemetry. Cross-reference with known dev/staging deployments to reduce false positives in controlled lab environments.

suggestion.title: Node process performing Promise constructor/Symbol.species manipulation without vm2 import context
suggestion.rationale: UC_7_3 searches for PoC keywords in cmdline ('Symbol.species', 'constructor.constructor') but does not verify that the node process has vm2 in its dependency tree. Detects POC but creates signal noise from unrelated Promise/Symbol manipulation. Article details the Promise species escape mechanism but UCs lack context filtering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate UC_7_3 cmdline hits with module dependency inspection: verify vm2 module is loaded into node.exe via module inspection (ETW, strace, /proc inspection on Linux). Reject matches where Promise/Symbol is invoked in legit frameworks (async/await transpilation, TypeScript Promise polyfills, etc.).

suggestion.title: npm registry interaction or code pull immediately preceding vm2 sandbox escape PoC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack as 'Attackers can write code which can escape' but does not address the supply-chain scenario: how does attacker code reach the vm2 runtime in the first place? If delivered via npm package or web request to a public app using vm2, earlier-phase detection of suspicious code fetch/pull is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl/wget/git clone/npm install originating from or targeting untrusted sources (pastebin, gist, raw.githubusercontent.com, suspicious domains) within 5–30 minutes preceding vm2 PoC execution or node.exe child process spawning. Filter known CI/CD patterns.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 instantiation with untrusted input — CVE-2026-47210 enablement
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability triggers when 'untrusted code is executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI'. Detection for vm2.VM() or vm2.NodeVM() constructor calls in source code or runtime bytecode patterns would identify active vulnerable configurations before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js processes loading WebAssembly.Suspending or WebAssembly.promising APIs in combination with vm2 code instantiation patterns. Look for process memory regions containing vm2 bytecode signatures or source patterns matching 'new VM(|NodeVM(' followed by .run() with untrusted input markers.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype species gadget chain manipulation — JSPI-backed sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47210)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploit mechanism: 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally() in a way that bypasses Promise-species hardening'. Direct detection of Promise constructor override or species manipulation patterns would catch the specific gadget chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js process for runtime bytecode patterns or source code containing Promise constructor reassignment (Promise = ...), Promise.prototype.finally override, or Symbol.species manipulation within vm2 execution contexts. Correlate with vm2 module presence and JSPI API loading.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI module instantiation from untrusted code path — CVE-2026-47210 detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'WebAssembly JSPI (WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending)' as the attack surface. Direct detection of these JSPI APIs invoked from vm2-sandboxed code would catch the exploit vector at invocation time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Node.js process event logs or DLL load sequences for WebAssembly.Suspending or WebAssembly.promising API calls originating from vm2 execution contexts, especially with async/await patterns. Look for WASM module instantiation immediately following vm2.run() or vm2.VM.eval() calls.

suggestion.title: Abnormal shell spawning ancestry from Node.js with low-privilege escalation pattern — vm2 sandbox escape post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sandbox escape leading to arbitrary code execution culminating in shell spawning. Detection should track Node.js → shell spawn with specific ancestry depth and timing patterns unusual for legitimate Node.js workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js spawning shell (cmd.exe, powershell, bash) where: (1) parent process command line or environment contains indicators of untrusted code execution (eval, user-supplied script paths, inline code), (2) spawn occurs <100ms after Node.js start (bypasses initialization), or (3) shell is spawned with network I/O or file exfiltration activity in same process group within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: vm2 module version detection against CVE-2026-47210 patch threshold
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable version: 'vm2 (<= 3.11.3)'. Proactive hunt for exact version strings in package.json or npm registry data would reduce false negatives from file-based detection and enable version-specific targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for vm2 package.json or npm manifest data where 'version' field is <= 3.11.3. Cross-reference with process execution of the Node.js application hosting that package. Flag any execution of that application for heightened monitoring of post-exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names ScreenConnect as the malware payload: 'ScreenConnect Malware' in title and describes it as delivery vector for attacker commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect executable creation and launch (typically scconnect.exe or variants). Alert on ScreenConnect processes spawning child processes indicative of command execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Correlate with outbound network connections to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Fake Adobe Document Cloud Phishing Link Click
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described as 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages'—users tricked into visiting attacker-controlled domains impersonating Adobe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS traffic to typosquatted or newly-registered domains mimicking Adobe Document Cloud infrastructure (documentcloud.adobe.com variants). Flag Office 365 URL click telemetry and email gateway logs for links matching Adobe domain patterns but resolving to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: User Execution of Malware from Fake Adobe Site
suggestion.rationale: Users deceived into downloading and executing malware: 'Hackers Use Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages to Deliver' indicates user interaction step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable downloads (suspicious file extensions: .exe, .scr, .ps1) originating from browser processes where referring domain matches known/suspected fake Adobe infrastructure. Correlate file creation in Downloads folder with immediate process execution within minutes.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect is a legitimate RMM tool co-opted for C2; article describes delivery of ScreenConnect malware implies C2 channel establishment for post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect default ports (5938, 5939) and known ScreenConnect certificate signatures. Alert on unusual ScreenConnect outbound connections from non-IT systems. Flag beaconing patterns (fixed-interval callbacks) to ScreenConnect C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Creation Spawned by ScreenConnect
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect enables remote command execution; once installed, attacker can execute arbitrary commands, which is core attack objective in delivery-and-execute chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other system utilities spawned with parent process ScreenConnect.exe or scconnect.exe. Flag unusual command-line parameters (network reconnaissance, privilege escalation utilities, lateral movement tools) executed from ScreenConnect context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Office/Browser Download of Executable from Fake Adobe Domain
suggestion.rationale: Fake Adobe pages deliver malware; users downloading files from these pages is a critical initial foothold step that must be detected before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads initiated by outlook.exe or browser processes (chrome.exe, iexplore.exe, firefox.exe) from non-standard/suspicious domains. Flag executable file writes to user-writable directories immediately preceded by network traffic to domains impersonating Adobe.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Video Player Software Update Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes fake video player updates as the initial compromise vector: 'Hackers Use Fake Video Player Updates to Deploy Miner and RAT Malware.' No use case for detecting update-like execution from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for video player executables (VLC, media-player binaries, custom players) being executed from non-standard locations (Downloads, Temp, AppData Local, user-writable paths). Cross-reference against known legitimate installation paths. Alert on unsigned executables masquerading as updates or running from URLs embedded in user documents.

suggestion.title: Crypto Miner Process Detection
suggestion.rationale: Payload explicitly includes 'Miner' malware deployment. Article states miner deployment but pipeline generated zero use cases for resource hijacking detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect miner processes by behavioral pattern: sustained elevated CPU usage (>60% across cores) paired with unusual process names or children of video player executables. Cross-reference with known miner pools (outbound connections to mining pool domains, high-volume traffic to fixed port ranges like 3333, 8332, 14444). Flag parent-child relationships where parent is video player and child consumes CPU anomalously.

suggestion.title: RAT Command-and-Control Communication from Video Player Context
suggestion.rationale: Payload includes 'RAT (Remote Access Trojan)' but pipeline did not surface detection for C2 exfiltration or RAT behavior. Article states RAT deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from video player processes or child processes spawned by them to non-standard destinations (non-HTTP/HTTPS ports, RFC 1918 ranges, bulletproof hosters). Flag sustained or periodic outbound connections to C2-like patterns (fixed destination, regular callback intervals). Cross-check against threat intel feeds for known RAT C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Process Injection or Hollowing from Video Player Executable
suggestion.rationale: RAT and miner payloads typically use process injection for stealth and persistence. Article mentions RAT but no detection for common evasion techniques like injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on video player process (or children) calling CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, or similar injection APIs targeting unrelated system processes (lsass, svchost, explorer, winlogon). Monitor for unsigned DLL injection into legitimate system processes where the DLL origin traces back to temp or download directories.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task or Registry Run Key Persistence from Compromised Video Player
suggestion.rationale: RAT and miners require persistence mechanisms. Article does not detail persistence but standard malware patterns include scheduled tasks or Run keys. Pipeline should anticipate this given RAT classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation with parent process traceable to video player installation path or temp locations. Alert on HKCU/HKLM Run or RunOnce registry modifications by video-player-spawned processes. Detect scheduled tasks executing from unusual paths (Downloads, AppData Local temp) or with encoded/obfuscated command lines.

suggestion.title: Unexpected DLL or Module Load in Video Player Process
suggestion.rationale: Miner and RAT functionality is often injected via DLL or sideloading. Article mentions both payloads but no detection for malicious module load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on video player process loading DLLs from non-standard directories (temp, downloads, appdata local, user-writable paths). Look for unsigned DLLs or those with names commonly associated with miners (xmrig, monero, opencl libraries not bundled with the player). Cross-reference against known malicious DLL hashes.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Phishing Link Detection and Response
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'LinkedIn Social Engineering' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection use case for identifying or blocking malicious LinkedIn profile messages, shortened URLs, or suspicious domain redirects from LinkedIn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks to uncommon external domains from LinkedIn URLs within corporate email/proxy logs. Cross-reference with unusual binary downloads or script execution within 1-2 hours of LinkedIn link interaction. Flag shortened URLs or domain redirects originating from LinkedIn messages.

suggestion.title: macOS Binary Execution from Suspicious Paths
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline does not detect 'Custom macOS Malware' execution. Phishing-delivered malware typically runs from ~/Downloads, /tmp, /var/tmp, or auto-extracted paths, requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or newly-signed Mach-O binaries executing from user download directories. Flag shell interpreters (bash, zsh, python) spawned as children of decompression utilities (unzip, tar, ditto). Cross-reference file modification times with browser download events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Python/Script Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware frequently uses Python or shell scripts for obfuscation and C2 communication. No detection rule generated for suspicious script interpreter activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python or zsh execution with network I/O, DNS queries, or system enumeration (whoami, uname, sw_vers, system_profiler). Alert on script interpreters running hidden files from user home directory or spawning unusual child processes.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: No detection use case for outbound C2 traffic or persistence mechanisms typical of macOS malware. Custom malware variants often establish regular callbacks to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS outbound connections from non-standard macOS processes (especially those recently launched from ~/Downloads) to non-corporate domains. Alert on periodic beaconing intervals or domain generation algorithm (DGA) patterns. Monitor for certificate pinning bypass or unusual TLS versions.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names HTTPSpy as a deployed tool ('Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy'); no use case exists to detect its launch or behavioral patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events matching HTTPSpy variants (known file names, parent-child relationships). Alert on unsigned executables spawning from temp directories or AppData with network connectivity patterns consistent with HTTP-based C2.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Abuse - Unauthorized Port Binding
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'VS Code Tunnels' as attack vector; no detection use case covers tunnel port binding or tunnel daemon spawning. Techniques like T1021.004 (Remote Service Session Hijacking) are not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect code.exe or codeserver processes with unusual command-line arguments (tunnel, --tunnel-uri, bind on non-standard ports). Alert on unexpected VS Code service spawning from system32 or suspicious user contexts.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Deployment & Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'HelloDoor' as new capability; pipeline extracted zero observables or use cases for detecting its installation or initial execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to Run/RunOnce keys or scheduled task creation matching HelloDoor signatures. Flag file system modifications in System32, AppData, or ProgramFiles with associated process creation from system services.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky HTTP/HTTPS C2 Beaconing Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes toolkit expansion; no use case detects C2 communication patterns from HTTPSpy, HelloDoor, or tunnel infrastructure. Missing coverage of T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections with Kimsuky-attributed User-Agent strings, domain patterns, or jitter intervals. Alert on beaconing from non-browser processes or encrypted tunneling over standard ports.

suggestion.title: VS Code Service Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: VS Code tunnel abuse can enable privilege escalation or persistence; article does not surface detection for token impersonation or service context switching via tunnel mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code.exe or tunnel services spawning child processes with elevated privileges or different user contexts. Alert on service account impersonation or token duplication tied to tunnel infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via HelloDoor/HTTPSpy
suggestion.rationale: Kimsuky historically targets credentials; article does not surface detection use cases for credential harvesting by new tools. Missing T1056 (Input Capture), T1555 (Credentials from Password Stores), or T1110 (Brute Force).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HelloDoor/HTTPSpy spawning processes associated with credential dumping (lsass, SAM registry access, password manager API calls). Flag clipboard monitoring or input hooks paired with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation from Non-Standard Source
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'Malicious NuGet Package as Sicoob SDK'—T1195.001 supply-chain compromise. No IOC extraction or kill-chain reconstruction occurred, despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag NuGet package installations (dotnet add package, nuget install) where package name closely resembles legitimate financial/banking SDKs (Sicoob, Bradesco, Caixa variants) or published by newly-registered authors. Correlate with subsequent unsigned DLL loads or child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Exfiltration via Untrusted .NET Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exfiltrates Banking Passwords'—credential access and exfiltration phases completely absent from pipeline output. No detection logic for password harvesting from browser credential stores, DPAPI secrets, or banking app memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET processes (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, dotnet.exe) spawned by or loaded from NuGet package directories. Flag access to LSASecrets, browser credential stores (Chrome, Edge LocalState), or calls to DPAPI unprotection APIs. Detect inline SecureString decryption or credential enumeration via System.Management.Automation.

suggestion.title: High-Entropy Data Exfiltration to Uncommon Destination
suggestion.rationale: Password exfiltration requires egress to attacker infrastructure. Article title contains 'Exfiltrates Banking Passwords' but pipeline generated zero exfiltration-phase detections (T1041).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from machines with banking-SDK-like packages installed, especially to newly-registered domains or IPs with no legitimate purpose. Flag high-entropy POST bodies (Base64, gzip) or DNS queries to C2 infrastructure. Correlate with .NET process creation timelines.

suggestion.title: NuGet Package Typosquatting of Banking SDK Names
suggestion.rationale: Title 'as Sicoob SDK' implies impersonation/typosquatting (classic T1195.001 variant). Pipeline failed to extract package name, version, or author as IOCs despite being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .csproj, packages.config, or .nupkg files for package dependencies with names matching banking SDKs (off-by-one chars, homoglyph variants, added prefix/suffix). Flag packages from single-package authors or with zero GitHub activity. Alert on first install of low-reputation packages in production environments.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Obfuscated DLL Execution from NuGet Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malware distribution via NuGet requires code execution post-install. Pipeline did not surface execution-phase techniques (T1204.002, T1059.003). No detection logic for suspicious child processes or script execution from package install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of DLLs or EXEs from %USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages\, %APPDATA%\NuGet\, or project bin/obj directories. Flag unsigned binaries, use of rundll32/regsvcs for DLL loading, or PowerShell scripts launched from post-install hooks. Correlate with unusual parent processes (msbuild, csc, dotnet).

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Install Script Execution in NuGet Package
suggestion.rationale: NuGet packages can embed .ps1 or .bat scripts in install.ps1 / uninstall.ps1 hooks. Article does not detail execution mechanism, but pipeline should surface common .NET supply-chain execution patterns absent from kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell or batch script execution from NuGet package directories during or immediately after package installation (dotnet add/restore/update). Flag scripts with obfuscation, network requests, or credential-access patterns. Alert on unsigned script execution policies or ExecutionPolicy bypasses.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials'—direct supply-chain vector requiring package-manager operation visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet.exe for installation of packages with financial-institution names or unusual publishers. Alert on installations from non-corporate feeds. Correlate with subsequent credential-store or cloud-secret access to establish exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets'—JavaScript runtime supply-chain requires detection of post-install script anomalies and embedded credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install with post-install scripts executing credential-harvesting commands (aws configure, kubectl auth, cloud CLI logins). Flag packages with names mimicking legitimate security or banking libraries.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Access from Package Manager Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states packages 'steal banking credentials'—requires detection of credential-access and exfiltration originating from package-installation processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NuGet/npm processes spawning children that access banking credential stores, browser password managers, or Windows credential manager. Correlate with network exfiltration to unknown C2 or attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloud Secret Retrieval During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies packages 'target Cloud Secrets'—requires cloud-audit-log detection of secret-access APIs called from build/install contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GetSecretValue, RetrieveSecret, or ListSecrets API calls from processes spawned by package managers. Unusual cross-account credential assumption or service-principal impersonation during development workflows indicates compromise.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Typosquatting and Metadata Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires upstream detection: article describes 'malicious Sicoob' packages in NuGet/npm—repositories must monitor for spoofed or newly-published packages mimicking legitimate banking software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag NuGet/npm packages from newly-created publishers with names resembling financial institutions, banking libraries, or infrastructure tools. Monitor for rapid version churn, mismatched metadata, or unusual geographic publisher location relative to organization.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers leveraging ChatGPT to 'turn web pages into phishing payloads'—direct social-engineering attack using AI-generated content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails for AI-generated language patterns (generic openings, templated urgency, repetitive formal structure). Flag messages with credential requests combined with newly registered or homoglyph domains. Alert on emails whose body could be traced to ChatGPT outputs via fingerprinting.

suggestion.title: Web-Based Credential Harvesting Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'turn web pages into phishing payloads'—implies malicious web forms harvesting credentials at attacker-controlled URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user visits to newly registered or suspicious domains ending in form submissions (POST to login/password endpoints). Monitor for HTML form injection or credential-field harvesting patterns. Alert on landing pages mimicking legitimate SaaS sign-in pages.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Prompt Injection for Payload Generation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits ChatGPT itself to generate phishing content—represents prompt injection / AI-service abuse attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API calls for unusual request patterns: rapid iteration on email/HTML templates, requests asking model to bypass safety guardrails, or craft credential-stealing content. Flag accounts with sudden surge in payload-generation requests.

suggestion.title: Homoglyph/Typosquat Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Phishing payloads require attacker-controlled hosting; article implies registration of lookalike domains mimicking ChatGPT or cloud services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registration of homoglyphs and Levenshtein-distance variants of OpenAI/ChatGPT/Azure/AWS domains. Cross-check newly registered domains against phishing reporting feeds (URLhaus, PhishTank). Monitor WHOIS changes for bulk registrations.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Click-Through and Credential Submission Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Attack sequence completes when users click malicious links and submit credentials; establishes impact phase of phishing kill-chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email clicks on suspicious URLs with subsequent POST requests to credential fields on landing pages. Alert on deviations from baseline (user never clicks such links, or sudden spike). Monitor for session token theft or subsequent lateral-movement attempts post-credential submission.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT-Generated Email Thread Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability enables crafting convincing phishing emails; attackers may spoof legitimate email threads using ChatGPT to generate contextually relevant body text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with spoofed in-reply-to headers but new sender domains. Monitor for contextually relevant (but fabricated) email replies that mention recent business events or projects without prior legitimate correspondence. Flag AI-generated tone/phrasing inconsistent with claimed sender.

suggestion.title: Detect GREYVIBE Threat Actor Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names GREYVIBE as Russian-linked APT. Pipeline failed to extract or track actor name. Title: 'New Russian-Linked GREYVIBE Targets Ukraine...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for C2 communications to known or suspected GREYVIBE infrastructure. Track DNS queries and network connections to domains/IPs previously associated with Russian-state APT activity targeting Ukraine. Establish baseline for actor-specific TTPs once article body is accessible.

suggestion.title: Detect AI-Assisted Reconnaissance or Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks' (title) but pipeline generated no detection for automated reconnaissance or LLM-powered social engineering. This is a significant gap for novel attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phishing or reconnaissance emails with unusually polished content, grammatical accuracy, or contextual specificity inconsistent with typical targeted phishing, suggesting LLM generation. Monitor for bulk reconnaissance queries (IP scans, port scans) with low entropy source patterns typical of scripted/automated tools.

suggestion.title: Monitor Ukraine-Sector Targeting by Russian Threat Actors
suggestion.rationale: Geographic targeting (Ukraine) and state attribution (Russian-linked) are explicit in title. Pipeline should create geolocation-based detection correlating to this actor group and region.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on intrusions or reconnaissance against Ukraine-based IP blocks or Ukrainian-targeted sectors (energy, government, military) by Russian ASN space. Correlate failed logins, scanning activity, and persistence indicators from Russian IP ranges against Ukrainian targets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation with SYSTEM Privilege
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'ransomware uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task'—the primary execution vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for scheduled-task creation despite this being the core attack mechanic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on schtasks.exe or PowerShell New-ScheduledTask with /ru:SYSTEM or RunLevel=Highest. Flag tasks with unusual action payloads (batch, .ps1, obfuscated commands) or scheduled to run at system startup. Exclude known admin/patch tasks.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Encryption Post-Scheduled Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'encrypt local drives' as outcome—T1486 impact is the goal. Pipeline must detect file encryption patterns following task trigger: high-velocity writes with entropy spikes, common ransomware extensions, or mass file modifications across user/shared directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >100 file creates/modifies in <10 minutes on user/Documents/shares after scheduled-task launch. Correlate to parent process spawned by task scheduler. Alert on file name patterns (.locked, .encrypted, .[random hex], .pix).

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Context Process Spawning Encryption Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'elevated privileges (SYSTEM)' enabling the encryption. Pipeline must detect anomalous SYSTEM-context process execution (cmd, powershell, batch) with file-iteration or crypto-library references—signature of post-privilege-escalation ransomware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SYSTEM-context cmd.exe or powershell.exe with command lines containing file patterns (dir /s, Get-ChildItem -Recurse, *.doc), wildcards, or encryption-related keywords (crypt, lock, aes). Require correlation to scheduled-task creation within last 2 hours.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Registry Persistence Write with Suspicious Payload
suggestion.rationale: Scheduled tasks are created via registry writes under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\. Pipeline must detect registry modifications coupled with encoded/obfuscated action arguments—common for fileless ransomware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to Task Scheduler registry paths (TaskCache\Tasks) where Actions field contains base64, hex, or multi-stage PowerShell. Flag if written by non-admin user or from unexpected process context (Office, browser).

suggestion.title: Local Drive Encryption Detection via File Extension Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'encrypt local drives'—likely C:, D:, etc. Pipeline must detect volume-wide file extension shifts or new extension patterns appearing post-ransomware-execution, especially on fixed drives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline file-extension distribution per drive monthly. Alert when >50 new file extensions appear in <1 hour on fixed drives, or when a single uncommon extension accounts for >10% of new files. Exclude archive and temp directories.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Typosquatted Name
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'typosquatted npm packages'—packages with names similar to popular libraries. No detector exists for suspicious package install patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installs for names that are close string-matches to known legitimate packages (Levenshtein distance, character substitution). Cross-ref against whitelist of approved registry sources. Alert on first-time installs or installs from non-standard registries.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via npm Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets'—implying malicious postinstall hooks. Pipeline has no detector for credential access triggered by package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process lineage: npm install → sh/bash/powershell child processes accessing common credential stores (~/.aws, ~/.azure, .env files, CI env vars like GITHUB_TOKEN, SLACK_WEBHOOK). Detect file reads from process spawned by node_modules/* scripts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from Developer Machine Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials must be exfiltrated; article implies data leaves developer systems. No detector for post-install exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal egress from developer workstations. Alert on new external domains contacted within 10 minutes of npm package install, especially HTTPS POST requests with JSON/credential-like payloads or large data transfers to IPs not in org IP space.

suggestion.title: Registry Poisoning or Alternative npm Registry Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article implies packages come from npm registry or lookalike; pipeline should surface registry switching or mirror usage anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc files for registry URL changes pointing to non-official registries. Alert on .npmrc modifications in user home or project root. Correlate against known malicious mirror IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: AWS/Azure/GCP Credential Harvesting from Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'cloud and CI/CD secrets'; pipeline should detect credential enumeration from environment variables and config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes of npm/node for subprocess calls to 'env', 'printenv', or direct file reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure/*, KUBECONFIG, CI provider secrets. Alert on credential-like strings (base64, AWS key patterns) in memory/subprocess arguments.

suggestion.title: Unusual Script Execution from node_modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatted packages execute code at install time via postinstall/preinstall hooks. Pipeline has no baseline for node_modules execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent is npm/node and child process binary path is within node_modules/ or script is prefixed with node_modules. Baseline common postinstall behaviors; tune on compilation/build tools. Flag obfuscated scripts, heavy use of curl/wget, or credentials in argv.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious npm packages to target cloud and CI/CD credentials'—packages will execute postinstall scripts during npm install. No detection for process execution from node_modules or build contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution originating from node_modules directories or npm postinstall hooks. Alert on parent process npm.exe/npm spawning shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) with access to sensitive environment variables or credential files.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Enumeration by npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing 'cloud and CI/CD secrets'—threat model requires reading AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_*, GitHub tokens, etc. No coverage for env var enumeration or /proc/self/environ reads from npm child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm-spawned processes executing commands like 'env', 'printenv', or reading credential files (.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh, .env). Flag process syscalls to access environment or /proc in CI/CD contexts (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins runners).

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from npm Processes to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials must exfiltrate; article implies network callback. 'npm packages used to steal... secrets' requires C2 or data-exfil connection. No network signature for npm child processes opening unexpected external connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm.exe/npm child processes initiating outbound connections to non-CDN, non-registry IPs/domains (especially if destination is not npmjs.com, github.com, or known package registries). Flag POST requests during package install phase.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Package Name Detection and Dependency Review
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'typosquatted npm packages'—supply-chain vector requires detecting similar-looking package names. No IOC list provided, yet the campaign is centered on package-name spoofing attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Review package.json and package-lock.json for suspiciously similar names (e.g., 'aws' vs 'aws-sdk', 'express-server' vs 'express', 'lodash-core' vs 'lodash'). Cross-reference against typosquatting databases. Alert on first-time or newly-published packages pulled into build environments.

suggestion.title: Secrets Files Access by npm Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires reading credential stores: 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets' implies filesystem access to .aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa, .docker/config.json, .kube/config, or env-file artifacts. No detection for file-access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm-spawned processes reading from credential paths: ~/.aws/*, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.kube/config, CI secrets directories, or environment-variable dump files. High-confidence signal in CI/CD contexts (GitHub Actions runners, GitLab CI, Jenkins).

suggestion.title: Unusual Credential Export and Env Var Dump Operations
suggestion.rationale: To exfil secrets, malware must enumerate and serialize credentials. Article implies bulk credential theft; no detection for 'env > /tmp' patterns, 'cat ~/.aws/credentials | curl', or credential dumping via base64 encoding in npm install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell invocations within npm postinstall hooks that pipe credential files (aws, ssh, docker, kube config) through compression, encoding, or curl. Alert on base64 encoding, gzip, or tar operations on .aws, .ssh, or .docker paths inside CI/CD runs.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Vulnerable Container Image Supply Chain Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can compromise containers through 'ready-made Docker images' from Docker Hub and 'third-party images' with unreliable provenance: 'the infrastructure inside containers is typically updated less frequently and may contain outdated and vulnerable software versions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deployment of container images from untrusted registries, images with known vulnerabilities in their layers, or images with stale or unpatched base OS versions. Cross-reference image digests against vulnerability feeds.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Sudo Misconfiguration in Container
suggestion.rationale: Article dedicates section to 'Attacks on sudo' and 'Privilege escalation in the container' with 'insecure file permissions' enabling abuse of elevation mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocations without password in containers, NOPASSWD sudoers entries, or privilege escalation from unprivileged container processes. Monitor for chmod/chown operations on sudoers files or sudo binary.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded or Default Credentials in Container Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Use of default passwords' and 'Passing passwords via command arguments' as configuration vulnerabilities: 'developers often face constraints when preparing images; to overcome these, they may resort to insecure solutions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process command lines or environment variables containing known default password patterns, credential literals in docker run/exec commands, or container startup logs with plaintext secrets. Flag Dockerfile COPY/RUN statements with credential material.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining or Unauthorized DDoS Activity in Container
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a compromised container can be used for DDoS attacks, cryptocurrency mining, or traffic proxying' and notes this is the minimum risk profile of container compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high CPU sustained usage patterns within containers running non-compute workloads, spawning of known mining or DDoS tool binaries, or outbound connections to mining pool domains or botnet C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Container Escape or Host Compromise via Vulnerability Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'once an attacker gains control of a container, they can steal or destroy data directly from it, access neighboring containers, or even attempt to escape the container, compromising the entire enterprise network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious system calls from container contexts (ptrace, kexec, module loading), attempts to mount host filesystems, access to /proc/sys, or spawning of host-level processes from within container namespaces.

suggestion.title: Integrity Check Failure or Unexpected File Modification in Container Image Layers
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Lack of integrity checks' and 'Insecure file permissions' as critical risks: developers 'making only minimal changes' to pre-built images without verification mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify container image layer digests against expected SHA256 hashes at deployment and runtime. Alert on unexpected file modifications within container read-only layers or deviation of runtime file state from image manifest.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign - World Cup Event Lure
suggestion.rationale: Phishing explicitly listed in keywords as attack vector; World Cup is high-profile lure vector for targeted campaigns against infrastructure operators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound email with World Cup or sporting-event keywords targeting critical infrastructure domains. Flag suspicious sender-domain reputation, URL shorteners, and embedded links with low VirusTotal detections.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing - Redirect to Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: QR codes explicitly mentioned in keywords as attack vector; QR-in-email phishing is common for bypassing email link filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing embedded QR codes (image-scanning or email parser rule). Track URL redirects from QR-decoders to known phishing/credential-harvesting domains. Flag if redirect domain is newly registered or typosquatted variant.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration - FIFA/World Cup Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatting explicitly in keywords; World Cup 2026 provides high-value domain variants for infrastructure impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and passive DNS feeds for one-character or homoglyph variants of FIFA, World Cup, and critical infrastructure domains (broadcast, stadium, ticketing, security ops). Flag domains with WHOIS registration ≤30 days prior to campaign.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Execution - Post-Compromise Impact
suggestion.rationale: Wiper malware explicitly in keywords; suggests destructive post-breach payload targeting critical infrastructure tied to World Cup operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wiper malware execution patterns: raw disk/partition access (IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY), mass file deletion with MftZero, or known wiper process signatures. Monitor for sudden file deletion activity mass-deleting critical volumes post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Multi-Actor Coordination Targeting World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Four distinct threat actors named (Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra, Razing Ursa) suggest coordinated or parallel campaigns; article likely analyzes shared targeting or TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing, infrastructure reconnaissance, and social-engineering attempts across geographies/networks by attacker alias. Flag if multiple actor-attributed campaigns target same infrastructure owner or ticketing/broadcast platforms within 7-day window.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Beacon from Compromised Stadium/Broadcast Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: High-severity article focused on World Cup attack surface suggests C2 infrastructure risk; critical infrastructure compromise would enable live-event disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous outbound connections from stadium/broadcast networks to known or suspected C2 IP ranges. Flag encrypted DNS queries (DoH/DoT) or DNS tunneling from critical infrastructure segments post-phishing compromise.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Permission Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is a privilege escalation detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK packages requesting BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission combined with subsequent elevation-of-privilege indicators. Flag apps requesting accessibility access that then modify system settings, hide their own icons, or capture screen content without explicit user approval per session.

suggestion.title: Fake Google Play Portal Access and APK Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' and 'BTMOB is distributed via phishing websites masquerading as streaming services and cryptocurrency mining platforms.' Initial access vector missing from detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic to domains spoofing Google Play Store (*.google.com lookalikes, play.google lookalikes, playstore-like domains). Correlate with APK downloads from non-Google Play domains. Flag Telegram clickthrough patterns matching known BTMOB campaign templates.

suggestion.title: MaaS Payload Builder Activity - High-Volume Custom APK Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'APK builder included in the offer provides easy customization of the payload without any need to code' and 'rapid generation of new payloads can undermine the effectiveness of single-layered defenses.' The high churn of APK variants suggests infrastructure access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file system activity consistent with APK templating/compilation (dex file generation, manifest manipulation, repackaging tools like apktool, aapt invocations). Monitor for parallel compilation of multiple similar Android packages with identical base behavior but variant C2 or phishing lure references.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception Intent Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'intercepting financial transactions' and 'stealing specific data.' Monitor for Android payment/banking hook APIs being invoked by non-banking apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-banking APKs requesting permissions for payment API interception (android.permission.BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN combined with financial app targeting). Flag unexpected hooks to Google Pay, Samsung Pay, or banking app package names. Monitor for screen capture events during financial app foreground time.

suggestion.title: App Icon Hiding and Persistence Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device, or prevent sleep mode.' Indicates defense evasion tactics requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-installation manifest modifications or runtime AppOps changes that hide launcher icons (FLAG_SYSTEM, PackageManager.setComponentEnabledSetting to COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED). Correlate with BOOT_COMPLETED receivers that re-enable hidden apps. Flag apps with 0 launch intents but active background services.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Campaign Variant Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'researchers spotted BTMOB campaigns that used an Argentinian government agency as a lure' and 'helps operators generate custom, localized phishing lures to match the campaign's topic.' Suggests detection of geographically-targeted lure variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster phishing messages by lure template similarity (government agencies, financial institutions, streaming services, crypto platforms mentioned in article). Flag campaigns with identical APK delivery infrastructure but localized social engineering (Argentina government, Brazil banking, etc.). Correlate with BTMOB technical signatures in reverse-engineered payloads.

suggestion.title: Git repository mass-clone or push activity with data exfiltration patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'exfiltrate source code'—git operations are the direct mechanism. Article topic (trusted dev tooling) strongly implies git/GitHub abuse as primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git clone, git push, or git pull operations with large data volumes or targeting external repositories. Flag when system account or unexpected user initiates repository export. Alert on git credentials being passed as CLI arguments or environment variables.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting from developer configuration files and IDE storage
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'secrets' exfiltration. Trusted dev tooling (IDEs, git clients, CI/CD tools) routinely cache API keys, tokens, SSH keys in dotfiles and config directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.git/config, ~/.docker/config.json, and IDE credential stores (.vscode, .idea). Alert when non-standard processes (shell, archive tools, curl, scp) access these paths. Track environment variable reads for AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.

suggestion.title: Archive or bulk export of source code repositories by dev tooling
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 'source code' (plural or large volume) requires staging—attackers would archive or tar repositories for efficient exfil. Trusted dev tooling includes tar, zip, git archive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when compression utilities (tar, zip, 7z, rar) or git archive commands create archives >50MB in developer directories. Flag archive creation followed immediately by copy to shared drives, cloud storage, or exfil endpoints. Monitor for --include-secrets or similar repo-export flags.

suggestion.title: Trusted developer tool process spawning shell or network utilities for data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via dev tooling often involve trusted process (git.exe, devenv.exe, dotnet.exe) as parent for curl, powershell, or ssh—defense evasion via process legitimacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git, IDE, or build-tool processes (dotnet, gradle, maven, npm) spawning curl, wget, powershell, cmd, or ssh with exfil-like arguments (out-of-process downloads, reverse shells, archive transfer). Flag mismatches between parent tool purpose and child activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious git or package manager credential injection or supply-chain compromise indicators
suggestion.rationale: Title implies attackers 'abuse' tooling—implies compromise of tool binary, config, or plugin layer, not just misuse. Should detect modified/unexpected git hooks, package manager repositories, or CI/CD pipeline injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .git/hooks, npm package.json scripts, Maven pom.xml plugin sections, GitHub Actions workflows for unexpected execute permissions or network-calling entries. Alert on git config remote URL changes or unexpected SSH key material in repo history.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration of source code or secrets via developer tool outbound connections
suggestion.rationale: Attack concludes with 'exfiltrate'—requires outbound network transmission. Dev tooling legitimately makes HTTP/SSH connections; must baseline and alert on anomalies (unusual IPs, domains, ports, volumes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of git, npm, pip, docker, and CI/CD tool outbound connections (repos, registries, cloud providers). Alert when git client connects to non-standard domain or port. Flag large data volume over non-standard exfil channels (HTTPS POST to unusual destination, SSH to non-repo host). Monitor for credential strings in exfil traffic.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as initial attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero vulnerability indicators or Marimo-specific exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Marimo instances for exploitation attempts: POST requests with malicious cell code injection, file traversal patterns in notebook parameters, or version-detection queries. Establish baseline for legitimate Marimo cell execution traffic and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation' but no use cases generated for detecting LLM framework instantiation, execution, or inference calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of LLM libraries/frameworks (LangChain, Autogen, LlamaIndex imports, `ollama`, `llama-cpp-python` process spawns). Flag Python interpreters or shell contexts that import and instantiate LLM agent classes, especially in post-compromise context following vulnerability exploitation.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative centers on 'LLM Agent' for post-exploitation operations, implying LLM-crafted commands for lateral movement or data collection, but no detection rule for anomalous command patterns typical of LLM output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal command syntax and flag combinations; flag commands with unusual orderings, rare flag combinations, uncommon tool chaining, or verbose/redundant arguments suggestive of LLM generation. Detect commands executed via Python `subprocess`, `os.system`, or shell invocations initiated by LLM runtime.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Marimo Notebook Modification
suggestion.rationale: Marimo is a Python notebook tool; post-exploitation likely involves executing payloads within notebook cells or persisting via modified notebooks, but pipeline did not surface notebook-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation and modification of `.py` files in Marimo app directories or notebook output caches. Detect Marimo processes spawning unexpected child processes (shells, interpreters, network utilities). Flag file writes from Marimo processes to startup/scheduled task locations or shared library directories.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Salesforce bulk data export by compromised user
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance'—bulk enumeration and export from breached account is core collection pattern pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce for bulk record exports from single user session (>100k records in <1 hour), API calls returning large result sets, or repeated SOQL queries with LIMIT clauses suggesting systematic harvesting. Correlate with anomalous Entra login (geolocation, time-of-day, device).

suggestion.title: Voice phishing targeting privileged cloud identity accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' via 'voice phishing (vishing) attack'—vishing targeting cloud identity infrastructure is foundational initial-access pattern with zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound calls to employees with subsequent Entra sign-in anomalies (atypical location, device, time) or MFA bypass attempts within minutes. Flag when Entra logs show legitimate-looking but temporally correlated unusual access within 2 hours of reported inbound call.

suggestion.title: Compromised cloud identity pivoting to enterprise SaaS platform
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'used this access' (Entra account) to 'steal 42 million records from...Salesforce'—lateral movement from identity provider to SaaS application requires cross-platform correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra sign-ins from risky/impossible-travel locations immediately preceding Salesforce OAuth grants or API authentication. Flag when identity performs data access (record exports, API pagination) inconsistent with role or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Large-scale data exfiltration over web service to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site'—exfiltration of stolen enterprise data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted tunnels or web connections from compromised identity with large byte transfers (multi-GB of data). Flag attempts to reach Tor exit nodes or anomalous HTTPS SNI patterns. Correlate with Salesforce data access patterns in preceding hours.

suggestion.title: Threat-actor leak site enumeration and attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility' and posted data to 'their dark web leak site'—visibility into threat-actor operational patterns and victim data exposure requires proactive leak site monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning of ShinyHunters leak site and associated channels for presence of Charter customer records. Alert on new leak posts containing customer PII (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses). Index leaked data schema and sample records against HIBP for victim notification prioritization.

suggestion.title: Ransomware/extortion group operational attribution via communication artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters 'told BleepingComputer that they breached' and demanded ransom—extortion communications contain threat-actor operational TTPs and signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ransom notes, extortion emails, dark web leak-site posts for linguistic markers, ransom demand structures, and victim-specific metadata. Correlate with known ShinyHunters communication patterns (formatting, payment instructions, public disclosure timelines). Flag rapid progression from breach to extortion demand (<72h) as signature of this group.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL Injection into ChatGPT Web Summaries
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface'—clear indication of injection-based phishing delivery. No use cases were generated despite this explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious URLs or HTML injection payloads embedded in ChatGPT API responses and web summary outputs. Monitor for user clicks on ChatGPT-originating links to known phishing/credential-harvest domains. Alert on obfuscated URLs within ChatGPT context.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability-specific attack requires detection of malicious payloads targeting the web summary feature. No technical attack reconstruction or API-level indicators were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify payloads in ChatGPT API requests attempting HTML/JavaScript/URL injection into summary endpoints. Alert on error responses indicative of exploitation probing. Detect API rate anomalies or repeated malformed requests to summary feature.

suggestion.title: Credential Capture Following ChatGPT Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attack chain logically progresses to credential harvesting; pipeline did not model downstream collection/impact phases or establish secondary indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ChatGPT access with subsequent traffic to spoofed login pages or credential-capture infrastructure. Alert on failed login attempts or anomalous geographic logins post-phishing interaction. Monitor for browser credential-store access after ChatGPT context shift.

suggestion.title: Malicious Installer Download from Spoofed Portal Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'offers both macOS and Windows downloads that install malware' from cloaked site 'impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal.' Delivery mechanism and file execution must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .exe/.dmg executables downloaded from domains impersonating legitimate software vendors (openai, anthropic, etc.) that do not resolve to official infrastructure. Correlate with subsequent installer execution from %TEMP% or %DOWNLOADS%.

suggestion.title: VM Detection Execution from Recently Downloaded Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Malware performs defense evasion checks post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process execution patterns typical of VM detection (WMI queries for guest OS, registry reads for Hyper-V/VMware artifacts, CPUID execution, /proc/cpuinfo parsing) spawned from recently-downloaded installers or from %TEMP% directories.

suggestion.title: Cloaked Malware Distribution Site Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' Differential content delivery based on User-Agent or context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS requests to suspicious domains that serve executable payloads only to non-security User-Agents (not Googlebot, URLScan, curl, etc.). Use threat intelligence on openew[.]app and pattern-match similar domain registration (registered post-campaign date, domains impersonating SaaS vendors).

suggestion.title: Malicious Content Download from AI Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com' and 'Claude Artifacts...to host ClickFix-style lures.' Users execute or download content from legitimate platform share URLs that host attacker payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file downloads initiated from chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai artifact share URLs (legitimate domains, but abused as hosting). Flag executable or script downloads from these links. Cross-reference with execution events on downloaded files.

suggestion.title: Google Ads Redirect to Malicious Share URL Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com.' Attacker leverages legitimate ad network to seed credential harvesting and malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for click chains: Google Ads domain → redirect via goog\.xxx → landing on chatgpt\.com/s/* with unusual query parameters or path indicators. Correlate with searches for 'ChatGPT download' or 'ChatGPT outage' and check for fake outage messaging in rendered page.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Outage Message Rendering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: Attackers created 'fake outage notice...rendered through ChatGPT itself' claiming 'website is temporarily unavailable' to drive users to malicious download. Social engineering vector embedded in legitimate platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outage or service-status lures served from legitimate AI platform share URLs (chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts). Signature match on phrases like 'temporarily unavailable,' 'high traffic,' combined with 'download desktop app' CTA. Flag if subsequent network activity includes downloads from non-official domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as the attack outcome. Pipeline missed the lateral-movement/impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN gateway logs for connection attempts immediately following failed or suspicious auth events on PAN-OS. Look for new or anomalous source IPs establishing VPN tunnels, particularly if correlated with CVE-2026-0257 scanner hits or auth-bypass signatures.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts Against PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'authentication bypass' per article. No detection for malformed or unauthenticated requests attempting to establish admin/service sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS authentication logs for failed login attempts followed by successful session establishment without credential submission, or HTTP 401/403 responses followed by successful requests to restricted endpoints. Flag if source IP is external or non-whitelisted.

suggestion.title: Unpatched PAN-OS Instance Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due-date 2026-06-01 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Asset-exposure hunt template is referenced but no specific UC for vulnerability scanning CVE-2026-0257.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-0257 against PAN-OS device inventory. Flag any instance running affected PAN-OS versions without documented patches applied before 2026-06-01 due date.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS External Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is the mapped technique; pipeline should surface detection for externally-reachable PAN-OS management interfaces or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PAN-OS management ports (443, 8081, 10.x admin interfaces) reachable from internet-facing network boundaries. Correlate with open-port scan results and threat-intel feeds. Priortize instances without WAF or VPN-gating.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '200 servers used to host the infrastructure' controlling '17 million infected devices to carry out cyberattacks.' No detection logic for outbound C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices establishing persistent outbound connections to infrastructure IP sets with C2 behavioral traits: small set of destination IPs, non-standard ports, regular beacon intervals. Correlate residential/IoT device networks with known proxy infrastructure. Alert on mass connection initiation from single command vector.

suggestion.title: Default Credential Exploitation on Network Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation: 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong'—implying initial compromise vector was unchanged defaults on network devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor successful logins using known default credential pairs (admin/admin, root/123456, etc.) on routers, NAS, and IoT admin interfaces. Alert on rapid failed-then-succeeded attempts on non-standard admin ports. Cross-reference successful default-cred logins with subsequent suspicious process execution or network behavior.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Residential Proxy Egress Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article: Asocks provides 'residential and mobile proxies'—botnet exploits consumer IP ranges for DDoS and malicious proxying. 'Companies, tablets, and smartphones' were commandeered for 'cyberattacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect consumer ISP-ranged IPs with unusual egress volume, connection velocity, or targeting patterns (same-second connections to 1000+ unique destinations, HTTP floods to known DDoS targets). Flag SOCKS5/HTTP CONNECT tunneling from residential devices. Alert on rapid IP rotation within proxy pools.

suggestion.title: Firmware Currency and Vulnerable Device Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'latest firmware update has been applied' is primary mitigation. Implies botnet prevalence on devices running outdated firmware with exploitable bugs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all network-accessible devices and flag firmware versions older than 12 months or with published critical CVEs (cross-reference NVD). Trend firmware recency by device class and ISP. Correlate out-of-date devices with C2 communication or botnet indicators. Alert on firmware downgrades.

suggestion.title: Exposed Remote Administration Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote administration panels are disabled when not needed.' Indicates devices exposed SSH/Telnet/HTTP admin endpoints to internet, allowing initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for and alert on inbound WAN connections to standard admin ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 8080, 3389, 5900) on consumer devices. Flag successful admin logins from external/residential IP sources. Detect port-scan patterns targeting admin ports across device clusters.

suggestion.title: Mass Worm/Botnet Propagation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: '17 million infected devices' and 'owners... did not knowingly participate.' Suggests rapid automated propagation, not consent-based.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect identical file hashes written to hundreds of devices within short time windows. Monitor for suspicious process spawning from network services (SMB, UPnP, HTTP). Alert on lateral movement initiation from compromised devices toward new targets. Flag rapid propagation vectors (SMB worm, peer-to-peer replication).

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Code with Known Vulnerable Dependency Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states '65–70% of production code is now generated by AI, and nearly half of it contains exploitable vulnerabilities.' This describes code commits with predictable vulnerability signatures, detectable via dependency tree fingerprinting and known-bad SCA patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repository commits for AI-generated code markers (copilot, Claude, etc.) coupled with dependency manifests matching known-vulnerable SCA profiles. Correlate commit timestamps with AI assistant activity logs to detect staged vulnerable code deployment.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Batch Dependency Upgrade Campaigns
