suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JWT signing key defaults to hardcoded "dev-secret-change-me", allowing token forgery for any user'. Direct detection of attacker creating valid JWTs with the known secret should be pursued via application logs showing cryptographic library calls or token validation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JWT token claims that mismatch the issuing service, or for rapid-succession token generation/validation cycles from external sources. Flag tokens signed with 'dev-secret-change-me' if cryptographic logs are available.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV=dev Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'A safety check exists but only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != "dev"; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is "dev"'. Configuration audit should detect deployments where PLATFORM_ENV is explicitly set to 'dev' or entirely unset in production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for praisonai_platform processes with PLATFORM_ENV unset or set to 'dev' in production namespaces/accounts. Flag as misconfiguration allowing default hardcoded secret.

suggestion.title: Cross-Workspace User Impersonation via Token Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token forgery 'for any user'. Detect cases where a single API token/source claims multiple conflicting user identities across workspace boundaries, or where token claims diverge from IAM mappings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API requests from same source IP/API client claiming different user_id claims across multiple workspace endpoints. Anomalous if user identities are not typically shared cross-workspace.

suggestion.title: Workspace member role enumeration before escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can promote 'themselves or others to owner'—attackers first need to discover valid user_ids and current role structure. Detect GET requests to /workspaces/{id}/members or /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} from authenticated sessions immediately before PATCH attempts to the same endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GET requests to membership endpoints (200 responses) followed within 5 minutes by PATCH requests from the same src/user. High volume of GETs before any PATCH suggests reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Failed role escalation attempts (403/401 on PATCH)
suggestion.rationale: If the application includes any validation, attackers may trigger 403/401 before finding a working endpoint or user_id combination. Detect repeated failed PATCH attempts to /members/{user_id} with 403/401 status from the same src.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ≥3 PATCH requests to /workspaces/*/members/* with status 401 or 403 from the same src/user within 10 minutes, followed by a 200/204—indicates role-change probing.

suggestion.title: Newly-elevated workspace owner making API calls to previously-inaccessible endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1213, T1530—post-escalation data access. Correlate a successful role-change PATCH (UC_4_2) with subsequent API calls to admin-only or elevated-privilege endpoints the requester did not previously access (e.g., /workspaces/{id}/settings, /workspaces/{id}/audit_logs, /workspaces/{id}/members with write methods).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful PATCH to /members/{user_id} with role→owner. Then validate whether that user_id made requests to elevated endpoints in the 15 minutes post-change. Use baseline API call profiles per user to flag anomalous resource access.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via newly-promoted owner account (cross-workspace abuse)
suggestion.rationale: Once escalated to owner in one workspace, attacker may use that access token/session to target other workspaces. Detect when a user who recently gained owner role in workspace A immediately accesses or modifies workspace B.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authenticated API calls from a user within 30 minutes of a role-change PATCH if the user is accessing a workspace_id different from the one where the escalation occurred.

suggestion.title: Workspace ownership change cascade (bulk re-role after escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: attacker escalates self to owner, then demotes legitimate owners and promotes accomplices. Detect when a newly-escalated owner immediately issues multiple PATCH requests changing other users' roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate a PATCH that grants owner role to user A with subsequent PATCHes from user A to /members/{other_user_id} within 15 minutes. Aggregate by workspace to detect bulk ownership consolidation.

suggestion.title: Session/auth token anomalies post-escalation (if SaaS provides session logs)
suggestion.rationale: Some platforms log token generation or session elevation. Article vulnerability allows privilege escalation without logout/re-auth. Detect elevated-permission API tokens issued to a user without corresponding auth/login events immediately prior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If auth logs exist, flag API tokens or sessions with elevated scope (owner-level) that were NOT generated by an explicit re-authentication event (login, MFA challenge, token refresh with privilege escalation). Indicates in-band privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Disable or Bypass Pre-Commit Security Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'forces the research right there while it's in front of you' via custom pre-commit hooks. Detection should monitor for developers circumventing these controls ('git commit --no-verify', environment variable overrides, hook removal) which would indicate an attempt to skip mandatory security scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for --no-verify flags in git commits, deletion of .git/hooks files, or environment variable overrides (GIT_HOOKS_SKIP, etc.) that would bypass pre-commit security scanning. Correlate with code commits that introduce known vulnerable patterns.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Spearphishing Link Click from Suspicious Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'LinkedIn social engineering' as attack vector; no detection for malicious links from fabricated/compromised LinkedIn profiles leading to download pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users clicking LinkedIn message links pointing to attacker-controlled domains. Correlate newly created/compromised LinkedIn profiles with bulk user connections and suspicious URL click patterns. Monitor for URL shorteners or redirect chains from LinkedIn to non-LinkedIn domains hosting file downloads.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Binary Execution from Downloads Folder
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom macOS malware deployment' without specifying execution detection; user downloads payload via LinkedIn and executes it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned binaries or scripts from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or email attachments. Prioritize parent processes like Finder, bash, or zsh spawning processes with non-standard code signatures or no signature verification.

suggestion.title: macOS LaunchAgent Persistence Registration
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware typically establishes persistence via launchd agents or launch daemons; article implies long-term compromise but no persistence detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons for .plist files containing suspicious executable paths. Correlate with process creation of launchd spawning previously-unknown binaries or shell scripts.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployed malware but provides no C2 IOCs; behavioral detection of malware reaching out to attacker infrastructure is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from user-writable directories making repeated outbound HTTPS connections to low-reputation domains or IPs on non-standard ports. Correlate with timing patterns suggesting heartbeat or tasking behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Shell Command Injection via AppleScript
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware frequently abuses osascript and shell interpreters for command execution; article mentions custom malware but execution mechanism was not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag osascript or shell (bash/zsh) execution with base64-encoded commands, inline script payloads, or suspicious function calls. Parent process should be unusual (not Terminal, IDE, or admin tools).

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Remote Access Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly cites 'VS Code Tunnels' as expanded arsenal. This is T1219 (remote-access software) abuse for unauthorized persistence. Pipeline generated zero detections for tunnel creation or anomalous code process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code.exe or CodeServer launching with --tunnel or tunnel-related CLI arguments, or unexpected tunnel.exe variants. Monitor for tunnel listener sockets on non-developer machines. Correlate with lateral-movement timeframes or off-hours process spawns.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Proxy Listener Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'HTTPSpy' as deployed tool. This is an HTTPS/HTTP proxy for traffic interception and credential harvesting (T1557, T1040). No detection rule for proxy bind operations or HTTPSpy process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPSpy binary creation/execution by hash or name; monitor for netstat/netsh rules creating local proxy listeners on ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443. Flag processes modifying WinINet proxy settings or installing root certificates in SYSTEM certificate store.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Backdoor Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'HelloDoor' as component of Kimsuky toolkit. Name pattern suggests backdoor; no detection rules generated for this implant's startup mechanisms, process spawning, or persistence indicators (T1547, T1574).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HelloDoor binary execution and registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU RunOnce, Run, or Services keys. Flag anomalous scheduled tasks, startup folder additions, or WMI event subscriptions created shortly after HelloDoor spawn. Baseline legitimate Hello* processes first.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Multi-Tool Deployment Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes orchestrated deployment of three distinct tools. Pipeline produced zero kill-chain reconstruction despite clear progression: initial access → tool deployment (execution) → persistence setup → C2 activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent-child process chains: suspicious interpreters (powershell, cmd, cscript) spawning legitimate tools (code.exe, svchost) with non-standard arguments. Alert on rapid sequential spawning of multiple tools within 5 minutes. Establish baselines for legitimate tool deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Traffic Exfiltration via HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: HTTPSpy as proxy explicitly handles data interception and exfiltration. Article positions it as C2 infrastructure component. No detection for HTTPS traffic anomalies, unusual port usage, or certificate pinning bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTPS egress per user/workstation. Alert on: high-volume HTTPS to rare destinations, HTTPS to non-standard ports (8443, 8880, 9443), missing SNI headers, self-signed certificates, or TLS version downgrades. Correlate with HTTPSpy process uptime.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Reconnaissance Post-Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Expanded toolkit implies reconnaissance phases. Title does not detail discovery activities, but APT toolkits always include initial enumeration (T1082, T1087). Pipeline's empty kill chain fails to surface this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-compromise discovery: whoami, net user, systeminfo, tasklist, ipconfig spawned shortly after tool deployment. Alert on LDAP queries targeting user/computer objects, registry enumeration of network adapters or installed software, or file-system enumeration of sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation Mimic Legitimate Library
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package impersonates 'Sicoob SDK'—the delivery mechanism is a trojanized package designed to fool developers. 'Malicious NuGet Package as Sicoob SDK' establishes initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect nuget.exe or dotnet.exe installing packages with names typosquatting legitimate libraries (e.g., 'Sicoob.SDK', 'sicoob-sdk' vs legitimate), from newly-registered NuGet feeds, or with mismatched publisher metadata. Correlate with developer machines or build infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from .NET Process Post-Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the package 'exfiltrates banking passwords'. Detection must capture credential access and exfil from processes executing NuGet-loaded assemblies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from .NET runtime (dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe child processes) that enumerate credentials (LSASS access, browser store queries, Windows Credential Manager), then immediately open TCP/443 connections to non-whitelisted domains within 30s window.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Anomalous .NET Assembly in Package Cache
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized NuGet packages contain malicious .dll files. Detect when package installation downloads result in unsigned, recently-modified, or hash-mismatched assemblies vs. official vendor repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor %USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages and %ProgramData%\NuGet\Cache for .dll files with missing or invalid digital signatures, creation timestamps post-installation, or hashes not in NuGet.org official manifest. Correlate with process execution from same directory.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning or Code Execution from NuGet Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: The malicious assembly must execute to steal credentials. Detect when NuGet-cached assemblies directly spawn processes, load modules, or invoke unmanaged code (T1559 alternatives, P/Invoke).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes are spawned from dotnet.exe with parent in .nuget\packages path, or when processes in that path load native .dll files (kernel32.dll, advapi32.dll calls for credential/registry access). Monitor for CLR profiler hooks or reflection-based code generation.

suggestion.title: Registry or File Modification by Package-Loaded Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages often establish persistence or disable security controls. Detect registry/file writes from NuGet-spawned processes to sensitive hives (HKLM\SYSTEM, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HKLM or HKCU registry writes to Run, RunOnce, Startup, or security-related keys (Windows Defender, UAC bypass) from processes spawned by dotnet.exe. Track file system writes to system directories (System32, Program Files).

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band HTTP Exfiltration with Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies banking passwords are exfiltrated—network telemetry should show credential-sized data (typically <10KB per request) sent to attacker C2 infrastructure with POST/PUT methods characteristic of stealer beacons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) POST/PUT requests from dotnet.exe child processes or processes in NuGet cache to non-whitelisted, newly-registered, or geographically-anomalous domains. Alert on payloads containing URL-encoded strings matching credential patterns or encryption headers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet/npm Package Installation with Unexpected Child Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'malicious Sicoob NuGet steals banking credentials' — package installation is the initial compromise vector; malicious code executes post-install
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet.exe or npm installation processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or NET-based utilities within 5s of install completion. Baseline legitimate post-install tasks; alert on deviations accessing credential stores or system binaries.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Access via Malicious Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'steals banking credentials' — suggests keylogging, memory access, or credential-store enumeration triggered by package code execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by NuGet/npm contexts accessing HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\PasswordLess or browser credential databases. Detect API calls from package code to Windows credential manager or keylogging libraries.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Exfiltration from npm Package Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'npm packages target cloud secrets' — suggests install scripts exfiltrate environment variables or .env files containing cloud/API keys
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install script execution for file reads of .env, config.json, and environment variable access (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GCP_CREDENTIALS, AZURE_TOKEN patterns) followed by outbound network connections to non-NPM-registry hosts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Name Typosquatting / Publisher Impersonation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Sicoob NuGet' — supply-chain attacks often use name-squatting (e.g., 'Sicoob-Helper' vs 'SicoobHelper'). Pipeline should flag similar package names and publisher mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference project dependency files (packages.config, .csproj, package.json, package-lock.json) against a baseline of known-legitimate Sicoob packages. Alert on Levenshtein-distance typosquats (edit distance ≤2) or publisher name changes.

suggestion.title: Staged Payload Execution: Package Install Writes Executable to Temp
suggestion.rationale: Banking-credential stealers typically stage payloads. Article implies multi-stage: package → credstealer executable → exfil. Look for temporary file creation.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Package-Spawned Process to External Domains
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealers require exfiltration channel. Article context suggests attacker infrastructure C2. Monitor for egress from package contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and TCP/HTTPS connections from processes spawned by package installers to non-mainstream hosting (non-CDN, suspicious ASN, newly registered domains, no known reputation).

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Threat Actor Attribution Detection

Monitor for AI-obfuscated payload delivery mechanisms targeting Ukraine-based organizations.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Content Detection (Ukraine-Targeting)

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation Executing with SYSTEM Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task'—a direct attack primitive. Pipeline failed to surface detection for privilege-escalated scheduled task execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation where the task principal runs as SYSTEM but the scheduling process lacks admin privileges. Detect schtasks.exe or At.exe with /RU SYSTEM and /SC triggers pointing to encryption-capable executables.

suggestion.title: Privilege Elevation to SYSTEM Preceding Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly links 'Elevated Privileges' to encryption: 'Encrypt Local Drives With Elevated Privileges.' Pipeline failed to map privilege escalation technique as prerequisite to impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process elevation chains where a non-SYSTEM parent gains SYSTEM context, then immediately performs bulk file operations indicative of encryption (seek patterns, high-entropy writes to multiple file extensions).

suggestion.title: Encryption Activity Originating from Scheduled Task Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: scheduled task runs encryption. Pipeline did not generate use case for impact-phase detection linking scheduled task execution to crypto/ransomware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file write/modification activity from process trees rooted in Task Scheduler (taskeng.exe, svchost.exe with scheduled task context), especially targeting common data directories and multiple file extensions in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Parent-Child Process: Task Scheduler Spawning Encryption Routines
suggestion.rationale: Article describes scheduled task as execution vector for ransomware encryption. Pipeline did not generate detection for process spawning from scheduled task context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by taskeng.exe or Task Scheduler with command lines matching obfuscation patterns, unusual extensions, or known ransomware CLI signatures. Baseline expected scheduled task children in your environment first.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to ChatGPT/Gemini APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers "leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks"—pipeline missed the C&C and tool-abuse vector. Need detection for known threat actor infrastructure accessing AI service APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls to OpenAI ChatGPT or Google Gemini endpoints originating from known GREYVIBE infrastructure or anonymization services. Alert on unusual API patterns (high volume, rapid-fire requests, non-standard headers).

suggestion.title: Malware/Payload Generation via Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers using AI to "fuel cyberattacks"—directly implies code generation and weaponization. Detection should flag attempts to extract working exploits or malware via AI service prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious prompts submitted to ChatGPT/Gemini APIs requesting malware code, evasion techniques, or exploit payloads. Monitor AI-generated responses for markdown code blocks matching known attack frameworks (Metasploit, Cobalt Strike, etc.).

suggestion.title: Credential/Confidential Data Exfiltration via AI Services
suggestion.rationale: Attackers leveraging AI tools typically abuse them for data processing and exfiltration. Article implies broader attack lifecycle; missing detection for stolen data being submitted to AI services for analysis/refinement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag uploads of confidential file content (passwords, API keys, PII, source code) to ChatGPT or Gemini APIs. Correlate against DLP signals and suspicious account access patterns preceding the upload.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Threat Actor Reconnaissance via AI Chatbots
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on GREYVIBE as named actor; pipeline extracted zero actor IOCs. Need baseline detection for threat actor accounts probing AI services for social engineering, phishing template generation, or target research.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ChatGPT/Gemini accounts submitting reconnaissance-oriented prompts (target profiling, organizational structure, employee lists, security tool identification). Correlate account creation metadata (IP, registration patterns) against known GREYVIBE IOCs.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise — AI Service Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: "GREYVIBE Hackers Leverage..."—implies stolen or compromised credentials for AI services used in attack campaigns. Pipeline should detect credential stuffing or session hijacking against OpenAI/Google accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed/successful logins to ChatGPT or Gemini from geographically impossible locations, non-standard clients, or IPs previously flagged as GREYVIBE infrastructure. Correlate with multi-factor authentication bypass signals.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared AI Service Sessions
suggestion.rationale: High-severity campaign suggests multi-stage attack; shared or stolen AI service credentials could be pivot point between compromised environments and attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sessions in ChatGPT/Gemini originating from both internal networks and known external threat actor IPs. Flag credential sharing (same account used from incompatible networks within short time intervals).

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Non-Standard Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dependency confusion campaign leveraged 33 malicious npm packages' — attacker-controlled packages were installed by legitimate developers. Detection should flag installations where package version resolution unexpectedly favors public npm registry over private feeds or where package metadata mismatches repository origin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/yarn add operations for packages with recently-created versions, mismatched maintainers, or zero prior downloads. Correlate package installations with subsequent process execution from node_modules. Flag rapid installation-to-execution patterns in build environments.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and System Information Collection from Dev Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'malicious packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments' indicates reconnaissance phase. Detection must identify environment discovery patterns (reading PATH, HOME, NODE_ENV, CI-specific vars) and subsequent OS fingerprinting (hostname, CPU, OS version queries).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js child processes invoking system commands (uname, whoami, env, cat /proc/cpuinfo, systeminfo, Get-ComputerInfo) within npm postinstall/preinstall hooks or package initialization. Alert on aggregation of >5 reconnaissance commands in <10 seconds from node_modules context.

suggestion.title: Outbound Data Exfiltration from npm Module Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Campaign 'collected reconnaissance data from developer and build environments' implies C2 callback or data exfiltration. Detection should surface unexpected HTTP/HTTPS or DNS queries initiated by Node.js processes running under build contexts (CI/CD agents, developer machines).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries or HTTP POST requests from npm/node processes to domains registered within 90 days, lack HTTPS/TLS cert reputation, or resolve to non-CDN IPs. Correlate with preceding environment enumeration within 5 minutes. Prioritize package.json modifications or postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: Package.json Tampering or Malicious postinstall/preinstall Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute code during install phase. Detection should identify package.json files with suspicious script entries or packages declaring unusual lifecycle hooks that perform reconnaissance or network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package.json in node_modules for postinstall/preinstall/install scripts containing obfuscated code, shell command chains, or network utilities (curl, wget, nc). Flag scripts that invoke shell interpreters or execute binaries not typically found in npm packages.

suggestion.title: Dependency Version Mismatch Detection — Lockfile Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion succeeds when package resolution prefers attacker-controlled version. Detection should identify scenarios where installed package version differs from package-lock.json specification or where semver ranges resolve to unexpected versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package.json and package-lock.json against actual installed node_modules versions. Alert on discrepancies, missing lock entries, or version downgrades. Correlate with npm registry queries for non-canonical package sources (verdaccio, private registries not in .npmrc).

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass - Failed→Successful Auth Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Authentication Bypass...Under Active Exploitation.' Core exploit pattern: attacker bypasses auth validation. Detection should flag authentication sequence anomalies—multiple failed attempts immediately followed by successful access from the same source. Article phrase: 'Authentication Bypass'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid (sub-minute) state transitions from authentication failure to successful login from identical source IP. Look for HTTP 401/403 responses to /ssl-vpn/ or GlobalProtect portal endpoints followed by successful session establishment (HTTP 200, session cookie issuance) within 60 seconds. Filter for external source IPs and exclude known admin IP ranges.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Portal - Unauthenticated Resource Access
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass CVE typically allows access to protected resources without valid credentials. Article: 'Authentication Bypass.' Should detect GET/POST requests to /ssl-vpn/*, /global-protect/*, or admin endpoints lacking proper authentication headers or bypassing pre-auth checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: GlobalProtect portal endpoints typically require auth tokens (session cookies, OAuth, SAML assertions). Alert on requests to protected endpoints (/admin, /api/v1, /global-protect/login, etc.) that either (a) omit authentication headers entirely, (b) repeat the CVE-2026-0257 exploitation pattern (path traversal, header injection, or specific bypass payloads once documented), or (c) return 200 OK when unauthenticated access should fail. Cross-reference against PAN-OS patch dates.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation mentioned in title. Once exploit POC/signature is published, should detect injection or evasion attempts targeting the specific bypass mechanism (e.g., request header manipulation, path encoding, URL parameter tampering in GlobalProtect login flow). Article: 'Under Active Exploitation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once the CVE-2026-0257 bypass technique is reverse-engineered (expected within 1–2 weeks of disclosure), monitor for canonical exploitation signatures: unusual header values in /ssl-vpn/ POST requests, double-encoded or null-byte path traversal attempts targeting auth checks, or specific parameter injection patterns. Alert on any HTTP request to GlobalProtect endpoints containing known bypass payloads or anomalous header combinations.

suggestion.title: Unusual GlobalProtect Session Establishment from Non-Compliant Clients
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass often exploits protocol weaknesses or client validation gaps. Should detect sessions originating from non-standard or spoofed GlobalProtect clients, or from clients that skip TLS certificate validation. Article: 'Authentication Bypass' implies weakness in client-server validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect session logs (auth.log, traffic.log) for client-user-agent anomalies, missing or invalid TLS certificates in initial handshake, or session tokens issued without a corresponding prior authentication handshake. Flag if session establishment occurs without standard GlobalProtect client negotiation sequence or if User-Agent headers are blank/spoofed (indicating possible raw socket exploitation).

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Lateral Movement from Exploited GlobalProtect Session
suggestion.rationale: Once bypass succeeds, attacker is inside network. Should detect anomalous internal network activity emanating from GlobalProtect VPN sessions, especially to sensitive hosts (domain controllers, file servers, backup systems). Article: 'Under Active Exploitation' implies post-initial-access activities will follow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly-established GlobalProtect sessions against internal network traffic in the following 5–60 minutes. Alert if traffic from a GlobalProtect-authenticated IP (via exploit) targets internal systems at higher-than-baseline rates, especially to ports 22, 3389, 445, 389 (AD enumeration), or database ports. Apply behavioral baseline: legitimate VPN users typically access a small set of known internal services; exploit pivots show broad or targeted scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Firewall Logging Evasion - Disabled/Altered Auth Logs
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated exploitation may tamper with audit logs to hide the authentication bypass attempt. Should detect deletion, rotation, or suppression of GlobalProtect authentication logs coinciding with the exploitation window. Article doesn't mention this, but is standard defense-evasion for critical VPN bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gaps in GlobalProtect authentication logs (timestamp jumps, missing sequential entries) or sudden log purges around the exploitation timestamp. Cross-check SIEM ingestion timelines against PAN-OS local log indices. Alert if auth.log entries for a given time window are unexpectedly sparse, or if PAN-OS administrative logs show log-clearance commands executed via non-standard accounts immediately before/after an authentication anomaly.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Abuse for Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'attackers abuse trusted developer tooling.' Pipeline extracted zero detection use cases despite this being the core attack vector. Need UC to detect unusual IDE, build system, or VCS usage patterns tied to bulk data movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected developer tools (VS Code, IntelliJ, git CLI) spawning high-volume file I/O or network transfers. Baseline normal IDE behavior, alert on deviations like bulk repo cloning, archive creation of source trees, or exfil via atypical network endpoints.

suggestion.title: Source Code Repository Exfiltration via Trusted Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'exfiltrate source code.' No UC generated for repo-level data leakage despite being a primary objective. Should detect repo cloning, bulk commits, or mass repository access in short windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk git clone/pull operations from legitimate developer accounts, especially outside business hours or from atypical IP space. Monitor for large data transfers from source control platforms tied to service account or credential spray sessions.

suggestion.title: Secrets and Credentials Exfiltration from Dev Environments
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'exfiltrate secrets.' Pipeline generated no UC for credential discovery or exfil from secret stores, config files, or environment dumps. Should detect .env file access, secret manager queries, or API key enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reads of .env, .git/config, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, or cloud credential files. Flag discovery of environment variables containing API keys, tokens, or certificates. Alert on secret manager API calls from dev tooling.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Trusted Package/Dependency Management
suggestion.rationale: Abuse of 'trusted developer tooling' likely includes package managers (npm, pip, Maven, NuGet). Pipeline surfaced zero supply-chain compromise IOCs or techniques. Should detect unauthorized package installation or repo manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager operations pulling from unusual registries, installing unsigned or mismatched versions, or dependency injection patterns. Correlate with sudden credential access or data staging post-install.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Developer Tools and Build Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Trusted developer tooling often has elevated privileges and cross-system access (CI/CD pipelines, build agents). No UC generated for lateral movement or privilege escalation via these channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect build agents or CI/CD runners initiating outbound connections to non-standard targets. Flag unusual RDP/SSH from developer machines to infrastructure. Monitor for build pipeline modifications that execute arbitrary code.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as attack vector; pipeline extracted nothing. Should detect execution attempts against this vulnerable software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to known Marimo endpoints with malicious payloads, or abnormal process spawning from Marimo runtime. Correlate with CVE-2026-39987 proof-of-concepts if available.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Spawned as Post-Exploitation Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—a novel attack pattern not covered. Pipeline ignored this entire attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected Python, Node.js, or inference runtime processes spawned from web application contexts (Marimo). Flag subprocess invocation chains where parent is non-standard or process arguments contain model, agent, or inference keywords.

suggestion.rationale: Title establishes LLM agent execution post-exploitation but pipeline generated zero use cases. Need to detect agent-driven malicious commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell, cmd.exe, or bash processes spawned without user-initiated terminal, or with arguments that appear generated/tokenized. Correlate parent process chain to Marimo or Python inference runtime.

Cross-correlate with helpdesk tickets and security incident reports mentioning social engineering.

Correlate with subsequent high-privilege API calls to Salesforce or bulk data access. Flag accounts with >5 failed MFA attempts in a 30min window followed by successful login.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Export / Mass Records Extraction

Flag unusual data export destinations, high-volume downloads via REST/SOAP APIs, or access to sensitive objects (accounts, contacts, opportunities) by service accounts or newly-created users.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Data Publication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site' after ransom refusal. Detection for company data appearing on underground forums/marketplaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest threat feeds monitoring ShinyHunters' known leak infrastructure and dark web markets for mentions of company name, domain, or employee email domains. Alert when Charter customer names, phone numbers, or addresses are identified in leaked datasets. Correlation with breach timeline enables impact assessment.

suggestion.title: Extortion Demand / Ransom Communication Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions ShinyHunters 'told BleepingComputer that they breached the company' and 'demanded ransom.' No detection for extortion communication or threat actor outreach to company or media.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsolicited emails from attacker-controlled domains claiming data exfiltration, containing proof-of-theft (sample customer records), or demanding payment. Monitor for threat actor social media posts, leak site announcements, or journalist outreach mentioning your organization by name.

suggestion.title: Service Principal / API Credential Abuse via Compromised Entra Account
suggestion.rationale: Compromised employee Entra account was leveraged to access Salesforce; attacker likely abused service principals or API tokens. No detection for lateral movement via cloud service credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service principals or managed identities authenticating via compromised human account credentials, or service principals generating new credentials/tokens and immediately using them for high-risk operations (Salesforce bulk queries). Flag app consent grants to suspicious Salesforce integrations post-breach timeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious URLs Embedded in ChatGPT Summary Responses
suggestion.rationale: Article title states vulnerability 'turns ChatGPT web summaries into a phishing surface'—core attack is phishing URLs delivered via summaries. Pipeline extracted zero use cases detecting this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API responses for embedded URLs. Cross-reference URLs against phishing/malware feeds. Alert when users interact with ChatGPT summary-sourced URLs that resolve to known phishing domains or trigger credential-entry events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous ChatGPT Web Summarization Requests
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages ChatGPT's summarize feature; no UC detects weaponized summarization patterns. Title implies attacker-controlled inputs to summary function are being exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT API calls requesting summaries of newly-registered, low-reputation, or known-phishing domains. Flag summarization patterns where output contains credential-solicitation language, fake login instructions, or obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Exploitation and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'ChatGPhish' vulnerability but pipeline extracted zero CVE/threat-identifier IOCs. Should detect exploitation attempts or PoC scanning of this specific flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT endpoints for known ChatGPhish payload signatures or exploitation indicators (e.g., malformed summarization requests, recursive/nested payloads, protocol-level fuzz attempts). Alert on unusual API error patterns consistent with vulnerability probing.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission Following ChatGPT Summary Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attack objective is credential harvesting; article states summaries become 'phishing surface' implying data exfiltration. No UC detects post-summary credential capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ChatGPT summary-interaction sessions with subsequent credential-entry events (login attempts to non-standard URLs, form submissions, password-manager triggers). Flag if credential submission follows within minutes of summary access.

suggestion.title: Fake AI Platform Outage Page Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake outage notice is rendered through ChatGPT itself' via 'custom HTML and CSS rendered by a ChatGPT prompt' published as shared link. Clear phishing lure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ChatGPT/Claude share links (chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts) in access logs containing outage-related keywords ('unavailable', 'high traffic', 'download desktop') with embedded download prompts. Correlate with suspicious downstream file downloads and ad referrers.

suggestion.title: Website Cloaking for Malware Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains serving different payloads by comparing proxy-intercepted HTML content against public scanning engine results (URLScan, PhishTank). Flag domains where benign/decoy content is returned to security scanners but malware pages served to real users based on HTTP headers or source IP classification.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted AI Vendor Installer Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' with malware-laden executables for macOS and Windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executable downloads from domains typosquatting official AI platforms (openai, anthropic, google, etc.). Flag non-standard TLDs, character substitutions, and homoglyphs for official installers. Correlate downloads with execution of anti-VM code or network beaconing.

suggestion.title: Virtual Machine Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine'—execution guardrails to evade analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VM detection logic in executables via process execution of CPUID, WMI hardware queries, registry checks for VMware/VirtualBox keys, or hardware enumeration commands following binary launch. Flag suspicious binaries that abort execution in sandbox environments.

suggestion.title: Google Ads Abuse to Malicious Shared Conversation Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com'—attacker-paid ads amplify reach to legitimate platform.

suggestion.rationale: Article: 'earlier campaigns abusing AI platform sharing features have distributed infostealers' and states payload is likely infostealer. Explicit connection between artifact abuse and credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect known infostealer signatures (Vidar, Beagle, RedLine) spawned from downloads sourced from AI platform share links or typosquatted domains. Monitor for credential store access, screenshot/clipboard utilities, and registry/file enumeration from unknown installers.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers to bypass security restrictions' and 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection'—pipeline should surface active-exploitation-attempt detection. No use cases generated despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS threat logs and IDS/IPS alerts for exploit signatures matching CVE-2026-0257. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to PAN-OS management interface (default ports 443, 10443) with HTTP 400/401/403 responses that indicate exploitation attempts. Correlate with subsequent successful authentication from same source.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment (PAN-OS)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as direct impact—authentication bypass enables VPN access. Pipeline generated no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new VPN user accounts created on PAN-OS without corresponding ticketing/provisioning records. suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Indicators

suggestion.title: Suspicious PAN-OS Management Interface Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful auth bypass enables attacker to reach admin functions—article implies post-exploitation admin panel access. Pipeline generated no post-compromise activity detection.

Alert on successful VPN connections followed by admin panel access.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Server Communication Detection

suggestion.title: Device Compromise via Default Credentials and Firmware Exploitation

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Service Abuse and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Asocks as 'universal proxy service' with '7 million IP addresses, 150 locations, 100,000 clients' used for 'malicious traffic proxying.' No detection use case addresses identifying abuse of residential proxy networks for command evasion or exfiltration.

Alert on data volume anomalies and repeated connections to residential proxy endpoints from otherwise-clean hosts.

suggestion.title: Botnet-Driven DDoS Attack Pattern Recognition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet used for 'distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Despite this clear impact activity, no detection for orchestrated attack traffic from compromised bot fleet was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric anomalies and distributed traffic originating from non-datacenter IP ranges associated with residential ISP netblocks. Detect characteristic DDoS patterns (HTTP floods, SYN floods, DNS amplification) with source diversity indicating botnet coordination. Correlate with DNS queries to suspicious C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Persistence and Autostart Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'infected devices' maintaining botnet membership across 17 million hosts, requiring persistent execution. No detection rule addresses identifying botnet autostart mechanisms or boot persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious entries in autostart locations (HKLM\Run, cron jobs, .bashrc modifications, systemd services) on systems not known to run those processes. Detect unsigned or renamed system utilities in boot paths. Monitor for post-compromise lateral execution triggering autostart installers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access Services Enabled
suggestion.rationale: Remediation guidance states 'remote administration panels are disabled when not needed,' indicating RDP, SSH, VNC or similar were left open enabling initial compromise. No detection captured this configuration oversight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit devices with open RDP (3389), SSH (22), Telnet (23), or VNC ports accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on successful remote connections using default or weak credentials. Monitor for service enablement via registry or config changes on systems without legitimate remote-access requirements.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Dependency Installation Detected by SCA Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Snyk is now detecting six vulnerabilities for every one remediated' and discusses supply-chain SCA issues as the primary attack vector. Organizations need baseline detection for when known-vulnerable packages enter the dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager operations (npm install, pip install, maven resolve) and lock-file changes. Alert when a package version appearing in dependency resolution has a public CVE entry with CVSS ≥5.0 and install timestamp is within 30 days of CVE publication, indicating likely-unpatched supply-chain pull.

suggestion.title: Bulk Automated Dependency Upgrades Indicative of Remediation Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly emphasizes 'remediation at scale' and autonomous fix loops. Bulk version bumps in dependency manifests within short timeframes are either legitimate remediation or supply-chain attack via dependency confusion. Baseline this activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when ≥5 distinct dependencies are upgraded in the same commit or PR within 30 minutes. Correlate commit author (e.g., service accounts, CI bot users) and message keywords ('snyk-fix', 'remediation', 'automated'). Flag as remediation if legitimate, or investigate for supply-chain backdoor if actor is unexpected.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Code Introducing Known-Vulnerable Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '65–70% of production code is now generated by AI, and nearly half of it contains exploitable vulnerabilities.' Defenders must detect when LLM-generated commits introduce detectable weakness signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git commits for authorship metadata or commit messages indicating AI generation ('Claude-assisted', 'Cursor', 'Copilot generated'). Cross-reference against SAST results: flag commits where code introduces CWEs (hardcoded credentials, weak crypto, SQL injection stubs) at higher-than-baseline density relative to human-authored baseline.

suggestion.title: Remediation PR Rejection or Reversion Indicating Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'PRs that introduce more issues than they solve' and discuss failed remediation loops. Repeated fix failures or deliberate reversions of security upgrades indicate either operational friction or active evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD logs for remediation PRs (detected by commit message or automated-fixer authorship) that fail validation, are closed without merge, or are reverted within 24 hours. Alert if the same vulnerability-remediation cycle repeats >2 times on the same package, suggesting either misconfiguration or deliberate bypass.

suggestion.title: Frontier Model API Calls for Unauthorized Code Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses embedding remediation into frontier-model contexts (Claude, frontier LLMs) within IDEs and CLI. Unauthorized or anomalous LLM API calls during development could indicate data exfiltration or malicious code suggestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound API calls to LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) from development environments. Alert on API calls containing code context or diff payloads outside approved code-review gates. Baseline legitimate /snyk-fix and IDE remediation calls; flag calls with unusual frequency, payload size, or from non-developer service accounts.

suggestion.title: vm2 Module Load Followed by Prototype Chain Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC explicitly chains require('vm2') with __lookupGetter__ / __lookupSetter__ access: 'By combining Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")...the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained.' This sequence is the attack. Should detect vm2 load in same process context as prototype-chain escapes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe processes where command line contains require('vm2') or 'vm2' module initialization, followed by child processes or inline script execution containing __proto__, __lookupGetter__, or __lookupSetter__ patterns in the same time window (within 5 seconds).

suggestion.title: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article mechanism: 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error' is leveraged to obtain TypeError constructor for escape. This is a specific error-handling abuse pattern that could be detected. Article explicitly states this in summary.
log_sources: ProcessCreation events with specific error handling
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe processes writing 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE' to stderr or application logs in sequences where Buffer.prototype manipulation precedes or follows. This error is abnormal in benign Node usage.

suggestion.title: Unsandboxed Code Execution via mainModule.require from vm2 Context
suggestion.rationale: Article detection rules explicitly flag 'mainModule.require' as a signature in both Splunk and KQL. This is the mechanism to break out of the sandbox and access host require(). Article: the escape allows 'run arbitrary code' via this path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution where node.exe/node processes spawn unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) AND command line or parent script contains 'mainModule.require' or 'mainModule.exports' patterns indicating sandbox context misuse.

suggestion.title: compileStreaming / Dynamic Code Compilation in Node VM Context
suggestion.rationale: Article's provided detection rules include 'compileStreaming' as a signature. This function is used in the sandbox-escape code path for dynamic compilation. Should detect this compilation technique in untrusted code paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe processes with 'compileStreaming' in command line or process memory/script content, especially when combined with vm2 module imports or untrusted input sources. This is an evasion technique for dynamic code execution.

suggestion.title: vm2 Package Installed on System with Vulnerable Version and Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vm2 as used by 'vm2' library users who expose Node.js to untrusted input. Should correlate vulnerable package presence with network-listening node processes. Article: vulnerability is 'exploitation for privilege escalation' when untrusted code reaches the VM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for systems where vulnerable vm2 (<=3.11.3) is installed AND node.exe is listening on network ports (especially 80, 443, 8080) or receiving inbound HTTP. Correlation of inventory + network exposure + version = high-risk asset.

suggestion.title: Node.js vm2 nesting enabled without require protection
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability: 'nesting: true without explicit require still allows full RCE' and 'the check uses strict equality... which is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely.' Source code or runtime configuration must show vm2({nesting: true, require: undefined}) pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Node.js source files and package.json configs for vm2 instantiation with nesting:true and no require field (or require not explicitly false). Pair with runtime instrumentation of vm2 module calls to detect at invoke time. High fidelity if correlated to application deployment or package update events.

suggestion.title: vm2 sandbox escape via child_process module spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article shows RCE is achieved by executing OS shell commands. The techniques list T1611 (Escape to Host) and T1059.* (shell execution). Detection must fire when vm2 context (nesting+undefined require config) transitions to child_process.spawn/exec.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hook Node.js child_process module; flag spawns where the call stack includes vm2 library frames and nesting=true was configured. Alternatively, look for sudden process tree changes (parent=node, child=shell) immediately after vm2 module import or instantiation events.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt: Node.js requiring child_process inside vm2 VM
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative: attacker uses 'child_process' and 'execSync' to break out. The patch being bypassed is designed to block require() inside sandboxed code. Detection: vm2 VM executing require('child_process') or equivalent dynamic requires.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument vm2.run() or vm2.runFile() to log code being sandboxed. Flag any code containing require('child_process'), require('fs'), require('os'), or similar dangerous built-ins. Cross-reference to nesting=true configs. High confidence if require attempt occurs inside a VM execution.

suggestion.title: node.exe process object exfiltration via Promise escape
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit allows 'execute arbitrary commands on the host system' via sandbox breakout. The technical mechanism (Promise species + Symbol manipulation) grants access to the Node.js `process` object—but no detection for post-escape enumeration of process.env, process.cwd(), or process.platform. Detection gap: reading sensitive environment variables (DATABASE_PASSWORD, API_KEYS, SSH keys via SSH_AUTH_SOCK) after sandbox break.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After node.exe spawns a shell child process (post-escape), hunt for immediate reads of .env, .ssh, config files, or environment variable dumps. Look for child processes reading from %USERPROFILE%\.ssh or ~/.ssh, or env var enumeration commands (set, env) executed by that child.

suggestion.title: vm2 script invocation with Promise/Symbol-based payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack as targeting 'code which can escape from the VM2 sandbox.' The exploit code is written *within* or *passed to* vm2.run() or similar VM2 execution APIs. Current hunts detect post-escape indicators (child spawns, PoC strings in node cmdlines) but miss detection of *the VM2 script execution itself* that contains exploit payloads. Gap: no detection for vm2 require statements + Promise manipulation in the same process window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Node.js processes with both 'vm2' and Promise/Symbol keywords in cmdline or file I/O pattern (e.g., reading a .js file containing vm2 import + Symbol.species) within a narrow time window before child process spawn. Could be augmented with memory-scanning rules (EDR) for Symbol.species Promise prototype pollution patterns in Node heap.

suggestion.title: Sandbox escape technique fingerprints: resetPromiseSpecies absence
suggestion.rationale: The article's technical detail states: 'localPromise constructor was changed to call this.then(undefined, eater) to ensure a rejected promise is always used. However, this is missing a call to resetPromiseSpecies...' This is the *root cause* of the escape. Detection for running vulnerable vm2 code that doesn't call resetPromiseSpecies would be a leading indicator before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .js files or npm packages (via package.json dependency scan or SBOM) that import vm2, create Promise objects, and reference Symbol.species without downstream calls to resetPromiseSpecies (or equivalent mitigation). Can be implemented as static code review integrated into SIEM (parse source code drops on disk).

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation file access from node.exe child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions attackers can 'execute arbitrary commands on the host system.' After sandbox escape and child process spawn, attacker gains host-level file access. Current hunts detect the spawn event but not the follow-on data exfiltration (reading /etc/passwd, ~/.aws/credentials, /proc/*/environ, Windows credential files, etc.). Gap: no detection for sensitive file reads initiated by cmd.exe/powershell.exe spawned *from node.exe*.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30 seconds of node.exe spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe (post-escape), look for file access to sensitive paths: %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, %USERPROFILE%\.aws, %USERPROFILE%\.docker, /home/*/.ssh, /root/.ssh, /etc/passwd, /proc/*/environ, Windows\System32\config\SAM. Correlate by process tree (parent cmd.exe's parent is node.exe).

suggestion.title: vm2 vulnerability scanner probe activity
suggestion.rationale: Recon phase detection: before exploitation, attackers enumerate endpoints for vulnerable vm2 versions. Article discusses the CVE but no detection for pre-exploit scanning (checking package.json, npm registry queries, dependency checks). Gap: no detection for tools or scripts probing for vm2 presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes reading package.json or package-lock.json files at scale (multiple directories), or npm/yarn registry queries for 'vm2' version info. Correlate with network requests to registry.npmjs.org searching vm2 version metadata. Look for curl/wget/certutil requests to npm APIs enumerating vm2 releases.

suggestion.title: Node.js process spawns shell or LOLBin — vm2 sandbox escape post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Explicitly recommended in article: 'Node.js process spawns shell or LOLBin — vm2 sandbox escape post-exploitation (CVE-2026-47210)' with supplied Splunk SPL and Defender KQL. Pipeline completely failed to generate this UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-sandbox-escape, attacker spawns interactive shell (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh, mshta, wscript) as child of Node.js process. Detect parent_process_name=node spawning child in {cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash} with non-system user context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 (<= 3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47210 exposure
suggestion.rationale: Explicitly recommended in article: 'Vulnerable vm2 (<= 3.11.3) present on host'. Detects foundational recon indicator. Article provides complete Splunk and KQL templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts with vm2 module via node_modules/vm2/package.json file events or software vulnerability inventory matching CVE-2026-47210. Flags exposure to sandbox escape attack surface.

suggestion.title: JSPI WebAssembly runtime exposure with vm2 co-presence
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'untrusted code is executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI (WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending)'. This is a necessary precondition the pipeline should have flagged as a discovery/reconnaissance indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes running code with vm2 imported for evidence of WebAssembly JSPI API surface (WebAssembly.promising, WebAssembly.Suspending calls). JSPI exposure + vm2 presence = full prerequisite for sandbox escape exploitation.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype.finally() or species hardening bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names vulnerability as 'Promise .finally() species bypass'. The exploit specifically 'bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening'. Pipeline should have generated behavioral detection for Promise prototype manipulation or species constructor override attempts within vm2 execution contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js code attempting to override Promise.prototype.finally, set Symbol.species on Promise constructors, or manipulate Promise internal slots from within vm2 sandboxed code. These are smoking-gun indicators of active exploitation of CVE-2026-47210.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Tool Registration with eval()/exec() in PraisonAI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability: 'registers a `calculate(expression)` tool implemented with Python `eval(expression)`'. Pipeline should detect when an LLM-driven tool definition includes dangerous functions. No UC addresses tool-definition-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes loading PraisonAI agent definitions (import praisonai, A2AServer initialization) that subsequently register tools containing eval(), exec(), compile(), or __import__ in their function body. Correlate with inbound A2A requests to the same process within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: [LLM] eval()/exec() Execution with Network-Derived Parameters in Python
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unauthenticated network client can send a JSON-… reach real LLM-driven `eval()` tool execution'. Pipeline should detect when eval/exec are called with arguments originating from JSON-RPC input, not hardcoded values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python eval() or exec() calls where arguments are not static strings but are derived from parsed JSON or function parameters. In PraisonAI context, look for eval(expression) where 'expression' came from JSON-RPC request parameter.

suggestion.title: [LLM] A2A Server Binding to 0.0.0.0 Without Authentication Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'The example exposes an A2A server without configuring `auth_token`' and 'binds the server to `0.0.0.0`'. Should detect during initialization, not just runtime exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PraisonAI A2A server startup (uvicorn.run, A2A() constructor, a2a-server.py execution) where: (1) command line contains '0.0.0.0' or '--host 0.0.0.0', AND (2) auth_token is absent from process environment, startup config file, or command line.

suggestion.title: [LLM] JSON-RPC Method Injection Toward eval()-Capable Tools
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires sending 'JSON-...' (article truncated but describes JSON payload). Should detect suspicious JSON-RPC method names targeting calc/eval-like tools with code-like parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /a2a endpoint with JSON-RPC method names like 'tool_call', 'invoke_tool', 'execute_tool', 'calculate' where the parameter value contains Python syntax keywords (import, def, class, os., subprocess, __) or math expressions with unusual length.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI deploy --type api command execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PraisonAI `deploy --type api` emits a Flask server with authentication disabled by default'. Detailed hunt (UC_10_3) published in article 'Recommended hunts' but pipeline failed to extract or synthesize equivalent detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution matching praisonai deploy --type api or praisonai deploy -t api. Alert on provisioning of Flask API servers with disabled default authentication.

suggestion.title: External inbound TCP/8005 to Python/Flask process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per the recommended sample YAML' with default port 8005. Hunt UC_10_4 published but pipeline missed initial-access phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP/8005 from public IPs (non-RFC1918) to Python processes. Escalate confidence if initiating process is Python or contains 'praisonai'/'flask' in command line.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /chat or /agents endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposes `/chat` and `/agents` endpoints' and UC_10_5 details the attack pattern. Pipeline failed to synthesize exploit-phase endpoint abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST to /chat or /agents on port 8005 from external sources. Correlate with scanning patterns—CVE-Detector User-Agent, high request rates, multi-source probing.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI process spawning bash, curl, wget, or nc
suggestion.rationale: Article describes LLM code-execution capability enabling agent tool-use. UC_10_6 addresses post-exploitation. Pipeline missed command-and-control phase detection for tool invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Critical: Python processes (esp. spawned from praisonai deploy) creating child processes for bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, or socat. Indicates code execution and external tool access via LLM interface abuse.

suggestion.title: YAML configuration file with Flask 0.0.0.0 binding in PraisonAI project
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per the recommended sample YAML'. Configuration file modification is prerequisite step for deployment execution, not covered by UC_10_3 (which starts at command execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of YAML or Python config in PraisonAI directories containing Flask host='0.0.0.0' or address binding to 0.0.0.0:8005. Alert if no concurrent auth middleware setup.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI workspace permission enumeration via sequential resource access
suggestion.rationale: Article states dependency 'only checks that the caller is a member of the workspace_id in the URL prefix' then looks up inner resources by ID. Sequential or near-sequential resource ID access across a single workspace is a hallmark of IDOR discovery not captured by UC_7_3's high-cardinality heuristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for single user/source making sequential GET requests to `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/{resource_type}/{id}` where id values are monotonic or near-monotonic UUIDs, within a short time window (60s). High volume of 404 errors interspersed with 200s indicates enumeration probing.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI cross-workspace lateral movement post-privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation enabling cross-workspace resource access. The gap is detecting the moment escalated privileges are exercised: account goes from single-workspace member to accessing resources in previously-unauthorized workspaces. UC_7_3 detects enumeration but not the privilege boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user's baseline workspace membership (first 7 days) against access patterns. Alert when user accesses resources in workspace_id not in baseline, especially if preceded by member-role PATCH within 60 seconds. Reduces false positives from legitimate team additions.

suggestion.title: JWT token forgery via known weak signing key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'token forgery for any user' enabled by hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-me'. Detection should monitor for valid JWT tokens that can be forged/validated against this known weak key, or flag JWT issuance from praisonai-platform instances without proper PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET configured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for successful authentications where JWT tokens were issued by praisonai-platform instances running with default dev environment. Look for JWT validation failures or inconsistencies in token issuance patterns (e.g., tokens issued outside normal auth flow).

suggestion.title: Deployment configuration: PLATFORM_ENV unset or dev in production infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev, so the check is silently bypassed in any deployment'. Detection should identify Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Docker Compose files, systemd services, and .env configs where PLATFORM_ENV is missing or = 'dev' in non-dev namespaces/environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Kubernetes ConfigMaps/Secrets, Docker image build logs, and infrastructure-as-code repos for praisonai-platform deployments. Flag when PLATFORM_ENV environment variable is absent or explicitly set to 'dev' in production/staging namespaces or infrastructure tags.

suggestion.title: Authentication bypass: successful API calls with forged/weak JWT tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'actions' (POST/DELETE/PATCH) against workspaces enabled by forged tokens. Forged tokens would bypass normal authentication flows, appearing as successful auth events with no preceding MFA challenge, device attestation, or corresponding login record for that user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful workspace API operations (/workspaces/* DELETE/PATCH/POST) from valid JWT tokens where no corresponding user login or MFA challenge event exists in the auth log for that user/timestamp, or where the JWT was issued by a dev-mode praisonai-platform instance.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via PATCH followed by workspace deletion or mass role reset
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers promote themselves to owner status. Logical follow-on: newly elevated owner might delete the workspace or reset all other owners' roles to isolate the workspace. Article says 'Account Access Removal' (T1531) is a mapped technique, but no hunt directly addresses rapid destructive actions post-escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /workspaces/{id}/members/* that change role to 'owner', immediately followed (within 10 minutes) by DELETE /workspaces/{id} or bulk PATCH requests that strip owner role from all other members in that workspace.

suggestion.title: Workspace enumeration or API token escalation post-promotion
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1087.004 (Account Discovery: Cloud Account), but no hunt checks whether a newly-promoted owner immediately requests elevated API tokens, regenerates credentials, or queries workspace membership/settings that would not be visible to regular members.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 minutes of a successful role-change PATCH to owner, detect GET /workspaces/{id}/members or GET /workspaces/{id}/api-keys, or POST requests to credential/token endpoints. Correlate by source IP.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via workspace invitation link generation post-elevation
suggestion.rationale: Once owner, attacker can invite external users or create shared links. Article does not specify post-privilege-escalation lateral movement detection. The mapped T1136.003 (Create Account: Cloud Account) suggests this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /workspaces/{id}/invitations or similar endpoints immediately after a successful owner-level role promotion. Especially suspicious if invitations are sent to external email domains or if link-sharing is enabled for a previously private workspace.

suggestion.title: Detect Bypass or Disable of Pre-Commit Security Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'custom pre-commit hooks that automatically scan all newly introduced code before it could be committed' and states 'Before this even makes it to the PR, I want it to scan and catch everything.' An attacker or malicious insider circumventing this control is a high-fidelity signal of a compromise attempt or intentional injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when developers use git commit --no-verify to skip pre-commit hooks, when hook files (.git/hooks/*) are deleted or modified, when commits bypass expected Snyk scan output, or when developers suddenly switch to direct branch pushes bypassing PR workflows.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized AI Tool Usage (Non-Approved GitHub Copilot)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Providing sanctioned tools also helps reduce shadow AI by discouraging developers from turning to unmanaged consumer services.' Unauthorized AI assistants bypass security scanning pipeline and represent a supply-chain risk vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls to external/unapproved AI services (ChatGPT, Copilot web tier, Claude API calls not routed through enterprise proxy, other LLMs) from developer workstations. Flag developers bypassing approved GitHub Copilot channel for code generation.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistent Unresolved or Ignored Security Findings
suggestion.rationale: Article describes developers getting 'security findings immediately' and applying 'fixes in real time.' A sudden shift from the described norm—developers ignoring Snyk alerts, marking findings false-positive at abnormal rates, or skipping remediation—could indicate either account compromise or deliberate code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track per-developer Snyk finding resolution patterns. Alert on MTTR deviation >2 sigma above baseline, false-positive dismissal rate anomalies, or security findings in commits suddenly marked as non-blocking when historically they triggered remediation.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Link Click Followed by macOS Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Using LinkedIn Social Engineering to Deploy Custom macOS Malware'—initial access vector combines spearphishing link with user execution on macOS platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LinkedIn URLs clicked from external email followed within minutes by suspicious process spawn (shell, curl, python, osascript) on macOS. Baseline: legitimate LinkedIn clicks rarely precede execution events same day.

suggestion.title: Custom Unsigned macOS Executable Execution Post-Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: 'Custom macOS Malware' indicates non-standard binary; likely unsigned or signed with stolen certs. Follows social engineering delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on macOS process execution where CodeSignStatus is 'Unsigned' or cert issuer is not Apple/legitimate vendor, preceded by user interaction (file download, link click) within 10 minutes. Custom malware will bypass notarization checks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon Persistence via Plist Modification
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware payloads on macOS commonly establish persistence via LaunchAgents (~/Library/LaunchAgents) or LaunchDaemons; 'custom' suggests native persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist or /Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist where the writing process is user-initiated (shell, installer, archive tool). Flag if the plist references binaries in temp directories or unsigned locations.

suggestion.title: macOS Process Spawning Suspicious Interpreters Post-Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: 'Custom macOS Malware' often scripts execution via Python, AppleScript, or zsh to evade detection. Follows LinkedIn delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of /usr/bin/python, /usr/bin/osascript, /bin/zsh, /bin/sh with unusual arguments or from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or /var/tmp. Flag if parent is Finder, Archive Utility, or browser process.
