Flag model weight downloads from HuggingFace, OpenAI API, or similar endpoints. Monitor for agent initialization objects and chat/completion API calls in post-exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: LLM-Mediated Command Execution Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Use of LLM agent for post-exploitation implies commands flow through LLM logic, not direct shell access. Article phrase 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation' describes novel execution pattern. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent Python/notebook processes spawning system commands via subprocess, os.system, or exec(). Flag command-line arguments that match LLM output patterns (unusual phrasing, structured reasoning chains, or tool-use syntax). Correlate with LLM library execution in same process tree.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Large Model File Download Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: LLM agent operation requires model weights (often multi-GB). Article states LLM agent deployment follows RCE. Pipeline did not flag model acquisition as a detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large (>100MB) file transfers from machine-learning model repositories (huggingface.co, models.openai.com, ollama registries) originating from compromised hosts. Flag archive extraction (tar, zip) of model directories. Detect cache directory creation in /tmp or %TEMP% for model storage.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Feature Abuse for Phishing Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title directly states 'Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface'—this is an initial-access attack vector leveraging a specific ChatGPT feature as an abuse surface. Pipeline missed the obvious kill-chain phase.

Monitor for user click-through on summary links that bypass reputation filtering because they originate from trusted ChatGPT infrastructure.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse for Phishing Infrastructure Setup
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to weaponize ChatGPT summaries; implies API calls to generate or host phishing content. Article title signals ChatGPT as the attack vector—need detection for abnormal ChatGPT API usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume API requests to ChatGPT/OpenAI endpoints from internal users, especially requests that generate URLs or content summaries. Flag accounts making unusual API calls immediately followed by external phishing infrastructure setup or email delivery.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Leveraging ChatGPT Summary Links
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have inferred from title that the attack surface is phishing emails using ChatGPT-generated or ChatGPT-hosted summary content as the lure. No mention of email-based detection despite 'phishing surface' in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to chat.openai.com, openai.com/api/*, or similar ChatGPT web-facing endpoints that serve user-generated summaries. Cross-reference sender reputation and email text for common phishing indicators. Alert on summary links that point to external domains or credential-harvesting pages.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability that 'turns summaries into phishing surface' implies attacker-controlled ChatGPT accounts or API keys used to generate or host phishing. Pipeline missed credential-access and account-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ChatGPT login anomalies (unusual geolocations, IP addresses, or login times). Track API key usage spikes or calls from residential/VPN IPs. Detect if a single OpenAI account generates dozens of summary links to different attacker-controlled domains in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Exposed Management Interface — Exploitation Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'attackers to bypass security restrictions' on exposed assets; CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Yet no use case detects exploitation attempts targeting exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed or anomalous HTTP/HTTPS requests to exposed PAN-OS management interfaces (ports 443, 8080, 8081) from external sources exhibiting exploitation patterns: specific payload signatures, header anomalies, rapid enumeration, or CVE-2026-0257 exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass — Unexpected Access Post-Failure
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability described as 'authentication bypass.' Article phrase establishes attacker objective but no use case captures successful unauthorized access or anomalous post-authentication behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events bypassing normal auth flows: successful login immediately after multiple failures, login from unexpected geolocation, successful admin access via non-standard methods, or management-interface access from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability 'allows attackers...to establish an unauthorized VPN connection.' This is a primary attack outcome yet zero detection use cases generated to identify unauthorized VPN sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN connections initiated by non-administrative accounts, from non-standard geolocations, outside business hours, or exceeding baseline patterns. Alert on rapid VPN connection attempts or connections immediately following auth-bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Configuration/Persistence Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Successful auth bypass typically enables attacker configuration changes and persistence. Article describes 'bypass security restrictions' implying admin-level access but no use case captures post-exploitation administrative activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual administrative commands, configuration modifications, new user account creation, security policy changes, or credential modifications on PAN-OS devices, especially correlated with prior auth-bypass or external-access indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerability Confirmation in Fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-0257 with federal due date 2026-06-01, but pipeline produced zero IOCs and no use case to identify vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unpatched PAN-OS instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-0257 (from scanner data) with network telemetry showing inbound connections to management interfaces. Flag instances still vulnerable past federal due date (2026-06-01).

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Internet-Facing Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates 'currently being exploited' against exposed assets. Article implies internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces but no use case to identify them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PAN-OS management ports (443, 8080, 8081) responding to external inbound traffic or accessible from internet. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to flag unpatched exposed instances providing easy exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: PoC Pattern Detection — vm2 Prototype Pollution Strings in HTTP Request Body
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly demonstrates PoC: 'By combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")`' and provides HTTP-based detection rules. Pipeline produced no use case despite this being primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound HTTP requests containing prototype-pollution keywords (__lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, Buffer.call.call, mainModule.require, compileStreaming) in URL or body, particularly toward Node.js endpoints. High confidence due to specificity of these patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Shell Spawning — Node.exe → OS Shell After vm2 Sandbox Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative: 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code' and provides detection rules for node.exe spawning cmd/powershell/bash. Pipeline missed despite being explicit post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process node.exe spawning child processes cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash.exe, or sh.exe with command patterns indicating code execution (echo pwned, child_process, execSync). Baseline should flag any node-to-shell spawn unless explicitly approved by application owner.

suggestion.title: Asset Vulnerability — vm2 Package ≤3.11.3 Installed and Discoverable
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions ≤3.11.3 and provides software inventory detection. Pipeline extracted CVE identifier but not the version-range IOC or the software-discovery use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for vm2 package (vendor: npm/openjs/nodejs) with version matching regex ^([0-2]\.|3\.([0-9]|10|11)(\.[0-3])?$). Medium confidence; indicates exposure but not active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Prototype Pollution via Buffer Constructor Access — __proto__ Mutation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")`, `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupSetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")`. Pipeline did not extract this as a distinct attack primitive despite it being the technical foundation of the sandbox escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript code patterns attempting to access or mutate __proto__ via lookupGetter/lookupSetter on Node built-ins (Buffer, Object, Function). Can be detected in source analysis of uploaded files or via JavaScript AST inspection in runtime environments.

suggestion.title: vm2 Module Invocation Tracking — New VM() Instances from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article shows PoC: `const { VM } = require('vm2'); const vm = new VM()`. Pipeline did not flag vm2 instantiation as an execution pattern that warrants monitoring in a vulnerable environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Node.js processes whose command line or loaded modules include vm2 instantiation (require('vm2'), new VM(), new NodeVM()). Establish baseline of legitimate use; flag deviations or usage from unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 configuration in runtime code — nesting:true without explicit require
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The fix…introduced a check in nodevm.js line 263 that blocks the combination nesting: true + require: false. However, the check uses strict equality (options.require === false), which is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely.' This behavioral pattern is the actual attack surface—code instantiating NodeVM with nesting:true and no require parameter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Node.js process arguments or source code repositories for NodeVM instantiation patterns matching {nesting:true} without explicit require property. Correlate timing of such configuration discovery with subsequent shell spawns from the Node process.

suggestion.title: vm2 sandbox escape via undefined require bypass — post-exploitation enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full RCE via sandbox escape. The core behavioral signature: Node process with vm2 in call stack spawns shell, then executes system discovery commands (child_process.execSync patterns visible in logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript heap/memory patterns in Node debugger logs or app-level logging showing child_process module accessed within vm2 context, followed by immediate OS command execution from same process context.

suggestion.title: Supply chain: vulnerable vm2 dependency in application manifest
suggestion.rationale: Article scope includes distribution risk—any application using vm2 <=3.11.3 is exploitable. Package-lock.json or yarn.lock files in repositories/deployments are actionable hunting surfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application dependency manifests (package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml) for vm2 versions matching the vulnerable range. Prioritize production deployments and CI/CD logs showing vm2 installation.

suggestion.title: Node.js child process escape with insufficient sandbox context
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability specifically allows escaping Node.js vm2 sandbox (T1611). When vm2's sandbox is bypassed, parent Node process becomes the attack surface: article shows shell execution with OS commands confirming escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js process (or process cluster) spawning child OS shells when vm2 module has been loaded. Baseline: legitimate Node apps rarely spawn shells directly; escapes manifest as unexpected cmd/bash children of node parents.

suggestion.title: Rapid system enumeration post-vm2 sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article payload pattern: sandbox escape → immediate OS enumeration (whoami, id, uname, hostname, /etc/passwd reads). This is classic post-exploitation recon signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of OS discovery commands executed in rapid succession (< 2 sec apart) from a single parent Node.exe/node process that did not previously show shell-spawning behavior. Focus on sequences: whoami → id → uname → hostname, or Windows equiv: whoami → systeminfo → net user.

suggestion.title: Application-level vm2 error/exception logging indicating sandbox bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerable code may log errors when sandbox restrictions are hit. Error signatures like 'ERR_SANDBOX_VIOLATION', 'require not allowed', or segfaults in vm2 library during nested execution are indicators of exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs (NodeJS stderr/stdout, syslog) for vm2/NodeVM exception patterns: heap buffer overflows in native modules, context boundary violations, or repeated require() rejections followed by success after restart/reconfiguration.

suggestion.title: vm2 vulnerable version in software inventory or registry — version matching detection
suggestion.rationale: UC_21_1 detects file presence but not version. Article specifies '≤3.11.3' vulnerable. Quote: 'vm2 is Vulnerable to Sandbox Breakout' with specific version constraint. Software inventory tools (CMDB, Defender TVM, pkg managers) can match exact versions without filesystem parsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory or registry for vm2 package with version field matching vulnerable range (3.0.0 through 3.11.3). Prioritize by-host inventory if available; cross-reference with asset scanning results.

suggestion.title: Escaped child process spawning with SYSTEM/admin privileges — post-breakout privilege abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1068 (Privilege Escalation) and describes arbitrary command execution post-escape, but no UC detects privilege escalation tactics. Quote: 'execute arbitrary commands on the host system.' Attackers will likely escalate privileges after breaking out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or children spawning processes with SYSTEM/admin token (ProcessIntegrityLevel='System'), or spawning privilege escalation tools (wsusa, schtasks, net localgroup, Add-LocalGroupMember). Correlate with UC_21_2 baseline.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement or persistence after node.exe sandbox breakout — scheduled tasks, WMI, or RDP abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article says attackers can 'execute arbitrary commands' suggesting post-exploitation actions beyond the immediate host. No lateral movement or persistence hunts present. Typical post-breakout adversary behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or its children executing wmic, schtasks, net, psexec, or RDP-related tools; also DNS queries or outbound connections to new hosts post-sandbox escape. Chain alerting: UC_21_1 + UC_21_2 + lateral movement = high confidence compromise.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 library presence — CVE-2026-47210 asset exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A sandbox escape vulnerability in vm2 allows arbitrary code execution' with explicit version bound (<=3.11.3). UC_19_3 in the article provides recon-phase hunt. Pipeline must recognize bounded vulnerability as primary asset-discovery signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate systems with vm2 npm package installed via inventory, package.json inspection, or TVM vulnerability matching. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-47210 severity; prioritize if vm2 is in sandboxed Node.js apps handling untrusted code.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawning shell post-vm2 sandbox escape — CVE-2026-47210 post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the host process'. UC_19_2 in article provides exact hunt template. Core technique T1611 (Escape to Host) maps directly; pipeline failed to recognize escape signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation: parent=node.exe/node, child=cmd.exe/powershell.exe/bash/sh/wscript/mshta. Filter service accounts. High confidence given JSPI trigger surface; low false-positive rate in sandboxed VM contexts.

suggestion.title: Promise species bypass gadget exploitation in vm2 — JSPI-backed execution entry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation mechanism: 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally() in a way that bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening'. This is the execution phase trigger. Detection gap: behavioral signatures of Promise manipulation, WebAssembly.promising/Suspending invocation, or async/await chains in vm2 sandboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Promise.finally() or Promise species-constructor references in vm contexts; requires code-level visibility (Node.js debug logs, V8 profiling, or bytecode inspection). Difficult in pure EDR; recommend code audit + runtime instrumentation as supplementary control.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST to PraisonAI /a2a endpoint (CVE-2026-47391 initial access)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An unauthenticated network client can send a JSON-...' and provides UC_9_2 with full Splunk/Defender rules targeting this vector. Pipeline missed the primary initial access mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /a2a* endpoints on ports 8000, 80, 443, 8080 originating from non-RFC1918 sources. Alert on HTTP 200 responses without prior authentication. Correlate with python/uvicorn process parent to confirm A2A server as target.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning from Python/uvicorn A2A server (eval() RCE execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability is 'calculate(expression) tool implemented with Python eval()'. UC_9_3 explicitly hunts unintended child processes (sh, bash, curl, whoami, id) spawned from python/uvicorn parents. Pipeline generated zero process-level execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes spawn from python or uvicorn parents running a2a-server.py/praisonai, especially if children are shell interpreters (sh, bash, dash, zsh), remote tools (curl, wget, nc), or reconnaissance utilities (whoami, id, hostname, env). This indicates attacker-controlled code execution via eval().

suggestion.title: Vulnerable A2A server configuration: 0.0.0.0 binding without auth_token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability as combination of three misconfigurations: exposed A2A server, 0.0.0.0 bind, eval() tool. UC_9_4 provides Defender KQL specifically detecting this pattern. Pipeline produced zero install/configuration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on python/uvicorn processes executing a2a-server.py with command-line patterns containing '0.0.0.0', '--host 0.0.0.0', or 'uvicorn.run*0.0.0.0*' AND NOT containing 'auth_token' or 'AUTH_TOKEN'. Flag as security misconfiguration on first occurrence per host.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation credential and system file access from eval() child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_9_3 explicitly hunts child processes accessing /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.aws/credentials, and environment variables containing API keys (GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). This is confirmation of successful RCE, distinct from process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate child processes derived from a2a-server parents with file access to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, or enumeration of environment variables. Alert if child command-line references credential file paths, API key variable names, or outputs secrets.

suggestion.title: A2A-specific artifact detection: named binaries and example code paths
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_9_1 provides high-fidelity artifact hunting for specific process names (server.py, a2a-server.py, official-a2a-example-real-llm-canary.py) and code paths. Pipeline generated zero artifact-based detections despite article explicitly providing these indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation for server.py, a2a-server.py, or official-a2a-example-real-llm-canary.py. Alert on file creation/modification in PraisonAI/examples/python/a2a/* directories. Flag if these processes bind to ports 8000, 80, 443, 8080. Baseline against expected deployments to identify rogue instances.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI listening socket exposure on public-facing interface (recon phase)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per the recommended sample YAML'—discovery of listening instances is the first attack step. Pipeline missed recon-phase detection entirely despite public exposure being the root vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inbound connection probes to TCP/8005 from non-RFC1918 sources with successful handshake but no TLS negotiation (raw HTTP) indicate PraisonAI discovery. Correlate multiple unique external IPs scanning the same internal asset within narrow time window.

suggestion.title: JSON prompt injection payload in /chat POST (exploit phase signature detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article: unauthenticated POST to '/chat and /agents endpoints'—but UC_11_5 only triggers on request frequency, missing actual exploitation payloads. LLM prompt injection via JSON is the attack vector; requires signature inspection for command syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST to /chat or /agents with JSON payloads containing shell metacharacters ($(), ``, &&, |), absolute filesystem paths (/bin/, /etc/, C:\), or subprocess keywords (exec, spawn, popen) in text/string fields. Alert on payloads with 3+ indicators of command execution intent.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI spawning additional Python interpreters (plugin/tool abuse post-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: UC_11_6 covers shell/curl spawning but misses Python child processes. Article implies LLM-directed 'tool-use' likely includes spawning Python scripts or virtualenvs for plugin execution, a distinct post-exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent: Python process with praisonai in command line. Child: Python interpreter spawned with arguments containing dynamic imports (import X, -m module, urllib.request), file downloads (wget, curl URLs), or base64-encoded payloads. Indicates LLM tool-invocation abuse.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform newly-created account immediate privileged resource modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables privilege escalation via role mutation (T1548). Newly-created or low-history accounts performing admin operations (PATCH/DELETE to agents, projects) within minutes of registration indicate rapid exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account creation timestamp (successful POST /api/v1/auth/register) with first privileged write operation (PATCH/DELETE to workspace resource). Flag if admin-level action occurs <5 min post-registration. Baseline against legitimate workflow.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform resource ID enumeration via sequential access patterns
suggestion.rationale: IDOR vulnerability described as 'look up inner resource (agent_id, issue_id, project_id, label_id, comment_id, dependency_id) by primary key'. Attacker enumerates by iterating IDs. Detect 404→200 sequences indicating discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/{resource_type}/{id} endpoints. Detect 404/403 followed by 200 on same resource type from single source within 1 minute. Flag sequential ID patterns (numeric increments, UUID prefix matches).

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform workspace-membership abuse following cross-workspace enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: enumeration via IDOR (T1190) → membership join → role escalation. Detect the progression within 30 minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chain: (1) source generates 10+ 404/403 responses across distinct workspace resource endpoints, (2) followed by successful POST to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members, (3) followed by PATCH to member role endpoint. Anomaly if account typically single-workspace.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform bulk data export from elevated account within newly-accessible workspace
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation: attacker escalates role, then exfiltrates data (T1213, T1530). Detect large GET responses to resource lists after privilege elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 10 min of successful member-role PATCH, flag user generating GET requests to /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/{resource_type} with response size >1MB OR >100 distinct resource IDs returned, especially if IP shows concurrent activity from untrusted ranges.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform endpoint-structure probing before successful member-role mutation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/members/{id} PATCH endpoint. Detect endpoint fuzzing (multiple 404s) preceding successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ 404 responses to /api/v1/workspaces/*/members/* URL variations from single source, followed within 10 min by successful PATCH/POST to similar structure. Suggests endpoint discovery before exploitation.

suggestion.title: JWT token forgery detection via hardcoded secret signature validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'token forgery for any user' via hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-me' secret. No detection for actual exploitation phase (crafting/validating tokens signed with known secret). Article describes destructive workspace operations as result of forged tokens but provides no hunt for the forging itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode JWT tokens in authentication logs and detect: (1) tokens with HS256 signature valid under 'dev-secret-change-me' string, (2) successful authentication events for different users from same IP within <10 seconds (behavioral indicator of token forgery rather than credential reuse), or (3) bearer tokens where payload user_id mismatches authenticated user in request context.

suggestion.title: Configuration audit: PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET unset and PLATFORM_ENV equals dev in production
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'safety check exists but only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev' making the check silently bypassed. Should hunt for deployments where critical safety mechanism is disabled due to environment variable misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify production/staging systems where PLATFORM_ENV is unset, equals 'dev', or PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is unset. Cross-reference environment context (deployed to prod infrastructure) with environment configuration to find safety-check bypasses. Can surface via container config inspection, k8s pod spec analysis, or process environment variable dumps.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded secret string exposure in runtime artifacts and deployments
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly emphasizes hardcoded secret 'dev-secret-change-me' as root cause. Should hunt for literal string appearing in configurations, container images, source repos, or process memory as evidence of incomplete secrets rotation or development-to-production code copy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for literal string 'dev-secret-change-me' in git history, docker image layers, k8s manifests, config files, environment variable exports, and process memory. Correlate findings with deployment timeline to identify when production systems were exposed to hardcoded credential.

suggestion.title: Workspace privilege escalation without role elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers performing 'destructive' DELETE/PATCH/POST operations on /workspaces/* endpoints. Privilege escalation detection should trigger when authenticated user performs admin-level workspace operations (delete workspace, modify workspace config) without admin role assignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE or PATCH operations targeting /workspaces/{id} endpoints where authenticated user lacks workspace_admin or organization_admin role in authorization policy. Correlate with recent authentication events to identify token-forgery sessions. Alert if same IP performs destructive operations across 3+ distinct workspaces within one hour.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} HTTP 200/204
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint is 'gated by require_workspace_member(workspace_id)' with default 'min_role=member' and 'handler then calls MemberService.update_role()' — direct exploit path for privilege escalation. Detection must catch PATCH requests modifying workspace member roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PATCH requests to /workspaces/[workspace-id]/members/[user-id] returning HTTP 200 or 204. Baseline successful requests and alert on unusual volume, inter-workspace patterns, or role escalation (member→owner). High-confidence because the endpoint name and HTTP method are explicit in the CVE title.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Workspace role PATCH chaining — self-promotion followed by legitimate owner demotion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vertical escalation where attacker 'promote[s] themselves or others' — implies multi-step abuse. Chaining self-promotion with immediate demotion of legitimate owners within a narrow timeframe is a behavioral marker of coordinated privilege hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where the same source IP/user executes ≥2 PATCH role-change requests to /workspaces/*/members/* within 60 minutes, with at least one request targeting the same user_id as the requester (self-promotion) and another targeting a different high-privilege user (demotion). Confidence: High.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Bulk enumeration of agents/issues/projects after workspace role escalation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase: article implies attacker escalates to owner 'to' access workspace data — manifests as enumeration of GET requests to /workspaces/*/agents*, /workspaces/*/issues*, /workspaces/*/projects*, /workspaces/*/comments* immediately following PATCH role-change. Temporal correlation indicates abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GET requests to workspaces enumeration endpoints (agents, issues, projects, comments) from the same source/user within 15 minutes of a successful PATCH role-change to /workspaces/*/members/*. Alerting threshold: ≥10 enumeration requests within window. Medium-high confidence; differentiates post-compromise recon from normal admin activity by temporal proximity to privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Anomalous workspace member role distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a member-to-owner privilege escalation vulnerability, implying the normal distribution of workspace roles should be audited. Workspace with unexpectedly high owner count or recent bulk owner promotions suggests exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and monitor the count of 'owner' role users per workspace. Alert on workspaces where the owner count increases by >1 within 24 hours or where >50% of active members hold owner role — statistical anomaly indicating bulk privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Third-Party AI Tool Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article states Relay standardized Copilot specifically to 'reduce shadow AI by discouraging developers from turning to unmanaged consumer services.' SOC should detect circumvention—code exfiltration to unapproved LLM APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS POST requests to ChatGPT, Claude, or other third-party AI endpoints originating from developer workstations. Flag curl/wget commands piping code to external services. Alert on API key usage for unauthorized LLMs in GitHub Actions logs.

suggestion.title: Pre-Commit Hook Disable or Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes custom pre-commit hooks 'forces the research right there while it's in front of you' as critical enforcement. Detecting bypass (git commit --no-verify, hook deletion, permission change) indicates intentional policy evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to .git/hooks/ directory. Flag git commands with --no-verify flag. Monitor for .git/hooks/pre-commit deletion or permission changes to read-only. Alert on git config hooks.allownonascii changes.

suggestion.title: Snyk Security Scan Failure Ignored or Suppressed
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Snyk integration as gate: 'developers could generate code, receive security findings immediately, and apply fixes in real time before code was ever committed.' Merging code with unresolved high/critical Snyk findings indicates policy violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub pull request merges where Snyk security status check shows 'failed' or 'did not run.' Flag commits to main/master with unresolved Snyk findings. Alert on CI pipeline steps skipping or commenting out snyk test invocations.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Credential Harvesting or Profile Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'LinkedIn Social Engineering' as the attack vector. Pipeline extracted no initial access detection despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed LinkedIn connection requests from a single user, or emails referencing LinkedIn offers/job opportunities with suspicious sender domains or 'verify identity' language. Track users who accept connection requests and immediately receive file-sharing links or download prompts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Application Execution from Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes custom macOS malware deployment; no execution-phase detection suggested. Pipeline should detect user-executed binaries from typical social engineering delivery paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code execution from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or /var/tmp shortly after a user received a LinkedIn message or email attachment. Baseline common legitimate applications and flag unknown binaries.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates custom malware; no persistence-phase detection suggested. macOS malware typically installs LaunchAgents, startup scripts, or cron jobs after initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons, /etc/cron.* shortly after suspicious application execution from user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: macOS Process Obfuscation or Code Signing Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware typically employs defense evasion; no technique capture for obfuscation, unsigned binaries, or code-signing abuse on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned or ad-hoc signed binaries, or binaries with cryptographic mismatches between claimed and actual signers. Flag process names that are generic/system-like (e.g., 'system', 'helper', 'agent') launched from non-system locations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network Activity from macOS
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware would require command-and-control or exfiltration; no C2 detection suggested. macOS typically generates distinct network patterns for beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for regular connection attempts to non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 443 with certificate anomalies) from newly-executed binaries. Flag beaconing patterns (fixed intervals, repeated destinations) originating from users who recently accepted LinkedIn messages.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy C2 Deployment and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names HTTPSpy as newly deployed Kimsuky malware; no detection use case was generated for this critical named indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTPSpy is a Kimsuky-attributed remote access tool used for C2 communication and exfiltration. Monitor for HTTPSpy process execution from unusual directories, HTTP-based beacon traffic with characteristic headers, and parent-child process relationships consistent with malware delivery chains.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Malware Execution and C2 Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies HelloDoor as component of expanded Kimsuky arsenal for command-and-control; pipeline generated zero detections for this named malware family
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HelloDoor serves as remote access tool in Kimsuky infrastructure. Detect HelloDoor execution by process name/path anomalies, network connections to non-standard C2 infrastructure, registry modifications for persistence, and DLL side-loading patterns typical of this malware family.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnels Abuse for Malicious C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Kimsuky expanded arsenal to include VS Code Tunnels as attack vector; pipeline failed to surface defense-evasion and tunneling detection opportunities
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Legitimate VS Code Tunnels create predictable connection patterns to known infrastructure. Detect anomalies: VS Code/code-server process spawning unexpected tunneling, connections to attacker-controlled IPs, tunnel creation without developer context, or persistence mechanisms modifying tunnel configuration.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky APT Malware Family Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article is actor-attributed to Kimsuky deploying multiple new tool variants; pipeline generated no detection use case mapping Kimsuky-specific execution patterns, obfuscation tactics, or behavioral signatures
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Kimsuky campaigns feature distinctive command-line obfuscation, staged script execution, and malware staging patterns. Monitor for execution of known Kimsuky tool variants (HTTPSpy/HelloDoor process names/hashes), PowerShell/cmd with suspicious entropy or encoding, and DLL injection patterns consistent with actor TTPs.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Kimsuky Infostealer Artifacts

suggestion.title: Exfiltration from npm Package Installation Context

suggestion.title: OSINT Queries via LLM-Assisted Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: LLM-fueled attacks include reconnaissance; article implies information gathering but no detection for LLM API queries requesting target intelligence.

suggestion.title: Malware Code Generation via LLM Code Assistants
suggestion.rationale: LLMs fueling 'cyberattacks' likely includes malware and exploit code generation; no detection for suspicious code requests to ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar services.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion: npm Package Installation from Non-Official Registry

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Reconnaissance from npm Package Context

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Environment Metadata Over HTTP(S) from npm Package Installation

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall/Preinstall Script Lifecycle Hook Abuse

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Lookups and Version Resolution Anomalies

suggestion.title: Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect Portal/Gateway

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains serving different HTTP response bodies based on User-Agent string, IP reputation, or SSL fingerprinting. Monitor for high content variance from same domain across short time windows and multiple source IPs.

suggestion.title: Executable Downloads from Non-Official AI Vendor Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'macOS [ VirusTotal ] and Windows [ VirusTotal ] downloads that install malware on devices' from openew[.]app masquerading as ChatGPT desktop app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .exe, .dmg, .pkg, .msi downloads from domains not on official OpenAI/Anthropic allowlists. Alert on subsequent execution from Downloads, temp, or %APPDATA% directories matching file names of legitimate software.

suggestion.title: Fake Service Outage Lures on AI Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article quotes fake outage message 'We're experiencing high traffic right now. Our website is temporarily unavailable due to a large number of users. Download our desktop app to continue.' rendered through legitimate ChatGPT domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT/Claude shared pages for outage-themed content, urgency language, or unsolicited download prompts. Correlate with legitimate status pages. Flag share links referencing service disruptions or requesting immediate desktop app downloads.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Sandbox/VM Detection Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'BleepingComputer's test of the Windows version on Any.Run found that it executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Signature infostealer evasion pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WMI/registry queries checking for VM artifacts (system manufacturer, BIOS, adapter names) executed immediately post-download. Monitor for systeminfo, Get-WmiObject, or registry lookups for VirtualBox/VMware/Hyper-V signatures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PAN-OS Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions' on the management interface of a public-facing asset. Should detect unauthenticated or unusually-sourced access to PAN-OS mgmt ports (typically 443, 22) followed by authentication events or management actions without corresponding login logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management interface (web UI, SSH) for connection attempts from external IP ranges, especially those not in allow-lists. Baseline legitimate admin access, flag outliers. Correlate with failed authentication followed by successful command execution without valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: VPN Connection Establishment Post-Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' after bypassing auth. Should detect VPN tunnel creation from PAN-OS with new or anomalous endpoints, especially those initiated by non-admin service accounts or without matching VPN provisioning workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new VPN connection tunnels initiated from PAN-OS management plane, especially to internal networks or with unusual peer endpoints. Correlate with authentication logs that show failed or anomalous login sequences before tunnel creation.

suggestion.title: Credential Account Creation via PAN-OS Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass (T1556) often precedes account creation for persistence. Should monitor for new admin account creation on PAN-OS devices post-exploitation, especially outside change-control windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS system logs for new admin/super-user account creation, API token generation, or privilege elevation events. Baseline legitimate provisioning; flag any outside change windows or initiated by service accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active exploitation signature or pattern likely exists or will be published. Should hunt for HTTP request patterns or payloads known to trigger the auth bypass, if snort/yara rules or vendor guidance is available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Palo Alto Networks publishes exploit signature(s) or pattern guidance, create detection rules matching the payload/request structure. Monitor HTTP/S traffic to PAN-OS management ports for known exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes T1190 is applicable because PAN-OS is 'public-facing.' Should enumerate external asset inventory for PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to internet and verify patch status against CVE-2026-0257.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run or schedule scans for open ports 443/22 on known PAN-OS device IP ranges and check service banners. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-0257 patch database. Flag any unpatched instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing from Infected Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states '200 servers used to host the infrastructure' controlling '17 million infected devices' — periodic command callbacks from compromised hosts to known C2 IP ranges should be detectable via network logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic outbound connections from non-server devices to hosting infrastructure in Netherlands or to known proxy service endpoints. Flag beaconing patterns (consistent time intervals, small payloads) from devices not normally initiating external connections.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the botnet was linked to Asocks, a 'residential proxy service' with '7 million IP addresses' — detection should flag internal devices tunneling traffic through known residential proxy platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to Asocks or similar residential proxy service domains/IPs. Flag devices establishing proxied tunnels for outbound traffic, especially from non-approved users or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Distributed Denial of Service Attack Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet was used 'to carry out cyberattacks' including 'distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks' — synchronized traffic surges from multiple internal sources to external targets indicate attack coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for synchronized outbound traffic from multiple devices targeting the same external destination within a narrow time window, with traffic patterns inconsistent with legitimate business activity (high request rates, small payloads, non-standard ports).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Process Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet used for 'cryptocurrency mining' — detection should flag resource-intensive mining processes spawned on compromised endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of known cryptocurrency mining tools (xmrig, minergate, stratum-mining processes) or unusual high-CPU processes communicating to mining pool domains (mining.*.com, pool.*.com).

suggestion.title: Device Infection via Weak Credentials on Network Services
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'ensure the default credentials have been changed' and 'remote administration panels are disabled' — implies infection vector was default/weak credential access to network-exposed management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated failed authentication attempts against network devices (routers, modems, NAS, printers) followed by successful logon with default or weak credentials from external IPs. Flag successful logons from non-standard locations or times.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload Delivery and Installation on Mobile/IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies infected devices include 'computers, tablets, and smartphones' — detection should cover malware installation mechanisms across heterogeneous device types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sideloaded APK installations on mobile devices from untrusted sources, unauthorized app installations on tablets, and unusual binary execution on smartphones (not typical for platform). Flag installation of tools capable of background communication (HTTP clients, SSH clients) on mobile devices.

suggestion.title: Node.js process spawning shell with enumeration after vm2 sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes post-exploitation pattern: 'Node.js process spawning OS shell with enumeration commands' including whoami, id, uname, hostname, ifconfig, /etc/passwd — this is the direct behavioral indicator of successful RCE after nesting:true bypass. Article provides reference UC_24_2 with working Splunk/KQL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js parent process spawning command shell executables (cmd.exe, bash, sh, etc.) combined with discovery/enumeration CLI flags. Filter for non-system accounts. The parent process (node, node.exe) and the enumeration arguments (whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd) together indicate sandbox escape exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package (≤3.11.3) present on asset
suggestion.rationale: Article states bypass affects 'nesting:true without explicit require' in versions ≤3.11.3. Detection of the vulnerable library artifact (*/node_modules/vm2/package.json, */node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js) is the primary asset-exposure hunt. Article provides reference UC_24_3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query file system for presence of vm2 package installation artifacts in node_modules directories. Cross-reference package.json version fields or nodevm.js file existence to enumerate affected hosts. This identifies the attack surface (vulnerable dependency exposure) before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious vm2 configuration patterns: nesting enabled without explicit require handling
suggestion.rationale: The core bypass exploits strict equality check on `options.require === false`, which is bypassed by omitting the require option entirely. Detection should hunt for vm2 instantiations with nesting:true and missing or undefined require parameter in application code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application source code (JavaScript/Node.js) for vm2 NodeVM instantiation patterns with nesting:true and either absent require option or require:undefined. Flag files in version control or deployed code as suspicious configuration. This catches attacker-crafted code or vulnerable application patterns before runtime.

suggestion.title: nodevm.js or exploit.js process execution or file creation events
suggestion.rationale: Article provides article-specific bespoke hunt (UC_24_1) hunting for named binaries 'nodevm.js' and 'exploit.js' as process execution or file modification indicators. These are explicit artifact names likely to appear in vm2 exploitation tooling or payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or file creation/modification events matching FileName in ('nodevm.js', 'exploit.js'). Flag especially when parent is Node.js or file is created in temp/writable directories. Low-noise high-specificity indicator for post-compromise artifact staging.

suggestion.title: Node.js require('process').exit() or process.getBuiltinModule('fs') from VM2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article states the bypass allows 'sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives' via process builtin. This is the direct exploitation step before shell spawning; detection must target the module escape itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js processes executing JavaScript code containing require('process'), process.getBuiltinModule, or Inspector.Runtime.evaluate calls that break sandbox isolation. Correlate with known-vulnerable vm2 package versions or suspicious npm install patterns.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2/NodeVM package deployment or dynamic require patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article's threat model depends on vm2 being installed and executed with untrusted code. Detection should capture deployment of vulnerable versions and suspicious script execution patterns that indicate vm2 is being used as an attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/update of vm2 package, NodeVM module imports in JavaScript files, or execution of Node.js scripts that dynamically require or instantiate vm2.NodeVM with attacker-controlled code payloads.

suggestion.title: Node.js process spawning Windows/Unix utilities without parent npm/package-manager context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute code in the host process' as end-state. Legitimate Node.js development spawns subprocesses (npm scripts, git hooks) with traceable parent context. Naked node.exe→cmd.exe chains without npm/yarn parent are suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe directly spawning system utilities (cmd, powershell, bash, curl, wget, whoami) where the NodeVM parent process is NOT preceded by npm.exe, npm.cmd, package.json parsing, or standard CI/CD orchestration patterns.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype constructor override in node.exe context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'localPromise constructor was changed to call this.then(undefined, eater)... missing call to resetPromiseSpecies' but no hunt targets gadget-chain activation. Missing: runtime detection of Promise prototype manipulation from within sandboxed context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe process loads of vm2 module with subsequent Promise method/constructor overwrites in the same execution context. Look for Symbol.species assignments or Promise.prototype manipulation in debug/trace output or via instrumentation hooks.

suggestion.title: vm2 sandbox context escape detection via failed-then-success require() patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker escapes to 'execute arbitrary commands on the host system' but no hunt detects the escape moment itself. Missing: detection of require() calls succeeding after vm2 context isolation should block them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe with require('child_process'), require('fs'), or require('path') appearing in syscall traces or module-load ETW events when running code that was supposed to be sandboxed by vm2.runInThisContext(). Requires Node.js with --trace-warnings or advanced instrumentation.

suggestion.title: Software inventory hunt: npm packages with vm2 ≤3.11.3
suggestion.rationale: Article suggests 'pair with DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory' but provides no inventory-based hunt. Reconnaissance phase critical for asset exposure scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDE DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory or parse package-lock.json / yarn.lock for vm2 version ≤3.11.3. Cross-reference with applications/services running on those devices. High-confidence asset exposure list for risk prioritization.

suggestion.title: Child process execution from node scripts with suspicious I/O redirection
suggestion.rationale: UC_25_2 detects spawned children but article emphasizes arbitrary command execution. Missing: detection of child_process calls with obfuscated or dynamically-constructed commands (common in shellcode/PoCs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe child processes where ProcessCommandLine contains hex-encoded, base64, or string.fromCharCode() patterns. Correlate with vm2 module presence in parent's working directory or command arguments.

suggestion.title: Windows command shell spawned with CONOUT$, nul redirects from node.exe
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape followed by 'arbitrary command execution' typically uses hidden/redirected subprocess execution. Article lacks this execution-hiding pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from node.exe where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains shell redirection (e.g. '< nul', '> CONOUT$') or where process is launched with CREATIONFLAGS indicating no window. High signal post-sandbox-escape.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable JSPI runtime + untrusted async code in vm2 — CVE-2026-47210 precondition
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'untrusted code is executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI'. No detection looks for JSPI-enabled runtimes or async code execution contexts within vm2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process starting with WebAssembly JSPI features enabled (runtime detection or feature-flag logging). Correlate with vm2 module load and script execution with async contexts. Look for command-line flags like --experimental-wasm-jspi or runtime version checks for JSPI support.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype.finally() manipulation or species override from vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is specifically about 'Promise.prototype.finally() in a way that bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening'. No behavioral detection targets Promise prototype manipulation or species bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual Promise manipulation patterns: Promise.prototype.finally reassignment, Promise[Symbol.species] override, or cross-realm Promise instantiation from sandbox contexts. Correlate with parent vm2 process and child process spawning. Requires runtime/engine-level instrumentation (V8 isolate boundaries).

suggestion.title: Host object leak from vm2 sandbox to Promise chain — species bypass indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article describes how JSPI-backed Promise reaches 'host-originate[d]' context. The exploit succeeds by leaking host objects into the sandbox's Promise chain, bypassing containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process memory access patterns or API calls from sandboxed vm2 context that reference host-memory addresses or system objects (e.g., require() calls, filesystem/network APIs) originating from Promise finalization paths. Look for cross-context object property access or constructor re-binding anomalies.

suggestion.title: vm2 module version downgrade or deliberate selection of vulnerable version (<=3.11.3)
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47210 is version-gated (<=3.11.3). Package installation patterns favoring the vulnerable version could signal intentional exploit preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn install logs for explicit version pinning of vm2 to <=3.11.3. Detect package-lock.json or yarn.lock modifications that lock a vulnerable version despite newer releases available. Correlate with untrusted code execution or test-environment setup.

suggestion.title: [LLM] LLM-driven eval() execution detection via process lineage and parent-command context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'real LLM-driven eval() tool execution' and detection queries reference 'official-a2a-example-real-llm-canary.py' suggesting the pipeline detected LLM steering. No UC directly captures Python subprocess spawning with LLM context (e.g., uvicorn process with A2A in cmdline spawning interpreters with suspicious code/imports).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a Python/uvicorn process bearing A2A indicators ('a2a-server.py', '--host 0.0.0.0', praisonai in cmdline) spawns child interpreters (sh, bash, python, perl) or suspicious utilities (curl, wget, nc) with cmdline arguments containing code patterns (__import__, compile, open('/etc/passwd')).

suggestion.title: [LLM] API key environment variable exfiltration via eval() side-channel
suggestion.rationale: Article's KQL hunt references GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in ProcessCommandLine and /etc/passwd access, indicating API credentials are at risk. No dedicated UC for detecting environment variable enumeration (env, printenv) or file reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_* in the context of A2A eval execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (env, printenv, cat, grep) spawned from uvicorn/PraisonAI context that read or enumerate credential-bearing files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, /etc/passwd) or environment variables containing API keys.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Egress connections from vulnerable PraisonAI process post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a true RCE vulnerability but contains no hunt for post-exploitation lateral movement or data exfiltration via outbound network connections initiated by the compromised uvicorn/Python process. eval() could establish C2 or exfil to attacker-controlled endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections initiated by processes matching A2A server signatures (uvicorn, python with a2a-server.py) to non-RFC1918 IP addresses or suspicious ports (443, 8080, 4444, 9999) shortly after /a2a POST requests are observed.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Malformed or code-injection JSON-RPC requests to /a2a endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'JSON-RPC POST' but provided detection (UC_11_2) only checks for existence of /a2a POST, not payload inspection. No UC detects LLM-prompt-injection or code-injection patterns within the JSON body (e.g., over-long expressions, Python builtins, __import__, exec).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to /a2a with JSON body containing suspicious Python built-in references (__import__, eval, exec, compile), file-path traversal (/etc/, /home/, C:\), or unusually long expression strings (>1KB) indicative of code injection attempts.

suggestion.title: [LLM] PraisonAI library import or installation in vulnerable version context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-47391 but no UC detects the actual import or installation of PraisonAI versions vulnerable to this CVE. pip install logs, Python site-packages changes, or dynamic import of praisonai.a2a modules should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pip install, git clone, or Python import statements for praisonai, praisonaiagents, or a2a libraries, especially in contexts lacking proper authentication or version pinning. Match against CVE-2026-47391 vulnerable version baseline.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform HTTP 403→200 IDOR exploitation signature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes accessing cross-workspace resources that should be forbidden. Exploitation pattern: HTTP 403 Forbidden on resource Y, then successful 200 access to same resource after ID manipulation = IDOR. Not detected by any existing UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each user/source, identify HTTP 403 responses to `/api/v1/workspaces/*/` endpoints followed within 30s by HTTP 200 responses to the same endpoint or similar resource. This 403→200 transition suggests IDOR resource ID enumeration and exploitation.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform permission group enumeration via member list requests
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'member-role privilege escalation' and cross-workspace member discovery. Missing explicit detection for `/api/v1/workspaces/*/members` GET requests used for reconnaissance. Article states vulnerability depends on attacker knowing valid member IDs in other workspaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GET requests to `/api/v1/workspaces/*/members*` endpoints by users not in workspace admin roles. Alert on users querying member lists from multiple workspaces in short timeframe (< 1 min) or users discovering high counts of members in workspaces they don't belong to.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform new account immediate workspace escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation via account manipulation. Attack chain: register account → assign to workspace with member POST → escalate role via PATCH. UC_10_4 is broader; this targets the specific escalation pattern post-registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account registration (POST /api/v1/auth/register, status 201) with immediate POST to `/api/v1/workspaces/*/members` adding that account to workspace, followed by PATCH to escalate the member's role to admin/elevated. Timeline should be <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform single source, multiple workspace resource access
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'dependency only checks that the caller is a member of the workspace_id in the URL prefix' — misses access from accounts that should not be members. Attacker with valid account in Workspace-A accesses resources in Workspace-B.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each user/API token, track which workspace IDs they successfully access (HTTP 200 to `/api/v1/workspaces/{id}/*`). Alert if a user accesses resources from workspaces they are not listed as members in, based on workspace membership API responses.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV=dev or Unset on Production Host
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'PLATFORM_ENV is unset... [and] defaults to 'dev'... safety check... only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev'. Bypassing the safety check is the root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for praisonai-platform uvicorn processes where PLATFORM_ENV environment variable is either missing, set to 'dev', or set to anything other than production-tier values (prod, production, stage, staging). Configuration baseline violation indicates hardcoded secret is active.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forge Signature Mismatch and Re-Use
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'token forgery for any user' using hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-me'. Attackers craft tokens with arbitrary claims and stolen/forged signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JWT validation events. Flag tokens that pass signature validation but contain impossible claims (admin=true for non-admin user IDs, role elevation, cross-workspace ownership). Correlate with repeated use of same token from different source IPs or timestamps.

suggestion.title: Single Principal Multiple Workspace Ownership Claim
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_9_3 describes cross-tenant operations. Forged tokens allow single attacker to claim ownership/admin access to workspaces belonging to different users/tenants simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In workspace API endpoints (/workspaces/{id}), track authorization principal (user_id from JWT claim). Flag when single principal successfully authenticates to 3+ workspaces with different owner_ids within 1 hour, especially if token issue times are identical (indicates batch token forgery).

suggestion.title: Workspace Member Addition from Unexpected Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'valid accounts' abuse and destructive workspace operations (UC_9_3 flags DELETE/PATCH). Attackers using forged tokens would add new admins to compromised workspaces for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt /workspaces/{id}/members POST/PATCH operations where the actor's JWT claims (user_id, role) do not match stored workspace membership. Flag additions of new admin members from IPs outside organization's typical ranges.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secret String in Logs or Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Article references hardcoded literal string 'dev-secret-change-me' as the default. Misconfigured deployments may log this value or have it visible in config dumps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search logs and captured config files for the string 'dev-secret-change-me' or variations. Also hunt for any environment variable output or debug logs containing PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET values. Presence indicates secret is either default or improperly logged.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Reconnaissance and Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Using LinkedIn Social Engineering to Deploy' — establishes initial-access phase and delivery mechanism. No UC generated despite clear behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid LinkedIn connection requests to security-adjacent personas, profile scraping activity (high view counts from single new account), and distribution of shortened URLs or suspicious domains in connection messages. Correlate with downloader/browser user-agent chains within 4 hours of connection acceptance.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Downloaded Files
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Custom macOS Malware' and social-engineering delivery implies user downloads malicious file. No execution-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS process creation from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or other user-writable directories with suspicious code-signing status (revoked, missing, or ad-hoc certificates). Baseline expected applications (Zoom, Slack installers) and alert on deviations, especially .app bundles launched within 5 minutes of download.

suggestion.title: Custom Malware Behavioral Pivot on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Custom macOS Malware' but provides no post-execution detection logic. Behavioral signatures should be extracted or suggested (process tree, file system writes, network callbacks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious parent-child process chains on macOS where unsigned/newly-seen binaries spawn shell interpreters (bash, zsh, sh) or call out-of-process frameworks (curl, wget, nc). Correlate with network egress to non-standard ports or to IPs without established trust relationships.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names HTTPSpy as Kimsuky's deployed tool. Pipeline missed execution context: 'Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPSpy process creation with suspicious parents or child process spawning. Correlate execution timing and network footprint against known Kimsuky C2 infrastructure. Flag registry modifications associated with malware persistence.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Persistence Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Second malware family explicitly named in title as arsenal expansion: 'Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor'. Pipeline failed to generate installation/persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HelloDoor binary drops in Startup folders or AppData, registry persistence mechanisms, and process execution sequences tied to malware delivery chains.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Abuse for Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes VS Code Tunnels as C2 infrastructure: 'VS Code Tunnels'. Legitimate tool abuse for protocol tunneling and obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code (code.exe, codeserver) spawning tunnel processes with abnormal outbound connectivity outside dev environment patterns. Monitor tunnel token creation and port forwarding configuration changes. Correlate with malware process timelines.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Multi-Malware Delivery Sequence Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes coordinated deployment of multiple tools implying sequenced attack: 'Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate execution timelines: initial payload → HTTPSpy installation → HelloDoor deployment → VS Code Tunnel setup. Flag compressed execution of multiple Kimsuky malware families on same host within hours.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Malware Family C2 Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have surfaced actor-level linking: HTTPSpy, HelloDoor, and VS Code Tunnel abuse all attributed to Kimsuky. Creates infrastructure correlation opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build actor-level IOC feeds linking HTTPSpy C2, HelloDoor C2, and VS Code Tunnel infrastructure on same host or shared timeframe. Correlate network patterns and timing across malware families.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials' — primary attack vector is NuGet supply chain, no detection logic generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet package installations from non-standard or attacker-controlled sources, packages with names mimicking banking/financial libraries, and .nupkg files with suspicious post-install scripts. Alert on nuget.exe or dotnet package operations spawning child processes for credential access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — secondary supply-chain vector via npm, zero detection coverage
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installations with typosquatted or entropy-high names, packages requesting system/credential permissions, and post-install hooks attempting cloud credential enumeration or environment variable exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Theft Post-Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Steals Banking Credentials' — core impact phase with no credential-access detection use case
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes spawned by NuGet/npm package manager contexts accessing credential stores (browser profiles, .NET credential cache, local banking app data). Flag processes reading %APPDATA%, credential provider APIs, or password manager DBs within 5min of package install.

suggestion.title: Cloud Secrets Exfiltration from Package Manager Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — exfiltration of cloud credentials is explicit threat, no detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS from NuGet/npm install contexts to non-CDN/non-registry IPs. Monitor for API calls to AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, or GCP Secret Manager within minutes of package installation or package-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Execution in NuGet .targets or npm postinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages inherently execute scripts at install time — execution phase has no detection use case
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .targets files downloaded with NuGet packages for suspicious PowerShell/cmd invocations. Alert on npm postinstall scripts containing base64-encoded commands, environment variable access, or network callbacks; track parent-child process trees from package-manager contexts.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Threat Actor Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes GREYVIBE as active threat actor targeting Ukraine; no IOCs or reconnaissance techniques proposed despite 'AI-Powered' language suggesting prior targeting research.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance activity targeting Ukrainian organizations: whois queries, domain registration checks, LinkedIn profiling, and email enumeration consistent with GREYVIBE prior-attack patterns. AI-powered campaigns typically precede with detailed org mapping.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Delivery (GREYVIBE)
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks' but pipeline offers no delivery or initial-access detection. AI tooling is likely used to generate convincing phishing content or social-engineering payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spear-phishing emails targeting Ukraine orgs with unusually fluent, personalized language or context-aware payload URLs. AI-generated content often has non-standard obfuscation patterns or unusual recipient specificity. Correlate with known GREYVIBE infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Over AI-Abstracted Channels
suggestion.rationale: AI-Powered attacks may use LLMs or chatbot APIs (Discord, Telegram bots, ChatGPT) for C2. Article title implies sophisticated tooling; pipeline included no C2 or exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing or API calls to LLM services, chatbot platforms, or cloud-hosted inference endpoints. Look for encoded payloads in Chat/API responses, unusual callback patterns from Ukrainian networks to AI-provider infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation for Ransomware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task' — this is the core attack primitive. Pipeline did not generate any detection for task creation, the initial execution vector for privilege-elevated encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or PowerShell.exe creating scheduled tasks with paths or arguments referencing system drives, encryption utilities, or random-looking payload names. Correlate with SYSTEM-level process spawning shortly before bulk file activity. Alert on any scheduled task execution with encryption-suspicious command-line arguments (rijndael, AES, crypt patterns).

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Privilege Execution for File Bulk Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'With Elevated Privileges' and 'Encrypt Local Drives' — indicates SYSTEM token assumption. Pipeline did not flag privilege escalation or SYSTEM execution in file encryption context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with TokenElevationType=SYSTEM spawning file-operation tools (cipher.exe, fsutil, encryption libraries). Look for parent processes that are scheduler components (taskhost.exe, svchost.exe hosting TaskScheduler service) spawning user-mode encryption or deletion tools.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption Activity on Local Drives
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes encryption of 'Local Drives' as the impact — central to ransomware detection. Pipeline generated no data-collection or impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity file writes or modifications to user data directories (C:\Users, network shares) from an executable running as SYSTEM, especially combined with file-extension renaming patterns (e.g., .txt → .encrypted or .ransom). Baseline normal system processes and alert on anomalies with low FP likelihood (e.g., known backup software excluded).

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence with Encryption Payload
suggestion.rationale: Scheduled tasks serve both execution and persistence in ransomware. Article does not clarify if task is one-shot or recurring, but persistence is a likely intent. Pipeline did not address scheduled-task-as-persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TaskScheduler operational logs for task creation with high-entropy or obfuscated names, unusual trigger times (e.g., on system startup, on idle), or actions pointing to system paths. Correlate creation time with initial compromise indicators. Check created task binaries for signing anomalies or non-Microsoft provenance.

suggestion.title: Command-Line Scheduled Task Registration
suggestion.rationale: Scheduled tasks are typically created via schtasks.exe or powershell.exe; article title does not specify method. Pipeline should flag command-line creation of system-privilege tasks to distinguish from legitimate admin tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe or schtasks.exe with parameters creating tasks that reference drives, encryption binaries, or obfuscated payloads. Correlate parent process (cmd.exe, explorer.exe, services.exe) with task creation privilege level. Baseline legitimate administrative task creation in your environment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Gemini API Activity
