suggestion.rationale: Article shows chain: compromised Entra account → Salesforce breach. Entra is the gating credential; unusual cloud-app access patterns post-compromise are detectable at the identity layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users with risky sign-in flags (impossible travel, atypical MFA behavior, token anomalies) accessing SaaS applications with unusual patterns: bulk API calls, access to non-assigned tenant resources, or activity at off-hours. Correlate Entra risk scores with downstream cloud-app activity.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Salesforce-Targeting Campaign Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers over the past year, breaching hundreds of companies worldwide.' Actor and target ecosystem are established; should integrate threat intel on gang infrastructure, phishing campaigns, and victim announcements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to Have I Been Pwned or dark-web monitoring feeds for ShinyHunters leak-site updates. Alert on new Salesforce victims posted. Cross-correlate phishing/vishing campaigns targeting Salesforce admins or customer-success teams with ShinyHunters known TTP timelines. Flag organizations in same vertical if ShinyHunters announces Salesforce breach.

suggestion.title: Telecom CPNI Data Exfiltration (Charter-Specific Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers claimed 'they also stole additional CPNI data' (Customer Proprietary Network Information—telecom-specific PII). This is a regulated data type; exfiltration should be detectable through telecom-specific DLP and database monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For telecom/ISP networks: monitor for access to CPNI databases (call history, plan details, billing records) by non-telecom-operations users or during non-business hours. Alert on SQL queries selecting multiple CPNI fields in bulk, or exports of CPNI tables to cloud storage, personal email, or external FTP/SFTP.

suggestion.title: Phishing via ChatGPT Web Summary Link Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface' — the core attack is injecting phishing URLs into ChatGPT summaries to bypass trust filters. Zero use cases generated despite this being the attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag URLs appearing in ChatGPT-generated summaries that point to newly registered domains, lookalike domains, or credential harvesting sites. Detect click patterns where users interact with ChatGPT content then immediately navigate to untrusted external domains. Correlate ChatGPT summary clicks with failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Post-ChatGPT Summary Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing vulnerability implicitly targets credential theft; the kill-chain flows from summary → click → credential submission. Pipeline generated zero collection/credential_access use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where ChatGPT usage is followed by login failures to non-standard domains or forms. Monitor for credential submission events to IPs/domains not in corporate asset inventory. Alert on unusual authentication patterns immediately following documented ChatGPT summary interactions.

suggestion.title: Abuse of ChatGPT Domain Reputation for Phishing Delivery Evasion
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability's impact depends on ChatGPT's trusted reputation being exploited to bypass email/web filters — defense evasion is implicit in the attack model. Zero T1562 techniques extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT-sourced URLs bypassing reputation-based URL filters. Detect homograph domains or internationalized domain names in summaries. Flag summaries containing encoded payloads, data exfiltration URLs, or command-and-control indicators masquerading as legitimate content.

suggestion.title: Detect Downloads from openew[.]app Malware Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'If the visitor clicks on the download button, they are brought to a website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal.' Domain is explicitly hostile infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests and downloads from openew[.]app. Cross-reference downloaded file hashes (Windows and macOS binaries mentioned with VirusTotal references) against known malware signatures. Monitor for follow-on infostealer or credential-access behaviors within 10 minutes of execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious ChatGPT Share Links Delivered via Google Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The "LLMShare" campaign...uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com.' This is initial-access vector combining search-ad abuse with platform misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag navigation to chatgpt.com/s/* share links where referer contains 'google' or 'ads' and destination renders fake outage/urgency content. Use content inspection or DOM monitoring to detect injected HTML claiming service unavailability or prompting downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Fake System Outage Social-Engineering Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they are presented with a rendered outage notice claiming the web version is unavailable and that they should download the desktop application instead' and 'Download our desktop app to continue.' Rendered via ChatGPT's own HTML/CSS engine for trust exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT/Claude artifact shares containing urgency language ('temporarily unavailable,' 'high traffic'), fake system alerts, or download prompts. Inspect for HTML/CSS mimicry of official OpenAI interfaces. Flag if such shares correlate with subsequent malware downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Hypervisor/Sandbox Evasion Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'BleepingComputer's test...found that it executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Indicates anti-analysis behavior post-delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with VM-detection patterns: queries to Hyper-V registry (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Hyper-V), WMI Win32_ComputerSystem checks, or CPUID instructions. Correlate with origin (openew[.]app downloads or ChatGPT-share-derived binaries) to identify evasion malware.

suggestion.title: Detect Infostealer Payload Installation and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'earlier campaigns abusing AI platform sharing features have distributed infostealers.' No specific payload identified in this instance, but earlier related campaigns confirm infostealer pattern and threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-execution behaviors from openew[.]app downloads: browser cache/cookie enumeration, credential store access (LSASS, Windows Vault), keylogging hooks, or network exfiltration to non-standard C2 endpoints. Flag unusual process lineage or DLL injection.

suggestion.title: Detect Claude Artifact ClickFix Command-Injection Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Push Security also observed attacks abusing Claude Artifacts...to host ClickFix-style lures that tricked users into executing malicious commands.' Parallel attack vector using same social-engineering pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor claude.ai artifact shares for ClickFix-style payloads: fake installation wizards, system-error dialogs, or 'run this command' instructions. Detect embedded shell one-liners, PowerShell scripts, or obfuscated code blocks. Alert if artifact is subsequently followed by command execution on user device.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions'; no use case targets exploitation attempts against the public-facing auth mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS auth logs for failed login sequences followed by successful session establishment without credential submission; alert on management interface access from external IPs without preceding authentication success; detect exploitation tool signatures matching CVE-2026-0257.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Tunnel Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes how vulnerability 'establish[es] an unauthorized VPN connection'; no use case targets VPN tunnel anomalies correlated with auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN tunnel initiations without corresponding successful administrative authentication in PAN-OS event logs; correlate management interface compromise with tunnel creation; flag tunnels from external sources originating from exploited sessions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Management Interface Access from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-0257 is exposed PAN-OS; article implies public-facing exposure but no use case covers detection of management interface access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external HTTP/HTTPS connections to PAN-OS management ports (443, 3978, 10443); flag rapid authentication failure clusters followed by successful access from same source; alert on geographically impossible access patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised Device Using Default or Weak Credentials at Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong' — direct mitigation implies weak creds were the infection vector for 17M devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated failed and successful authentication attempts to network device management interfaces (SSH, Telnet, HTTP) using default vendor credentials (admin/admin, root/root, ubnt/ubnt). Track successful logins followed by unexpected privileged activity within minutes. Correlation with mass device scanning precedes infection waves.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Execution and C2 Communication Over Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 200+ C2 servers seized; botnet phones home to infrastructure. 'The seized servers controlled computers, tablets, and smartphones' indicates C2 channel establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from compromised device IPs to known seized server ranges (Netherlands hosting provider IP space). Flag non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 1080, 9090) from consumer devices. Detect beaconing patterns: consistent intervals, fixed packet sizes, encrypted payloads to proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Proxy-Like Traffic Forwarding from Infected Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Asocks service provided 'residential proxies' and article notes 'malicious traffic proxying' was a botnet use case — compromised devices redirecting third-party traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5/HTTP proxy requests originating from consumer endpoints to third-party IP ranges with low reputation. Monitor for 'Host: 0.0.0.0' headers, CONNECT tunneling abuse, and traffic relaying inconsistent with device role. Correlate multiple simultaneous tunnels from single source (residential proxy footprint).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Process Detection on Non-Mining Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'cryptocurrency mining' as a botnet impact. 17M devices were repurposed for computational tasks without owner consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for xmrig, stratum, or cryptonote processes (or variants named svchost.exe, rundll32.exe in non-standard paths). Detect sustained high CPU >70% utilization for hours on non-workstation devices (routers, IoT). Cross-reference process parent (often malware installer) and check for mining pool domains in netstat.

suggestion.title: Botnet Device Firmware Out-of-Date Against Known Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation: 'the latest firmware update has been applied' — implies 17M devices were running outdated firmware with known RCE/auth-bypass flaws.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory firmware versions across all network devices (routers, IoT, NVR, printers). Flag any device with firmware release date >6 months old. Cross-reference against CVE databases (e.g., CVE-2023-XXXX for that device model). Alert on gap >2 minor versions from current release.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Distributed Denial-of-Service Activity from Compromised Botnet Node
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks' as primary botnet purpose. Infected devices became DDoS agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume outbound traffic to single or few external IPs from consumer devices (asymmetric egress bandwidth). Detect SYN floods, UDP amplification, HTTP floods, or slowloris patterns. Flag devices sending traffic to known victim/infrastructure honeypots. Correlate with hundreds/thousands of other devices exhibiting identical traffic signature (botnet synchronization).

suggestion.title: vm2 sandbox-escape PoC strings in HTTP request body/WAF logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack method: 'By combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__`, `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupSetter__`, and Node.js's `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` Error' — these are concrete, searchable strings that would appear in HTTP payloads attempting exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request bodies and WAF logs for PoC code patterns including __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, and Buffer.call.call sequences. Correlate to Node.js-based services running vm2. High confidence due to specificity of PoC.

suggestion.title: Node.exe spawning unexpected OS shells post-vm2 exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article summary states 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code' — this attack step directly manifests as node.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash. Install phase of kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe as parent process spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, wmic.exe). Critical path post-exploitation. Filter out expected process trees from legitimate Node applications.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package inventory (≤3.11.3) present on systems
suggestion.rationale: Article title and advisory reference indicate versions ≤3.11.3 are vulnerable. Weapon/recon phase: identify assets before exploitation can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for vm2 package with version matching regex ^([0-2]\.|3\.([0-9]|10|11)(\.[0-3])?$). High confidence indicator of exploitable asset. Medium confidence due to potential false positives in dev/test environments.

suggestion.title: NodeVM instantiation with untrusted code source
suggestion.rationale: Article states NodeVM is used to 'block dangerous Node.js builtins' for sandboxing untrusted code. No detection suggested for the instantiation of NodeVM context itself, which would be first indicator of intended sandboxing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process with vm2/NodeVM library loaded and subsequent file I/O of potentially untrusted input (stdin, network, tmp directories, user-writable paths). Look for require('vm2') or new NodeVM() instantiations in process command-line or script arguments.

suggestion.title: Sandboxed context-to-host privilege boundary crossing via process builtin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'process' builtin as denylist-bypass vector allowing 'sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives.' No hunt targets the use of process object from within NodeVM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js process (parent or self) that loads/spawns child processes with high privilege indicators (SYSTEM, Administrator, >normal user privilege token) immediately after interpreter invocation, especially if parent was started with restricted/sandboxed user context or marked as VM/container process.

suggestion.title: Inspector protocol abuse (inspector/promises) for debugger breakout
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'inspector/promises' as second denylist-bypass vector but no dedicated detection for inspector protocol activation. Debugger protocol access from sandboxed context is strong indicator of escape attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node.js processes with --inspect, --inspect-brk, or --inspect-port arguments OR opening listening sockets on debugging ports (9229, 9230). Cross-reference with low-privilege parent process or VM/container indicators. inspector/promises module require is difficult to detect but listening on debug ports is high-signal.

suggestion.title: vm2 instantiation with untrusted script input
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers to write code which can escape.' Attacker-supplied code to vm2.run() or vm2.VM() is the entry point; detection should focus on vm2 initialization with external input sources before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe loading vm2 module followed by vm.run() or new vm.VM() calls where script content originates from network sources, file drops, or unsanitized user input. Target applications embedding vm2 for REPL, template engines, or plugin sandboxing.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype and Symbol.species mutations in JavaScript contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: missing resetPromiseSpecies allows Symbol.species manipulation. Direct detection of Symbol mutations in Promise chain could catch exploitation earlier than post-escape process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript source files or command-line arguments for Symbol.species assignments, Promise.prototype methods being overridden, or prototype chain mutations. High confidence in untrusted script contexts (user file uploads, dynamic eval, template injection).

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI / Suspenders API called from untrusted vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sandbox escape vulnerability in vm2 allows arbitrary code execution...when untrusted code is executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI (WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending)' — detect node.exe invoked with JSPI/Suspenders flags or executing code containing these APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Node.js processes with command-line flags enabling JSPI (--experimental-wasm-suspenders or equivalent) or code arguments containing WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending API calls. Correlate with vm2 module presence to isolate sandbox environments.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype mutation / species bypass from untrusted scope — vm2 sandbox escape indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally() in a way that bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening' — detect attempts to access or modify Promise internals from sandboxed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js application logs or crash dumps for stack traces showing Promise.__species__ access, Promise.prototype mutations, or .finally() calls originating from untrusted/sandbox scope. Correlate timing with vm2 script execution.

suggestion.title: Parent process (web framework / CI system) spawns Node.js with vm2 script evaluation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation when 'untrusted code is executed' in vm2—the trigger is user-controlled code reaching vm2. Detect applications instantiating vm2 with dynamic/unsanitized script arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify parent processes (web servers, CI runners, cloud functions) spawning node.exe with vm2 module imports where script/code arguments are derived from untrusted sources (request body, user upload, git push, webhook). Look for vm2.runInNewContext() or require('vm2') patterns in parent application code.

suggestion.title: [HUNT] PraisonAI-spawned Python imports restricted modules post-sandbox-escape
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary OS command execution' via __import__ extraction from builtins. After print.__self__ + vars(), attacker loads os, subprocess, socket. No hunt currently covers restricted-module import patterns post-sandbox defeat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes spawned by PraisonAI for .so/.pyd loads of os, subprocess, socket, sys.modules access via dlopen/mmap syscalls, or .pyc file writes in temp directories. High-fidelity: correlate with UC_13_6 hit in same parent process.

suggestion.title: [HUNT] Shell spawned by PraisonAI exfiltrating credentials outbound or executing C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'completely defeating the sandbox' implies arbitrary command execution. Hunts cover discovery/read but not egress: credential exfil, C2 callback, reverse shell. Article phrase implies attacker gains full OS control post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate shell spawns (sh/bash/cmd from Python) with outbound egress to non-RFC1918 IP within 60s. Flag curl/wget/nc child processes with env-var or /etc/passwd in arguments. Alert on simultaneous /etc/shadow read + external network connection.

suggestion.title: [HUNT] Obfuscated __import__ patterns (getattr, eval, string concatenation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'runtime string construction' for __import__. Attacker may use getattr(print, '__self__'), eval('__import__'), or chr() chains to defeat UC_13_6 literal pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Python cmdline with getattr(, '__self__', eval(, exec(, compile(, chr(*), ord(, ''.join([, or hex/octal escape sequences in context of PraisonAI parent. Cross-reference with UC_13_5 (shell spawn) to confirm post-exploit chain.

suggestion.title: [HUNT] Privilege escalation or lateral-movement post-PraisonAI sandbox-escape
suggestion.rationale: After achieving host-level code execution, attacker pivots: credential dumping (SAM, LSASS, /etc/shadow), privilege escalation (sudo, setuid), lateral movement (SSH keys, WMI). Article implies adversary controls host; no hunt for post-ex phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting UC_13_5 discovery phase, look for follow-on within 5 min: credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, hashcat, shadow reads), sudo/polkit abuse, kernel exploits, or lateral-move tools (SSH keygen, wmic, RDP). Alert on any privesc indicator in shell spawned by PraisonAI.

suggestion.title: [HUNT] PraisonAI execute_code receiving malicious prompt with sandbox-escape payload
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires attacker-controlled input to execute_code(). Article doesn't specify delivery (prompt injection, API, user input), implying detection should monitor for suspicious code patterns inbound to the vulnerable function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PraisonAI application/debug logs for execute_code() calls with arguments containing print.__self__, __import__, builtins, getattr, vars(, or other reflection keywords. Correlate with source IP/user to identify external vs. internal origin. High-confidence if source is untrusted (public API, external user).

suggestion.title: [HUNT] Base64/hex-encoded payload in Python subprocess (encoding obfuscation)
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may obfuscate exploit chain using base64 -d, xxd -r, or hex decoding. Article describes 'string construction'; attacker could encode print.__self__ payload to evade UC_13_6 literal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python-spawned shell processes with base64 -d, xxd -r, od, or tr in command line, especially with pipe to sh/bash/cmd. Examine decoded content for reflection keywords. Alert on rare encoding chains (chcp + base64, iconv + eval).

suggestion.title: PraisonAI vulnerable deployment configuration creation — authentication disabled, 0.0.0.0 bind
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability as 'authentication disabled by default' with deployment 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per recommended sample YAML'. No UC hunts for creation/modification of the vulnerable config files during initial deployment, only for process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .yaml, .yml, or generated .py files created/modified in user/deployment directories with patterns including 'praisonai', 'generate_api_server_code', Flask routing to /chat or /agents endpoints, and host bindings to 0.0.0.0 or 127.0.0.1 with absent/disabled authentication decorators.

suggestion.title: LLM agent tool discovery via unauthenticated /agents endpoint enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article exposes '/agents' endpoint unauthenticated but UC_14_5 only hunts /chat POSTs. Attacker can enumerate agent configurations and tool definitions via /agents GET requests — distinct account/resource discovery attack step with no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GET requests to /agents returning 200 status with large JSON responses (>5KB) containing agent metadata or tool definitions, especially if followed by POST /chat requests with tool invocations matching enumerated agent capabilities.

suggestion.title: Successful command execution via LLM tool-use — shell/curl output in /chat response body
suggestion.rationale: UC_14_5 hunts POST volume to detect probes; missing detection for successful exploitation where response bodies contain command artifacts (bash error output, curl status codes, stderr fields, shell command echoes indicating actual tool execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST requests to /chat endpoint with response bodies containing bash error patterns ('command not found', 'permission denied'), curl/wget output headers, or JSON-wrapped stderr/stdout fields — indicating successful command execution via LLM agent tool invocation.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery Indicators – Known Hardcoded Key Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hardcoded literal `"dev-secret-change-me"`' — no hunt for abnormal JWT claims or tokens signed with this key in application/auth logs. Logs containing token validation failures or suspicious token payload structures should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application authentication logs for JWT tokens with 'iss' claim matching 'dev' or encoding mismatches when compared against production-signed tokens. Cross-reference token timestamps against system time to detect pregenerated or backdated tokens. Look for token validation bypass patterns in web application firewalls or API gateway logs.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV and PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET Environment Variable Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'safety check only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev' and default PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET = 'dev-secret-change-me'. No hunt for exposure of these env vars via logs, process inspection, or config file reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt process creation and environment dumps for leaked PLATFORM_ENV and PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET values, particularly when set to 'dev' or 'dev-secret-change-me'. Monitor config file access (docker-compose.yml, .env, environ) in the application working directory. Alert on env var exfiltration via process inspection tools or container escape techniques.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Workspace Tenant Pivot via Forged Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cross-tenant workspace access' as post-exploitation lateral movement. Current UC_10_3 depends on web logs; need alternative for auth systems lacking full request logging. Look for workspace access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If praisonai-platform integrates with identity providers, profile legitimate workspace access patterns per authenticated user over baseline period. Flag workspace accesses from users in different geographic regions within seconds (impossible for human), accesses to workspaces the user has never accessed before, or accesses by service accounts to customer workspaces.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Deployment – Missing or Weak JWT Secret Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'when PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is unset' and 'default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev'. No hunt for configuration audit or secrets management logs to detect unset critical secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Kubernetes or container environments, audit ConfigMap and Secret creation/access events for praisonai-platform namespaces. Alert when PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is absent, equals 'dev-secret-change-me', or PLATFORM_ENV is unset or 'dev' in production-tagged workloads. In non-containerized, monitor /etc/environment, .env file reads, and startup logs for missing secret warnings.

suggestion.title: Uvicorn Process with Implicit Hardcoded JWT Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions uvicorn as the web server launching praisonai_platform.api.app. No hunt exists for uvicorn startup with unset or default-valued JWT env vars in production-like network zones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uvicorn processes (Processes.process_name = 'uvicorn' or InitiatingProcessFileName) launching praisonai_platform.api.app without PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET explicitly set in parent environment or command line. Correlate with network exposure (inbound listening on HTTP/HTTPS) and lack of reverse-proxy auth (X-Forwarded-* headers absent in logs). Distinguish from safe dev/test instances by network zone or host naming convention.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Non-admin workspace-member enumeration of owner/admin user accounts before privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Any workspace member can promote themselves or others to owner,' implying attacker first identifies target accounts (current owners or other members to demote). Article does not describe reconnaissance phase, but attack chain logically includes user discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to workspace-member listing or user-enumeration endpoints by non-admin users, followed within 10 minutes by a PATCH role-change request. Flag if same source queries `/workspaces/{id}/members` or similar role-listing endpoint, then issues a PATCH to escalate themselves or demote an enumerated owner.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Newly-escalated owner performing workspace user-invitation or account-creation
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1136.003 (Create Account: Cloud Account) and T1531 (Account Access Removal) but provides no narrative evidence. Logically, attacker escalates to owner to persist access via new accounts or disable legitimate owners. No hunt detects post-escalation account creation or user invitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a workspace member successfully executes PATCH to gain owner role, detect subsequent POST requests to user-invitation, account-creation, or workspace-access-grant endpoints from the same source IP/user. Alert if a member-to-owner promotion is followed by inviting external email domains or creating new workspace accounts within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Existing workspace-owner role demotion immediately before or after member self-promotion
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly mention removing legitimate admin access, but privilege-escalation attacks commonly include disabling audit/oversight. Demoting an existing owner from the target workspace is a defense-evasion pattern. No hunt captures owner-removal chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{owner_user_id} where role is downgraded from 'owner' to 'member', 'viewer', or 'read_only', immediately preceded or followed by a separate PATCH promoting a different user (or the same attacker account) to owner. Alert on any demotion+promotion pair within a 5-minute window from the same or related source IPs.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Rapid workspace-role changes affecting authorization-audit or logging accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation but does not mention how attackers evade detection logs. If workspace has designated audit users, compliance accounts, or logging-service accounts, an attacker may demote or disable these to hide traces. No hunt detects targeting of sensitive roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a baseline of workspace accounts with audit, compliance, or logging-related role names or descriptions. Alert when any member issues PATCH requests that demote, delete, or revoke permissions from these sensitive accounts. Escalate if demotion occurs after a successful privilege-escalation PATCH in the same workspace.

suggestion.title: AI Code Generation Without Integrated Security Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI also accelerated the generation of insecure code and vulnerable dependencies. Without new controls, Relay Network risked scaling vulnerabilities.' Detect GitHub Copilot or similar tools deployed without corresponding Snyk/SAST hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub Copilot, Codeium, or comparable AI coding assistants execute on developer machines in repositories lacking integrated pre-commit security scanning or Snyk policy enforcement. Correlate AI tool activity with absence of corresponding security scan logs.

suggestion.title: Shadow AI Services Bypassing Security Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Providing sanctioned tools also helps reduce shadow AI by discouraging developers from turning to unmanaged consumer services.' Detect access to unauthorized AI/LLM services (ChatGPT, unauthorized Claude instances) outside approved GitHub Copilot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for developers accessing consumer AI endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral APIs) from corporate networks or development machines. Alert on unapproved LLM services used for code generation outside auditable channels.

suggestion.title: Circumvention of Pre-Commit Security Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Esaie extended the capability with custom pre-commit hooks...Before this even makes it to the PR, I want it to scan and catch everything.' Detect disabling, bypassing, or deletion of pre-commit security enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git commits using `--no-verify`, `GIT_SKIP_HOOKS`, or `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file deletion/modification. Flag commits in repositories with enforced pre-commit scans that bypass the security hook without corresponding remediation or override records.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Profile Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'LinkedIn Social Engineering' is the attack vector. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for anomalous LinkedIn profile creation, rapid connection requests, or impersonation of known employees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or compromised LinkedIn accounts initiating connection requests to target organization employees, especially those with no prior connection history. Cross-correlate with subsequent email opens, attachment downloads, or malware execution within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Execution Post-Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deploy custom macOS malware' via social engineering. Detection needed for unusual process spawning on macOS following user interaction with external links or attachments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on macOS processes with low/zero reputation, unsigned code signature, or unusual parent-child relationships executing within 10 minutes of user clicking external links or opening email attachments sourced from social media platforms.

suggestion.title: Custom macOS Malware Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'custom' malware. Generic file-hash detections insufficient; behavioral indicators (library injection, process hollowing, obfuscation) required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect macOS processes with environment variables like DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, unsigned or recently-modified binaries in temp directories, process memory protection flags removed, or network connections immediately after execution.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article language ('deploy') suggests persistence, not one-time execution. Custom macOS malware typically persists via plist-based launch mechanisms (T1547.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or system-wide launch directories. Flag if timestamps correlate with social engineering events or if referenced binaries have low reputation.

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Threat Actor Campaign Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'JINX-0164.' Pipeline failed to extract this actor identifier for threat-intel enrichment, historical pattern matching, and cross-organizational alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain IOC list for JINX-0164 (known infrastructure, malware signatures, LinkedIn profile patterns). Trigger alerts on new detections matching historical JINX-0164 TTP: LinkedIn-based targeting, macOS-specific payloads, custom malware families.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Gateway Activity from LinkedIn Referrers
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering attack via LinkedIn likely followed by phishing emails or malware delivery. Detection needed at email gateway for messages from compromised accounts or external URLs masquerading as LinkedIn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with LinkedIn profile links, shortened URLs redirecting to file-hosting services, or sender reputation anomalies within 24 hours of LinkedIn connection requests to target employees.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnels Abuse for Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Expands Arsenal with VS Code Tunnels.' This is legitimate-tool abuse (T1219) for lateral movement. Code.exe spawned with tunnel/server CLI arguments or VSCode tunnel service listeners establish post-compromise control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Code.exe or VSCode processes with --remote-auth=off, --tunnel-password, or server-listen command-line arguments. Alert on tunnel service listening on non-loopback interfaces. Cross-correlate process parent (cmd.exe, PowerShell) with execution from staged directories.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy C2 Beaconing and Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Deploys HTTPSpy.' Named as new Kimsuky C2 tool. Implies HTTP/HTTPS-based command callbacks, data exfiltration channel (T1041).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish behavioral baseline: HTTPSpy process name, parent (likely legitimate dropper), network callbacks. Monitor for periodic HTTP/HTTPS requests with C2-like patterns (fixed intervals, encoded payloads, suspicious URI paths). Alert on processes binding HTTP listeners or spawning with sockets.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Delivery and Post-Exploitation Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor.' Context suggests delivery mechanism or post-exploitation tool. Title structure implies active deployment in intrusions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HelloDoor likely delivered as file attachment or via web download. Monitor for HelloDoor binary creation in temp/staging directories, unusual child processes (cmd.exe, PowerShell, certutil, net.exe), and command-line arguments suggesting credential access or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Legitimate VSCode Process Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Article context: Kimsuky 'expands arsenal'—implies toolkit refinement including evasion. VSCode is signed and whitelisted; abuse masks C2/lateral movement activity (T1036.003, T1036.005).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: VSCode process abuse bypasses application-allow lists. Monitor for Code.exe network activity deviating from baseline (enterprise VSCode development). Detect unsigned or Microsoft-signed but suspicious child processes. Flag VSCode execution with administrative tokens or from non-standard paths (%temp%, %appdata%, attacker-staged folders).

suggestion.title: Persistence via VSCode Extensions or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Expands Arsenal'—implies persistence for sustained access. VSCode supports extension-based code execution and auto-load on startup (T1547.014).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VSCode extension directory (%userprofile%\.vscode\extensions) for suspicious extension creation or modification. Alert on registry changes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSCode\Extensions or Run/RunOnce keys launching VSCode with unusual arguments. Detect VSCode DLL hijacking via PATH manipulation or sideloading.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Toolkit Fingerprinting via Network and Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article names three distinct new tools—HTTPSpy, HelloDoor, VSCode Tunnels abuse. These establish Kimsuky operational footprint (T1081, T1005 collection implications embedded in C2 channel design).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTPSpy process spawning, VSCode tunnel listener establishment, and HelloDoor execution as signature cluster for Kimsuky campaigns. Alert when all three indicators observed in same session or host. Monitor for tool-specific network signatures (HTTPSpy request/response patterns, tunnel handshake flows).

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation with Credential Harvesting Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials'—detection must capture installation of typosquatted or novel packages followed by process behavior indicative of credential access (lsass.exe interaction, browser credential store reads, banking app memory inspection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on NuGet.exe or dotnet.exe restore/install operations installing packages with minimal metadata, recent creation dates, or names resembling banking/security libraries (Sicoob-like variants). Correlate with child processes attempting to access credential stores or inject into browser/banking application memory.

suggestion.title: Cloud Secret Exfiltration Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets'—detection should identify environment variable enumeration and network exfiltration of AWS/Azure/GCP credentials immediately following npm package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn install processes and their children for access to credential paths (.aws/credentials, .azure, KUBECONFIG) and environment variable reads (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET). Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP POST to rare or reputation-unknown domains within 60 seconds of credential file access.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Script Execution from Package Cache
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute embedded payloads via install hooks or post-install scripts; detection must identify suspicious PowerShell/cmd execution spawned during or immediately after package installation in package-controlled directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all PowerShell and cmd.exe execution within NuGet cache (%USERPROFILE%\.nuget), npm cache, and .csproj post-install hook directories. Alert on -EncodedCommand, obfuscated code, or use of common credential-theft tools (curl, Invoke-WebRequest, net.exe, reg.exe querying credential repositories).

suggestion.title: C2 Communication and Persistence Establishment from Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages establish persistent backdoor access; detection must identify scheduled tasks, service installations, registry persistence, or C2 beaconing spawned by package-related processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track child processes spawned by NuGet/npm installation for schtasks.exe or net.exe service creation, modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, and suspicious network connections (non-standard ports, long intervals, low entropy payloads indicating C2 handshake).

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Untrusted or Unexpected Registry Sources
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often redirect package installs to rogue registries or compromise package.json/packages.config to point to malicious sources; detection should identify registry source changes or installations from sources outside organizational allowlist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .nuget/NuGet.Config and .npmrc for runtime modifications to package sources. Alert on NuGet.exe/npm install with explicit -Source flags pointing to non-standard registries, and track package.json/packages.config changes that introduce unfamiliar package names or versions inconsistent with project history.

suggestion.title: Memory or File-Based Credential Dumping from Banking Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states banking credential theft; detection must identify tools or techniques targeting banking app memory, browser credential caches, or keychain access following package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation or image loads of credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump, Get-Credential) post-package-install. Alert on file access to browser credential databases, banking app config directories, or .dll/.so/.dylib loading in browser/banking processes from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Detect GREYVIBE Infrastructure and C2 Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Russia-Linked GREYVIBE' as threat actor targeting Ukraine, but pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no actor-specific detections. C2 domains, malware hashes, or network signatures attributable to GREYVIBE should be surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound/outbound network connections to known or suspected GREYVIBE C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS queries to domains previously linked to the group, or protocol anomalies in C2 traffic.

suggestion.title: Detect AI-Assisted Phishing or Reconnaissance Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks' but pipeline mapped zero techniques related to LLM-assisted reconnaissance, phishing, or social engineering. No detection logic for AI-generated lures or automated enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with anomalous linguistic patterns (overuse of common phrases, low variance in templates) or bulk reconnaissance activities (account enumeration, domain crawling) consistent with LLM-generated campaigns targeting Ukrainian entities.

suggestion.title: Detect Targeting of Ukrainian Government and Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states targets 'Ukraine'—no geolocation or sector-specific filtering applied. Pipeline should generate detections specific to Ukrainian .ua domains, government networks, and CRIT infrastructure sectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email/malware delivery attempts targeting Ukrainian government agencies, critical infrastructure (energy, telecom), or .ua domain holders. Correlate with known GREYVIBE tooling or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation Under SYSTEM Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'SYSTEM Scheduled Task' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection for scheduled task creation despite this being the stated persistence/execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on schtasks.exe or powershell.exe creating scheduled tasks with /ru:SYSTEM. Flag tasks created from non-standard parent processes, from %TEMP%/%APPDATA%, or lacking network connectivity context. Correlate creation time with prior anomalous process execution.

suggestion.title: High-Velocity File Write Activity Consistent with Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Encrypt Local Drives'—ransomware encryption manifests as sustained, high-throughput write operations. No use case generated for this impact-phase signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormally high file-write counts or sustained write throughput from SYSTEM-account processes targeting user-data directories (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, shares). Flag as urgent if parent process is taskhostw.exe or spawned by recent scheduled task.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM Context Prior to Task Scheduling
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires elevation to SYSTEM to create system-level scheduled tasks. No detection surfaced for T1134, T1548, or process-token manipulation preceding scheduled-task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-SYSTEM user processes creating child processes with SYSTEM integrity. Correlate token-elevation events temporally with schtasks.exe execution. Alert on unusual process ancestry (e.g., explorer.exe → cmd.exe → schtasks.exe → elevated context).

suggestion.title: Process Execution Spawned from Recently-Created Scheduled Task
suggestion.rationale: Once SYSTEM task is registered, it spawns the actual encryption process. No UC captures execution of binaries from scheduled-task contexts or taskhostw parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes with parent taskhostw.exe spawned from scheduled tasks created within the prior hour. Flag non-standard or packed executables. Correlate command-line arguments with file enumeration (dir, Get-ChildItem) or encryption-tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Logical Drive Enumeration and Network Share Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware enumerates drives and shares before encrypting. Title mentions 'Local Drives'—implies discovery phase. No UC for drive/share enumeration by ransomware context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid directory traversals (dir /s /b, Get-ChildItem -Recurse) or WMI queries for logicaldisk information from SYSTEM-context processes. Flag net view commands enumerating shares. Correlate with scheduled-task parent or non-admin child of explorer.exe.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Write-to-Disk or In-Memory Injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires staging ransomware binary or DLL before execution. Title implies a pre-execution payload phase but pipeline surfaced no initial-access/delivery detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executable or DLL writes to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or ProgramData immediately preceding privilege escalation or scheduled-task creation. Alert on file entropy, signatures of packed/obfuscated malware. Correlate file-write timestamps with subsequent elevation/task-creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Gemini API Calls for Malware/Exploit Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks'—pipeline generated zero detection for LLM-assisted code or payload development, the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT/Gemini API endpoints for requests containing keywords: 'exploit', 'payload', 'phishing', 'malware', 'reverse shell', 'obfuscate'. Flag accounts making repeated requests for code generation combined with suspicious follow-up infrastructure queries or file uploads.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Actor Infrastructure and IOC Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor 'GREYVIBE' appears in article title but zero IOCs or actor identifiers were extracted. Pipeline should surface all known domains, IPs, or file hashes attributed to this group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any historical or newly discovered IOCs, malware families, or C2 infrastructure associated with GREYVIBE. Correlate with recent phishing campaigns or suspicious OAuth token usage from high-risk Gemini/ChatGPT API consumers.

suggestion.title: Mass Phishing Email Generation via LLM APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes LLM-assisted attacks but pipeline has no detection for high-volume phishing campaigns, which is the most probable attack surface given LLM abuse headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect campaigns with identical grammatical/stylistic patterns, statistical anomalies consistent with LLM output (uniform token entropy, template placeholders). Flag sudden spike in phishing emails from same sender infrastructure or identical redirect domains.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attack: Public Registry Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Article title states packages 'abuse dependency confusion'—fundamental attack vector where attacker publishes packages to public npm registry with names matching private scopes. No use case captures the install-time package resolution anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/resolution behavior for attempts to pull from public registry when .npmrc or package.json lockfile indicates private scope. Flag when package version jumps or source changes unexpectedly between runs.

suggestion.title: Environment Profiling via npm Postinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack goal is to 'profile developer environments'—malicious postinstall scripts commonly harvest env vars, git configs, credentials. No use case detects reconnaissance-phase exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall or preinstall scripts that invoke shell builtins (env, printenv, cat ~/.gitconfig, npm config), enumerate /usr/bin or PATHEXT, or spawn curl/wget immediately after install.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Metadata Mimicry
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion attacks succeed via typosquatting or name confusion. Pipeline should flag packages with names similar to popular legitimate packages or internal company scopes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed npm packages against known-good registry snapshots; flag installs of packages where name is edit-distance ≤2 from legitimate packages or contain common obfuscation patterns (extra underscores, hyphens, numbers appended to legitimate names).

suggestion.title: Outbound Data Exfiltration from Build/Dev Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'developer and build environments' for reconnaissance. Malicious packages must exfiltrate collected data; no use case detects anomalous egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from npm/node processes to non-standard destinations. Alert on DNS queries for newly-registered or suspicious domains during/immediately after npm install phases. Correlate with environment collection activity.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing or Code Injection from Node Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises often inject into trusted runtimes. Title mentions profiling but tactics likely include runtime injection. No use case covers process manipulation during install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node.exe or npm.exe spawning unexpected child processes (powershell, cmd, bash) without explicit user script invocation, or creating threads in explorer/svchost. Monitor API calls indicating DLL injection (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory).

suggestion.title: Forged Authentication Override Cookie Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers can retrieve the public certificates exposed by a GlobalProtect portal or gateway, generate a forged authentication override cookie for an arbitrary user, and authenticate without knowing valid credentials.' Core attack step with no corresponding detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect authentication override cookie validation events for signature verification failures on admin account authentication. Alert when authentication override cookies decrypt successfully but fail integrity checks, or when admin account VPN access occurs without corresponding successful credential authentication in the pre-VPN window.

suggestion.title: HTTPS Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies reconnaissance prerequisite: 'attackers can retrieve the public certificates exposed by a GlobalProtect portal or gateway' and 'use it to create forged cookies.' Certificate extraction activity is directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of X.509 certificates served by GlobalProtect HTTPS interfaces. Alert on repeated certificate extraction requests from single source IPs within short time windows, or certificate extraction followed within minutes by VPN authentication anomalies from the same source.

suggestion.title: Admin Account VPN Authentication via Override Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attacks began with hackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account.' Baseline admin VPN access should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin account VPN authentication when GlobalProtect authentication override is enabled. Establish baseline for expected admin VPN sessions and flag deviations: new geographic locations, unusual timing, or infrastructure sourced from cloud hosting providers (Vultr, AWS, etc.).

suggestion.title: Certificate Reuse Across HTTPS and Auth Override Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies.' Configuration-level detection of vulnerable state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Configuration audit: Flag GlobalProtect devices where the certificate used for authentication override cookie operations matches the certificate used for HTTPS service (portal/gateway). This configuration enables public key extraction and subsequent cookie forgery.

suggestion.title: Successful VPN Establishment Post-Authentication Failure
suggestion.rationale: Rapid7 documented 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks.' VPN session success after legitimate auth failure is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VPN session establishment immediately following authentication failures or from source IPs without successful credential-based pre-authentication events. Flag VPN connections that bypass standard authentication pathways, especially when admin account or override mechanisms are involved.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Network Reconnaissance from Compromised Gateway Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise outcome: 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks' with subsequent attempted lateral movement. Post-access reconnaissance patterns should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For VPN sessions established to unpatched GlobalProtect devices during exploitation window (May 17 onwards), alert on network discovery activity (host/service enumeration, ARP scanning, port probing) immediately following VPN connection establishment. Rapid7 noted lateral movement largely failed, but reconnaissance artifacts should still appear.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly flags 'GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass' under active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero kill-chain reconstruction; no detection use case for the exploitation phase itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect portal/gateway endpoints for authentication requests that succeed despite missing or malformed credential fields, or requests matching known exploit payloads (typically HTTP POST to /global-protect/login.esp or /sslvpn/login.esp with crafted session tokens). Baseline: legitimate auth requests should have complete, well-formed credentials; exploits often bypass or skip fields. Alert on 401→200 sequences without credential re-submission or on successful auth from IPs with no prior authentication history.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GlobalProtect Session Activity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation article implies attackers gain access; no use case covers post-auth reconnaissance or lateral-movement behavior that typically follows VPN compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After GlobalProtect session establishment, flag accounts that immediately enumerate internal resources, query domain controllers, or establish multiple outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations. VPN sessions from newly compromised accounts typically exhibit spiky behavior: authentication → discovery scan → C2 callbacks. Look for GlobalProtect sessions spawning SMB, LDAP, or DNS queries to internal infrastructure within minutes of login.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Portal/Gateway Vulnerability Scanner Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies attackers scan for vulnerable instances. Article does not mention reconnaissance indicators; pipeline missed detection for pre-exploitation discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated requests to GlobalProtect paths (/global-protect/login.esp, /sslvpn/index.html, /sslvpn/login.esp, /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi) from single source IP, especially with User-Agent strings associated with automated tools (curl, wget, python-requests, Burp Suite). Exploit scanners typically send HTTP HEAD/GET requests to identify GlobalProtect instances; baseline traffic should show login attempts, not reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Patch Status / CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerable PAN-OS Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-specific exploitation requires vulnerable versions of PAN-OS. Pipeline extracted zero technical details, IOCs, or vulnerability indicators from the article title and metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate asset inventory (PAN-OS version) against CVE-2026-0257 patched versions. Flag any GlobalProtect instance running unpatched PAN-OS release. Shodan/Censys queries for GlobalProtect banners can identify internet-facing instances; prioritize those versions marked vulnerable in Palo Alto Networks advisory. Internal scans should confirm patch level via system logs or version strings in HTTP responses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Administrative / Root Access After GlobalProtect Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of authentication bypass often leads to privilege escalation or direct admin access. Article mentions 'active exploitation' but pipeline generated no privilege-escalation or impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management logs for configuration changes, firewall policy modifications, or credential creation initiated from recently-authenticated GlobalProtect sessions. Auth bypass may allow attackers to directly assume admin or read-only roles without proper RBAC enforcement. Alert on API calls or CLI commands (via SSH/management interface) originating from VPN IP ranges that escalate to elevated permissions or modify security policies.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from GlobalProtect Session
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation campaign implies post-compromise beaconing. Article title signals ongoing attacks but pipeline generated no command-and-control or exfiltration indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After GlobalProtect compromise, watch for outbound HTTPS or DNS tunneling from VPN IP addresses to known C2 domains/IPs. Attackers establishing persistence post-authentication typically maintain encrypted channels (HTTPS with self-signed certs, DNS over HTTPS, or raw TCP/UDP to fixed ports). Flag any single GlobalProtect session maintaining persistent outbound connections to non-business destinations or exhibiting periodic beaconing patterns (regular callbacks with fixed intervals or jitter).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Binary Execution with Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Attackers Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling.' Any supply chain compromise of build tools (Maven, npm, pip, Go, etc.) or IDEs should emit detection on process execution combined with outbound connections to non-standard IPs. Article context: 'Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling to Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of known developer tools (javac, dotnet, npm, python, gradle, cargo, go) with unusual parent processes or command-line arguments containing known exfil tools (curl, wget, tar, zip). Correlate with outbound network activity to non-whitelisted C2 or cloud storage endpoints (OneDrive, Dropbox, pastebin-class services) on ports/protocols atypical for that tool.

suggestion.title: Extraction of Version Control Repositories or Source Code Directories
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets.' Core attack vector is lateral or vertical movement into code repos followed by bulk data staging. Article must describe discovery or collection of .git folders, GitHub credentials, or source archives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on tar, zip, 7z, rar commands targeting .git directories, src/ or app/ subdirectories in user home or shared repos. Flag archive creation then immediate deletion (staging for exfil). Monitor for git clone/pull on unusual accounts or outside normal CI/CD windows.

suggestion.title: Credential and Secret Material Exfiltration (ENV Files, SSH Keys, API Keys)
suggestion.rationale: Title: '...Exfiltrate...Secrets.' Attackers targeting developers will harvest .env files, .aws/credentials, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, API keys in source roots or home directories. Fundamental attack post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cat, find, grep, or cp commands targeting .env, *.pem, *credentials*, .ssh/, config files in user home, project root, or CI/CD agent directories. Flag reads of these high-value files by non-owner or non-CI process. Monitor for writes of credential material to /tmp, /var/tmp, or cloud sync folders.

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Variable Leakage via Process Memory or Build Logs
suggestion.rationale: Source-code-stealing malware often exfiltrates environment variables (containing API keys, DB passwords, tokens) from running processes or CI/CD build logs. Article title implies 'Secrets' are exfiltrated—these are often in ENV vars.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for printenv, env, set commands that pipe to files, curl, or echo. Flag spawning of debuggers (gdb, lldb, cdb) or memory read tools targeting running processes that hold secrets (git, docker, aws-cli). Alert on CI/CD logs being written to world-readable paths or exfil-like destinations.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Tampering (Trojanized Binaries in Developer Tool Chains)
suggestion.rationale: Title 'Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling' most likely means the attacker compromised the tooling itself (npm package, Maven artifact, Pip package, Docker image, Homebrew formula, or binary repo). Requires monitoring package manager repos and artifact integrity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager command execution (npm install, pip install, mvn dependency, go get, cargo build) for unexpected post-install hooks or scripts. Flag hash mismatches of downloaded artifacts vs. known-good repository manifests (npm lockfile, Pipfile.lock, Maven checksums). Alert on modified binaries in /usr/local/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, node_modules/.bin, or similar tool install dirs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Staging and Transfer to External Storage (Developer Code and Secrets Egress)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets.' This is the final step: moving staged repos and credential files over the network to attacker-controlled infrastructure or public cloud.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large file uploads (>100MB) from developer workstations or CI/CD agents to non-approved cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, Pastebin) or unknown IP ranges. Flag unusual TLS SNI or HTTP Host headers. Alert on tar/zip uploads containing .git, .env, credentials, or source patterns (*.py, *.js, *.go, .yaml configs).

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as the attack vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain mapping for this initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting known Marimo application endpoints with payloads matching CVE-2026-39987 exploitation patterns. Track successful requests (HTTP 200/302) followed by unusual process spawning from the web application process or its child processes. Look for POST requests with suspicious parameters to Marimo web interfaces.

suggestion.title: LLM API Call from Compromised Web Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation' but pipeline generated no detection logic for LLM API calls as a post-exploitation command channel. This is a novel IOC category.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS requests from web application processes (e.g., Marimo) to LLM API endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, local LLM servers) with authentication tokens or API keys in headers. Flag POST requests with JSON payloads containing system command strings or exfiltrated data being sent to LLM inference endpoints outside expected business context.

suggestion.title: Process Creation via LLM-Generated Command String
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation via LLM agent implies the attacker is using LLM outputs to generate and execute system commands; pipeline did not suggest detection for this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, python.exe) spawned by or as children of web application processes (Marimo) with command lines containing markers of LLM-generated code (unusual spacing, comments with tokens like 'assistant:' or 'user:', or semantically valid but contextually anomalous commands).

suggestion.title: File Write Activity Post-Marimo Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase likely includes data exfiltration, persistence, or tool staging; no detection UC provided despite clear attack narrative progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to unexpected locations (temp, web-accessible directories, user home directories) by Marimo or its child processes within 5 minutes of a successful CVE-2026-39987 exploitation attempt. Flag creation of scripts, archives, or reverse shells in these directories.

suggestion.title: Marimo Process Spawning Unusual Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation will require command execution; article mentions this but pipeline provided no process-tree detection. Marimo is a Python notebook environment and should not spawn system shells or compilers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Marimo process (python.exe running Marimo app) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, gcc, curl, or wget as direct or indirect child processes. Marimo notebooks should execute user cells only within the Python interpreter; external process spawning indicates exploitation or post-exploitation code injection.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Targeting Microsoft Entra Users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' as initial access vector. No vishing-specific detection logic present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Microsoft Entra sign-in events from new geographic locations or unusual device types shortly after SPO/Teams calls logged to the same account. Correlate with employee help-desk reports of unsolicited phone calls requesting credentials. Flag accounts that authenticated successfully from multiple countries within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Salesforce Bulk Data Export
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' No detection rule generated for anomalous Salesforce API calls or bulk export attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce API export operations (bulk export, report generation, data loader jobs) involving >50k records in a single transaction, especially from newly-compromised user accounts. Correlate with failed login attempts preceding success. Monitor for API calls that export contact, customer account, or CPNI fields to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra Account Post-Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Entra account used for Salesforce access indicates lateral movement from identity layer to SaaS. Article shows no detection hypothesis for cloud-to-cloud pivoting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Entra accounts that successfully authenticate, then immediately access high-value SaaS apps (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Google Workspace) they have never touched before in historical window. Flag if the Entra session originates from external VPN/proxy or Tor exit node. Generate alerts for API-based Salesforce logins from non-browser clients within minutes of Entra compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Extortion Gang Dark Web Leak Site Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'ShinyHunters...leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' No monitoring or notification rule for brand/customer data appearing on known extortion sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain list of known ShinyHunters leak site mirrors and periodically crawl for posted datasets mentioning 'Charter', 'Spectrum', or customer account identifiers. Correlate dark web post timestamps with internal exfiltration alerts to confirm data was stolen. Alert SOC if Charter customer records appear alongside other organizations (pattern suggests multi-customer breach campaign).

suggestion.title: Multiple CPNI Exfiltration from Telecom CRM
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers stole 'some CPNI data' and 42 million Salesforce records including 'phone types, plan information, support ticket data.' CPNI is telecom-regulated sensitive data; mass export should trigger compliance alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For telecom/ISP organizations, monitor Salesforce reports and queries that select CPNI-tagged fields (phone plan, service address, account status, billing) in bulk. Flag if the same user account exports both customer contact data AND CPNI in separate operations within 12 hours. Alert if exports are followed immediately by credential destruction or account cleanup.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Phishing Link Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChatGPT's web summary feature being weaponized as 'a phishing surface'—malicious URLs injected into summaries to deliver phishing content. Pipeline produced zero detection logic for this initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when summarization API requests return URLs pointing to known phishing/credential-harvesting domains, or newly registered suspicious domains. Alert on repeated summary requests for URLs sharing phishing indicators (lookalike domains, free hosting providers, shortened URLs with no prior reputation).

suggestion.title: Abnormal ChatGPT Web Summary API Query Volume
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation would require batch-processing URLs through summary feature to generate phishing content at scale. Article frames feature as weaponizable attack surface but pipeline missed behavioral abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls to web summary endpoint with anomalously high QPS, batch URL submission, or repeated queries from same user/IP. Cluster by URL destination—if majority of URLs in summary requests point to attacker-controlled infrastructure or phishing domains, escalate.

suggestion.title: Post-Summary Phishing Page Credential Entry
suggestion.rationale: User clicks ChatGPT-summarized phishing link and enters credentials on landing page. Article implies user interaction but pipeline reconstructed zero kill-chain phases for credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP traffic: user accessed ChatGPT summary feature, clicked a URL from the summary, then landed on a credential-harvesting form (detected via phishing page ML models, form-submission patterns to non-matching domains, or known phishing infrastructure). Same session, <5 min delta.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download from OpenAI Lookalike Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'visitors are brought to a website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' offering Windows and macOS executables. Typosquatting + malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS/HTTP requests to domains matching OpenAI lookalikes (openew.*, openai-*.com, etc.). Alert if followed by executable download to %TEMP% or Downloads folder within 5 minutes, especially if unsigned or flagged by Windows Defender.

suggestion.title: Execution of VM Detection Commands Post-Malware Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'it executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Observed in Windows sample testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of systeminfo, wmic, or registry queries within 2 minutes of suspicious .exe/.app launch from Downloads/Temp. Parent process should be explorer.exe or self-extracting archive.

suggestion.title: Malicious Google Ads Redirecting to LLM Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com.' Google Ads as initial-access vector for entire campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ad-click logs and proxy traffic for Google Ads with ChatGPT/Claude/Grok keywords redirecting to chatgpt.com/s/*, claude.ai/share/*, or grok.ai/share/* URLs. Flag if destination renders download button or installation instructions.

suggestion.title: Content Cloaking on Malware Distribution Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' openew[.]app exhibits selective content delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains serving different content based on User-Agent, IP geolocation, or referrer. Check if URLScan/VirusTotal report different payloads for same URL. High-risk if legitimate-looking site (AR/VR company) masks malware distribution.

suggestion.title: User Downloads Malware-Disguised ChatGPT Desktop App from Fake Outage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they are presented with a rendered outage notice... they should download the desktop application instead... click on the download button, they are brought to openew[.]app.' Social-engineering lure triggering user execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser visits to chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai/share/* with subsequent .exe/.dmg/.app downloads to user Downloads folder. Flag if executable lacks Microsoft/OpenAI signature or triggers antivirus on execution.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Legitimate LLM Platform Sharing for Malware Hosting
