suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the fake outage notice is rendered through ChatGPT itself' and 'attacks abusing Claude Artifacts.' Legitimate platform features repurposed for malware distribution infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for chatgpt.com/s/*, claude.ai/artifacts/*, grok.ai/share/* URLs in proxy logs. Flag if page renders download UI, installation instructions, or developer controls ('Show code', 'Remix' buttons). Correlate with subsequent traffic to suspicious domains like openew[.].

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt... Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-0257'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability and network scanners for internet-facing PAN-OS instances running vulnerable versions. Correlate with asset inventory and flag all matches for remediation by federal deadline 2026-06-01.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions'. Exploitation attempts are detectable through PAN-OS interface logs and web traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin interface for HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns. Detect failed authentications immediately followed by successful admin sessions or lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicit consequence: 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection'. VPN access establishment is the direct persistence outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN connections to compromised PAN-OS from unusual geographies, times, or sources. Flag any new VPN user account provisioning or credential changes in the exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Attack Patterns from Residential Botnet Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnets were 'used for illegal activities such as distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Direct impact-phase activity with clear detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on simultaneous, distributed DDoS request patterns originating from large sets of residential IP addresses within a time window. Baseline request volume per source and flag anomalous surges characteristic of botnet-powered attacks (many sources, similar patterns, short duration).

suggestion.title: Identify Initial Compromise via Default Credentials on Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article's remediation advises 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong'—indicating credential abuse as entry vector for botnet infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to network devices (routers, switches, IoT) using default admin credentials, especially when followed within seconds/minutes by process spawns, task scheduler entries, or outbound connections to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Proxy Service Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article names Asocks proxy service controlling botnet C2; infected devices must communicate with control servers. 'The 200 servers used to host the infrastructure' explicitly describes C2 (T1071).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of known residential proxy service endpoints and alert on internal hosts initiating outbound HTTPS/HTTP to those servers, especially devices without proxy configuration or from unexpected departments/subnets.

suggestion.title: Detect Cryptocurrency Mining Abuse on Residential Botnet Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'cryptocurrency mining' as botnet use case: 'botnets are networks of compromised devices used for illegal activities such as...cryptocurrency mining.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process spawns of known mining tools (xmrig, ethminer, cgminer binaries or known command-line signatures) with sustained elevated CPU/GPU utilization. Alert on anomalous resource consumption patterns on endpoints not expected to run compute-heavy workloads.

suggestion.title: Identify Traffic Proxying Activity via Asymmetric Connection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnets were used for 'malicious traffic proxying.' Asocks advertises 'residential proxies with 7 million IP addresses'—infected devices act as proxy nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to internal hosts from large sets of external IPs within short time window (proxy request distribution). Flag endpoints with high inbound-to-outbound traffic asymmetry or rapid IP/geolocation rotation in request patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet C2 Infrastructure Access and Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes seizing '200 servers at a local provider that supported the operation' and recommendations to disable 'remote administration panels when not needed'—indicating C2 panel/SSH/RDP access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on remote management access (RDP, SSH, web panels) to network devices followed by execution of network utilities, PowerShell, or binaries consistent with botnet payloads. Flag failed default credential attempts preceding successful logins.

suggestion.title: Node.js source code containing nesting:true without require option — vm2 payload staging
suggestion.rationale: The article explicitly states the bypass is triggered by 'nesting:true without explicit require' — the actual exploit code pattern. Yet no detection hunts for this code signature in source files or logs. Article phrase: 'The fix...introduced a check...which is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Node.js source code (git commits, stored code in CI/CD, deployment packages) for vm2.runFile() or new NodeVM() calls with nesting:true and either no require option or explicit require:undefined. Correlate against repositories with vm2 as dependency.

suggestion.title: npm audit / dependency scan detects vm2 ≤3.11.3 — vulnerability exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable version range but no proactive dependency scanning UC. For orgs running npm audit or SBOM tools: 'vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3)' is the exposure trigger. Article phrase: 'vm2 has a CVE-2023-37903 patch bypass' (implying version-bounded flaw).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate npm audit outputs, SBOM reports, or Snyk/Dependabot alerts for vm2 with version ≤3.11.3. Trigger on any CI/CD pipeline that reports this package in the dependency tree without a documented mitigation (e.g., network isolation, input validation wrapper).

suggestion.title: Node.js application logging reveals vm2 NodeVM creation with unexpected options — runtime exploitation indicator
suggestion.rationale: The article does not mention how vm2 instantiation is logged/telemetered. If apps log vm2.NodeVM() calls (framework instrumentation, APM), looking for nesting:true + missing require in structured logs would catch execution. Phrase: 'nesting:true without explicit require still allows full RCE' — implies runtime behavior capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If app logs contain structured vm2 NodeVM instantiation events, hunt for options={'nesting':true} paired with absence of 'require' key or 'require':undefined. Correlate with subsequent process spawning or file I/O anomalies from the Node process.

suggestion.title: JavaScript AST / static analysis flags risky vm2 configuration — pre-deployment control
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a logic error in the fix check (strict equality vs truthiness). SAST tools could flag this pattern before deployment. No mention of static-analysis-time detection. Phrase: 'strict equality (options.require === false), which is trivially bypassed' — this is a pattern SAST can detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy ESLint/SonarQube rules that flag vm2 NodeVM configs with nesting:true and missing require key. Alert on code commits or PRs that introduce this anti-pattern, blocking merge until remediated.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning from Node.js with command-line enumeration flags — post-exploitation discovery phase
suggestion.rationale: UC_25_2 exists but is too generic. The article explicitly enumerates discovery commands (whoami, id, uname, etc.) that confirm exploitation success. Tighter detection: Node + shell + discovery-class commands. Phrase: 'Processes.process="*whoami*" OR Processes.process="* id*" OR Processes.process="*uname*"' (from article).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.exe spawning sh/bash/cmd with discovery commands (whoami, id, uname, hostname, whoami, net user, cat /etc/passwd) within 2 minutes of app startup. Exclude npm build/test scripts via parent_process filtering. High confidence if preceded by file I/O to node_modules/vm2.

suggestion.title: vm2 library update/patch events followed by revert — indicator of failed patch deployment or rollback
suggestion.rationale: Article implies patch existed (CVE-2023-37903 fix) but was bypassed. No UC for detecting failed patch rollouts or reverts. If teams update vm2 to patch and then revert, this signals either patch compatibility issues or active exploitation attempts triggering rollback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt git commit logs or package manager audit trails for vm2 version changes. Alert if version updates to >=3.11.4 (patched) followed by revert to <=3.11.3 within 7 days, especially if paired with exploitation-phase detections (UC_25_2).

suggestion.title: Sandboxed code accessing process global object from VM context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'process' is a denylist bypass: the vulnerability exists because NodeVM blocks certain builtins but misses 'process' and 'inspector/promises'. Direct detection of `process` object access from within a vm2/NodeVM context would catch the exploit attempt pre-shell execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vm2/NodeVM sandboxing frameworks attempting to restrict builtin module imports, then detect evasion via process or inspector/promises object references in the sandboxed script payload. Look for process.getBuiltinModule, process.binding, or require('inspector/promises') chains within node process execution contexts after vm2 module load.

suggestion.title: Inspector/promises module invocation chains leading to Runtime.evaluate
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'inspector/promises' and 'Runtime.evaluate' as part of the attack chain. UC_23_4 captures raw strings, but missed is the sequential pattern: inspector/promises → Runtime.evaluate → shell execution. Chaining these improves precision.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process execution that loads inspector/promises module followed by Runtime.evaluate invocation in the same command or script context. EventID sequencing across process/module load events would identify the exploit chain with high specificity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 module version paired with abnormal child process spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable vm2 versions 3.0–3.11.3. Pairing software inventory (UC_23_2 identifies vulnerable versions) with post-exploitation behavior (UC_23_3 detects shell spawning) creates a pivot for high-confidence incident response: if vulnerable version + shell spawning from node occur in the same time window on the same asset, it's exploitation in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join vulnerability scanner results (vm2 3.0–3.11.3 detected) with process execution data within 10 minutes; flag if node.exe spawns cmd/powershell/bash without intermediate npm/yarn/build process. Baseline legitimate build timings to distinguish development workflows.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package installation detection (CVE-2026-47208)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vm2 is Vulnerable to Sandbox Breakout' with affected versions ≤3.11.3. Detection of vulnerable package presence is the prerequisite for exploitation. Article's 'Recommended hunts' section explicitly models this as UC_26_1 with Splunk/KQL, but pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for package.json files in node_modules/vm2 paths to identify systems with vulnerable vm2 versions. Extract version strings from package.json content and alert on ≤3.11.3.

suggestion.title: Node.exe spawning unauthorized child processes post-sandbox-escape
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'escape from the VM2 sandbox and execute arbitrary commands on the host system.' Post-exploitation spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, etc. from node.exe is the exploitation execution step. Article models this as UC_26_2 but pipeline did not generate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe/nodejs.exe spawning shell interpreters or system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, bash, sh, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, curl, wget, certutil). Exclude legitimate npm/yarn/build processes via parent command line patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47208 Promise species exploitation fingerprint detection
suggestion.rationale: Article details the vulnerability mechanism: 'localPromise constructor,' 'missing resetPromiseSpecies,' 'Symbol.species.' Active exploitation scripts will contain these JavaScript patterns. Article's UC_26_3 models this with PoC string hunts but pipeline generated no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe process command lines and .js file contents containing exploit marker strings: 'Symbol.species', 'constructor.constructor("return process")', 'mainModule.require', 'Promise.prototype[Symbol.species]'. These patterns indicate active CVE-2026-47208 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via sandbox breakout correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation) to this CVE. Sandbox escape IS privilege escalation—moving from restricted VM context to host privileges. Pipeline missed this dimension despite technique being explicitly listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe processes executing with vm2 context (process name, parent, or loaded modules) with subsequent high-privilege operations or filesystem writes outside vm2 sandbox boundaries. Successful correlation indicates privilege escalation via sandbox escape.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI / Suspending API usage in Node.js context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'JSPI-backed Promise' and 'WebAssembly.Suspending' as the exploit mechanism. Detection should hunt for unusual WebAssembly API calls in Node.js (WebAssembly.promising, WebAssembly.Suspending) or process arguments containing these strings—highly anomalous in typical applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js processes with command-line arguments or process environment containing 'WebAssembly.promising', 'WebAssembly.Suspending', or 'JSPI' keywords. WebAssembly module loads from untrusted sources into Node.js are extremely rare and highly suspicious.

suggestion.title: vm2 module execution with async/await and Promise.finally() patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'untrusted code is executed with async support' and the exploit specifically chains through Promise.finally(). Detection should identify vm2 imports that also reference async/await patterns or Promise method manipulation in the same scope.
log_sources: DeviceProcessEvents (script content inspection or YARA signatures)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for vm2 require/import statements within code that also contain Promise.finally(), Promise.prototype manipulation, or async/await keywords. Combine with JSPI detection for higher confidence. This captures the specific attack chain from the vulnerability description.

suggestion.title: vm2 package.json version alignment with running Node.js process cmdline
suggestion.rationale: UC_24_3 detects presence; this complements by correlating vulnerable package metadata with active Node.js execution and parent application context to reduce false positives from development/test environments.
log_sources: DeviceProcessEvents (Node.js startup with matching parent context)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-system discovery of vm2<=3.11.3 package.json with process events: Node.js spawned from the same application root shortly after (within 5 minutes). Higher fidelity than package presence alone by requiring active usage.

suggestion.title: Scanner reconnaissance targeting PraisonAI Flask listener (CVE-2026-47393)
suggestion.rationale: UC_14_5 references 'CVE-Detector scanner' user-agent but does not isolate the reconnaissance phase itself. Article establishes that public scanners will probe the 0.0.0.0-bound listener before attacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to TCP/8005 from public IPs with scanner user-agents (CVE-Detector, Nessus, Rapid7, OpenVAS) or generic connection-attempt patterns that probe but do not exploit. Baseline normal usage to distinguish reconnaissance from legitimate access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PraisonAI package version installation or upgrade
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in code-generator praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code and recommend patching. No UC detects installation of vulnerable versions or failure to patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager activity (pip, conda, apt) for PraisonAI installations matching vulnerable version ranges (pre-patch). Alert on requirements.txt or setup.py containing unpatched PraisonAI dependency.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Flask configuration with auth disabled detected in YAML or Python config
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authentication disabled by default' via YAML sample configuration, but no UC specifically hunts for the deployed config files or detect authentication-bypass flags in Flask startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Flask config files or praisonai deployment YAML containing auth=false, SECRET_KEY unset, or authentication_enabled=0. Monitor Python process command lines for Flask startup without authentication middleware.

suggestion.title: Lateral exfiltration of LLM responses from /chat endpoint abuse
suggestion.rationale: UC_14_5 targets unauthenticated POST requests but does not specifically flag data exfiltration patterns (e.g. large response bodies, repeated queries crafted to extract sensitive training data, prompt injection probing).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/GET to /chat endpoint returning large response bodies (>50KB) or repeated rapid queries from single external IP. Detect prompt-injection patterns (e.g. 'ignore instructions', 'system prompt', 'API keys') in request body.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery via Default Secret — Token Validation Against Known-Weak Keys
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allowing token forgery for any user' — pipeline should have generated a detection for validating API requests with JWT tokens that could have been signed with 'dev-secret-change-me'. Article establishes the attack vector but pipeline missed the exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API requests to /auth/me, /workspaces/*, /auth/register where JWT claims contain anomalies (e.g., user_id or tenant_id inconsistent with source IP historical baseline) or where the request originates from an IP never previously associated with that user. Cross-reference against successful JWT validations using hardcoded secret patterns.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret String Detection in Configuration Files and Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the vulnerability root cause: hardcoded string 'dev-secret-change-change-me'. Pipeline should have generated a file-search or config-audit detection for this exact string or variations in environment exports, .env files, and source code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for 'dev-secret-change-me' or similar patterns in process environment variable dumps, config files created/modified in /etc, /app/config, home directories, and in command-line argument snapshots. Flag any exposure of PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET in plaintext logs or process telemetry.

suggestion.title: Production Deployment with PLATFORM_ENV Unset or Set to 'dev'
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'A safety check exists but only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != "dev"; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is "dev", so the check is silently bypassed.' Pipeline should detect when PLATFORM_ENV is not explicitly set in production contexts, or is set to 'dev' in prod IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify uvicorn/praisonai-platform process launches where PLATFORM_ENV is either absent or explicitly set to 'dev', correlating against IP geolocation, hostname patterns, or network segmentation known to be production. Flag any such process on systems outside development VLAN or on public-facing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Workspace Access and Modification from Single Session
suggestion.rationale: Article implies impersonation across tenant boundaries after token forgery ('allowing token forgery for any user'). Pipeline should detect a single authenticated session accessing or modifying resources belonging to multiple workspace/tenant IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API calls from a single JWT token/session ID across distinct workspace_id values (extracted from URL path or request body). Alert when one session accesses ≥3 workspaces and performs ≥1 destructive operation (DELETE, PATCH, PUT) within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH request with owner role in JSON body
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'MemberService.update_role(workspace_id, user_id, body.role) which sets the target member's role' — pipeline skipped inspecting the actual request payload. Application or WAF logs must show role:owner or similar in the PATCH body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} where request body contains role set to owner or admin. Elevated priority if target user_id matches authenticated user (self-promotion).

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: 403 forbidden to successful PATCH auth-bypass pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as authorization check flaw ('require_workspace_member defaults to member, never overridden'). Detection should correlate failed auth (403) attempts on endpoint followed by successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 minutes, same source IP/user makes failed PATCH request (403) to /workspaces/*/members/*, then successful PATCH (200) to same/similar endpoint. Indicates testing and exploitation of auth bypass.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Workspace member list query post-escalation
suggestion.rationale: After gaining owner role, attacker needs to discover other admins/owners to avoid detection. Article implies post-exploit reconnaissance, but UC_9_4 is too narrow (enumeration only). Should trigger on owner discovery queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /workspaces/{id}/members with filter/search for owner/admin roles within 10 minutes after successful PATCH role promotion. Indicates post-escalation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes LinkedIn as attack vector; title states 'LinkedIn Social Engineering.' Pipeline generated zero initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for emails or messages with LinkedIn profile URLs, LinkedIn credential-entry redirects, or social-engineer pretexts. Monitor for users visiting attacker-controlled domains after LinkedIn contact. Alert on first-time LinkedIn connections followed by immediate file/link delivery.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Email/Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'custom macOS Malware' deployment; pipeline mapped no execution techniques. macOS process tree should show browser or mail app spawning unusual processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by Safari, Chrome, Mail, or Finder (common delivery vectors). Flag execution of unsigned binaries, Python scripts, or shell commands from ~/Downloads or ~/Library/Caches. Correlate with recent email/LinkedIn access.

suggestion.title: macOS Custom Malware Family Hash & Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies custom malware delivery; pipeline produced no IOCs. Hash/YARA signatures for 'custom' variants must be extracted and distributed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect by file hash, code signature, or behavioral indicators (keylogging, screenshotting, C2 beaconing). Scope: macOS only. Alert if file appears in /tmp, /var/tmp, or user-writable .app bundles.

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Actor Profile & Infrastructure Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Actor name 'JINX-0164' in title; zero actor-intelligence mapping. Pipeline should correlate this with known C2 domains, registration patterns, or TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain actor profile with known C2 IPs, domains, and malware variants. Monitor for DNS queries or connections to infrastructure linked to JINX-0164. Alert on lateral movement attempts or persistence mechanisms associated with this group.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headlines HTTPSpy as a Kimsuky deployment. Pipeline extracted zero indicators. Should detect execution, parent-child process chains, and network communication patterns of this tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPSpy process execution by name or hash. Alert on HTTPS C2 communication patterns consistent with this tool—look for POST requests to suspicious domains, unusual user-agent strings, or timing anomalies typical of APT malware heartbeats.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Tool Deployment and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: HelloDoor explicitly named as part of Kimsuky's expanded arsenal. Zero detection logic provided despite clear lateral-movement threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HelloDoor creation, execution, or file-system indicators. Track for lateral movement patterns (e.g., credential theft, pass-the-hash). Correlate with Kimsuky delivery vectors (spear-phishing, watering-hole).

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnels Abuse for C2/Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states Kimsuky expands arsenal with VS Code Tunnels exploitation—a living-off-the-land C2 technique. No detection use case was generated despite significant operability and novel attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code (code.exe, vsls-ai service) establishing outbound connections to non-development infrastructure. Monitor for unexpected tunnel creation or vsls-ai.azureedge.net traffic from non-developer machines. Detect anomalous process ancestry (cmd.exe → code.exe → network).

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Threat-Actor Indicator Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Kimsuky is the primary threat actor named in the article; no use case was created to surface known IOCs, infrastructure, or behavioral signatures associated with this group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference outbound network traffic against known Kimsuky C2 domains, SSL certificates, and ASNs. Monitor for user-agent anomalies and HTTP header patterns observed in prior Kimsuky campaigns. Alert on infrastructure overlap with historical APT activity.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials' — supply-chain package compromise is the primary attack vector and explicitly ties to credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet/dotnet restore operations for installation of packages with names mimicking banking libraries. Flag if followed by file reads to credential storage paths (%APPDATA%, AWS config dirs) within seconds of installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Execution Accessing Cloud Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — malicious npm code execution combined with cloud credential access is a distinct attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or npm processes reading from cloud credential paths (~/.aws, ~/.azure, KUBECONFIG, %USERPROFILE%/.kube) within parent chain of package installation. Alert on reads of cloud provider environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Package Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Title names the attack outcome: stolen banking and cloud credentials — detection must cover exfiltration channels used after theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from nuget.exe, npm, dotnet, or child processes to non-standard destinations. Baseline known package repository traffic and alert on out-of-band DNS queries or HTTP POST requests to unfamiliar domains during package execution.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Suspicious Binary Execution from Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages must execute payload code at install time; detection should identify execution of untrusted binaries from package paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unsigned executables or recently-signed binaries (cert issued <30 days ago) launched from node_modules/, packages/, or .nuget/ directories. Include command line arguments that indicate credential enumeration or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Before exfiltrating credentials, malicious payloads typically enumerate what credentials are available on the system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect directory listing or recursive file enumeration of credential storage paths initiated by package manager processes or their children. Flag access patterns (e.g., dir/ls on .aws, repeated stat calls on credential files) in rapid succession post-installation.

suggestion.title: Spawning of System Utilities from Package Manager Context
suggestion.rationale: Malicious package payloads commonly spawn curl, wget, cmd.exe, or powershell to execute secondary commands for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl.exe, or wget spawned by/under nuget.exe, npm, or node.js during or immediately after package install. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Created with SYSTEM Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task'—this is the persistence and privilege-escalation vector. No detection rule generated despite explicit description of the attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect schtasks.exe or Windows Task Scheduler API creating scheduled tasks with SYSTEM or NT AUTHORITY privilege context. Baseline: user-context processes should not spawn SYSTEM-privileged tasks. Correlate task creation to enrollment in unusual parent processes and look for task names with high entropy, random strings, or common masquerade patterns ('Windows Update', 'System Service', etc.).

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption by Scheduled Task Process
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Encrypt Local Drives'—describes the impact phase directly. Pipeline did not generate any detection rule for the encryption activity itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-velocity file I/O from scheduled-task-spawned processes. Detect bulk file extension changes (e.g., .encrypted, .locked, .ransom) or high-entropy write patterns across multiple directories on C: and attached drives. Correlate file operations to TaskScheduler process lineage and baseline: encrypt operations should not originate from scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Scheduled Task Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'elevated privileges'—implies elevation from user to SYSTEM context. No detection for this escalation vector was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process token elevation when user-context processes spawn scheduled tasks that execute with SYSTEM token. Look for schtasks.exe calls followed by TaskScheduler spawning child processes with elevated token integrity. Monitor for parent-child process relationships where parent is low-privilege but child runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Binary Execution from Scheduled Task
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware payload executing via scheduled task. Pipeline did not surface execution-phase detection despite this being the malware's final stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unknown or unsigned executables spawned by TaskScheduler or svchost.exe running in Task Scheduler context. Flag processes whose parent is scheduled-task execution if child process exhibits ransomware behavioral indicators: rapid file enumeration, registry modification (shadow copy deletion, recovery options), network outbound traffic, or bulk CryptoAPI calls.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Registry Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Scheduled tasks persist in Windows registry—article implies post-infection persistence. Pipeline ignored registry-level artifact generation for task persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache and task definition XML files for creation or modification. Detect: (1) tasks scheduled to run at startup or on logon, (2) task actions pointing to temp/AppData executables, (3) task ownership changed from admin to SYSTEM, or (4) task triggers modified post-creation.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Scheduled Task Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Using SYSTEM scheduled tasks masks execution attribution from user-context process trees. This evasion pattern is central to the attack method but was not captured as a distinct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process lineages where malware spawns schtasks.exe to delegate execution to TaskScheduler, thereby hiding the true parent process from typical parent-child forensics. Flag patterns: user process → schtasks.exe → legitimate system process → ransomware. Monitor for scheduled-task cleanup (schtasks /delete) post-execution, a sign of post-intrusion cleanup.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Gemini API Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article title states attackers 'leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini' to fuel attacks; pipeline extracted nothing about account compromise or API abuse. Compromised LLM accounts should trigger alerts on unusual access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful authentication to ChatGPT or Gemini accounts from anomalous geolocations, IPs, or during off-hours. Track API token generation and usage by service principals or user accounts that do not typically interact with LLM platforms. Flag bulk or rapid API calls.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Phishing Content in Email
suggestion.rationale: Title describes attackers using LLMs to 'fuel cyberattacks'; conventional phishing detection may miss LLM-generated content due to structural variation. Article implicitly describes phishing-as-a-service via LLM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with suspicious linguistic patterns consistent with LLM output (e.g., over-polished grammar, unusual phrase structures, generic urgency markers). Correlate sender reputation (new/repurposed accounts) with email body entropy and keyword indicators of malware delivery or credential harvesting URLs.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Usage for LLM Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article names GREYVIBE as leveraging these platforms; no mention of detection logic for account compromise itself. Attackers must first compromise or access ChatGPT/Gemini accounts before using them operationally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sign-ins to consumer LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Gemini) using corporate credentials or from IPs inconsistent with user baseline. Monitor for account recovery actions (password reset, MFA changes) followed by immediate API calls or application integrations.

suggestion.title: Malware Development Assistance via LLM Query Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates LLMs used to 'fuel cyberattacks' but does not detail malware generation detection. If attackers use LLMs to write malware or obfuscate payloads, API logs and query patterns should surface this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM API logs for queries requesting code samples for common attack primitives (reverse shells, credential dumpers, UAC bypass, lateral movement tools). Flag accounts issuing iterative refinement requests on malware code or obfuscation techniques.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Actor Attribution via Operational Security Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names GREYVIBE; pipeline extracted no actor context. Kill chain and IOCs should link observed tools, techniques, and infrastructure to this group. Pipeline should have produced actor profile and OPSEC indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known GREYVIBE indicators of compromise (C2 domains, tool signatures, TTP clustering) with LLM platform abuse reports. Flag infrastructure overlaps (shared VPNs, hosting providers, email registrars) between compromised LLM accounts and known threat actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Resolution from Public Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article core: dependency confusion exploits packages resolving from public NPM instead of private registries. 'Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion' requires detection of scope bypass or package name confusion during resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci operations resolving scoped packages (@namespace/name) from public registry when private registry should take precedence. Flag package names matching legitimate internal packages with minor edits (typosquatting). Correlate with npm config and .npmrc to identify missing private registry authentication.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Enumeration from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes packages 'profile developer environments'—this means reading env vars containing CI tokens, AWS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc. No detection for credential or environment data collection from npm/node child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by npm/node (especially postinstall scripts) that access or enumerate environment variables, particularly those containing secrets (AWS_*, GITHUB_*, GITLAB_*, TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, API). Baseline legitimate CI tooling; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via npm Package During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Profiling campaign implies collected environment data must be exfiltrated. Article describes packages gathering reconnaissance but no detection rule covers outbound data transmission during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by npm, node, or npm postinstall child processes to non-standard or suspicious destinations during package installation window. Correlate with process behavior indicating data collection (env var reads, file iteration). Alert on HTTPS POST/PUT to attacker infrastructure with system profiling telemetry.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Execution Spawning System Profiling Tools
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages use postinstall scripts to execute reconnaissance commands. Article states packages 'profile developer environments'—no detection for whoami, systeminfo, uname, wmic, env, or git config enumeration from npm postinstall context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm or node processes spawning discovery/profiling tools (whoami, id, systeminfo, uname -a, uname -m, sw_vers, lsb_release, wmic logicaldisk, ps aux, git config --global user.email, env, printenv). Exclude known legitimate npm packages (e.g., native module builders). Correlate with network activity to identify C2 callback.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write or Code Injection via npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion packages execute code during install. Article mentions profiling but doesn't explicitly cover payload write/persistence; however, any npm package with reconnaissance capability likely also establishes persistence or modifies build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm postinstall script file writes outside expected npm directories—especially writes to build output folders, CI config paths, SSH/Git credential directories, or Node global modules. Flag executables or scripts written with .post-install, .setup, or obfuscated names. Correlate timing with package installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomalies (Recent Creation, Suspicious Keywords)
suggestion.rationale: 33 malicious packages implies new or newly-modified packages on npmjs.com. No detection for package metadata red flags (fresh account, no history, dependency confusion keywords in description, high semver version jumps).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate installed npm package metadata (author creation date, publish date, version history, package description keywords like 'internal', 'private', 'company-specific') with npm registry API. Alert on install of packages published within 30 days of first mention in build logs, or from accounts created shortly before. Flag packages with zero external dependents but broad company-specific naming.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Admin Authentication with Override Cookie Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account' — explicit attack pattern requiring detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GlobalProtect authentication events where user=admin* AND authentication_override_cookie=true, especially from external or infrastructure-provider IPs. Correlate timeline with May 17-29 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: TLS Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies' — certificate enumeration precedes exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated TLS handshakes or certificate-fetch requests to GlobalProtect portal/gateway from same source IP within minutes. Flag when extracted certificates match those used for authentication_override_cookie signing.

suggestion.title: Incomplete GlobalProtect VPN Session After Cookie Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session' — signature validation bypass allowed auth but not VPN completion
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication_override_cookie=true with vpn_connection_status in (incomplete, failed_handshake) from same source within same session. Multiple failures from one IP indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication from Compromised Infrastructure Providers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'earliest observed exploitation was May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr... second wave detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems' — infrastructure-sourced VPN anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on GlobalProtect VPN connections originating from known compromised cloud providers (Vultr/Dromatics Systems in this campaign). Flag especially for admin accounts or unusual destination segments.

suggestion.title: Authentication Override Cookie Signature Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'device decrypts these cookies using a configured private key and then trusts the decrypted contents without performing any signature verification' — root technical flaw
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In PAN-OS logs, detect auth_override_cookie validation events where signature_verified=false OR absent. Review firewall configs to identify reuse of HTTPS certificates for auth_override_cookie signing (misconfiguration enabling exploit).

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequential User Account Authentication Attempts via Override
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern suggests systematic account targeting; article implies attacker enumeration across accounts via forged cookies with variable user fields
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥3 distinct user accounts authenticating from same source_ip where authentication_override_cookie=true within 5-minute window. Baseline expected admin/service account patterns.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Unauthenticated Access via CVE-2026-0257
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'authentication bypass' as the core vulnerability. Active exploitation confirms real-world attack attempts. This is the primary attack surface and must have a detection use case.

Flag authentication success (HTTP 200 or session grant) immediately following failed auth attempt (HTTP 401) without valid credential submission.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GlobalProtect Session Establishment Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Successful authentication bypass leads to session establishment. Must detect suspicious sessions spawned through vulnerable path vs. normal login flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GlobalProtect VPN session creation where login was not preceded by user portal interaction, MFA challenge, or normal authentication sequence. Correlate rapid session creation from non-residential IPs with exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Bypass Internal Reconnaissance or Lateral Movement from VPN
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gaining initial access via authentication bypass typically perform discovery or pivot internally. Expected kill chain includes post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN-sourced traffic for port scanning, DNS enumeration queries, or SMB/LDAP discovery attempts within 5 minutes of GlobalProtect session establishment via CVE-2026-0257.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Process Executing Unexpected Network Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'abuse of trusted developer tooling' for exfiltration—tools like git, npm, docker, IDEs should be monitored for abnormal outbound connections or data staging that contradict normal behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when legitimate developer tools (git, npm, cargo, gradle, maven, pip, docker, vscode, intellij) initiate outbound connections to non-standard ports or IP ranges outside known package repositories. Flag connections bundled with data staging in temp directories or .git/config manipulation.

suggestion.title: Source Code Repository Credential Exfiltration via Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'exfiltrate source code and secrets'—pipeline should detect when dev tools access credential files (.ssh, .aws, .netrc, .git-credentials) followed by their content being read into memory or written to network sockets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for developer tool processes reading credential stores (.ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials, ~/.netrc, git-credentials), particularly when followed by child process spawns for network exfiltration or when content size read exceeds expected token size.

suggestion.title: Trusted Developer Tool Binary Modification or DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Abuse of 'trusted' tooling implies either compromise of the binary itself or injection into a legitimate process. Pipeline should detect tampering with git, npm, docker executables or unsigned DLL loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unsigned or out-of-band DLLs loaded by dev tool processes; detect file modification timestamps on git/npm/docker/vscode executables that differ from installation records; monitor for sideloaded dlls in dev tool directories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Substitution (npm/maven/nuget Package Poisoning)
suggestion.rationale: Abuse of 'developer tooling' may involve injecting malicious packages into legitimate package managers or registries. Pipeline should generate UCs for detecting compromised package downloads or malicious manifest changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of packages from non-canonical repositories or with version mismatches; flag package manager processes downloading from unusual CDNs; correlate package hashes against trusted registries.

suggestion.title: Git Configuration Hijacking for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers commonly abuse git's credential helper system or ssh key configurations. Article mentions 'trusted' tooling abuse—git config poisoning is a known vector for developer credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to ~/.gitconfig, /etc/gitconfig, or .git/config; detect git credential helper invocations with unfamiliar helper binaries; flag git operations with credential.helper pointing to non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references this CVE as the exploit vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain phases despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting Marimo application endpoints with payloads or unusual parameter encoding. Correlate web requests with subsequent unexpected child process creation, especially Python or shell interpreters.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation LLM Agent Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—core attack pattern with zero corresponding use case or technique mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, sequential shell/Python command execution post-exploitation with minimal inter-command dwell time. Monitor for LLM framework instantiation or LLM SDK calls from compromised processes. Flag execution of commands that appear AI-generated or contain scripting loops.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Cron
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase logically requires persistence; LLM agents establish automated callbacks or scheduled execution. No use case generated for this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs within minutes of Marimo exploitation. Alert on tasks with obfuscated names, commands invoking Python/Bash, or callback patterns (DNS, HTTP beacons to external IPs).

suggestion.title: LLM Prompt Injection or Model Parameter Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Using LLM for post-exploitation implies attacker control over model behavior; no detection case for prompt injection, system instruction override, or model configuration abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for unusual LLM API calls, model state mutations, or loading of external/untrusted models. Detect strings in logs matching known jailbreak prompts or attempts to override system instructions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via LLM-Orchestrated Network Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase commonly includes internal reconnaissance; LLM agents automate discovery and pivoting. Article mentions post-exploitation but pipeline captured no lateral movement use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns of network scanning or enumeration following exploitation, especially if they follow unexpected sequences (scanning unusual port ranges, internal IP discovery, then targeted connections). Correlate with LLM process execution.

suggestion.title: Data Collection and Exfiltration via LLM-Driven Automation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attack chains typically include data staging and exfiltration; LLM agents can automate file discovery and exfil. No corresponding use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for automated file enumeration or archiving following Marimo exploitation, particularly if driven by Python scripts. Detect suspicious DNS or HTTP traffic patterns consistent with data exfiltration, especially bulk uploads or compression followed by deletion.

suggestion.title: Unusual Entra Login Patterns Post-Vishing Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' (April 1) — entry point should trigger cloud authentication anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra logins from unusual geographies, impossible-travel scenarios, or first-time device usage within 24 hours of detected vishing/social engineering reports. Correlate with subsequent high-volume cloud app or API access anomalies. Flag user accounts targeted by confirmed phishing calls for 72-hour elevated monitoring baseline.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Export by Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers' — classic SaaS data exfiltration requiring detection on export scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk record exports (>5k records) by non-service users, SOQL queries returning entire Account/Contact datasets, or Report exports 10x above user's baseline. Correlate export timing with Entra compromise timeline and unusual admin privilege elevation in Salesforce.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Compromised Employee Credential to Multi-Cloud App Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: compromised Entra account 'used...to steal...from the company's Salesforce instance' — attacker pivoted identity provider compromise directly to SaaS application access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single compromised identity accesses multiple cloud services (Salesforce, Sharepoint, Teams, etc.) in atypical order or from same session context. Flag first-time Salesforce API calls by standard employee accounts. Monitor for concurrent OAuth token reuse across SaaS boundaries post-credential-compromise.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Threat-Actor Salesforce Exfiltration Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters...has been targeting Salesforce customers over the past year, breaching hundreds of companies worldwide' and 'claiming the theft of billions of records in Salesforce Aura data theft attacks' — campaign-level pattern indicator for Salesforce-heavy organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Salesforce environment activity against known ShinyHunters victim list and Salesforce Aura attack signatures. Alert on admin account creation by non-IT users, permission escalation patterns matching previous ShinyHunters incidents, and bulk data access by newly-created or historically-inactive accounts.

suggestion.title: Vishing Attack Reported → Account Compromise Timeline Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article: primary attack vector 'voice phishing (vishing) attack' — user-reported social engineering calls should trigger proactive account monitoring, not post-breach forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate user vishing/social-engineering reports into security alerting pipeline. Flag reported target's accounts for 48-72 hour intensive monitoring of login patterns, API activity, and cloud app access changes. Alert on successful login within 24 hours of reported vishing attempt, especially from geography/device inconsistent with user baseline.

suggestion.title: Charter/Telecom Customer Data Exposure Validation (Salesforce Records)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed 4.9M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers and physical addresses' and '85k records originating from an internal employee directory also included job titles' — post-breach customer record leak warrant detection on record-dump indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web leak sites and OSINT feeds for Charter/telecom customer data dumps and employee directory disclosures. Alert on appearance of internal employee email lists, customer contact data matching company domain patterns, and known employee names in public breach databases. Correlate with ShinyHunters actor notification to enable rapid breach response.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT Summary Feature Abuse for Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface' — pipeline did not surface initial-access phishing use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ChatGPT web-summary API calls followed by redirects to domains with low reputation scores or recently registered. Correlate ChatGPT session initiation with subsequent phishing page access within <5min window. Alert if summary feature is used to render untrusted external content inline.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via ChatGPT-Summarized Phishing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern described in title implies victims receive summarized phishing content via ChatGPT, crediting unprotected credential-entry fields — no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential-submission forms rendered through ChatGPT summary feature (User-Agent or referer includes 'chatgpt' or 'openai'). Flag cases where form targets differ from ChatGPT's domain. Monitor for password-reset/2FA-prompt pages delivered via ChatGPT context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous ChatGPT API Usage Pattern for Phishing Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attackers weaponize ChatGPT summary API to deliver phishing at scale — no detection for unusual API call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ChatGPT API request volume and summary length per user/IP. Alert on 5x+ increase in summary requests within 1hr, especially if summaries return phishing-like keywords ('verify account', 'confirm identity', 'urgent action'). Correlate with known phishing domain IPs in summary responses.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Summary Feature Rendering Untrusted External Links
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables summary feature to render malicious external content — pipeline did not detect execution/delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT summary responses for embedded URLs pointing to newly-registered domains or high-risk TLDs. Trigger alert if user clicks link from within ChatGPT summarization context and lands on form requesting credentials or payment info within 10sec.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT-Mediated Man-in-the-Middle Injection of Phishing Content
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies attacker injects phishing into ChatGPT's summary rendering pipeline — no detection for content-injection attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from ChatGPT API containing unexpected HTML form fields or scripts not consistent with legitimate summarization. Flag if response Content-Type mismatches declared type. Monitor for JavaScript execution within ChatGPT iframe contexts.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Using ChatGPT as Trusted Delivery Vector
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attackers to leverage ChatGPT's trusted brand to deliver phishing — no campaign-level detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ChatGPT-delivered phishing summaries with upstream email messages or messages containing 'Check this summary' or 'See what ChatGPT found' — indicator of attacker-seeded prompt-injection attack. Alert if ChatGPT links appear in bulk messages or from external email domains.

suggestion.title: Executable download from domain impersonating legitimate vendor (openew[.]app pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states downloads from openew[.]app 'that impersonate OpenAI's desktop application download portal' — direct gap for masqueraded software distribution channels. Concrete IOC and attack pattern present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .exe/.dmg downloads from domains not matching official vendor registrations (openai.com, anthropic.com). Flag lookalike domains with 'open', 'ai', 'claude' in name, especially newly registered (WHOIS age <30d). Correlate with immediate child process execution spawning cmd/powershell to detect post-download malware activation.

suggestion.title: Fake outage/update prompts served via chatgpt.com/s and Claude Artifacts shared links
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake outage notice...rendered through ChatGPT itself' via chatgpt.com/s/ shares, and 'Claude Artifacts...ClickFix-style lures' — attackers weaponizing legitimate AI-platform content-sharing features for social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai/artifacts/* that render HTML pages containing 'outage', 'unavailable', 'download', or 'desktop app' language. Flag if followed by file downloads within 5 minutes. Check for HTML/CSS that mimics OpenAI or Anthropic UI but includes non-standard download domains.

suggestion.title: Virtualization sandbox evasion (VM detection commands in malware post-download)
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine' — explicit T1497.001 detection opportunity for evasion behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting suspicious .exe execution, monitor child processes for WMI/system queries checking VM presence: 'wmic os get caption', 'Get-WmiObject', 'systeminfo | find', VirtualBox/VMware driver checks. Flag if malware spawns multiple evasion checks (≥2 distinct techniques) in sequence within 10 seconds of execution.

suggestion.title: Google Ads steering to malicious chatgpt.com/s shared content
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page' — supply-chain compromise via ad network; requires referrer-based detection since destination domain is legitimate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP Referer headers containing 'google.com' or 'googleads' that direct to chatgpt.com/s/* URLs. Flag if ad search keywords include 'ChatGPT download', 'ChatGPT app', 'Claude download', combined with redirect to share/artifacts link rather than official vendor site. Correlate with subsequent malware downloads from openew[.]app or similar lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Content cloaking: benign response to security scanners, malicious to browsers
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware site 'uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims...URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website' — explicit evasion of threat-intel scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200 responses from openew[.]app or similar suspicious domains that vary significantly by user-agent. Flag if responses differ between security scanner user-agents (curl, URLScan, VirusTotal) and Chrome/Firefox browsers. Check for redirects or content-type mismatches that suggest conditional malware delivery. IP-based variance (different content per geolocation) also signals cloaking.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Attempts via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection.' Pipeline generated zero detections despite clear exploitation pathway: 'Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management and public-facing interfaces for exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-0257. Detect unusual authentication sequences, rapid invalid credential attempts, or suspicious HTTP/HTTPS traffic patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Alert on successful session establishment immediately following failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connections from PAN-OS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article's core attack outcome: 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' following successful bypass. This persistence mechanism requires explicit detection separate from initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN sessions created from PAN-OS devices lacking corresponding administrator authentication records. Flag VPN connections initiated by non-standard accounts, outside business hours, or from anomalous geographic locations. Correlate timing with known CVE-2026-0257 exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerable Asset Identification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article with explicit federal patch deadline (2026-06-01) and note 'patch lag is the silent killer' establishes vulnerability inventory as primary hunt. Article recommends asset-exposure template but pipeline generated no corresponding use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all PAN-OS deployments against CVE-2026-0257 vulnerable version ranges. Identify internet-facing instances. Cross-reference patch records. Escalate unpatched systems to asset owners with federal remediation deadline context. Prioritize based on exposure level and business criticality.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force and Credential Stuffing Against PAN-OS Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass exploitation typically involves reconnaissance phase. Article context ('allows attackers to bypass security restrictions') implies pre-exploitation attempts against authentication mechanisms that warrant anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS administrative services (SSH, HTTPS) for rapid failed authentication attempts. Alert on 10+ failed logins from single IP within 60 seconds. Correlate successful admin sessions immediately following brute-force patterns. Track unusual authentication sources or service account usage.

suggestion.title: Residential IP Proxy Botnet Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet was 'linked to Asocks, a universal proxy service' offering 'residential proxies' used by '100,000 clients' for legitimate-appearing traffic. Detection should flag anomalous outbound proxying patterns from consumer IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound connection volume or patterns from residential IP space to suspicious destinations, particularly traffic proxying to multiple third-party targets. Look for periodic beaconing or high-bandwidth transfers inconsistent with consumer device behavior.

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Execution from Botnet Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks' as primary botnet activity. 'Seized servers controlled computers, tablets, and smartphones to carry out cyberattacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect synchronized outbound HTTP/TCP floods from multiple compromised devices targeting the same destination IP or domain within short time window. Flag asymmetric bandwidth patterns (small inbound, large outbound) consistent with attack command execution.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Activity on Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'cryptocurrency mining' as explicit botnet capability. Requires CPU-intensive child processes and outbound connections to mining pool infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained high CPU usage (>80% for 5+ min) combined with outbound connections to known mining pool domains or IP ranges. Look for obscured process trees (parent process termination, renamed miners) and abnormal process scheduling.

suggestion.title: Botnet Initial Infection via Unpatched Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article's remediation guidance ('ensure...the latest firmware update has been applied, remote administration panels are disabled') strongly implies infection vector is unpatched device vulnerabilities and default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag exploitation attempts against known botnet family vulnerabilities on IoT/networking devices (routers, cameras, NAS). Monitor for successful exploitation indicators: unexpected firmware modifications, new user accounts, or lateral movement from device to internal network after compromise.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms botnet operated via '200 servers' C2 infrastructure. Post-takedown detection should identify surviving C2 beacons and orphaned botnet nodes attempting reconnection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or connection attempts to seized Netherlands hosting provider IPs or known Asocks infrastructure domains (if identified post-investigation). Alert on repeated reconnection attempts from previously-identified botnet device signatures, indicating failed C2 failover logic.

suggestion.title: Default Credentials and Exposed Remote Access Panels
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'ensure default credentials have been changed...remote administration panels are disabled when not needed'—indicating botnet initial access relied on default credentials and exposed management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to common management ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 8080, 9000) using default credentials for ubiquitous IoT/networking device brands (TP-Link, D-Link, Linksys, Synology, etc.). Flag successful logins followed by firmware modification or user account creation.

suggestion.title: vm2 module instantiation + Buffer prototype chain access patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit mechanism: 'By combining Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")' and '__lookupSetter__' — these exact patterns indicate exploit attempt. No detection suggested for the actual attack vector; all provided UCs focus on post-escape effects only.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution or HTTP payloads containing the phrase 'Buffer.call.call' adjacent to '__lookupGetter__' or '__lookupSetter__', combined with Node process context. This detects the exploit attempt itself, not just post-exploitation behavior.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 version installed via npm dependency management
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vm2 ≤3.11.3 as vulnerable. No detection for supply-chain compromise (npm package installation, dependency manifest updates). Pipeline output shows no kill-chain mapping for 'recon' or 'preparation' phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs and dependency lock files for installations or persisted references to vm2 versions matching regex ^([0-2]\.|3\.([0-9]|10|11)(\.([0-3]))?$). Alert on any deployment of these versions.

suggestion.title: TypeError constructor escape from sandboxed Node context
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained, which allows the escape from the sandbox.' This is the actual escape indicator. No detection for constructor access attempts or elevation of privilege from sandbox to host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js process errors and exception logs for Error objects instantiated with 'constructor' property access following vm2/NodeVM instantiation, or trace file descriptor escalation immediately post-Error instantiation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious nesting:true configuration without require specification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the bypass: 'when `require` is not specified, `options.require` is `undefined`, not `false`. The strict equality check is bypassed.' No UC detects this code-level pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan JavaScript source files in Node.js applications for NodeVM instantiation patterns with nesting:true but no require:false. Look for `new NodeVM({nesting: true})` or `new NodeVM({nesting:true,...})` without `require:false` in the same object literal.

suggestion.title: vm2 package.json version audit with CVE tag
suggestion.rationale: UC_25_3 detects presence but not patched vs. vulnerable versions. Article describes a patchable flaw (<=3.11.3). Need proactive version scanning before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json from all Node.js projects on host. Extract vm2 version field and flag any <3.11.4 or with version undefined. Correlate with deploy timestamps to identify when vulnerable code entered production.

suggestion.title: Unsafe ChildProcess spawning from NodeVM context with shell=true
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'full RCE' via escape. The exploit chain is sandbox escape → spawn shell. No UC detects the OS shell spawned SPECIFICALLY with shell:true (which amplifies command injection). The fix required is `shell: false`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for `child_process.exec()` or `child_process.spawn({shell: true})` patterns in Node.js that are called within vm2 NestVM contexts. Cross-correlate process parentage (Node.js parent, immediate shell child with no intermediate wrapper).

suggestion.title: Modifications to vm2 library files post-install (nodevm.js line 263 patch verification)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerability at 'nodevm.js line 263' where the strict equality check is. Attackers or post-exploitation activity might patch vm2 locally to remove the check entirely. No UC monitors for library tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file modifications to `node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js` after package installation. Baseline the hash of the patched version (3.11.3+) and alert on deviation. Flag file writes from non-package-manager processes.

suggestion.title: require() function availability checks in sandbox context
suggestion.rationale: The exploit hinges on attacker ability to call require() or access child_process despite sandbox. Article doesn't describe detection of require scope leakage, only the configuration bypass. Should hunt for runtime require() calls escaping intended scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Node.js apps using vm2, enable verbose logging of require() calls. Flag any require('child_process') or require('fs') calls that occur within a NestVM context where require was supposed to be disabled. Cross-reference with running parent context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious require('process') or require('inspector') module loading in Node.js contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'denylist misses `process` and `inspector/promises`' and 'getBuiltinModule' is the exploitation primitive. A require() call to these restricted modules from within a vm2-sandboxed context is the signature exploitation step, yet no detection for module-level code inspection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript files (*.js, *.mjs) in vm2-related paths or created by Node processes that contain literal strings matching 'require("process")', 'require("inspector")', 'getBuiltinModule', or 'inspector.promises'. These indicate denylist-bypass attempt.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning or file write post-vm2-module-loading anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'reach host-side execution primitives' and 'execute code in the host process.' After successfully requiring process/inspector, attackers immediately invoke dangerous operations (shell commands, file writes). Detection should correlate require() of restricted modules with subsequent suspicious I/O.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If a Node.js process loads require('process') or inspector/promises within 5 seconds followed by CreateRemoteThread, file writes to %TEMP%, or child process creation of cmd/powershell, escalate as post-exploitation. Baseline: legitimate vm2 usage should not load process module.

suggestion.title: npm/yarn package.json or node_modules/vm2 integrity monitoring
suggestion.rationale: vm2 vulnerable versions (3.0–3.11.3) are the attack surface. Attackers may inject malicious vm2 installation or modify vm2 module files post-compromise to persist or widen the denylist bypass. Article does not explicitly mention file modification, but supply-chain integrity is a natural extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node_modules/vm2/ directory for unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion. Baseline expected files and hashes. Flag suspicious version downgrades (3.11.x → 3.9.x) or file additions outside normal npm install operations.

suggestion.title: Debugging protocol activation (inspector/promises entry point)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'inspector/promises' as denylist-bypass vector. This module enables Node.js debugging protocol; activation outside dev environments or without explicit --inspect flag may indicate exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe processes spawned WITHOUT --inspect, --inspect-brk, or --inspect-port flags but with inspector/promises module instantiation in their working directory or loaded by parent sandboxing framework. Baseline: dev/CI environments expect inspector; production does not.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype.finally() species bypass detection — vm2 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47210)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'JSPI-backed Promise `.finally()` species bypass' and 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach `Promise.prototype.finally()` in a way that bypasses...Promise-species hardening'. The actual exploitation mechanism (Promise species manipulation) has no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Promise prototype chain manipulation attempts (Symbol.species assignment, finally() method override, constructor access) in Node.js processes executing untrusted code. Flag attempts to bypass hardened Promise constructors or species objects.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI instantiation in untrusted async contexts — vm2 precursor (CVE-2026-47210)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI (WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending)'. WebAssembly.instantiate/instantiateStreaming in vm2 contexts is an exploit prerequisite not covered by existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebAssembly module loading (wasm files, WebAssembly API calls) in Node.js processes executing untrusted scripts, especially in combination with async/await patterns. Monitor for wasm staged to temp or node_modules directories.

suggestion.title: Host object prototype escape from vm2 sandbox — T1611 (CVE-2026-47210)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes how vulnerability 'exposes a host-originate[d]' functionality via species bypass. T1611 'Escape to Host' is listed but has no corresponding detection for accessing host-level Promise constructors or global objects from the sandbox.
