suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Unsigned Binary Execution
suggestion.rationale: China-aligned APTs routinely use living-off-the-land binaries to avoid AV detection, but pipeline surface no evasion techniques for a 'ramped up' sustained campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of System32 binaries (mshta.exe, regsvcs.exe, InstallUtil.exe, wscript.exe) with unusual parent processes or command-line arguments. Alert on DLL injection into legitimate processes.

suggestion.title: Exposed WebLogic T3 Listener Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP' — requires baseline detection of exposed WebLogic T3 listeners accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebLogic instances (java.exe, weblogic.Server) with open T3 listeners on default ports 7001/7002 accepting inbound connections from external networks. Alert on established T3 connections from non-approved external sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 T3 Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism: 'unauthenticated attacker...via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server.' Requires network-layer detection of actual exploit delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect T3 protocol traffic containing known exploitation signatures, malformed T3 packets, serialized Java objects with RCE payloads, or unusual T3 handshake anomalies. Correlate with external IP sources probing WebLogic.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation WebLogic Data Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Requires detection of abnormal data exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic audit and database logs for bulk data queries, privilege escalation, or access to sensitive tables following successful T3 connection. Flag unusual data volume transfers from WebLogic application context.

suggestion.title: WebLogic RCE Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2024-21182 exploitation via T3 results in arbitrary code execution; article does not describe read-only data leaks, implying remote code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned by WebLogic JVM (weblogic.Server, java.exe processes) with command lines indicating cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, curl, or reverse-shell utilities. Alert on code execution in WebLogic process context.

suggestion.title: Docker Image Repository Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository' as initial access vector; pipeline failed to generate detection logic for malicious image distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Docker image tags pushed to public registries with version inconsistencies, rapid tag churn, or signatures indicative of trojanized binaries (entropy spikes, added binary sections). Alert on pulls of images from high-risk maintainers or repositories with no history.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration and Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers stole 'Kubernetes secrets' following container compromise; no detection logic provided for secret access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on get/list API calls to secretresources from service accounts, especially with list-all queries or cross-namespace access. Correlate secret reads with new environment variable injection or base64-decoding child processes.

suggestion.title: Stealer Payload Execution in Container Scanning Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stealer loaded during the KICS scanning process'—execution of malware within a build/scan tool is a distinct detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code execution (spawned processes, DLL injection, memory writes) originating from container scanning tools (kics, trivy, etc.) or package managers. Look for unsigned binaries, network activity to exfil domains, or creation of temporary credential-harvesting files.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capability Abuse (CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_MODULE)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE as escape vectors but pipeline generated no detection for privileged capability usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag containers spawned with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN unless explicitly whitelisted by workload. Alert on attempts to load kernel modules, modify proc/sysfs, or attach to host processes from within a container.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Host Filesystem Mount
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'container escape' and 'host compromise' but provides no detection logic for escape techniques using mounted volumes or cgroup manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes accessing /proc/self/cgroup, /sys/kernel, or mounted host filesystems (especially /etc, /root, /var/run/secrets). Alert on attempts to write to cgroup.procs or write_dominator_tree within container context.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Abuse for Cluster Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'exploitation of orchestration APIs' and credential theft but no detection for lateral movement or persistence via kubectl/API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service account API tokens being used outside their source pod/namespace. Alert on kubeconfig extraction, token exfil to external IPs, or API calls to create/modify resources (Deployments, DaemonSets, ClusterRoles) from compromised pods.

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection via Cache Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw'—this is deserialization attack, not merely public-app exploitation. Pipeline conflated T1190 with the specific vulnerability vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Magento cache-plugin paths (*/cache/*, */warmer/*) with payloads containing base64-encoded PHP serialized objects (O:\d+: pattern) or __PHP_Incomplete_Class markers in request body.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Plugin-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article says 'remotely execute malicious code' but pipeline omitted execution-phase detection. Process spawning should follow cache-endpoint HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash, sh, or perl spawned by web server user (www-data, apache, httpd) within 5 seconds following HTTP 200 responses to cache-plugin endpoints. Flag command lines with 'curl', 'wget', or /dev/tcp reverse shell patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Cache-Plugin Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required'—authentication bypass is the core weakness. Pipeline missed this fundamental characteristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log successful access (HTTP 200) to cache-plugin admin paths (/cache/config, /cache/manage, /warmer/settings) from source IPs without preceding authentication events or valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited'—pipeline must surface detection logic for requests targeting the vulnerable plugin endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints with POST payloads or unusual query parameters. Correlate spike in 200/403 responses on plugin paths with subsequent admin account creation events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Admin Account Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Create Admin Accounts' as the exploitation outcome—must detect new admin user creation outside provisioning workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table INSERT with role=administrator created by web service account (www-data/IIS AppPool) or during exploitation window. Baseline normal admin creation rate and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability exploitation leads directly to privilege escalation (admin creation)—need detection for the intermediate compromise step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests with PHP code patterns, function names (wp_create_user, wp_update_user), or parameter injection attempts targeting the plugin. Watch for requests originating from non-admin networks that precede admin account creation by <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Brute Force: Multiple Failed Auth Attempts Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'attempted logins...by trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' No use case generated for detecting this core attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single user account receives ≥5 failed authentication attempts within 5 minutes or ≥10 failed attempts within 30 minutes from any source. Exclude known automated processes and service accounts. Expected behavior: account lockout triggered within next 2-5 attempts.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Spike Detection: Coordinated Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple Dashlane users have been locked out...resulting in suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.' Pipeline missed detection of coordinated mass-lockout pattern indicating campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when account lockout events exceed baseline by >3 standard deviations within 1-hour window (e.g., normal=2/hr, spike=20+/hr). Correlate with source IPs and failed authentication attempts to confirm brute force vs. accidental lockouts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration: Unconfirmed Verification Codes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries. The emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for this secondary indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when device registration verification codes are issued following failed login attempts from same or adjacent IP/geolocation. Alert if >3 verification codes issued to same user within 30 minutes without successful device registration completion.

suggestion.title: Geolocation Velocity: Login Attempts from Impossible Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'attempted logins from distant locations' and 'suspicious access requests from foreign countries.' No use case for detecting geographic impossibilities (e.g., simultaneous logins across continents).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when same account has login attempts (failed or successful) from two geolocation IPs within timeframe shorter than physical travel distance would allow. Example: US IP at 10:00 UTC, then China IP at 10:15 UTC same account = alert.

suggestion.title: Rate Limiting Trigger: CAPTCHA and Lockout Cascades
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Dashlane deployed 'rate limiting, CAPTCHA challenges, and account lockouts to block automated attacks.' These are observable defense triggers but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 429 (rate limit) or 403 (CAPTCHA required) responses preceded by >5 failed authentication attempts from same source IP within 10 minutes. Correlate with account lockout events to confirm brute force response.

suggestion.title: Brute Force: Password Spraying Across Multiple Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly confirm single password tested on multiple accounts vs. multiple passwords on single account. Pipeline should generate detection hypothesis for both T1110.001 (password guessing per-account) and T1110.002 (password spray across population).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when authentication failures spike across multiple distinct user accounts from same source IP(s) within short window (e.g., 10+ distinct users with failed login from same IP in 10 min). Indicates spray attack vs. targeted brute force.

suggestion.title: Workspace member grants owner role to non-self account without elevated privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'forwards the request body's `user_id` and `role` straight into `MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role)` ... has no caller-permission check' — the vulnerability allows any member (role=member) to grant owner to ANY user ID. UC_18_2 catches the POST request, but should correlate: requestor privilege level BEFORE grant vs. role being assigned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST /workspaces/*/members where the requesting user's role in that workspace is 'member' or lower, yet the request succeeds in granting 'owner' role. This violates the implicit authorization boundary. Requires user-role context in the same log stream or correlated against a workspace-membership snapshot.

suggestion.title: Identical user_id in add-member requests (self-escalation variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any workspace member can add arbitrary user as owner' but attacker could add themselves (grantor_id == grantee_id). UC_18_3 requires distinct accounts. Should hunt separately for cases where the requesting user grants themselves owner role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST /workspaces/*/members where the authenticated user_id in the request matches the user_id in the JSON body. One-shot privilege escalation with no suspicious login pattern following.

suggestion.title: Workspace member enumeration or repeated failed member-add attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article shows gating only checks 'require_workspace_member(workspace_id)' — an attacker must first gain member access (via legitimate invite, insider, etc.). Should hunt for discovery phase: repeated queries to enumerate members or role-structure before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Pre-exploit reconnaissance: GET requests to /workspaces/*/members or /workspaces/{id} returning 200/403 across multiple workspace IDs, followed shortly by POST /workspaces/*/members on a workspace where the requestor was initially denied. Suggests targeting phase.

suggestion.title: Workspace owner permission revocation post-grant (cleanup evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistent privilege escalation but does not explicitly state whether logs show the owner revocation or cleanup post-attack. An attacker may remove the newly-granted owner to cover tracks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST /workspaces/*/members adds owner role within a short time window (minutes), followed by DELETE or PATCH /workspaces/*/members/{user_id} removing that user or lowering role. Temporal proximity suggests cleanup.

suggestion.title: ClickFix PowerShell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands'—need detection for malicious PS execution patterns triggered by social engineering. No use case generated despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell execution from unusual parents (rundll32, explorer, browser processes) with suspicious command line obfuscation, encoding, or known attack patterns. Alert on ps.exe spawned with base64 or IEX patterns commonly seen in ClickFix chains.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Executable Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' No detection for this common payload delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of executables with impersonated browser-update names (Browser Update.exe, ChromeUpdate.exe, etc.) from non-standard sources. Alert on ZIP downloads from web followed by extraction and execution of DLLs/EXEs within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: JavaScript t.js Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' as a technical fingerprint. This domain-level indicator should drive network/proxy detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to domains matching pattern t.js?site=* or similar TDS probe patterns. Alert on legitimate websites (identified by Silent Push or high Alexa rank) generating outbound requests to malware infrastructure after rendering this JS.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Compromise via Compromised High-Reputation Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware.' Needs detection for redirect chains from trusted domains to malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 302/301 redirects originating from high-reputation domains (Fortune 500 sites, CDNs, news outlets) to unknown malware distribution infrastructure. Alert on redirect chains >2 hops with destination domain reputation unknown or malicious.

suggestion.title: macOS ClickFix with Clipboard Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' No macOS-specific detection despite disclosed capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript execution with clipboard read/write access on macOS, especially paired with verification/security-themed prompts. Alert on bash/zsh child processes spawned from browser with clipboard data containing suspicious commands.

suggestion.title: Malicious DLL Extraction from Downloaded ZIP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs' as delivery mechanism. Need detection for ZIP extraction patterns containing DLLs from web downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect extraction of DLL files from ZIP archives downloaded from web. Alert on DLL extraction from browser Downloads folder followed by immediate rundll32/regsvcs execution or DLL injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to WebSphere Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'specially crafted HTTP requests' to 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component.' Pipeline produced zero detection use cases despite this being the actual exploitation mechanism. Need to detect anomalous request patterns (payloads, headers, method misuse) targeting known vulnerable plugin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WebSphere plugin endpoints for request patterns matching known exploit signatures (crafted payloads, abnormal header sequences, method combinations). Baseline normal request structure and alert on deviations; focus on requests that would trigger plugin deserialization or expression evaluation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from WebSphere JVM
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'execute arbitrary code' but pipeline only mapped T1190 (initial access), omitting execution phase entirely. Must detect unexpected child processes spawned from WebSphere Java process post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where parent is Java/WebSphere process and child is cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, or /bin/bash running suspicious commands. Baseline legitimate WebSphere process tree and escalate on new child process patterns, especially within seconds of suspicious HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Application Server HTTP Error Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts typically manifest as 400-series errors in application logs before successful code execution. Article's 'specially crafted' nature implies probing/fuzzing to find valid payloads—this phase is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for 4xx HTTP error rates on WebSphere plugin endpoints. Alert on sustained elevation (3+ std dev above baseline over 5-minute window) or spike patterns consistent with payload fuzzing or multiple exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from WebSphere Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RCE attacker will typically establish C2 or exfil channel. Article describes 'execute arbitrary code' implying post-compromise callback/reverse-shell, but network-based detection is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound connections from WebSphere Java process to non-whitelisted external IPs/ports, especially over HTTP, HTTPS, or raw sockets. Correlate with suspicious process execution from WebSphere parent.

suggestion.title: Malicious Serialized Object in WebSphere Request Body
suggestion.rationale: WebSphere vulnerabilities typically exploit insecure deserialization in plugin handlers. Article's 'specially crafted' requests likely contain gadget chains or serialized payloads—no payload-level detection mapped.
log_sources: WebSphere request logs with body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request bodies to WebSphere endpoints for Java serialization magic bytes (0xaced), base64-encoded serialized objects, or known gadget-chain signatures (Apache Commons, Spring, etc.). Correlate with HTTP methods known to trigger plugin processing (POST, OPTIONS, TRACE).

suggestion.title: Preinstall Hook Execution During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes, so simply resolving the dependency is enough to trigger the payload' — this is the primary execution vector and needs detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or node processes spawned during npm install with suspicious activity. Alert on index.js execution from npm package directories, especially with unusual file writes, environment variable access, or credential store reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Request in CI Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write' — this pattern is the initial access mechanism and should trigger on write-scoped OIDC requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows requesting OIDC identity tokens with write permissions, especially those modifying CI/CD config or package publishing workflows. Correlate with commits bypassing review processes.

suggestion.title: Orphan Commit Bypass of Code Review
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'pushed malicious orphan commits directly into two RedHatInsights repositories, bypassing code review' — this evasion technique bypasses normal review gates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for orphan commits (commits with no parent in repository history) or direct pushes that skip pull request workflows. Alert on commits modifying GitHub Actions configuration outside the review process.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'enumerates every identity the infected host can assume' for GCP and Azure — identity enumeration APIs called from npm/Node.js contexts are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GCP and Azure for identity enumeration API calls originating from Node.js processes or package manager contexts. Alert on iam.googleapis.com or Microsoft.Authorization read operations from unusual sources, especially bulk queries.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access During npm Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies harvesting of '~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens' — npm processes reading credential stores during installation is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Package Republication by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload' — this lateral propagation should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for unexpected re-publication of stable package versions by accounts with multiple publishing rights. Alert on rapid republishing without source code changes, especially outside normal CI/CD maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious codexui-android npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack' as the primary vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no detection logic for malicious package installation.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Exfiltration via Compromised Module
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen' — pipeline failed to create detection for credential harvesting and unauthorized token use.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound HTTPS from Development Machine
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages typically beacon to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline created no C2 detection despite supply chain context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Chains from Legitimate Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT 'chains multiple advanced techniques together'—process injection is core mechanism. This implies suspicious spawning patterns where legitimate Windows binaries (System32, Program Files) execute unusual children. Named as core technique in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for parent processes like explorer.exe, svchost.exe, or rundll32.exe spawning command-line tools (powershell, cmd, wscript) without corresponding user action or logged RDP session. Detect mismatched image paths or working directories. Prioritize if parent binary is unsigned or matches known injection vector (e.g., lsass.exe spawning anything except expected service DLLs).

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Initial Access Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article title references Dragon Weave conducting attacks; article body is truncated but title establishes active compromise attempt. Pipeline generated no use cases despite 'high' severity flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance activity (DNS queries, web browsing, passive fingerprinting) against Czech government and Taiwan-related entities consistent with pre-attack OSINT collection by China-aligned threat groups.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Malware Deployment C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article headline indicates active attacks; no IOCs extracted and no C2 detection logic generated despite being mandatory for operational-stage TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous outbound connections from Czech and Taiwan infrastructure to known or suspected Dragon Weave C2 ranges; look for beaconing patterns and encrypted DNS tunneling.

suggestion.title: China-Aligned APT Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title states attacks occurred but pipeline extracted zero details on post-compromise activity; standard APT workflow includes lateral movement not captured here.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for use of legitimate remote administration tools (RDP, WinRM, SSH) originating from compromised internal systems; flag credential re-use across administrative boundaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body directly name 'CVE-2024-21182'; pipeline generated zero use cases despite vulnerability matching being primary detection vector for known CVEs. Federal patch due 2026-06-04 makes scanner-based inventory critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result identifying CVE-2024-21182 in Oracle WebLogic Server. Prioritize internet-accessible instances with open T3 ports (default 7001, 7003). Flag unpatched systems as critical until remediated by federal due date.

suggestion.title: T3 Protocol Exploitation Attempts to WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector 'via T3, IIOP' protocols; pipeline failed to surface protocol-level IOCs. T3 is Oracle-proprietary and suspicious T3 handshake traffic to port 7001 is high-fidelity exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag malformed or failed T3 protocol handshakes to WebLogic default ports (7001, 7003) from external IPs. Alert on rapid T3 connection probing (scanning). Successful T3 session immediately followed by anomalous outbound connections indicates exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WebLogic Admin Console Access Post-CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker'; pipeline missed auth-bypass behavioral detection. Failed authentication followed by successful console access (via CVE exploitation) is definitive compromise signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP requests to WebLogic admin endpoints (/console, /weblogic) from IPs with no prior successful authentication. Correlate with suspicious payloads (Java serialization patterns, IIOP abuse) in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Command Execution via Compromised WebLogic Process
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'; pipeline missed execution/impact phase. Post-compromise command execution from WebLogic java context is behavioral evidence of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) spawned by WebLogic java.exe or weblogic.Server processes. Alert on suspicious tool execution (curl, wget, certutil, nc) from WebLogic context without corresponding change ticket.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised WebLogic Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'unauthorized access to critical data'; pipeline missed post-exploitation data collection/exfiltration detection despite being stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic process for bulk reads of database config files, sensitive application data, or credential stores. Flag unusual outbound connections to non-business external IPs/ports (especially SOCKS, SSH, SSH tunnels) immediately following successful exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Oracle WebLogic Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal remediation deadline (2026-06-04); organizations must inventory public-facing WebLogic instances. Pipeline referenced template but generated no concrete asset-exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and network scanning data for all Oracle WebLogic Server instances with accessible T3 (port 7001) or IIOP (port 7002) ports from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results. Flag any internet-routable unpatched instance as P1 exposure.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning: Stealer Payload in Scanning Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets' and 'tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' Supply chain attack requires detection of suspicious image pulls and child process anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KICS container pulls of modified/unsigned images from Docker Hub followed by unexpected child process execution (shells, curl, wget). Correlate image pull timestamps with manifest changes. Baseline KICS process tree and flag deviations indicating payload execution.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Theft from Container Runtime Mount
suggestion.rationale: Article: stealer payload aims to 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' executed within container context. Requires detection of credential access from /var/run/secrets mounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned within scanning containers that read /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount or similar Kubernetes secret mount paths. Alert if those processes then establish outbound connections or write to temp files resembling credential material.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capability Exploitation (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists: 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE CAP_SYS_PTRACE CAP_NET_ADMIN' as container isolation bypass mechanisms. These directly enable escape and host compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container creation with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_PTRACE. Escalate if container process then calls ptrace(2) on host PIDs, open(/proc/*/mem), or modifies cgroup.procs. Alert CAP_SYS_MODULE + module insertion syscalls.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Namespace and Cgroup Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Container escape followed by host compromise' using 'namespaces, cgroups, capabilities' abuse. Syscall-level detection of isolation layer exploitation required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clone/unshare syscalls from container context that merge namespaces (CLONE_NEWPID=0, CLONE_NEWNET=0). Alert on open() of /proc/sys/kernel, write to cgroup.procs, or mmap of host kernel memory. Flag privileged syscalls (ioctl, bpf) from container PIDs.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Exploitation: Unauthenticated or Lateral Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' and 'orchestration API abuse' as critical attack vector. Requires detection of K8s API reconnaissance and abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API server audit logs for high-volume GET requests to Secrets, ServiceAccounts, or ClusterRoles from single pod identity. Alert on API calls with missing/expired bearer tokens. Flag cross-namespace enumeration or list operations outside pod's own namespace.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Checkmarx KICS Container Image Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: TeamPCP 'compromised Checkmarx KICS across multiple attack chains' via poisoned Docker Hub image. Container scanning tools are attack surface requiring detection of malicious image layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement image content scanning to detect stealer payloads or modified KICS binaries in pulled images. Alert on KICS images with unexpected layers, added binaries, or altered entrypoints. Require image signature verification and tag pinning to prevent drift to poisoned versions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected WordPress Administrator Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation resulting in 'Create Admin Accounts' — core persistence mechanism. Detection of new admin-role user accounts in WordPress is a primary defensive indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events and role assignments. Alert on new user accounts with administrator role created outside normal change-management windows or by non-admin accounts. Correlate with failed login attempts or plugin exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'WP Maps Pro' as the vulnerable component and states it is 'actively exploited' — direct attack vector that should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests targeting WP Maps Pro endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) for POST requests with suspicious payloads, encoded parameters, or requests to admin-facing endpoints from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with 401/403 errors followed by successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via WordPress Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title describes exploit resulting in admin account creation from unauthenticated or low-privilege state — classic privilege escalation kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where unauthenticated HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro endpoints are followed immediately by successful admin login or WordPress user table modifications. Flag successful role changes from subscriber/contributor to administrator within minutes of plugin exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: WordPress Database Modification for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Creating admin accounts requires direct database modification or WordPress API calls — detectable via query logging and WordPress audit hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor INSERT and UPDATE operations on wp_users table and wp_usermeta for admin role assignments. Alert on modifications without corresponding WordPress administrative REST API calls or WP-CLI invocations. Cross-reference with failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Admin Functionality
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates vulnerability allows unauthenticated exploitation to create accounts — implies bypass of normal authentication/authorization controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal access patterns to /wp-admin and plugin admin endpoints. Alert on repeated HTTP requests from external IPs to wp-admin paths that normally return 302/403 but receive 200 responses, or requests with Admin Ajax parameters before authentication.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload via WP Maps Pro
suggestion.rationale: Plugin vulnerabilities often enable file upload attacks — article does not explicitly state upload vector but privilege-escalation exploits in mapping plugins frequently use this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/uploads/ directory for new PHP or executable files, and /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ for unexpected file modifications. Alert on POST requests with multipart/form-data to plugin admin endpoints or file handling functions.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Authentication from Distant Geolocations
suggestion.rationale: Article states brute-force attacks 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' No UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication failures that spike in count (e.g., >10 failures in 5 minutes) and originate from geographically distant locations relative to user baseline or registered devices. Correlate failed attempts with geographic distances >1000km or country code mismatches.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Triggered by Brute Force Threshold
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls'—an automated response to brute-force detection. No UC addresses detection of lockouts themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when account lockout events follow a sequence of 5+ failed authentication attempts within 10 minutes, especially from non-whitelisted IP ranges or new geographic regions.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Initiated Without User Request
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries. The emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Pipeline missed this secondary indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registration or MFA enrollment emails sent to users without a corresponding user-initiated password reset, registration request, or new device consent event. Flag if sender location/IP differs from known user patterns.

suggestion.title: Authentication Failure Rate Spike Correlated with Email Verification Surge
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force activity generated both failed logins and unsolicited verification emails. Pipeline should correlate these two signals occurring within same time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed sign-in attempts with unexpected verification/device-registration email dispatch to the same user account within a 15-minute window. If email count exceeds user baseline by >3x, escalate as potential brute force in progress.

suggestion.title: Authentication Failures from Multiple Unknown IP/Device Combinations
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unknown devices' and login attempts from locations users did not recognize. Pipeline should detect first-seen device + location pairs failing auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication failures where both the source IP and device user agent are first-seen for that user account. Threshold: ≥3 unique IP+device pairs with failures in 1 hour.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner (CVE-2026-47413)
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes UC_21_2 as high-confidence exploit detection: 'POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner' returning HTTP 201. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite detailed Splunk and KQL provided in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to /workspaces/*/members endpoints with role=owner in request body returning HTTP 201 status. Restrict to authenticated workspace-member sources, as non-members fail earlier authorization checks.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: owner-grant followed by account login (CVE-2026-47413)
suggestion.rationale: Article defines UC_21_3: correlate POST /workspaces/*/members role=owner grant with login of the newly-granted account from same source IP within 1 hour. Signals exploitation in-the-wild. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate owner-grant POST requests against login events: join on source IP, alert when the newly-granted user authenticates from the same IP within 1 hour of the grant, with new-user identity differing from grantor. Indicates backdoor account creation and immediate attacker use.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: MemberService backend module execution and file changes (CVE-2026-47413)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides UC_21_1: behavioral hunt for member_service.py and deps.py process execution or file modification. These are the backend modules performing unvalidated grants. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for execution of member_service.py or deps.py on praisonai-platform servers, or creation/modification of these files (file_action=created|modified). Correlate with suspicious parent processes (shells, attack frameworks, non-standard callers) to exclude benign CI/CD execution.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Detection via Executable Naming
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake update prompts downloading executable named 'Browser Update.exe' and similar browser-named payloads for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, etc. Pipeline missed detection of binaries with browser names + update-themed naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process execution or file creation with names matching pattern <BrowserName>*[Uu]pdate*.exe where BrowserName ∈ {Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave}. High fidelity indicator of FakeUpdates payload. Alert especially on execution from Downloads or temp directories without a legitimate browser update context (timing, parent process).

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection (zTDS Fingerprint)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'eight technical fingerprints' with specific mention of JavaScript injection following 't.js?site=<id>' pattern. Pipeline missed the most concrete IOC: the script source pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to domains serving 't.js' with query parameter site=<numeric|hex_id>. Flag domains not whitelisted as known CDN or analytics providers. Cross-reference against DNS query logs for domains with high request velocity but low domain age or reputation. zTDS infrastructure frequently reused across multiple compromised sites.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution via ClickFix Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands that deceive users into copy-pasting and executing. No detection logic for suspicious clipboard-sourced PowerShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe or pwsh.exe execution with parent process Internet Explorer, Edge, Chrome, or Firefox where command-line contains base64 encoded content OR arrives within seconds of a clipboard-access event. ClickFix campaigns use copy-paste social engineering; correlation with web browser + rapid shell invocation is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: Compromised Site Redirect Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'legitimate, high-reputation websites...silently redirects visitors to malware.' Redirect chains from known-good domains through zTDS to delivery infrastructure represent initial compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for redirect chains (HTTP 301/302) originating from legitimate, highly-ranked websites (Alexa/Similarweb top 1M) to unranked or low-reputation domains. zTDS will issue rapid geo-profiling probes before final redirect. Alert on repeat redirect destinations from multiple source sites or short time-to-execution of follow-on executable download.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking in Verification-Themed ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS...hijack the clipboard, indicating that the campaign extends beyond Windows.' No detection for clipboard manipulation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On macOS endpoints, monitor for JavaScript execution (Safari, Chrome, Firefox) followed by clipboard read/write system calls in short succession. ClickFix variants modify clipboard contents to inject malicious commands. Correlate with failed verification-themed dialogs, unusual script origins, or obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Browser Update Spoofing Across Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article lists FakeUpdates targeting 10 distinct browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, UC Browser) from same campaign. A single source offering updates for multiple browsers is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains or redirect chains that serve fake update prompts for multiple browser vendors within a short window. Legitimate updates come from single browser vendor per domain; multi-browser update sources are almost always malicious. Track across geolocation and user-agent strings.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation Followed by Credential Store Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing worm' delivered via npm packages. Any npm install that accesses ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or .env-like files is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm postinstall/preinstall scripts or spawned child processes (node, bash, powershell) accessing credential repositories (SSH keys, AWS credentials, password managers, Git configs) within 30 seconds of package installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connection from npm Package Installation Directory
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware must exfiltrate harvested credentials; article mentions worm behavior implying C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections initiated from node.exe or child processes spawned under node_modules directories to non-whitelisted IPs/domains, especially with uncommon ports or suspicious user agents.

suggestion.title: Lateral Propagation via Enumeration Post-npm Infection
suggestion.rationale: Title designates payload as 'worm', indicating self-propagating behavior and multi-host compromise capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid network scanning, SSH/credential spraying, or file share enumeration originating from systems after npm package installation; correlate with credentials accessed in prior stage.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Base64-Encoded Script Execution in npm postinstall Hook
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks commonly hide malicious payloads in install scripts. Article's silence on indicators suggests obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm lifecycle scripts (postinstall, preinstall, prepare) for invocation of cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash with Base64/hex-encoded arguments or suspicious shell redirections; regex: `(atob|Buffer.from.*base64|0x[0-9a-f])`.

suggestion.title: Red Hat npm Registry or Package Name Pattern Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'Red Hat npm packages'; legitimate packages may be mimicked or typosquatted. Pipeline should flag package name/source deviations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands for package names matching known Red Hat packages but sourced from non-official registries, or package versions with unusual hashes not matching npm public registry checksums.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution Harvesting Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes preinstall hook that 'runs an obfuscated payload the moment a package is installed, harvesting developer and cloud credentials.' No detection UC generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install process spawning node.exe/node with subsequent access to ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, environment variable reads, and cloud CLI tools (gcloud, az). Look for children of npm processes accessing /home/*/.*rc files, /root/.aws, or CI_* environment variable enumeration within 5 seconds of package install completion.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code in npm Package with Valid SLSA Provenance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The malicious code did not slip in through a typosquat or a poisoned transitive dependency' and 'published packages with valid SLSA provenance,' yet payload used 'eval() and ROT-based string decoding.' Detection of high-entropy obfuscation in provenance-verified packages is a novel trust-boundary attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with valid SLSA provenance (v1.0+, built from GitHub Actions) whose preinstall or prepublish scripts contain eval() calls, Base64-encoded segments >500 bytes, or String.fromCharCode patterns indicating deobfuscation. Baseline legitimate packages; alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Requesting OIDC Token to Publish Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes root cause: 'malicious orphan commits that requested an npm-publishing OIDC token' via GitHub Actions with `id-token: write` permission. This is the supply-chain injection point preceding all downstream compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows in publishing repositories that request OIDC identity tokens (`id-token: write`) without prior code-review approval, especially if commits came from off-business-hours or from new GitHub accounts. Cross-check against known publisher approval lists.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration via Compromised npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'newly created attacker repositories carry the description Miasma' and payload 'Enumerates cloud identities. The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume.' No detection UC for cloud enumeration from package install context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GCP ServiceAccount.get() or Azure role enumeration API calls (GET /subscriptions/{}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions) originating from npm install process context or from CI/CD runner executing npm install. Look for rapid enumeration of multiple identities within single session.

suggestion.title: Self-Replicating npm Package via Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm behavior: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' No detection UC for self-propagating package behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm registry API calls listing user-publishable packages (GET /user packages or equivalent) immediately followed by version bumps and re-publication of unrelated packages with identical payload signatures or obfuscation patterns. Alert if multiple packages from same publisher republished within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise Followed by Orphan Commits Bypassing Code Review
suggestion.rationale: Article describes account takeover vector: 'A compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account was compromised and used to push malicious orphan commits directly into two RedHatInsights repositories, bypassing code review.' No detection for review-bypass attacks from compromised maintainer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate login anomalies (new device, unusual geography, off-hours) on GitHub accounts with publishing permissions to the sudden appearance of commits to protected branches that merged without required reviewers or that added new GitHub Actions workflows with elevated permissions (id-token: write, secrets: read). Alert on orphan commits with no associated pull request.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack'—npm postinstall scripts are the standard vector for payload delivery during `npm install`. Pipeline missed detection of malicious execution during dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by npm.exe or node.exe during install phases, particularly in development/CI environments. Flag if package path matches public registry but executable signature/hash mismatches known-good or if process execution originates from npm cache directories with low prevalence on endpoint.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Exfiltration via Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen'—pipeline failed to generate detection for stolen token usage or transmission. This is a direct credential-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate OpenAI API token patterns (if logged in command-line args, env vars, or process memory) with outbound HTTPS connections to non-OpenAI infrastructure. Look for base64/hex-encoded token strings in process execution logs and correlate with npm-install timing windows.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Metadata Anomalies - Malicious Package Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'npm Supply Chain Attack'—packaging systems show behavioral telemetry (publish frequency, version bump patterns, maintainer account changes). Pipeline missed detection at publication/ingestion boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm registry API calls showing unusual publish activity from previously-inactive or newly-created accounts; version bumps to popular packages without code review; or package names with typosquatting patterns adjacent to known development tools (codex → codexui).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Token Emission from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens must be exfiltrated. Article says tokens were 'stolen'—implies data left the boundary. Pipeline failed to recommend detection of token-bearing HTTP/DNS traffic from developer workstations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound API calls from dev machines to OpenAI domains. Flag any HTTPS or DNS queries to low-prevalence external infrastructure from processes linked to npm, node, or code editors during/immediately after `npm install`. Correlate with process memory containing Base64-encoded OpenAI token headers.

suggestion.title: Rapid Mass Installation of Malicious npm Package Across Organization
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks scale horizontally. If codexui-android was installed in build pipelines or shared dev teams, detection must flag bulk ingestion. Pipeline provided no cross-machine aggregation strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate npm install telemetry across endpoints. Alert if a single package version (esp. codexui-android with anomalous version number) appears on >N% of developer endpoints within a short time window, or if package appears in automated CI/CD logs where it was not previously pinned.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Information Disclosure / Metadata Inspection
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies the package name but provides no version, no malicious domain, no detected filehash. Pipeline should have recommended metadata extraction (package.json tampering detection) as a forensic/detection baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For suspected malicious packages: parse package.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json for obfuscated dependencies, suspicious postinstall/preinstall/prepare scripts, or scripts with Base64/eval patterns. Cross-reference declared dependencies against actual downloaded files to detect manifest tampering.

suggestion.title: Detect T3/IIOP Access to WebLogic Default Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'via T3, IIOP' protocols with 'network access'—core attack vector; pipeline did not surface protocol or port-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network traffic to WebLogic default ports (7001, 7002) from external/untrusted sources using T3 or IIOP protocols. Flag connections from non-corporate IP ranges or sources with no prior WebLogic interaction history. Correlate with failed login attempts or service enumeration scans.

suggestion.title: Identify Unpatched WebLogic Versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerable versions; 1,592 exposed instances on Shodan include 961 on 12.2.1.4.0 and 631 on 14.1.1.0.0—asset discovery baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for WebLogic process execution with version strings matching 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 in command-line arguments, loaded DLLs, or server startup logs. Baseline vulnerable instances and flag those without recent patch-level updates.

suggestion.title: Detect Serialized Object Deserialization Exploitation in WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2024-21182 achieves remote code execution via network-accessible protocols; pipeline missed exploitation-phase detection for Java deserialization gadget chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child process spawning from WebLogic Java processes (wlogserver.exe, java.exe hosting WebLogic), especially cmd.exe or PowerShell launched with suspicious arguments. Correlate with T3/IIOP traffic spikes and unusual file write activity in TEMP or application directories.

suggestion.title: Monitor WebLogic Unauthorized Data Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—post-exploitation data theft is the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound data transfers from WebLogic-hosting servers to external IPs, especially over non-standard ports. Monitor for unexpected database connections, JDBC driver execution, or credential materials being passed from WebLogic to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Shodan-like Reconnaissance for WebLogic Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references Shodan discovery of 1,592 exposed WebLogic servers; attackers using similar scanning to identify targets—reconnaissance baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-scale port scanning (ports 7001, 7002) or service enumeration attempts against internal WebLogic ranges from external sources. Flag rapid successive connection attempts to WebLogic ports across multiple internal IPs within short timeframes (e.g., >50 unique IPs in 5 minutes).

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Login Attempts Against SaaS Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Brute-Force Attack' in headline. Pipeline must detect credential guessing/spraying against password manager or SaaS endpoints, especially rapid auth failures from single or distributed sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect aggregated failed authentication attempts within minutes (threshold: >10 unique failures/5min from single source, or >50 failures/hour from distributed IPs to same target account or service). Correlate with successful auth events to identify compromised credentials post-breach.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Vault / Credential Store Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—clear data exfiltration. Pipeline must detect large or unusual data transfers from password manager accounts or backup retrieval endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk vault/backup downloads from Dashlane APIs (e.g., /vault/export, /backup/download endpoints). Establish baseline: password managers rarely export vaults in bulk; flag any authenticated download >5MB or multiple exports in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Authentication From Impossible Travel or Anomalous Geography
suggestion.rationale: Fewer than 20 users compromised; pipelines should assume attackers accessed vaults from attacker IP space. Detection should flag auth sessions from geolocations inconsistent with user baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentications from IPs geolocation >500km from user's last known location, or logins within impossible-travel windows (e.g., US→China in <2hrs). Cross-reference with breach scope: expect 1–20 distinct victim geos.

suggestion.title: Mass Account Unlock or Password Reset Activity
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks often precede account takeover; victims may unlock or reset passwords post-incident. Pipeline should detect unusual account recovery activities correlating with incident timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spikes in password reset requests, account unlock actions, or MFA recovery code usage. Threshold: >2 resets/unlocks per user in <24hrs, or >10 unique users resetting within incident window. Correlate with failed login spikes.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing or Dictionary Attacks Against Named Service
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force implies attacker used wordlists or credentials from prior breaches. Pipeline should surface attempts using common weak passwords or leaked credential pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed auth events with known weak password patterns (rockyou.txt, SecLists) or public breach dumps. Flag auth attempts using leaked creds (cross-ref HaveIBeenPwned or similar feeds). Threshold: >3 attempts with identical or similar passwords across distinct accounts.

suggestion.title: Android Framework RCE via CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Local attackers can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability (tracked as CVE-2025-48595) to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later' and 'There are indications that CVE-2025-48595 may be under limited, targeted exploitation.' This is active exploitation with named CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts targeting Android Framework component on Android 14+ devices. Alert on suspicious process spawning from framework context with elevated privilege transitions, unusual memory access patterns to framework libraries, or crashes in framework processes followed by code execution.

suggestion.title: Remote Privilege Escalation – Android Framework (Unauthenticated)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The most severe of these issues is a critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.' This describes a network-exploitable priv-esc distinct from local-only attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network traffic to Android devices with unexpected privilege escalation events on Android 14+. Look for anomalous inter-process communication (IPC) to system_server or root-owned processes without corresponding user-initiated activity.

suggestion.title: Nation-State / Spyware Exploitation of Android Framework Zero-Days
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals,' establishing that CVE-2025-48595 class vulnerabilities are weaponized by advanced threat actors for surveillance of targeted individuals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Android devices with framework exploitation indicators (memory corruption signatures, unusual binder/RPC transactions, framework crashes). Cross-reference with known nation-state and commercial spyware deployment infrastructure; escalate for manual investigation if targeting high-value individuals or sensitive organizations.

suggestion.title: Critical Android Framework Zero-Day Patch Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed the enumeration of multiple concurrent zero-days (CVE-2025-48595, CVE-2025-48633, CVE-2025-48572, CVE-2026-21385) that 'may be under limited, targeted exploitation.' Multiple concurrent active zero-days indicate a coordinated exploitation campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android devices for delayed or skipped security patches (patch level pre-2026-06-01). Correlate devices remaining unpatched >7 days post-bulletin with behavioral indicators of exploitation (framework crashes, unusual system daemon behavior, spyware telemetry signatures).

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor Android Patch Lag Risk – Third-Party OEM Delays
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'While Google has yet to share technical details about the flaw or provide more information about the ongoing attacks targeting it... Google Pixel devices will receive these security updates immediately, other vendors will often take longer to test and tweak them for specific hardware configurations.' Non-Pixel devices remain at risk during OEM delay window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory non-Google Android devices and monitor patch deployment timelines. Flag devices still on pre-2026-06-01 patch level >21 days post-bulletin. Correlate patch lag with OEM identity; establish baseline for third-party vendors (Samsung, OnePlus, etc.) and alert on anomalous delays.

suggestion.title: Visual Basic macro execution with obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1059.005 (Visual Basic) and T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) in the kill-chain techniques. No detection for macro-level obfuscation patterns despite this being the stated delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Visual Basic/VBScript execution from Office parent processes where the script file or parent shows entropy anomalies (hex-encoded, Base64, or high-ASCII patterns). Correlate to downloads or email attachments from the past 24 hours. Focus on .docm, .xlsm, .pptm extensions.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage PowerShell execution chain with obfuscated cmdlines
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-stage attack chain (T1059.001 PowerShell) but no detection for chained execution or cmdline obfuscation indicators like '^' escaping, concatenation operators, or Base64 encoding patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent=Office or parent=mshta spawning PowerShell with ProcessCommandLine containing obfuscation signatures: encoded Base64 strings, escape characters (^), string concatenation (+ operators), or -EncodedCommand parameters. Multi-stage: child PowerShell spawning nested PowerShell or iex/Invoke-Expression.

suggestion.title: DNS-over-HTTPS C2 beaconing (TLS SNI fingerprinting)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) as a C2 protocol. UC_BEACONING only covers HTTP/HTTPS. DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) beaconing evades traditional DNS monitoring and the AZUREVEIL agent may use this covertly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track TLS connections to known DoH resolvers (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1:443, Google 8.8.8.8:443, Quad9) that fail TLS validation or show anomalous cert fingerprints. Correlate to beaconing periodicity and low data volume (DNS queries are <100 bytes). Alert on repeating SNI patterns that don't match standard DoH provider certificates.

suggestion.title: Attachment file hash match to IOC list (AZUREVEIL samples)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Detection gap: no hunt for attachments or downloaded files matching the provided malware hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file matching the 12 provided AZUREVEIL SHA256 hashes in EmailAttachmentInfo or DeviceFileEvents (downloads, temp folders). Correlate to recipient user and email metadata. Extend to network-based detection: YARA rules on file hashes observed in web logs or file transfer logs.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing targeting profiles (government, researchers, tech workers)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies geographic targets (Czech Republic, Taiwan) and profession profiles (government officials, researchers, tech workers). No contextual detection for recipient attributes matching threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails to users whose department=Government|Research|Engineering or whose organizational unit maps to sensitive divisions, sent by external senders with newly-registered domains or no email history with the organization. Especially alert if subject contains technical terms (exploit, advisory, research, vulnerability) matching the threat actor profile.

suggestion.title: C2 command execution latency anomaly (Operation Dragon Weave signature)
suggestion.rationale: Article names campaign 'Operation Dragon Weave' and describes a China-linked actor with specific TTPs. No behavioral detection for command-response timing that might be unique to AZUREVEIL's callback implementation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound web/DNS beacons to subsequent process creation or file writes on the host. Measure time delta between last beacon and execution. AZUREVEIL may show consistent command-response latency (e.g., 2-5 sec after each beacon). Flag hosts where outbound connections precede suspicious process spawns by a consistent delta, suggesting automated command dispatch.

suggestion.title: Phishing Links to Spoofed Recruitment Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake recruitment operation' and 'carefully crafted fake recruitment portal' — core initial access vector. Pipeline failed to generate network IOC hunt despite article recommending it. Domains (boeing-careers.com, airbus.global-careers.com, etc.) are obvious spoofs impersonating real defense contractors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DNS queries or HTTP(S) connections to the seven recruitment-themed domains. Monitor for user clicks on phishing emails linking to ebix.recruitment-flow.com, boeing-careers.com, etc. Expected FPs minimal given domain spoofing nature.

suggestion.title: Malware Download and Execution from Recruitment Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'pushed onto unsuspecting victims' via fake portal. T1204 (user clicks malicious link) and T1105 (malware ingress) are implicit. Detection should key off downloaded executables matching the 15 provided SHA256 hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File creation or process execution matching any of the 15 SHA256 hashes. High-fidelity: look for parent process chains where recruitment-domain downloads spawn child execution. Custom malware attribution justifies low tolerance for FP.

suggestion.title: Malware Obfuscation and Custom Packing
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline listed T1027 (Obfuscated Files) but failed to generate corresponding detection. Article emphasizes 'custom malware' suggesting evasion techniques. This should trigger defense-evasion hunt during installation/execution phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-entropy code sections or runtime unpacking behavior from SHA256 hash matches. Monitor for obfuscated imports, delayed code execution, or reflective injection patterns associated with custom malware families.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing Over HTTP/HTTPS to Recruitment Domains
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) listed but no C2 hunt generated. Recruitment domains are likely also C2 callback infrastructure. Post-compromise, endpoints should beacon to one or more of the seven domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodic or event-driven HTTP(S) POST/GET requests from infected endpoints to recruitment domains. Flag for data exfiltration, command injection, or tasking patterns inconsistent with legitimate recruitment browsing.

suggestion.title: Targeting of Aerospace/Defense Sector Employees
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies targets as 'professionals in aerospace and defense sectors across Middle East and Europe.' Detection should correlate hiring-related emails and portal visits with users matching industry/geo scope to raise suspicion of targeted social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Anomalous click-through rates on recruitment links from aerospace/defense verticals (Airbus, Boeing, Thales, Rheinmetall employees). Correlate domain registrations (recent, lookalike TLDs) with personnel directories sourced from LinkedIn/OSINT to confirm targeting.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Redirect Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'malvertising campaign' as delivery mechanism; pipeline extracted no detections for redirect chains or ad-injection activity. Cite: 'malvertising campaign spreading new FlutterShell backdoor.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS browser processes for suspicious redirects to attacker-controlled domains via ad networks. Detect rapid redirect sequences, unusual URI path patterns, or connections to newly-registered domains masquerading as legitimate ad infrastructure.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'new backdoor FlutterShell' as the payload; pipeline produced zero execution detection. Expected: hash-based detection, behavioral signatures, or code-signing anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FlutterShell execution by signature, recent-file hash, or Flutter-framework-specific behavioral artifacts. Monitor for suspicious binaries written to ~/Downloads or /tmp that subsequently launch with unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: macOS Download-Directory Execution Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising delivery model implies user downloads malware from browser; no detection for execute-from-cache pattern. Expected: browser→/tmp→execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable process creation from macOS browser cache (~Library/Caches/*), /tmp, or ~/Downloads directories. Detect unsigned or oddly-signed Mach-O binaries launched immediately after download, especially with non-standard bundle identifiers.

suggestion.title: Flutter Framework Obfuscation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes backdoor 'built using the Flutter framework' as evasion technique; pipeline produced no obfuscation or framework-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Flutter-compiled binaries by characteristic runtime imports and symbol patterns. Detect atypical inter-process communication, network beaconing, or child process spawning from Flutter apps masquerading as legitimate tools.

suggestion.title: Backdoor C&C Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell is described as a backdoor (implies command-and-control); pipeline extracted zero network IOCs, domains, or C&C beaconing detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from FlutterShell process to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Detect periodic beaconing patterns, anomalous DNS queries, or connections to recently-registered or bulletproof-hosting domains.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor functionality implies reconnaissance (process enumeration, privilege discovery); article likely describes discovery behaviors. Pipeline produced no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process enumeration syscalls (proc_listpids, sysctl) or command invocations (/bin/ps, launchctl) issued by FlutterShell or child processes. Alert on unusual system-profiling tool execution from unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Xeno RAT Process Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Xeno RAT' as deployed malware; pipeline generated zero detections for RAT spawning, beacon activity, or C2 footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Finance Ministry endpoints for Xeno RAT process signatures and command-line patterns. Correlate process execution trees (Office → rundll32/cmd/powershell). Detect outbound HTTPS or custom-protocol beacons to known SideCopy C2 infrastructure using NetFlow or proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Detect Spear-Phishing Emails with Trojanized Attachments to Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Targeting 'Afghanistan Finance Ministry' implies phishing delivery; SideCopy's typical initial-access vector. Pipeline output contains zero phishing indicators or email IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails from external senders to Finance Ministry users with Office attachments or credential-harvest links. Look for spoofed ministry domains, urgent/official-sounding subject lines, and attachments with macro-enabled Office extensions. Flag for sandboxing and block senders.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Document Macro Execution on Finance Ministry Workstations
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy campaigns historically deliver macros in Office docs; article context suggests trojanized documents as vector but pipeline output has no T1204.002 or T1105 detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Word/Excel spawns cmd.exe, PowerShell, or rundll32. Monitor for macro-warning dialogs followed by immediate child process creation. Correlate with Finance Ministry user logins from unusual geographies or times.

suggestion.title: Detect Registry and Scheduled-Task Persistence by Xeno RAT
suggestion.rationale: Sustained APT access to Finance Ministry requires persistence; typical SideCopy pattern includes Run-key or scheduled-task hooks but pipeline reconstructed no persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run and HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run for new entries pointing to %Temp% or %AppData% after macro execution. Alert on scheduled tasks created by Office or system processes. Baseline Finance Ministry startup tasks and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration from Finance Ministry to SideCopy C2
suggestion.rationale: APT targeting a treasury ministry implies intelligence collection; article context suggests data theft but pipeline output contains no exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Finance Ministry outbound traffic volume and destinations. Alert on beacons to non-whitelisted external IPs with payload size anomalies, encrypted tunnels from non-browser processes, or archived document uploads to cloud services.
