suggestion.title: PowerShell Command Execution from ClickFix Clipboard Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes ClickFix's mechanism: 'deceives victims into copying and executing malicious commands' and 'the ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands.' Attack vectors use clipboard to trigger execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell invocations with suspicious parent processes (browser, editor, clipboard monitor) or command-line arguments matching obfuscated loaders. Monitor for clipboard read+execute patterns in rapid succession. Flag PowerShell execution of commands containing encoded/obfuscated payload markers.

suggestion.title: ZIP Archive Extraction Followed by DLL/EXE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Specific attack payload identified: 'a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe' delivered via fake update. Direct chain: download → extract → execute.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .zip file extraction in user directories (Downloads, AppData, Temp) followed by .exe or .dll execution within seconds. Specifically monitor for 'Browser Update.exe' execution. Flag .dll files loaded from extracted archives via unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via Verification-Themed ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals macOS targeting beyond Windows: 'researchers discovered an obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized clipboard access from Safari, Chrome, Firefox processes on macOS. Monitor for sudden clipboard content changes followed by Terminal or shell execution. Flag obfuscated JavaScript payloads in web context that target pasteboard APIs.

suggestion.title: Compromised Site Redirect via Traffic Distribution System (zTDS)
suggestion.rationale: Core infrastructure mechanism: 'Visitors of compromised websites are redirected through a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as zTDS, which profiles them and determines whether a FakeUpdates or a ClickFix lure is more appropriate.' zTDS in use since September 2025.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 30x redirects from known-legitimate domains to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Monitor for TDS fingerprinting requests (site= parameter, visitor profiling queries). Flag redirect chains that serve different payloads (FakeUpdates vs ClickFix) based on visitor profiling headers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Supply Chain Source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Red Hat npm Packages' as compromised in supply chain attack; no detection logic generated to identify installation of malicious packages. Article phrase: 'Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci commands and package manager logs for installation of Red Hat-attributed packages with abnormal versions or from non-standard registries. Alert on packages with supply-chain indicators: injected dependencies, shell spawning, base64-encoded payloads in manifests.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from Node.js/npm Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm' but no detection generated for credential harvesting originating from npm package execution. Article phrase: 'credential-stealing worm.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential access patterns (password manager APIs, SSH key enumeration, environment variable reads) from Node.js child processes. Correlate with npm package install timing and suspicious manifest entries.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Lateral Movement from Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Payload characterized as 'worm' implies automated propagation; no detection generated for self-replicating behavior or horizontal spread patterns. Article phrase: 'credential-stealing worm.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning and connection patterns from development machines: package registry enumeration, mass SSH/git connection attempts, repeated lateral connections. Detect child process spawning and module injection indicative of worm self-replication.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to C2 from npm Package Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm would necessarily exfiltrate stolen data; no detection generated for C2 communication or data egress from npm process context. Article phrase: 'credential-stealing worm.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) or DNS exfiltration from Node.js processes to attacker infrastructure. Flag base64-encoded payloads in DNS queries, high-volume outbound HTTPS from development machines, and tunneling patterns over unexpected protocols.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Manifest Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm commonly exploit postinstall/preinstall hooks in package.json; no detection generated for suspicious build-time script execution. Article phrase: 'Red Hat npm Packages.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json files for suspicious postinstall/preinstall/prepublishOnly script entries. Detect shell command execution during npm install phases. Alert on obfuscated JavaScript, base64/hex-encoded payloads, or commands spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes, so simply resolving the dependency is enough to trigger the payload.' This is the primary infection vector with zero detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or npm.exe process spawning during package installation with preinstall context in command line or package.json references, especially when installing @redhat-cloud-services packages. Alert on large, unusual child processes or file-access patterns spawned from preinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Malicious orphan commits to package repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious code did not slip in through a typosquat or poisoned transitive dependency. Evidence indicates a Red Hat employee's GitHub account was compromised and used to push malicious orphan commits directly into two RedHatInsights repositories, bypassing code review.' Initial-access vector completely absent from kill-chain reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag orphan commits (commits with no parent in branch history) pushed by previously-inactive developer accounts to package repositories, especially bypassing code-review workflows. Correlate with subsequent GitHub Actions workflow creation or OIDC token requests.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions workflow requesting OIDC tokens with id-token write scope
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Those commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that triggered on push to any branch, requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write, executed an obfuscated payload.' Credential-access mechanism via OIDC is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows requesting id-token: write scope, especially in workflows triggered on push-to-any-branch or created by non-service accounts. Cross-reference with subsequent npm publish or registry-access patterns.

suggestion.title: Cloud identity enumeration via GCP and Azure from compromised host
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets. Earlier variants focused on lifting credentials; this one is oriented toward mapping and reaching the cloud control plane itself.' Cloud-discovery phase entirely absent from kill-chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected cloud API enumeration from npm/node processes or CI runners: GCP's ListIdentities, GetIAMPolicy, GetBindingPolicy; Azure's List* identity operations. Baseline and alert on anomalous callers or permission-discovery patterns from non-service principal accounts.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting from CI and local environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' Credential-access is core attack phase with zero detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node/npm processes or npm preinstall hooks reading sensitive files (~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, .env files) or accessing environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_* secrets, or CI platform tokens. Correlate with subsequent network connections to external hosts or npm registry operations.

suggestion.title: Automated npm package republishing by compromised identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' Self-propagation mechanism is lateral-movement vector with no coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry audit logs and HTTP logs for automated npm publish commands from CI runners or developer machines, targeting multiple packages in short timeframe or originating from unusual accounts. Correlate with suspicious preinstall hook payloads (large, obfuscated, eval-based) in published package tarballs.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack'—detection must trigger on package name, version, and installation event. No use case generated despite this being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn install commands and registry calls for suspicious package metadata, version mismatches, or recently-published packages with names similar to legitimate libraries. Alert on installation of 'codexui-android' or variants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks commonly use package.json postinstall hooks to execute payload. Article describes token theft mechanism which implies script execution post-download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by npm/yarn with parent process 'npm install' or similar. Flag execution of unexpected scripts, encoders, or network utilities during package installation. Cross-reference process invocations with package.json postinstall directives.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of OpenAI Authentication Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Authentication Tokens Stolen'—the exfiltration event is the attack's objective and must have detectable network/file access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes of npm for file reads of token storage locations (~/.openai, config files, environment variables). Alert on unexpected DNS queries, TLS connections, or HTTP requests to non-standard domains from npm or child processes. Detect read access to files containing 'token', 'api_key', or 'credential' patterns.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beaconing from Compromised Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens imply attacker gains persistent access to exfiltrated credentials. Article describes token theft but pipeline did not map the post-exploitation C2 communication phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile normal outbound connectivity from developer workstations post-npm-install. Alert on DNS requests to newly-registered domains, IPs with no prior DNS history, or connections to known C2 infrastructure from processes spawned during package installation window.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Token Extraction from Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: OpenAI tokens are typically stored in ~/.openai or environment files; attack must access these. Pipeline missed the file-access pattern that enables the theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file read access to common token/credential storage locations (.openai, .env, config.json, ~/.aws, etc.) by processes with low reputation or unexpected provenance. Cross-reference with parent process (npm) and child process chain.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages often exhibit unusual patterns: rapid version churn, unusual registry timestamps, or mismatched dependencies. Pipeline did not flag the package name as an IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query npm registry API for package metadata (codexui-android): check publish date, maintainer reputation, dependency graph for beaconing libs, download spike anomalies. Flag if package was published recently, has few stars/downloads, or impersonates a legitimate library naming pattern.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections.' Pipeline captured no C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution chains involving Python/Rust/Go followed by HTTP/HTTPS outbound connections to api.telegram.org. Flag requests containing Telegram bot token patterns in headers. Correlate with command execution patterns suggesting remote tasking via Telegram callback.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Redirector Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' No infrastructure-layer C2 detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect C2 traffic tunneled through Cloudflare workers.dev domains. Monitor for DNS queries to *.workers.dev subdomains followed by POST/GET requests with Cobalt Strike beacon characteristics (jitter, User-Agent spoofing, encrypted payloads).

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Enumeration Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' with 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.' No reconnaissance detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process execution spawning sequential LDAP queries or AD enumeration commands (net group, dsquery, AdFind) in rapid succession with result-fed iteration patterns. Flag unusual combinations of forest/domain/OU enumeration executed programmatically.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' Core execution technique not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes reading legitimate system executables (.exe, .dll), performing binary manipulation, and writing modified versions. Detect execution of modified binaries with anomalous memory imports or from untypical paths (Documents, AppData).

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor EDR Evasion Module Testing Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'modular Windows payload loader generator wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques' with testing against Sophos, CrowdStrike, Microsoft EDR. No defense-evasion testing pattern detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid cycles of binary artifact creation, deletion, and execution in test directories (C:\Users\User\Documents\test). Monitor for process hollowing, IAT hooking, or deliberate EDR service enumeration/tampering attempts within iterative development loops.

suggestion.title: Compiled Payload Generation from Scripting Languages
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Python tool that generates payloads, mostly in Rust and Go' with 'Close to 80 modules were generated and tested.' Supply-chain pattern of script-to-binary compilation not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process spawning Rust (rustc.exe) or Go (go.exe) compilers with non-standard output directories. Detect high-volume binary artifact generation (80+ modules) followed by execution testing. Flag compilation activities in Documents or user-writable temp paths.

suggestion.title: Cloud Provider IP as C2 — outbound to AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure... to sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations.' This is the core attack pattern — using legitimate provider IPs to hide C2. Beaconing to a cloud provider IP is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from non-cloud workloads to AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare CIDR ranges with C2-pattern timing (regular intervals, small packet counts, persistent destination). Exclude legitimate cloud API calls (SDK, auth, CDN). Beaconing to a cloud provider IP is unusual unless the endpoint is a cloud-integrated app.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Abuse for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names GitHub as abuse vector alongside AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare. Attackers use GitHub gists, repos, or API for command delivery. No hunts provided for GitHub-based C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on programmatic access to GitHub API by non-developer endpoints; look for GETs to /gists, /repos/<attacker>, or raw.githubusercontent.com with high frequency, or POST/PATCH to repos followed by immediate reads.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare DNS / Redirect Loop as C2 Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article includes Cloudflare as abuse vector. Attackers abuse Cloudflare's DNS, Workers, or redirect rules to proxy C2. Article phrase: 'Cloudflare' camouflage for malicious traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-frequency DNS queries to subdomains under fast-flux Cloudflare nameservers, or HTTP redirects through Cloudflare Workers to non-Cloudflare IPs. Classify as fallback channel if destination switches after first connect.

suggestion.title: Process Executing File with Matching Hash (Any.RUN IOC)
suggestion.rationale: Article references ANY.RUN Threat Intelligence Lookup and provides MD5. Need process-level detection for this hash. Article phrase: 'threat intelligence investigation using ANY.RUN's Threat Intelligence (TI) Lookup.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process execution with MD5 hash 1af33e1657631357c73119488045302c or file write with this hash. Escalate to critical if process is launched from browser, email client, or temp directory.

suggestion.title: Masquerading as Legitimate Cloud Service Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Core attack is masquerade: 'camouflage malicious traffic' by using legitimate cloud provider IPs. Need detection for traffic that looks legitimate but exhibits C2 behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on traffic to AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare IPs with anomalous port/protocol combinations (e.g., C2 beacon patterns to HTTPS port 443 that does not complete TLS handshake, or raw TCP to port 80 with binary protocol). Use JARM/TLS fingerprinting to verify service identity.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'enables attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms.' No detection logic generated for this core attack behavior. Look for failed logins followed by successful post-exploit access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin console logs for authentication failures followed by successful logins from unexpected source IPs. Alert on CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns: malformed requests to auth endpoints, unusual credential resets, or privilege escalation events in firewall management plane.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of PAN-OS Public-Facing Interface
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) was identified but no detection use case built. Article describes active attacks leveraging the vulnerability. Need hunt for exploit payloads, known vuln-exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to PAN-OS web management interfaces (port 443, 8443) for known CVE-2026-0257 exploitation signatures (POST patterns to /api or /admin endpoints with malformed JSON, oversized Content-Length, SQL injection payloads, or LDAP filter injection patterns).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Firewall Compromise
suggestion.rationale: If attacker gained access through PAN-OS, pivoting to internal network is likely next step. Article mentions 'real-world attacks' but no post-compromise detection. Missing T1021 (Remote Services) and internal reconnaissance hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal network connections originating from compromised firewall appliance (especially non-standard service accounts or root): scans to RFC1918 ranges, SMB connections to domain controllers, LDAP queries for active directory enumeration, or SSH attempts to internal servers.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Firewall
suggestion.rationale: Six command-and-control IPv4 addresses listed; T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) suggests C2 communication, but no exfiltration detection generated. Missing T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall session logs for high-volume outbound connections to the six flagged C2 IPs (104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119-120-125, 209.99.191.137, 79.130.26.202). Flag SSL/TLS connections with no matching SSL certificate validation, unusual cipher suites, or traffic to non-standard ports masquerading as common services.

suggestion.title: T3 Protocol RCE Exploitation to WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server' with 1,592 exposed systems on Shodan. T3 is WebLogic's proprietary RMI protocol and primary attack vector. No detection generated despite clear exploitation pathway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound T3 protocol connections to WebLogic listener ports (7001, 7002) from untrusted sources. Monitor for failed T3 handshakes, rapid sequential connection attempts, or non-standard T3 packet sequences indicating CVE-2024-21182 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WebLogic Version Indicator (12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides specific vulnerable version enumeration with Shodan counts: 961 instances on 12.2.1.4.0, 631 on 14.1.1.0.0. No version-based alerting or patch-gap detection generated despite quantified inventory of at-risk systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Oracle WebLogic Server instances running versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 without July 2024+ security patches. Cross-reference endpoint inventory and patch management logs to identify unpatched systems exposed to networks where T3 reconnaissance is possible.

suggestion.title: IIOP Protocol Exploitation to WebLogic RMI
suggestion.rationale: Article lists IIOP alongside T3 as exploitation vector: 'network access via T3, IIOP to compromise.' IIOP is WebLogic's Java RMI binding protocol; no detection rule generated despite being named attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IIOP traffic (port 7099 or dynamic RMI registry ports) to WebLogic servers. Alert on failed IIOP service binding attempts, rapid scanning across multiple WebLogic instances, or IIOP connections from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access Post-WebLogic Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacks result in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' No detection generated for post-exploitation data enumeration or bulk queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous database queries or file reads initiated from java.exe processes outside normal application behavior baselines. Alert on large data transfers from WebLogic servers to external IPs, especially within hours of successful T3 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via WebLogic Process
suggestion.rationale: Article's language 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' and 'compromise' strongly implies code execution capability. No detection generated for child process spawning under WebLogic JVM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh spawned as child processes of java.exe running WebLogic (identifiable via CATALINA_BASE or Oracle-specific environment variables). Alert on interactive shell execution or suspicious command-line patterns, especially post-T3 reconnaissance phase.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends substituting CVE-2022-0492 into standard asset-exposure templates. No implementation was generated despite explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Linux systems via vulnerability scanner, patch-compliance databases, or asset inventory. Flag any system still reporting CVE-2022-0492 as vulnerable or unpatched. Federal deadline: 2026-06-05.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Exploitation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' as the attack vector. No detection logic for the actual exploitation mechanism was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent files, child processes spawned with elevated privileges post-cgroups modification, or process escapes from cgroup namespaces. Correlate with privilege-escalation outcomes (uid=0 transitions).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms CISA KEV status means 'currently being exploited.' Successful exploitation results in privilege escalation; pipeline generated no detection for post-exploitation privilege-level changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-root processes obtaining uid=0 or calling setuid/setgid/capset syscalls on vulnerable Linux kernels. Correlate process execution before and after privilege boundaries crossing; flag anomalies on patched-deadline dates.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Inventory vs. CISA KEV Deadline Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date' (2026-06-05) and notes auditor/regulator scrutiny. Pipeline generated no compliance-monitoring or deadline-alert use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously inventory Linux kernel versions across all infrastructure. Generate alerts for unpatched CVE-2022-0492 systems as the 2026-06-05 deadline approaches. Track remediation rate and flag systems not yet patched within 5 days of deadline.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attack on Password Manager Authentication Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'brute-force attack'—T1110 is the core attack vector. Pipeline assigned zero techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login endpoints showing abnormal request velocity from single source IPs, high failure-to-success ratios, or distributed attempts across multiple user IDs. Baseline per-user and per-IP login frequency; alert when velocity exceeds +3σ over 5-minute windows.

suggestion.title: Bulk Exfiltration of Encrypted User Vaults
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded'—explicit data exfiltration event. Pipeline produced no collection/exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls to vault-export or vault-download endpoints for bulk requests. Alert on transfers of encrypted vault containers exceeding single-user typical size or frequency. Cross-correlate with suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Account Activity Post-Breach for Affected Dashlane Users
suggestion.rationale: 20 compromised accounts are now exposed; post-breach logins will exhibit new geographies, devices, hours. Pipeline omitted persistence/collection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins from geolocations never seen for the account, new device fingerprints, or atypical hours. Assign higher weight if login follows a failed authentication burst. Maintain breach-victim roster and prioritize survivors.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Process Execution with Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver GammaWorm and GammaSteel'; malware execution follows archive extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WinRAR.exe spawning child processes (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, rundll32.exe, or renamed executables) with command lines containing archive paths or unusual working directories in %TEMP% or %AppData%.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel Malware Process Signature
suggestion.rationale: Named malware families 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel' are specific indicators for this Gamaredon campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation with known GammaWorm/GammaSteel signatures (file hashes, mutex names, command-line patterns, registry keys). Monitor for execution from temp directories, unusual code pages, or parent-child relationships inconsistent with normal user workflows.

suggestion.title: Archive Extraction Followed by Remote Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery chain is: archive extraction (WinRAR) → malware execution → C2. Detection must bridge initial access to command & control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file extraction event (WinRAR or explorer.exe decompressing .rar/.zip) within 2 minutes of child process execution from %TEMP% or %AppData%, followed by outbound network connection to non-standard ports or known malicious IPs. Elevated risk if parent process is outlook.exe or thunderbird.exe.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry/Scheduled Task Post-WinRAR Execution
suggestion.rationale: APTs establish persistence after initial malware execution; 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel' delivery suggests staged deployment with follow-on persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Registry modifications to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce, or Winlogon keys within 5 minutes of WinRAR child process execution. Correlate with schtasks.exe or PowerShell -Command 'Register-ScheduledTask' invocations.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon from Malware-Sourced Process
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies GammaWorm and GammaSteel as delivered malware; C2 communication is necessary for attacker control and data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from processes spawned by WinRAR extraction to non-standard User-Agent patterns, unusual Host headers (Cyrillic domains, newly registered), or IPs geolocated to Russia/Belarus. Monitor for POST requests with suspicious beacon payloads or unusual TLS certificate thumbprints.

suggestion.title: Ukraine-Targeted Phishing with WinRAR Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'Against Ukraine'; attack vector is phishing with WinRAR-based exploit. Initial access detection critical for early kill-chain intervention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with .rar or .zip attachments containing booby-trapped files (fake documents, Office files with embedded archives) to Ukrainian government/military/energy sector domains. High risk: sender spoofs known Ukrainian government address, subject references Cyrillic terms or contains urgent language ('urgent', 'verify', 'immediate').

suggestion.title: Android Framework Privilege Escalation via CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-48595 'exploit[s] the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability...to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' This is the kill chain center—detection is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege transitions from unprivileged process to system/root context through Android Framework syscall boundary, particularly on Android 14.0–14.x where CVE-2025-48595 is confirmed exploitable. Look for fork/execve chains originating in Framework.apk or related services attempting uid=0 transitions.

suggestion.title: Targeted Android Compromise Detection for High-Profile Users
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals.' Targeting context requires behavioral detection tied to user profile risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag exploitation attempts on Android devices registered to high-risk user profiles (C-suite, government, research, journalism). Correlate CVE-2025-48595 exploitation signals (privilege escalation attempts) with enterprise identity metadata to escalate severity for sensitive user populations.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Devices Running Vulnerable Framework Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'We encourage all users to update to the latest version of Android' and references 18 critical vulns. Deployment of June 2026 patches (levels 2026-06-01 or 2026-06-05) is measurable and should trigger compliance alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when enterprise-managed Android devices remain unpatched beyond 30 days of Google's June 2, 2026 release. Cross-reference device inventory with security patch levels 2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05; flag org-owned or BYOD enrollment if patch lag exceeds policy threshold.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Display Driver Exploitation (CVE-2026-21385)
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out 'another zero-day flaw in a Qualcomm display component (CVE-2026-21385)' patched in March, 'tagged as under limited, targeted exploitation.' Separate attack surface from Framework.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous syscalls from graphics subsystem processes (surfaceflinger, hwcomposer) attempting memory mapping or ioctl commands to Qualcomm display drivers with unusual parameters. Alert on SELinux denials followed by successful execution in display driver context.

suggestion.title: Framework-to-Kernel Privilege Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article states the 'most severe' issue is 'critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed.' This implies Framework→Kernel boundary bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Framework process (uid 1000 or system uid 1001) initiating syscalls restricted by SELinux policy to kernel-only interfaces. Flag patterns where normal deny audit events are absent despite attempted access, indicating policy circumvention or kernel bypass.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection—Active Android CVE
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'One Actively Exploited.' Pipeline must generate detection templates for the disclosed CVE once available. Phrase: 'actively exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process crashes, segmentation faults, or native exceptions in Android logs correlated with vulnerable app version execution. Flag unexpected privilege transitions or memory access violations immediately post-app invocation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: 124-flaw patch batches typically include privilege-escalation vectors. No use case generated despite high severity. Phrase: 'patches 124 flaws.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected uid/gid transitions, unexpected system service spawning, or capability grants to third-party apps post-exploitation. Correlate with crashed or hanging vulnerable-version apps.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from Android Device
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities (likely in the batch) enable data theft. 'Actively exploited' implies secondary objectives include data extraction. No exfiltration-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk reads from sensitive content providers (contacts, messages, location, calendar) with unexpected network egress to non-standard ports or domains. Flag rapid data-access patterns followed by network-based transmission.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Android Device
suggestion.rationale: Device with RCE capability would pivot to internal network. 'Actively exploited' status suggests in-the-wild compromise scenarios. No lateral-movement detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from Android devices to internal network ranges, credential-spraying patterns, or SMB/SSH reconnaissance correlated with exploitation-attempt timeframes.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise—Developer Build System Infection
suggestion.rationale: Android SDK or dependency vulnerabilities in the 124-flaw patch could compromise developer build chains. Pipeline must address supply-chain vectors for patch announcements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process execution, network connections, or artifact modification during gradle/maven builds on dev machines post-SDK update. Flag unauthorized gradle plugin downloads or compiler-wrapper substitution.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service via Android Framework Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Not all 124 flaws enable RCE; DoS vectors are typical. 'Actively exploited' could include service-disruption scenarios. No impact-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated app crashes, system hangs, excessive battery drain, or CPU spikes correlated with vulnerable-app execution or algorithmic complexity attacks on framework parsers.

suggestion.title: Git Tag Rewriting and Historical Ref Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—tags are being modified post-facto to redirect version resolution, a classic supply-chain evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor version control audit logs for tag updates or force-pushes that change the commit a release tag points to. Alert when tags are rewritten without corresponding new commits or deployment events. Correlate tag rewrites with subsequent package downloads to detect propagation of malicious versions.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secret Exfiltration from Build Logs and Environment
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective explicitly 'Steal CI Secrets'—indicates environment variables and credentials are being extracted during the package build/install process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CI/CD build logs that print, export, or transmit environment variables with secret-related names (AWS_, TOKEN, API_, SECRET_, PASSWORD). Detect when build scripts read .env files, call credential managers, or exfiltrate logs to external URLs. Alert on modifications to CI/CD runner scripts that inject variable logging.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Version Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Rewritten tags mean the code at v1.x.y is different from what the package registry originally signed, creating a hash integrity violation between lock-files and actual installed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compute and monitor SHA-256 hashes of installed Composer packages against package-registry manifests and historical composer.lock files. Alert when a package version's installed hash differs from the expected hash registered at that version. Flag download of packages where integrity metadata (signatures, checksums) is missing or recently modified.

suggestion.title: Force-Push to Release Tags and Version Control Branches
suggestion.rationale: Rewriting tags requires destructive git operations (force-push, ref-delete); these are abnormal in stable production repositories and should trigger immediate investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any force-push (--force, --force-with-lease) to release branches or version tags, especially from automation accounts or newly-privileged users. Correlate force-pushes with timing of account compromises, credential rotation, or unusual CI/CD activity. Flag cases where force-push precedes public package releases.

suggestion.title: Bulk Package Release Activity from Attacker-Controlled Account
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of 'Multiple Composer Packages' indicates coordinated malicious releases; bulk publishing by a single account is rare and suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-registry API logs for bulk version releases (5+ packages from same account in <2 hours). Flag new versions published without corresponding changelog entries or without legitimate code changes. Correlate bulk releases with tag rewrites, force-pushes, or account-access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Repository Access from Anomalous IP / Geolocation During Tag Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Tag rewriting requires repository write access; detecting unusual access patterns during this manipulation can identify account compromise or insider threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repository push operations (especially force-pushes) from IP addresses, geographies, or times-of-day inconsistent with historical account activity. Alert on tag rewrites performed outside normal CI/CD automation (e.g., manual pushes from unexpected locations). Correlate with credential-access logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Agent Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'securing agents across the development lifecycle'; implies agents can be hijacked or abused with elevated permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AI agents requesting or executing actions outside their declared scope or requesting elevated permissions not present in their deployment manifest. Monitor for agents executing shell commands, file writes, or API calls inconsistent with their intended function.

suggestion.title: Model Parameter Injection via Development Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes securing 'models across the development lifecycle'; development tools integrating ML models are vulnerable to prompt injection and parameter tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor development tools (IDEs, CI/CD platforms, GitHub Actions) for injection of unexpected parameters, environment variables, or inline prompts targeting integrated ML/LLM models. Flag when user input is passed unsanitized to model inference APIs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Compromise via Trusted Action Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions GitHub and securing code; GitHub Actions workflows can be exploited to exfiltrate or tamper with code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of GitHub Actions workflows by unexpected accounts, introduction of external repository checkouts, or workflows exfiltrating environment variables/secrets to external URLs.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Development Dependency Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Lifecycle security focus implies concern for compromised dev dependencies and build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected package downgrades, installation of beta/pre-release versions of critical build or model training libraries, or packages from recently-created accounts in package repositories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution from VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Nx Console VS Code Extension Compromised'—malicious extensions execute arbitrary code; no execution-vector detection was generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by code.exe or VS Code extension subprocess (code-server, node.exe from extension host) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash). Alert on unusual parents or paths outside %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Development Tool Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Nx Console is a widely-distributed VS Code extension; article title explicitly indicates compromise; pipeline missed T1195.001/T1195.002 mappings and distribution-vector detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installations from non-official sources or unusual versions. Track code-insiders.exe or code.exe reaching non-standard extension registries. Alert on downloads of .vsix files with anomalous hashes.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions establish C2 or exfiltrate data—no network-based detection use case was generated despite 'compromised' status implying malicious communication
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from code.exe or node.exe (VS Code extension host process) to non-standard domains, newly-registered IPs, or known C2 infrastructure. Alert on HTTPS to suspicious domains or high-entropy subdomains.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Injection in Extension Directory
suggestion.rationale: Compromising an extension requires injecting or modifying .js, package.json, or bundled files; no persistence/modification detection was generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\nx-console* (and similar extension paths) for new or modified .js files, unexpected changes to package.json or node_modules/, and file writes outside normal update windows.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extensions in developer environments harvest SSH keys, Git credentials, or API tokens from .ssh, .git, .aws/; pipeline did not generate credential-access detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file read operations from code.exe or VS Code subprocesses targeting %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\, %USERPROFILE%\.git\, %USERPROFILE%\.aws\, or browser profile directories. Alert on sensitive file access outside normal IDE workflows.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package Installation via NPM Registry Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Nx Console is part of development toolchain ecosystem; malicious extensions can poison npm/yarn installs or redirect registry; no package-management detection was generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn install, pnpm install commands for requests to non-official npm registries. Alert on .npmrc modifications or environment variable changes (npm_config_registry, YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER) from VS Code or extension processes.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Triggers Unsigned Executable Download from Malvertising Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign spreads malware via malvertising. No use case addresses the vector: browser receives malicious ad, user clicks, binary downloads. Article phrase: 'malvertising campaign spreading FlutterShell'.

suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell is a macOS backdoor. Persistence on macOS typically occurs via LaunchAgent plist creation. Pipeline did not surface persistence indicators. Article phrase: 'new backdoor FlutterShell'.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Beaconing from Non-Browser Process to High-Entropy Domain
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies C2 communication but pipeline identified zero command-and-control IOCs or behavioral detection. Article phrase: 'backdoor FlutterShell'.

suggestion.title: Execution of Downloaded Mach-O with Invalid or Absent Code Signature
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell malware execution is a core attack phase but pipeline generated no detection for code-signing evasion or suspicious execution context. Article phrase: 'malvertising campaign targets macOS users'.

suggestion.title: Flutter Framework Artifacts in Suspicious Binary or Process Memory
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not surface technique-specific detection for Flutter-based malware. Article mentions 'built using the Flutter framework' as distinguishing characteristic but no behavioral signatures for Flutter binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Mach-O binaries containing Flutter library artifacts (libflutter.so) originating from non-vendor locations, especially if launched from browser context or with unsigned/tampered entitlements.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Infection: Browser → Download → Persistence Check → C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Complete attack chain missing from kill-chain reconstruction. Malvertising campaigns follow predictable pattern but pipeline failed to chain phases. Article phrase: 'malvertising campaign spreading new FlutterShell backdoor'.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Xeno RAT' as deployed malware; pipeline extracted zero malware IOCs or execution-phase detections despite this being the central technical artifact.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Finance Ministry Systems

suggestion.title: Malicious Maven Dependency jqwik-engine 1.10.0 Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies compromised artifact: 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine Affected version: 1.10.0' as the attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero package-level IOCs.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes evasion: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice... [2K means erase the entire current line.' The ANSI escape byte sequence 0x1B[2K is the obfuscation IOC. Pipeline missed defense-evasion pattern entirely.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Payload in Dependency Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies payload: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code' and instructs: 'Grep your CI and IDE logs for the phrase about disregarding instructions and deleting jqwik tests and code.' Exact text IOC for detection in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search test and build output for phrases matching 'disregard previous instructions' or 'delete.*jqwik' in suspicious context. Correlate presence of these strings in Maven/Gradle output with recent jqwik dependency changes. Alert if such text appears in logs fed to agentic tools.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Agent-Targeting Method in Dependency Code
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector by method signature: 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class. Decompile resolved JARs and audit method names for agent-specific logic.

suggestion.title: Rapid Dependency Version Increment Following Malicious Release

Detect rapid version pins or overrides of 1.10.0 in lock files. Alert on projects explicitly downgrading from 1.10.0 with commits citing 'malware' or 'injection'.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Detection and Refusal of Tool Output Prompt Injection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agentic coding tool logs for refusal/alert events triggered during dependency testing or tool output parsing. Alert on agents that detect and reject prompt-injection-like directives in test output. Correlate such refusals with jqwik or similar library execution in the same session.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook execution from package.json
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install.' No detection exists for preinstall script invocation itself—the primary attack vector. Need to detect when node/npm executes embedded preinstall scripts.

Look for process parents of node pointing to package.json preinstall script invocation during npm install. Correlate with package installation timing.

suggestion.title: Credential provider access from npm/node context

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from npm/node to external C2

Monitor for DNS queries from npm install phase contexts. Detect HTTPS POST/PUT to uncommon destinations carrying base64/encoded credential payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious package.json manifest with preinstall script
suggestion.rationale: Article: malicious 'preinstall hook on every npm install.' Artifact-level detection for package.json containing preinstall scripts that invoke obfuscated or network-calling code should precede execution detection.

Flag if preinstall script contains: shell metacharacters (|, >, $), network calls (curl, wget, curl), base64/encoding functions, or file write operations to /tmp. suggestion.title: Multi-cloud metadata API queries from build/CI contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: targets 'AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes' credentials. Instance metadata API requests from npm/node in CI environment (GitHub Actions runners, build agents) are high-signal indicators of credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via npm Environment Variable Exfiltration

suggestion.title: WebLogic JSP/WAR Deployment Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation of WebLogic often culminates in malicious WAR/JSP deployment. Hunt for unexpected application deployments or file writes to WebLogic directories during or after exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic deployment directories for unexpected WAR/EAR/JSP uploads or modifications during or immediately after detected exploitation attempts. Cross-reference with absence of legitimate deployment requests.

suggestion.title: Poisoned Container Image Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' with 'stealer loaded during the KICS scanning process'—explicit supply chain attack. No detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry push events for images with unexpected modifications, manifest digest changes, or pushes from anomalous accounts. Correlate image pull events with known-malicious scanning tool execution (KICS). Alert on images where content scanners detect embedded credential stealers or reconnaissance code in layers.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Theft via Container Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' following container compromise. No detection for secret enumeration or exfiltration from containers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container processes reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ (especially token), followed by outbound network connections. Monitor for env-var enumeration or grep-like operations against mounted secrets. Track suspicious service account token usage in Kubernetes API audit logs (bulk secret list, cross-namespace access).

suggestion.title: Privileged Capability Abuse for Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN under 'Container escape' section. No detections for malicious capability usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when containers with privileged capabilities execute dangerous syscalls: CAP_SYS_ADMIN + bpf/ptrace/mount/kexec, CAP_SYS_MODULE + insmod/rmmod, CAP_NET_ADMIN + network namespace manipulation. Flag any capability inheritance mismatches between workload policy and runtime execution.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Abuse from Compromised Workload
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'exploitation of orchestration APIs' and scenarios where container compromise leads to API credential theft. No detection for abnormal API usage patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for service account tokens making bulk list/get requests across secrets, configmaps, or role bindings. Alert on API calls from service accounts originating from pod IPs not matching expected deployments. Flag authentication failures followed by privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Container Runtime Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'exploiting host system vulnerabilities and container runtime components' as attack path. No detection for runtime binary tampering or malicious hook installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/lib/docker, /var/lib/containerd, and runtime socket directories for unexpected binary modifications or injected shared objects. Alert on container runtime daemons executing unusual child processes or accessing unexpected device files. Track docker.sock abuse from containers (direct image pull/push, network policy changes).

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' — a core persistence and privilege escalation indicator. Pipeline produced zero use cases for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table INSERT records, wp_create_user() function calls) for new admin-role accounts created outside normal administrative windows. Correlate with HTTP requests to known WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/). Alert on successful user creation immediately following failed authentication attempts or unusual HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability in specific plugin. Title references active exploitation but no IOC or endpoint-level detection suggested. Article should contain specific vulnerable endpoint paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on HTTP requests matching WP Maps Pro plugin paths (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ and subdirectories) with POST requests containing user/admin creation payloads. Detect parameter fuzzing or unusual query strings targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via User Role Modification
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation IS privilege escalation. The article title describes the end goal of the exploit, yet kill chain contains no privilege_escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_usermeta table for role changes from subscriber/contributor to administrator (wp_capabilities field updates). Alert on any role escalation for accounts created within the last 24 hours. Cross-reference with plugin error logs for exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is exploited via HTTP—likely GET/POST requests to the plugin. No detection hypothesis provided for identifying malicious request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200/302 responses following requests to wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ containing exploitation payloads or user creation parameters. Baseline normal plugin traffic and detect anomalous request patterns (unusual User-Agent, source country misalignment, off-hours requests).

suggestion.title: Failed-to-Successful Login Sequence Before Admin Creation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely involves reconnaissance and authentication attempts before successful compromise. Pipeline should detect pre-exploitation footprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed WordPress login attempts from a single source with a subsequent successful admin account creation event within 15 minutes. Flag accounts created by users with < 5 prior successful logins or from geographies not in the organization's baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Database Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation modifies wp_users and wp_usermeta tables. Direct database access or ORM exploitation should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress database for INSERT operations on wp_users or wp_usermeta tables originating from non-admin database users or from application layer (wp-config.php queries). Alert on rapid multi-row modifications to wp_capabilities, wp_user_roles, or user meta fields.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Rate Spike — Brute Force Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices'—core T1110 behavior: multiple failed password attempts in rapid succession against target accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on accounts receiving >N failed login attempts within time window T. Enumerate distinct source IPs; baseline per account and flag statistical anomalies. Variant: failed attempts clustered by time but dispersed by geography.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Correlated With Failed Authentication Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'resulting in the suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.' Lockout events must correlate with preceding failed auth attempts to establish brute-force cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account lockout events backwards to failed authentication logs within preceding 10-minute window. Surface lockouts preceded by >10 failed attempts; score by geographic scatter of source IPs.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Attempt From Unrecognized Location After Failed Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' following brute-force attempts—indicates attacker persistence attempt or account compromise assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registration events where source location differs from user baseline and registration occurs <1 hour after account lockout or failed auth spike. Flag registrations from countries not in user's historical location set.

suggestion.title: Verification Code Email Generation Spike Per Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple Dashlane users...received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries'—each brute-force attempt triggers verification email; spike indicates automated attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email service logs for verification/MFA challenge sending rate per account. Alert when single account receives >N verification emails within 15-minute window; enrich with associated authentication attempt logs.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel — Login Attempts From Geographically Scattered Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations'—attackers using distributed proxy/botnet IPs. Same account receiving auth attempts from multiple continents in impossible timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: GeoIP-enrich login events per account. Flag when same account receives auth attempts from >2 distant geographies within 5 minutes. Whitelist known VPN/travel patterns; escalate novel geography combinations.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace membership list changes by newly granted owner
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker gaining owner role via membership injection. Post-exploitation impact includes 'now owner can perform admin actions'—need to detect rapid workspace configuration or member-list changes immediately after owner grant. Article does not specify which admin actions, but membership/role changes are high-fidelity signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/{id}/members (role=owner response 201) with subsequent GET/PUT to workspace configuration, member list, or role-change endpoints within 15 minutes from the same user/account. Flag if newly granted owner immediately enumerates or modifies other members.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Failed login attempts before successful owner-account compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover or guess the user_id to inject as owner (article states 'forwards the request body's user_id'). Article does not describe password-spraying or enumeration, but pre-compromise reconnaissance is implicit. Detect failed auth attempts followed by successful login from the same attacker IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to praisonai-platform (invalid user, invalid password) from a source IP, followed within 1 hour by successful login as a different user. Escalate if that login IP later performs a POST /workspaces/*/members grant with role=owner.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace member count spike—mass role elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability allows adding 'arbitrary user as owner'. Attacker could inject multiple users (not just one) to increase persistence or blast-radius. Article does not describe multi-user attacks, but the permission flaw is per-request; multiple requests compound the risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline workspace member count over 7 days. Alert if POST /workspaces/{id}/members succeeds 5+ times within 1 hour from the same source IP or user, particularly with role=owner or role=admin in request body.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: API token or session creation by low-privilege user followed by owner-role assumption
suggestion.rationale: Article assumes attacker is already a workspace member (require_workspace_member gate); method of member acquisition not specified. If membership is open-enrollment or unverified-invite, attacker joins first, then escalates. Detect fast token/session acquisition → immediate privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within same session or 10-minute window: user created, API token issued, workspace membership confirmed (role=member), then POST /workspaces/{id}/members with role=owner succeeds. Flag as suspicious privilege escalation chain.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Asset exposure—CVE-2026-47413 inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article is a published CVE with GHSA advisory. Recon phase detects unpatched praisonai-platform instances. Article does not specify default ports/paths, but asset enumeration is early in kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for praisonai-platform in installed software inventory or running services (process name, http service banners, port 8000-8100 web app detection). Cross-check against CVE-2026-47413 patched-version list. Alert on unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Injection via t.js Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' as a key fingerprint. This is a direct, observable web-layer indicator that should trigger detection when embedded in compromised sites or observed in web logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for script injections matching the pattern t.js?site= with numeric or alphanumeric site identifiers. Look for inline script tags or external script tags loading from zTDS-owned domains. Correlate with traffic redirects to malware-delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompts (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'FakeUpdates lures contain bogus update notices for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser.' These prompts are visually detectable and often served from non-standard domains or localhost.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect fake update prompts by monitoring for suspicious download patterns: executables or ZIP archives with names containing 'update', 'browser', or version numbers originating from non-official update domains. Cross-reference domain reputation and SSL certificate issuer legitimacy.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution via ClickFix Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' that victims are tricked into copying and executing. Detection should focus on PowerShell spawned from user interaction contexts with suspicious encoded/obfuscated arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe spawned from user context (explorer.exe, browser processes, terminal) with encoded parameters (-EncodedCommand, -enc), downloaded content paths, or IEX/Invoke-Expression patterns. Correlate with recent clipboard operations or user interaction events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Archive Extraction and Executable Launch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'a fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' This multi-stage pattern (ZIP → DLL + EXE) is anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archives downloaded from non-official sources followed by extraction and execution of binaries with benign-sounding names (e.g., 'Browser Update.exe', 'Security Check.exe'). Alert on ZIP/RAR extraction followed by executable launch within 1-2 seconds and from temp/download directories.

suggestion.title: Website Traffic Redirection via zTDS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware' via zTDS. Detection on web servers should identify unexpected redirect rules or injected redirection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web servers for injection of redirect rules to unfamiliar domains, particularly those matching zTDS infrastructure signatures. Alert on HTTP 302/301 responses to domains not in baseline. Cross-reference redirected domains against threat intelligence feeds for known malware-delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via Obfuscated JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' This is a platform-specific indicator absent from Windows-centric detection baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On macOS endpoints, monitor for JavaScript processes accessing clipboard (pasteboard) APIs with obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads. Alert on clipboard read/write patterns preceded by browser or verification-themed prompts, particularly from non-standard origins.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vector: 'Compromises Red Hat npm packages' — initial access occurs when developers or CI/CD systems install the malicious package from the registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require operations for packages with suspicious metadata (author account created <30 days ago, unusual download spikes, version number gaps). Correlate with known-bad package hashes or maintainer account takeovers. Flag installations outside normal development windows.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting by npm Package Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm' — detection must identify the malware reading credential stores, environment variables, SSH keys, or API tokens after code execution within the package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/Node.js processes accessing credential file paths (.ssh/, .aws/, .kube/, browser credential stores, .env files). Alert on child process spawning from npm modules, especially shell invocations (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) for credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from npm Module Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials must be exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure. Detection captures outbound command-and-control traffic initiated by the compromised package's execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/Node.js or child processes with outbound HTTPS/DNS to newly-registered domains, suspiciously-timed connections (off-hours for development), non-standard ports, or geolocations inconsistent with legitimate business operations.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Maintainer Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must gain control of package author accounts or exploit registry credentials to push malicious versions. Detection at auth layer catches compromise before package distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry authentication for: new login IP addresses for known maintainers, password reset events, MFA bypass or disable operations, and batch package uploads within short timeframes or from unexpected geolocations.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Before widespread installation, malicious packages exhibit observable registry-level anomalies: dependency injection, size changes, author field modifications in patched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with: unusual new dependencies (especially network/crypto libraries), file size deltas >20% in minor/patch versions, author or repository URL changes post-publication, or modifications to package.json timestamps suggesting republication.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes'—primary execution vector. Requires process telemetry to detect node children spawned by npm with unusual command lines or credential file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or node processes spawned as children of npm during package installation. Correlate with subsequent file I/O to ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or CI/CD credential directories and environment variable reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC token request in Actions workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that: Triggered on push to any branch. Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write'—ingress point for package publishing exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows with id-token: write permissions in newly-modified workflows triggering on any branch. Correlate with subsequent npm publish commands or npm_token environment variable usage.

suggestion.title: Environment and CI credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets'—requires file access and env var monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access to ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, or CI/CD secret directories by node processes. Detect reads of sensitive env vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, GCP_KEY, AZURE_CREDENTIALS) by unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Cloud identity enumeration (GCP/Azure)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume'—novel variant capability detectable via CLI process creation and cloud audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gcloud, az, or gsutil CLI invocations enumerating service accounts, IAM roles, or identity bindings from anomalous contexts (npm install, build agents). Correlate with preinstall script execution timing.

suggestion.title: Package republication with payload propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload'—worm lateral movement via supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry audit logs for unexpected republications by legitimate maintainers, especially rapid burst patterns. Correlate with preinstall script additions, new dependencies, or bundle size increases in otherwise stable packages.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript eval() chains in preinstall hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unusually large, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file. The author relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding'—defense evasion signature detectable in package manifest analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package preinstall scripts for obfuscation: multiple eval() calls, ROT cipher patterns, high-entropy strings, or multi-stage decoding chains. Flag preinstall scripts >10KB or with low code coverage.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Masquerading as Legitimate Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' Core C2 evasion requiring detection of beacon patterns hidden within HTTP normality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic exhibiting beacon hallmarks (fixed intervals, fixed payload sizes, encoded response body, atypical User-Agents, communication to content-delivery infrastructure). Correlate with Cobalt Strike JARM/JA3 signatures and process context (unexpected child processes from cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe).

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API C2 Channel Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Explicit use of messaging API for C2, bypassing traditional C2 network signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes initiating connections to api.telegram.org with bot token patterns, or spawning with Telegram library imports. Monitor for sustained or automated bot interactions; flag processes with no legitimate reason to contact messaging APIs (non-browser, non-messaging-app binaries).

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery via Iterative Agent-Driven Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' with 'collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.' Systematic, iterative LDAP/WMI enumeration driven by automation logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid LDAP queries with evolving filter parameters (suggesting iterative refinement), Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer chains enumerating organizational structure, or LDAP user/computer enumeration from unusual processes. Alert on automated discovery: multiple queries from single process/user within minutes with changing search parameters.

suggestion.title: Multi-Layer Payload Encryption and Runtime Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Core capability: 'wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables or DLLs.' 80+ modules with runtime decryption for EDR bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables with abnormal entropy (indicating encryption), embedded decryption keys in .data/.text sections, or runtime deobfuscation via ROP chains. Detect memory sections with execute+write permissions, process hollowing patterns (parent terminates after spawning suspended child), and dynamic import resolution from import tables.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
