suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'the recent LLMshare campaign used legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clicks on legitimate AI chat service sharing URLs (chatgpt.com/share, claude.ai/share, etc.) that redirect to phishing domains or unknown file hosts. Monitor for rapid URL creation and rotation on legitimate services. Correlate with search engine ads pointing to sharing links.

suggestion.title: Browser-Native Attack Detection Without Endpoint Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Attacks increasingly take place inside the browser, without touching the endpoint' and attacks use 'browser-native mechanics (session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads)' operating entirely in-browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser session hijacking and AiTM token theft without process-level execution artifacts. Monitor for HTTP session cookies stolen via clipboard or local storage exfiltration. Alert on suspicious login replays from different geolocations within minutes. Track in-browser credential entry patterns (multiple password entry attempts, copy-paste cycles).

suggestion.title: WordPress to Steam Profile HTTP/S Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'hiding command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments'—malware must fetch profile pages to parse commands. Detection gap for web-server processes reaching specific Steam profile URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: WordPress processes (php, apache, wp-cli) initiating HTTPS to steamcommunity.com/profiles/[ID] or /id/[username] URLs. Focus on outbound from web servers. Correlate with process memory inspection for regex/string parsing of web response bodies.

suggestion.title: Command Deobfuscation from Web Content in Process Memory
suggestion.rationale: Malware must extract/decode hidden commands from Steam profile comments. Article describes commands as 'hidden' implying obfuscation/parsing logic. No detection for process behavior indicators like base64 decode, regex string searches in HTTP response streams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PHP or web processes calling string parsing/regex/decode APIs immediately after fetching web content. Look for patterns: curl/wget followed by base64 decode, regex match, JSON parse, or environment variable set from command output.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Download from hello-mywordl.info
suggestion.rationale: Malware domain 'hello-mywordl.info' listed as primary IOC. Initial infection likely via malicious plugin hosted or referenced from this domain. Detection needed for WordPress plugin installation/fetch from this C2 domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP/S requests from WordPress servers to hello-mywordl.info, especially toward plugin install endpoints (/wp-admin/plugin-install.php) or direct .zip fetches. Correlate with wp-content/plugins/ directory writes.

suggestion.title: Malware Artifact File Creation in Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'newly discovered malware' targeting WordPress but provides zero file hashes. Pipeline output for 'Pipeline output — IOCs' is empty, suggesting extraction logic failed. Need file-based detection for plugin directory writes from unexpected processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File creation in wp-content/plugins/ from non-WordPress-service processes. Collect MD5/SHA256 of newly created plugin files and cross-reference against malware repositories. Look for files with obfuscated names or base64-encoded content.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to Steam Profile Comments (Data Exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies bidirectional use of Steam profiles (commands IN via comments). Malware likely also exfiltrates data OUT via comments posted to attacker-controlled Steam profiles. No detection for unusual HTTP POST to steamcommunity.com comment endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound HTTPS POST from internal systems to steamcommunity.com with comment endpoints (/comment/add or similar parameters). Flag if POST body contains binary/encoded data, SQL query fragments, or sensitive strings (API keys, credentials, database exports).

suggestion.title: WordPress Configuration Tampering (wp-config or .htaccess Modification)
suggestion.rationale: Article truncated mid-sentence 'The malware works in two [...]'—likely describes persistence or execution steps. Malware typically modifies wp-config.php or .htaccess to maintain access or inject code. No detection for post-exploitation tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File modification events on wp-config.php, .htaccess, or wp-settings.php with unusual content additions (eval(), base64_decode(), or new database credentials). Monitor for changes outside of WordPress auto-update windows.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script with Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines' via postinstall hooks. No detection UC was generated despite this being the core execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes spawned with suspicious child process execution (shell, curl, powershell) or file access to credential directories (.ssh, .aws, .config) immediately after package.json install triggers. Monitor for environment variable access patterns consistent with credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration from CI/CD Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' and stealing credentials, but no detection for environment variable enumeration or exfiltration was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from node_modules or npm context that invoke env enumeration commands (env, printenv) or access process memory/environment structures. Correlate with outbound HTTPS/DNS from same process tree to unknown domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Republish Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages' — no detection for unauthorized package version updates or registry API abuse was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm registry authentication (npm login, .npmrc writes) followed by npm publish commands on legitimate package names. Flag version bumps that deviate from expected maintainer behavior or originate from CI/CD pipelines with recently-installed malicious dependencies.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from Non-Git Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article cites theft from 'GitHub' and 'local machines', implying .git config, SSH keys, and cloud credential files are targeted. No detection for anomalous access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git/config, or cloud credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file read access to credential paths (.ssh/id_*, .aws/credentials, .git/config, .kube/config) by processes in node_modules, npm cache, or spawned by Node.js with no legitimate reason to access them.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Network Callback to Unknown Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Credential exfiltration implies C2 communication; article describes data sent to attacker infrastructure, but no detection for npm postinstall network callbacks was outlined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/node process spawning with first-time network connections to non-package-registry domains (not npmjs.com, registry.yarnpkg.com, etc.). Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS during package installation phases.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages postinstall scripts to execute arbitrary code; no detection for shell/curl/wget spawned from npm context was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process parent chain: npm → node → bash/PowerShell/cmd, or npm → curl/wget. Flag if child process arguments contain base64 encoding, environment variable substitution, or redirection to /dev/null.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Cloud Provider IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure... to camouflage malicious traffic.' Existing beaconing hunt will detect periodic outbound to cloud IPs but will drown in legitimate cloud service traffic. Need inverse: detect C2-like patterns (high-entropy user agents, TLS cert anomalies, DNS CNAMEs) originating FROM cloud provider IP ranges TO internal hosts or unusual destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections from known cloud provider IP ranges (AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare) that exhibit C2 signatures: rare destination ports, irregular byte counts, certificates issued to suspicious domains, or DNS queries to high-entropy subdomains. Cross-reference source IP against cloud provider ASNs to confirm origin.

suggestion.title: DNS C2 via Cloud Provider Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) as a technique. Attackers may tunnel C2 commands via DNS queries to cloud-hosted nameservers (e.g., AWS Route53, Google Cloud DNS, Cloudflare) to blend with legitimate DNS traffic and avoid DGA detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries to cloud provider-owned nameservers (Route53, Cloud DNS, Cloudflare NS records) with high-entropy subdomains or unusual query patterns. Filter out legitimate cloud service health checks by whitelisting known FQDN patterns and correlate against network baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious TLS Cert from Cloud CDN
suggestion.rationale: Attackers hiding C2 in cloud infrastructure will issue TLS certs that appear legitimate (from cloud issuer) but with suspicious details. Article describes using 'trusted cloud infrastructure' to evade—this implies abusing legitimate trust relationships. T1027 (Obfuscated Files) extends to certificate obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect TLS certificates for connections to cloud provider IPs: flag certificates with mismatched CN/SAN (e.g., cert for attacker domain but served from AWS IP), short validity windows, or unusual issuer OIDs. Correlate with process execution and file writes to detect certificate installation by suspicious processes.

suggestion.title: Long-lived Connections to Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations' — this differs from bursty beaconing. Need hunt for sustained TCP sessions (hours/days) to cloud IPs with low data volume and consistent timing, indicating persistent C2 tunnels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect long-duration connections (>1 hour) to cloud provider IPs with minimal data transfer (<1 MB/hr) and periodic keep-alive patterns. Exclude known legitimate services (RDP, SSH to cloud instances) via whitelist. Flag if process spawning connection has no parent or is running from temp directory.

suggestion.title: GitHub/Gitea Abuse for C2 Tasking
suggestion.rationale: Article lists GitHub alongside AWS, Google Cloud, Cloudflare, and Microsoft—implying attackers use GitHub repos, gists, or releases as C2 delivery infrastructure. T1071.001 applied to HTTPS traffic to GitHub.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious access patterns to GitHub: requests to repos with obfuscated names, frequent downloads of releases or raw gists, or clones of recently-created private repos. Correlate with process execution (curl, git, PowerShell) and file staging in temp directories. Whitelist legitimate CI/CD and development tools.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempt to WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server'—this is the primary attack vector and must be detectable from network logs showing T3/IIOP traffic to unpatched WebLogic ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound T3 or IIOP traffic (ports 7001–7002) to WebLogic servers from external sources, especially if followed by anomalous memory access patterns or deserialization errors. Cross-reference against known WebLogic version in use; versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0 are critical if unpatched as of June 4, 2026.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic Server Vulnerable Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2024-21182 affects specific versions: '12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0'—Shodan tracks 1,592 exposed instances. Detection must flag version banners from T3 handshakes or HTTP headers indicating these exact versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for T3 protocol banner grabs or HTTP GET requests to WebLogic admin console (typically /console) that return version strings matching 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0. Flag if version detection occurs from external IPs or recurring scans suggest reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Unauthorized Data Access from Compromised WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—detect anomalous data exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual outbound data volumes or SQL queries from WebLogic server processes after T3 exploitation window. Look for batch data extraction, new scheduled tasks, or HTTP exfiltration to external hosts in close temporal proximity to exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-61884 SSRF Exploitation in Oracle E-Business Suite
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'In October, the cybersecurity agency also ordered government agencies to patch an unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2025-61884) in Oracle E-Business Suite, after flagging it as actively exploited'—separate active threat requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Oracle E-Business Suite logs for SSRF-like patterns: requests from the application to internal IP ranges, unusual outbound connections to 127.0.0.1, localhost, or private subnets, or HTTP requests with Host headers pointing to internal services.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Exposed WebLogic Instances via Public Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Internet intelligence platform Shodan now tracks over 1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online'—attackers scan Shodan data for exposed targets. Detection should flag port-scanning activity consistent with WebLogic enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on widespread scanning of TCP ports 7001 (WebLogic default), 7002 (SSL), or 9002 (debug) originating from single IPs or ASNs known for vulnerability scanning. Correlate with external IP geolocation; flag if scans precede exploitation attempts by hours.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2022-0492 Detection — Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2022-0492 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV due diligence ('patch lag is the silent killer'). Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunting rule for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections reporting CVE-2022-0492 on any Linux system. Cross-reference asset inventory to confirm patch status. Prioritize internet-facing or DMZ-resident systems, as T1190 implies external attack surface.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release Agent Abuse — Suspicious Writes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies privilege escalation vector: 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' Pipeline missed the execution-layer detection for this specific abuse mechanism—unauthorized writes to cgroup release_agent paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to cgroups v1 release_agent files (typically /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/*/ns/cgroup). Flag non-root or unexpected process UIDs writing to these paths. Cross-reference against approved container/cgroup management tools (systemd, Docker daemon, Kubernetes).

suggestion.title: Cgroups Release Agent Execution — Unintended Shell Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes abuse of release_agent feature, which triggers arbitrary command execution on cgroup termination. Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection: monitoring for shell/binary execution triggered by cgroup events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell or binary execution (sh, bash, /bin/nsenter, etc.) spawned by root from cgroup-related PIDs or with cgroup-related parent paths. Correlate with prior suspicious cgroup release_agent writes within a 60-second window.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation — UID/GID Elevation from Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes this is a 'privilege escalation' vulnerability. Pipeline did not surface detection for outcome-level indicators: processes inside containers gaining root or unexpected high-privilege UIDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In containerized environments, alert on processes transitioning from unprivileged UIDs (e.g., UID 1000+) to UID 0 or other sensitive UIDs (e.g., 0, 33, 48) without corresponding setuid-bit-based execution or sudo log entries. Correlate with cgroups release_agent activity.

suggestion.title: Container Escape Indicators — Cgroup Breakout Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article targets cgroups v1, which is heavily used in container isolation. Pipeline omitted use case for container escape detection, a critical downstream impact of this CVE in containerized infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container processes accessing host cgroup directories (/sys/fs/cgroup on host mount points), writing to release_agent files, or spawning processes outside the container namespace. Cross-reference with container escape indicators (procfs mounts, nsenter usage, host binary execution).

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: CVE-2025-48595 Android Framework Integer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Compliance hunt required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch management systems for unpatched instances of Android Framework vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595. Alert on any systems still missing patches as of 2026-06-05 federal deadline. Focus on externally-exposed Android services.

suggestion.title: Detect Local Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Integer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'allows for code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation'—the post-exploitation behavior needs detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual privilege elevation attempts involving Android Framework components. Look for processes spawning with elevated privileges after interaction with vulnerable Framework APIs. Baseline normal privilege escalation patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Integer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability mechanism is 'integer overflow'—exploitation attempts may exhibit characteristic memory or arithmetic patterns in exploit delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for abnormal integer arithmetic or boundary-crossing operations in Android Framework context. Look for suspicious memory allocations, realloc patterns, or buffer manipulations that indicate integer overflow exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Authentication Followed by Successful Login
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Brute-Force Attack'—the core credential-access technique. Pipeline missed detection for repeated failed-login clusters against same account followed by successful authentication, which is the attack path disclosed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >10 failed authentications to a single Dashlane account within 1 hour followed by successful login within 5 minutes. Establish baseline for geo, device, time-of-day patterns to surface impossible-travel or untrusted-device anomalies.

suggestion.title: Bulk Encrypted Vault Download from Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discloses 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—direct exfiltration indicator. Pipeline completely missed the data-theft phase and should surface detection for large vault blobs exfiltrated post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of vault files (typically 1–100 MB binary blobs) from Dashlane infrastructure minutes after successful authentication from a new device/location. Flag unusual destination IPs, bandwidth spikes, or download-to-upload patterns indicating re-exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Dashlane Account Logon from New Geolocation Without Identity Verification
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies the attacker accessed accounts from geographies/devices not associated with legitimate user activity. Pipeline should propose behavior-baselining to identify geographic anomalies on password-manager accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish user baseline for Dashlane login locations and devices. Alert on successful login from country/city/ISP never seen for that user, especially if preceded by multiple failed-login attempts from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Multiple Password Manager Accounts Compromised from Single Source IP
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force against password managers typically targets many users; pipeline should propose cross-account anomaly detection to identify distributed credential-validation attempts (T1110.004 - Credential Stuffing).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts across all Dashlane users. Alert if single IP attempts login to >5 distinct accounts within 30 minutes, even if all fail—indicates credential-stuffing attack. Look for request patterns (timing, user-agent consistency, geo) to rule out legitimate concurrent-session activity.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Process Spawning Interpreter via Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver'—CVE-2024-20656 (path traversal) or similar allows arbitrary code execution. Pipeline missed detection for WinRAR/unrar spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on winrar.exe, unrar.exe, or rar.exe as parent process to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or wscript.exe. Enforce baseline: extract operations should not spawn interpreters. Raise on unusual CLI arguments or execution from user writable paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%).

suggestion.title: GammaWorm / GammaSteel Named Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names two payloads ('GammaWorm and GammaSteel'). Pipeline must detect these by process name, file hash, or behavioral signature including rapid discovery and registry enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes matching GammaWorm*, GammaSteel*, or obfuscated variants; correlate with rapid registry queries to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion, HKCU\Software\*, user enumeration via net.exe or Get-LocalUser, and process enumeration (Get-Process, tasklist).

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Extraction from WinRAR Archive to Temp/AppData
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires extraction of malware to filesystem before execution. Article describes delivery mechanism but pipeline missed file-system IoA: WinRAR writing binaries to user-writable directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR-initiated file creation in C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp, C:\Windows\Temp, or %LOCALAPPDATA% directories with extensions .exe, .dll, .scr, .ps1, or .bat, especially if followed by process execution within 5 seconds of write.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from WinRAR or Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Both GammaWorm and GammaSteel are command-control malware per article title; pipeline produced zero C2 detection use cases despite this being signature behavior for reconnaissance/data exfiltration against Ukrainian targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS/DNS queries originating from WinRAR.exe, cmd.exe, or powershell.exe spawned by WinRAR; flag non-standard ports (8000–9999, 10000+), missing or self-signed TLS certificates, domains registered to Russian/Eastern European infrastructure, or known Gamaredon C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Code Injection or DLL Side-Loading Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon historically employs process injection (T1574.002) and DLL side-loading; GammaWorm/GammaSteel payloads likely hide C2 in legitimate process contexts. Article title does not describe evasion techniques but pipeline should baseline Gamaredon's known TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CreateRemoteThread or suspicious module loads from GammaWorm/GammaSteel and WinRAR child processes; alert on unsigned or publisher-mismatched DLLs loaded from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, user directories, or non-system paths; correlate with process hollowing signatures.

suggestion.title: Registry Discovery: Rapid Multi-Key Enumeration for Recon
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon performs heavy registry enumeration for OS version, user accounts, installed software, and credential sources; article targets Ukraine (nation-state recon). Pipeline missed this baseline Gamaredon IoA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >8 distinct registry query attempts within 30 seconds from WinRAR or child processes, especially targeting HKCU\Software, HKLM\Software\Wow6432Node, and credential-storage paths. Flag queries to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion and HKCU\Environment.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-48595 'may be under limited, targeted exploitation' as a 'high-severity Android Framework vulnerability' enabling 'code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later'; primary IOC with zero pipeline coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework components for exploitation patterns consistent with CVE-2025-48595 on Android 14+. Track framework module exceptions, memory access violations, and privilege transitions indicative of local privilege escalation exploits.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability enabling attackers to 'escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later' and notes 'critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation attempts targeting Android Framework. Monitor transitions from app_process to system context in framework modules. Track SELinux denials preceding successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Patch Non-Compliance: Android June 2026 Updates
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patches released 2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 targeting 124 vulnerabilities including actively exploited CVE-2025-48595; organizations need asset visibility on unpatched exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Android 14+ devices with patch level older than 2026-06-01 remaining unpatched beyond grace period. Escalate for high-value targets: 'high-profile or high-interest individuals' per article (executives, security staff, VIPs).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Spyware Indicators on Android
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals'; expects post-compromise collection behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized collection: contacts, call logs, location history, SMS, media files post-exploitation window. Detect exfiltration over non-standard channels or to low-reputation IPs.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'two other high-severity zero-days (CVE-2025-48633 and CVE-2025-48572)...under limited, targeted exploitation' and 'another zero-day flaw in a Qualcomm display component (CVE-2026-21385)'; co-exploited vulnerabilities not surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2025-48595, CVE-2025-48633, CVE-2025-48572, and CVE-2026-21385 within same session. Alert on chained privilege escalation across multiple kernel subsystems.

suggestion.title: Android Device OS Version Lag Post-Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 124 flaws patched and one actively exploited—devices not updated within SLA are direct targets. 'Google June 2026 Android Update' establishes baseline patch date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices reporting Android build date prior to June 2026 patch release. Escalate to critical if device count exceeds patch SLA (e.g., unpatched 30+ days post-release). Cross-reference CVE CVSSv3 scores for actively exploited variants.

suggestion.title: Exploit-Traffic Pattern Detection for Android Memory Corruption Flaw
suggestion.rationale: 'One actively exploited' indicates in-the-wild attack delivery; Android kernel/memory vulnerabilities are network-deliverable via malformed media, JavaScript, or serialized objects. Look for anomalous inbound network patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic to Android devices matching known exploit payloads: oversized media files, malformed WebView requests, or serialization gadgets. Correlate hits with unpatched device inventory to confirm exploitability.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Via Kernel Exploit on Android
suggestion.rationale: Android CVEs commonly chain to root/system privilege via capability abuse or SELinux policy bypass. 'Actively exploited' suggests adversaries are moving past initial code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed/successful uid transitions from user-mode process to system (uid 0, uid 1000/shell). Monitor for capability manipulation or SELinux policy violations. Baseline legitimate capability transitions and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Access on Compromised Android Device
suggestion.rationale: If exploit occurred pre-patch, detector should catch post-compromise artifacts: unauthorized file access, screen capture, or exfiltration to external command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file access patterns (bulk reads of /data/data, /sdcard) with screen-capture requests or app-manifest violations. Flag processes accessing contacts, SMS, location APIs without user interaction.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Google Services via Compromised Android Device
suggestion.rationale: Android compromise can pivot to corporate Google Workspace/Cloud identity if device is enrolled in MDM and holds cached credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual geographic/IP-based authentication to Workspace/Cloud from device post-compromise. Flag token refreshes from unpatched devices combined with subsequent unusual cloud-service access patterns.

suggestion.title: Mobile Threat Intelligence Feed Update for June 2026 Android Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Organizations require timely IOC/YARA/Snort rule distribution for the 124 patched flaws; 'one actively exploited' signals rule urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE list and exploitation POCs for the June 2026 patch set. Publish YARA signatures for exploit payloads. Distribute Snort/Zeek rules for network detection. Update mobile MDM policies to enforce 30-day patch SLA.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Repository Tag Rewrite Across Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' — detection must identify when git tags on a package are retroactively modified post-release, which is anomalous for legitimate package maintenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository audit logs for tag modification/deletion events on previously-released versions. Alert when a single commit hash receives multiple conflicting tag assignments across version branches, or when tag timestamps predate commit dates. Composer caches package metadata; detect when deployed package version hash differs from declared tag hash.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment Variable Exfiltration in CI Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack goal as 'Steal CI Secrets' — pipeline should detect unauthorized access or exfiltration of CI environment variables (GitHub Actions secrets, GitLab CI variables, etc.) from build contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/Laravel build tasks that enumerate or read CI environment variables (env, $_ENV access, getenv() calls) followed by network egress to non-whitelisted domains. Flag when build logs show command output containing common CI secret patterns (API_TOKEN=, SECRET_KEY=, AWS_SECRET=) being logged or exfiltrated.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Maintainer Account Access or Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise requires prior account takeover of package maintainer — article implies account credential theft or compromise as initial attack vector ('Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' requires maintainer permissions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository login events for anomalies: logins from new geolocations, logins at unusual times for the maintainer, or rapid successful logins followed by package modifications. Detect API token creation or SSH key registration immediately before repository modifications. Flag when malicious packages are published/updated but no corresponding commit appears in git history.

suggestion.title: Detection of Known-Malicious Laravel-Lang Package Versions via Hash Validation
suggestion.rationale: Composer packages installed in CI/prod environments should be validated against known-good hashes; pipeline should publish IOCs for compromised package versions to enable downstream detection via artifact integrity verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed Laravel-Lang package hashes against a maintained list of known-compromised versions. Alert when composer.lock or installed packages match malicious package hashes identified in this breach. Detect composer.json or composer.lock modifications by CI pipeline user that downgrade or pin to known-malicious versions.

suggestion.title: Multiple Package Modifications by Single Maintainer Account in Short Time Window
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack compromised 'Multiple Composer Packages' under Laravel-Lang umbrella — unusual burst of modifications across package portfolio by one account is supply-chain indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single maintainer account modifies >3 packages in the same package family/namespace within a 1-hour window, especially if modifications include tag rewrites or retroactive commits. Establish baseline for typical package release cadence per maintainer and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Laravel-Lang Package Installation from Unexpected PHP Project Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks are most dangerous when malicious packages execute in victim CI/development environments — detection should trigger on Laravel-Lang package installation in non-standard or high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag composer install operations that fetch Laravel-Lang packages during CI runs, especially in sensitive environments (payment systems, credential-handling services, internal tooling). Alert on installation from non-primary package registry or when version resolution falls back to git branches instead of release tags.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Compromised Development Tool
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses securing 'code across development lifecycle' and mentions GitHub/agents, likely covers compromised build dependencies or malicious toolchain components—a known attack vector. Article keywords include 'GitHub' and 'development lifecycle' suggesting CI/CD security context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or revoked-certificate build tool execution, unexpected package manager calls during CI/CD stages, or outbound connections from build agents to non-approved artifact repositories.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Extension Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article signals compromised extension distribution; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Expected malicious version identifiers, package hashes, or publisher identification from supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation or activation of Nx Console extension in VS Code with suspicious version signatures, unsigned manifests, or from non-canonical publishers. Alert on extension directory modifications outside normal upgrade patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from Malicious Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions execute arbitrary code in developer context; article title implies active compromise but no execution detections mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected shell, Node.js, or PowerShell process spawning from VS Code extension directory or from VSCode.exe context. Flag execution of build scripts, package managers, or curl/wget from extension activation paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Dev-tool compromise typically targets git tokens, npm credentials, API keys; article implies active attack but zero credential-access indicators extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to .npmrc, .git/config, .aws/credentials, .env files or OS credential vaults from VS Code child processes. Alert on reads to home directory credential stores immediately after extension initialization.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks on extensions establish outbound C2; HIGH severity article should surface network indicators, none extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound TLS connections from VS Code/Node processes to domains not in organizational Nx/npm/GitHub whitelist. Flag periodic beaconing patterns or connections to IP space inconsistent with known Nx infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm/Build System Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Extension compromises often intercept build processes to inject malicious payloads; no execution-at-build-time detections proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm lifecycle scripts (prepare, postinstall, build) for unexpected child processes or network calls. Flag modifications to nx.json, package.json scripts, or injection of preload modules in Node process environment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Flutter App Execution from Non-Standard Location
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates 'FlutterShell backdoor built using the Flutter framework'—Flutter executables have distinct runtime signatures and should be monitored when executed from /tmp, /var/tmp, or user library paths rather than standard application bundles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of Flutter-based executables or processes with 'flutter' or 'dart' in the command line originating from browser cache directories, temp folders, or suspicious Downloads subdirectories. Correlate with parent process being a browser or advertising service.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent/Daemon Persistence from Malvertising Campaign
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell backdoor for macOS must establish persistence; article describes 'malvertising campaign targeting macOS users,' suggesting use of standard macOS persistence mechanisms like LaunchAgents in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor filesystem writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ and /Library/LaunchDaemons/ for plist files created within hours of suspicious process execution. Alert on LaunchAgent execution referencing previously unseen or unsigned binaries in user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Redirect Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign is explicitly named 'malvertising'—requires detection of ad network domains redirecting to malicious infrastructure; article describes initial infection vector as ad-based.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to legitimate ad networks (doubleclick.net, adnxs.com, etc.) where the response includes redirect chains to unknown or recently-registered domains, particularly those with low reputation scores or no ASN whitelisting.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell C2 Beacon Pattern on Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell backdoor requires command-and-control communication; malware often uses non-HTTP ports or obfuscated HTTPS to evade detection, typical of mature backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to uncommon or newly-registered domains from infected macOS hosts, followed by connections to non-standard HTTPS ports (8443, 9443, 8080) or obfuscated TLS handshakes with certificate pinning bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: Process Injection or Code Execution via Browser Extension
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising attacks often inject malicious content or extensions into browsers; FlutterShell persistence may leverage browser plugins or injected code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious browser extension installations or modifications to ~/Library/Application Support/[browser]/Extensions/ directories, especially when paired with unsigned code or obfuscated JavaScript. Correlate with malvertising-attributed domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Minecraft JAR Execution from Non-Standard Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'is distributed through Minecraft-related malicious mods, clients, cheats, and utilities' delivered as JAR files totaling '3,820 unique malicious JAR files.' Detection should flag JAR execution from temp directories, Downloads, or AppData paths inconsistent with legitimate Minecraft launcher behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .jar file execution where parent process is not official Minecraft launcher or JRE, particularly from user-writable temp or Downloads directories. Cross-reference filename against known Minecraft client projects (Meteor, Radium, Wurst, LiquidBounce, etc.) for obfuscation or suspicious naming.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Minecraft Session ID Theft and Browser Password Store Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes WeedHack steals 'Minecraft session ID theft, cookies, and saved passwords across 36 browsers' plus Discord, Steam, Telegram credentials. This is T1555 applied to gaming platforms. Detect suspicious file access patterns to browser credential stores and .minecraft/launcher_profiles.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes (excluding browser/OS processes) accessing credential storage paths like %APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, %APPDATA%\.minecraft, or Discord appdata. Correlate with unsigned/recently-created executables. Look for rapid sequential file reads across multiple credential stores within seconds.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Download: Malicious Minecraft Client Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'SEO poisoning distribution method targets keywords that correspond to clients: Meteor Client, Radium Client, Wurst Client, Aristois, LiquidBounce, Impact Client, Future Client, Inertia Client, Cornos Client, WWE Client, 3arthh4ck, Salhack, Phobos, and Gamesense.' Detect downloads from imposter domains mimicking these projects (e.g., typosquats, newly-registered domains linking to malicious sites).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of JAR files from domains containing variations of known Minecraft client names but lacking official GitHub/Discord footprints. Detect when user visits lookalike domains (edit distance analysis) of legitimate Minecraft projects before downloading unsigned JAR. Flag network requests to domains newly-registered within 30 days if they serve .jar downloads.

suggestion.title: Premium Tier Remote Access: Webcam/Keylogger Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states premium subscribers gain 'remote control with input access (mouse and keyboard), webcam access, keylogger, remote shell, and remote file management.' These are high-confidence indicators of code execution and privilege—monitor for suspicious webcam/microphone access from JAR processes and keyboard hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned/suspicious Java/JAR processes requesting camera or microphone permissions, or loading keyboard-hook libraries (e.g., user32.dll exports CreateHookEx from unusual processes). Detect unusual WMI calls to grab webcam data or clipboard contents originating from JAR child processes.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet and Discord/Steam Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: WeedHack targets '56 cryptocurrency add-ons, 12 desktop cryptocurrency wallet apps, Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials.' Detection should look for suspicious file access to wallet software data directories and read-after-write patterns to Discord/Steam token storage locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading from crypto wallet app directories (Exodus, Electrum, Ledger Live config paths) and Discord/Steam credential caches. Flag when non-legitimate processes enumerate or copy files from %APPDATA%\Discord, %APPDATA%\Steam, or crypto wallet app folders in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Clearnet Infostealer Dashboard Access and Telegram C2
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'WeedHack malware platform is hosted on the clear net' with 'dashboard that shows an overview of their victims' and 'Telegram channel has over 800 members.' Detect traffic to clearnet infostealer panel domains and Telegram bot/channel activity consistent with C2 exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify network beacons to known WeedHack dashboard domain(s) and unusual Telegram client activity originating from compromised systems (API calls to Telegram Bot API from non-standard clients or at unusual times). Monitor DNS queries and HTTP POST requests to clearnet infostealer infrastructure. Correlate Telegram traffic volume anomalies with process execution timelines.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Execution Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Malware explicitly named in title. Article describes RAT deployed against Finance Ministry; no execution-phase detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Xeno RAT process execution, child-process spawning from suspicious parents, command-line arguments with encoded payloads, and suspicious imports or registry modifications consistent with RAT behavior.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Spear-Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy is documented as using spear phishing for initial access. Article targets Finance Ministry, a high-value government entity. No email-based initial access use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spear-phishing targeting Finance Ministry staff: suspicious attachments mimicking financial reports, malicious macros, and social engineering pretexting government officials or budget processes.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: RATs require C2 infrastructure. Article context demands detection for command-and-control phase, yet none present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous HTTPS/HTTP beaconing to unknown or newly-registered C2 domains, DNS queries to suspicious infrastructure, and encrypted traffic on non-standard ports from Finance Ministry systems.

suggestion.title: OSINT Harvesting of Government Finance Staff
suggestion.rationale: Targeting a specific ministry indicates reconnaissance. Article does not explicitly detail recon methods, but standard SideCopy playbook includes LinkedIn profiling and public directory scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk queries to public directory services, LinkedIn reconnaissance of Finance Ministry personnel, and unusual DNS lookups for ministry subdomains or employee email patterns.

suggestion.title: Maven Central malicious package version deployment (jqwik 1.10.0)
suggestion.rationale: "Any project that pulled net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at 1.10.0, directly or transitively." Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite explicit package:version:method identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Maven Central repository metadata and build logs for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0 or 1.10.1. Flag any project dependency resolution events pulling these versions. Correlate with suspicious test output or agent-readable streams to determine exposure.

suggestion.title: ANSI escape sequence obfuscation in build/test output streams
suggestion.rationale: "The code prints the instruction line, then prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice." This obfuscation hides text from humans but remains in machine-parsed logs. "Watch for stray ESC[2K and carriage-return artifacts around your test summaries."
log_sources: Build job logs (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, CI/CD)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Maven/JUnit test output for sequences matching ESC\[2K (0x1B\[2K) or CR (\r) immediately following printable text. Flag unusual combinations of erase-line codes in non-interactive contexts (CI logs, agent output). Correlate with suspicious method names like *ForCodingAgents or *ForAgents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious agent-targeting method names in Java dependencies
suggestion.rationale: "The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents()." Method naming alone revealed intent. Pipeline missed class-level and method-level IOCs (net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor.printMessageForCodingAgents).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform static analysis on newly-pulled dependencies for method names containing 'Agent', 'Coding', 'LLM', or similar patterns combined with 'Print', 'Message', or 'Output'. Flag classes in execution or engine packages with these signatures. Baseline against known good versions.

suggestion.title: Prompt injection patterns in AI agent tool output processing
suggestion.rationale: "Any pipeline that pulled the dependency and fed test output back into an LLM agent could have triggered the prompt injection." The attack specifically targets agents reading raw output. Pipeline missed detection of agent-readable injection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent-executed tool output (mvn test, gradle test, etc.) for imperatives targeting agent behavior: 'disregard', 'delete', 'remove', 'ignore previous'. Flag when such imperatives appear in non-interactive test/build output contexts where humans would not act on them but agents might.

suggestion.title: Rapid security-related package version bumps on Maven Central
suggestion.rationale: "Version 1.10.0 lands on Maven Central. [Two days later] Version 1.10.1 ships. The directive gets softened, and the hiding becomes opt-in." A patch release within 48 hours for a supply-chain attack. Pipeline should detect urgent remediation patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patch-level version releases (e.g., 1.10.0 → 1.10.1) released within 48 hours for packages with known security incidents. Correlate with public disclosure/GitHub issues. Flag downstream builds that have not yet transitioned from the malicious version.

suggestion.title: Decompiled JAR artifacts matching known malicious methods
suggestion.rationale: "They decompile the JAR and find the print calls." The method printMessageForCodingAgents() in JqwikExecutor class is a concrete IOC. Pipeline output contains {} (empty), indicating complete miss on extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected class/method signatures for known-good versions of dependencies. Flag unexpected methods in execution-path classes (*.engine.execution.*, *.execution.*, *Executor). Cross-reference commit hashes against public repositories to validate legitimacy.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook script execution via node
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install.' No detection for the hook execution itself (T1546.016). This is the initial payload trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node or npm-cli spawning JavaScript processes immediately post-install with command-line arguments matching preinstall script patterns. Look for npm-driven process creation of 'node -e' or 'node ./node_modules/.bin/*' in the context of ongoing package installations.

suggestion.title: Credential file access post-npm-install (GitHub, Vault, AWS, CircleCI)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI.' No detection for reading these specific credential sources (T1552.001, T1555).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node processes accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, VAULT_ADDR env vars, or .circleci/config.yml within seconds of @redhat-cloud-services npm installation. Alert on file read followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage payload decompression/execution in /tmp
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester' but no detection for unpacking or staging of secondary payloads. Most npm malware extracts gzip or base64-encoded payloads to /tmp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node process writing files to /tmp with characteristics of encoded payloads (gzip headers, base64 entropy) or spawning child processes with /tmp/ file arguments immediately after npm install completes.

suggestion.title: Outbound credential/secret exfiltration via node HTTP(S)
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens' but no detection for the actual theft/exfiltration (T1041, T1071). Harvesting is useless without egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node processes making HTTP POST requests to non-standard or C2-like domains within 5 minutes of accessing credential files. Correlate node_modules/.bin/* execution with outbound connections to unfamiliar IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious environment variable exfiltration via node
suggestion.rationale: Malware likely reads environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, VAULT_TOKEN, etc.) injected by CI systems. Article implies broad credential targeting but no env var harvesting detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node processes executing with visible environment variable enumeration (process.env iteration, env|grep, printenv) or accessing .env files immediately post-install. Alert if paired with DNS/HTTP egress.

suggestion.title: npm package preinstall/postinstall hook anomaly
suggestion.rationale: While UC_12_7 detects package installation, no behavioral anomaly detection for hooks themselves. Legitimate preinstall hooks rarely spawn network activity or file I/O outside package.json declared paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline preinstall/postinstall hooks from package.json and alert when runtime behavior deviates: network access (especially to non-npm registries), credential file reads, /tmp writes, or child process spawning that isn't declared in the hook script.

suggestion.title: npm Package Execution via Install Hook / postinstall Script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses worm propagation and CI/CD persistence vectors in npm context. npm postinstall scripts execute arbitrary code during package installation—foundational attack pattern for npm supply-chain malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by npm.exe or node.exe with parent process link to package.json parsing or node_modules directory access. Alert on spawned shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) launched from npm install context with encoded/obfuscated command arguments.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Credential Harvesting via Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'credential harvesting' and .npmrc access patterns. Malicious packages commonly target .npmrc files containing npm registry tokens to propagate laterally to downstream packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads of .npmrc, package-lock.json, or .npmtoken from npm-related processes outside normal dependency resolution. Alert on exfiltration of home-directory dotfiles via HTTP/HTTPS POST to external C2 or package registry lookalike domain.

suggestion.title: npm Package Worm Self-Propagation via Dependency Tree
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'worm propagation' in npm context. Malicious package increments version, updates its own dependencies, and re-publishes to trigger installation of infected version across downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish operations (npm-cli.js publish, registry API calls) triggered from automated contexts (CI/CD) with abnormally high version-bump frequency or self-referential dependency changes. Alert on npm registry API calls originating from compromised package maintainer CI/CD environment.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated / Encoded Payload Execution within npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords emphasize 'obfuscation' and 'payload'. npm supply-chain malware commonly uses base64, eval, require(), or unicode obfuscation to evade static detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on eval(), require() calls with variable/dynamic string arguments within npm package load path. Detect node.exe spawned with --input-type=module or --eval flags alongside hex/base64 decode operations (Buffer.from). Monitor for runtime decompression of gzip payloads within postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: npm Package Typosquatting / Similar-Name Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks leverage human error via package names similar to legitimate dependencies (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'loadash'). Article context on npm threat landscape implies namespace-based attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed npm packages against Levenshtein distance from common high-value packages. Alert on package installations from accounts without prior history of that package use. Monitor npm registry queries for near-matches to legitimate packages followed by install of alternative package.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration via npm Package Environment Access
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'GitHub' and 'credential harvesting'. npm malware frequently targets CI/CD environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) to compromise downstream repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall script reads of process.env object variables matching CI/CD token patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, CI_TOKEN). Detect exfiltration of environment variable contents to external HTTP endpoint not in allowlist. Monitor for GitHub API calls (git push, workflow dispatch) from npm install context.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Phishing Kits (18+ Active Variants)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'device code phishing, which abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid device code redemption, geographic anomalies in device code claims, codes claimed within minutes of issuance without user interaction, or multiple failed device code attempts from suspicious sources preceding successful auth.

suggestion.title: ClickFix/InstallFix/ConsentFix Search Result Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The rapid evolution of ClickFix, with new techniques like InstallFix and ConsentFix' and '4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of fake Windows Update, installer, or consent dialog processes following suspicious search result navigation; look for msiexec/setup.exe spawned from browser context with characteristic ClickFix lures.

suggestion.title: Malicious Links Hosted on Legitimate AI Chat Sharing (LLMShare)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Recent examples are even seeing attackers host malicious links via legitimate AI chat sharing functionality' and 'The LLMshare campaign used legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor legitimate AI sharing URLs (chatgpt.com/share/, claude.ai/share/, etc.) for phishing landing page redirects, suspicious external referrers, or malvertising campaigns promoting shared links as ads.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI Tool Shadow Adoption and Data Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: '45% of employees are now regular AI users on corporate devices, with 67% using non-corporate accounts' and '38% of file uploads to AI tools are made from personal shadow accounts rather than organizational ones.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to unapproved AI services (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini) via personal accounts; flag large or sensitive file uploads, clipboard data written to AI tool requests, or multi-document exfil patterns.

suggestion.title: AI Browser Extension Browsing Context Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser extension access to internal applications, clipboard operations from extension processes, network beaconing from extension context, or extensions transmitting page DOM/session data to external domains.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle + Device Code Kit Convergence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'As AitM and device code kits converge into single platforms, we're seeing signs of heavy AI use — as we observed when we got an inside look at Doko's Panel and derivative kits, used extensively by ShinyHunters and BlackFile.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate session cookie interception indicators with device code token redemption; detect MFA prompt anomalies followed by successful auth, proxy/DNS configuration changes before credential claims, or out-of-band OAuth approval patterns.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg DLL Side-Loading from Game Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states a 'modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin' and 'the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Direct description of DLL injection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ffmpeg.dll is loaded from game install directories and subsequently loads natives2_blob.bin or other suspicious exports. Monitor for DLL load chains originating from RenPy or RPG Maker MV processes during game startup.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via InprocServer32 Registry Write
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' Specific registry target and trigger condition stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 entries targeting 'Windows Color System Calibration Loader' with suspicious DLL paths. Correlate registry modification timestamp with user login/COM object instantiation events.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from DLL Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' as Stage1, which 'performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Named entry point for behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand or Base64 payload arguments spawned as a child of game processes or from InprocServer32-registered DLLs. Flag Base64 scripts that decode to VM/sandbox detection logic.

suggestion.title: natives2_blob.bin DLL Load Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names natives2_blob.bin (SHA1: edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d) as the malicious execution stage. Hash and file name are directly observable indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create deterministic alert on image load of natives2_blob.bin by hash (SHA1: edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d) or file name from unexpected paths. Monitor for DllGetClassObject export calls on this DLL.

suggestion.title: Secondary Trojan Download Post-Implant Delay
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' Multi-stage execution with network pivoting occurs days after initial breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP(S) downloads initiated by processes spawned from COM-hijacked DLL execution after multi-day delay. Establish baseline for legitimate game network traffic and alert on anomalous outbound connections to non-CDN IPs.

suggestion.title: Game Archive Extraction with Trojanized FFmpeg
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'archive containing the infected game' with 'fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL.' Game archives distributed via PixelDrain and torrent trackers are the delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for game archive extraction (RAR/ZIP) from PixelDrain or torrent downloads followed by ffmpeg.dll placement in game directory. Alert on modification timestamps of ffmpeg.dll that differ from expected game distribution dates.

suggestion.title: npm post-install script spawning suspicious children
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'silently infecting CI/CD environments'—this occurs via post-install lifecycle hooks. Pipeline missed detection of shell/PowerShell/cmd processes spawned as children of npm/node during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm.exe or node.exe spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/sh with network I/O or file I/O to credential stores within 5s of install. Look for parent=npm, child containing shell with env-var reads or file exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration by npm processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—pipeline missed detection of file access to credential files (.ssh, .aws, browser profiles, git config) by node/npm processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe reading ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/*, HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\MountPoints2, or browser credential database files. Baseline: npm should not access these paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm package republication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—detection pipeline missed the C2 communication and authentication to npm registry to push modified versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS to registry.npmjs.com with POST/PUT methods from non-CI/CD build systems. Alert on npm authentication tokens (Bearer) exfiltrated via env-vars to external domains. Detect republication of existing package versions with modified content.

suggestion.title: Environment variable exfiltration in CI/CD context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack targets 'CI/CD environments'—these contain GitHub tokens, cloud provider credentials, deploy keys. Pipeline missed detection of process access to CI/CD environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, etc.) by npm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe accesses environment variables containing auth tokens in a CI/CD context (detect CI indicators: env vars like BUILD_ID, CI=true, GITHUB_ACTIONS). Look for env-var reads followed by DNS/HTTP to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Browser and local credential harvesting by npm
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'clipboard data, browser credentials' among stolen data—pipeline did not create detections for browser profile access or clipboard monitoring from npm process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe/npm.exe accessing browser SQLite databases (Chrome, Firefox, Edge credential stores) or clipboard APIs. Monitor for spawning xclip, xsel, or wl-paste on Linux, or Windows clipboard read APIs from untrusted npm modules.

suggestion.title: npm module dependency injection and supply chain propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack as 'over 90 versions'—pipeline missed detection of version inflation, typosquatting variants, or dependency-substitution patterns in package.json modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package.json and package-lock.json for unexpected version changes, new dependencies added at install time, or resolved versions deviating from lockfile. Alert on high-volume version bumps across a package family in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'install malicious extensions' by 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension.' This is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension installations where no extension marketplace UI activity preceded the install event. Alert on extension installation triggered by webview child processes. Detect simulated keyboard input (SendInput, keybd_event) originating from VS Code renderer/webview processes immediately prior to extension installation attempts.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'malicious extension that extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev' and 'The token is not scoped to the particular repo you interacted with, meaning it has full access to every other repo.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing GitHub OAuth Bearer tokens originating from VS Code processes or browser child processes spawned by VS Code. Flag GitHub API calls using stolen tokens from unusual source IPs or user agents. Monitor for bulk repository enumeration API calls (GET /user/repos, /graphql queries for repository lists) in short time windows following extension installation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Private Repository Enumeration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access.' This discovery activity follows credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API GET /user/repos calls with high result counts or graphql queries requesting allRepositories fields originating from developer workstations. Correlate with recent unusual extension installations or webview activity. Baseline per-user API call patterns and flag anomalous enumeration bursts.

suggestion.title: VS Code Webview Message-Passing Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'exploiting VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system' to 'simulate keypresses in the main editor' and trigger extension installation from unprivileged context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for webview child processes that call postMessage() with extension installation payloads or requests to invoke main editor commands (vscode.commands.executeCommand). Detect IPC abuse where webview process context reads from main VS Code process memory. Alert on renderer process creation with unusual command-line arguments enabling file access or API execution.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Exploitation of VS Code URI Scheme
suggestion.rationale: Initial access: 'attackers to steal GitHub authentication tokens by tricking users into clicking a link.' Attack exploits integration between github.dev webview and VS Code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks on github.dev or vscode:// URI links in email, Slack, or browser history that trigger VS Code launch. Flag mismatch between link target and actual VS Code context opened (e.g., URL parameter tampering). Correlate email receipt with subsequent malicious extension installation or webview activity within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unencrypted GitHub OAuth Token Storage in github.dev Cookies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev that allows it to interact on your behalf' stored in cookies/local storage accessible to webview. Mitigation confirmed: 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser cookie storage for GitHub OAuth tokens (prefix ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_) in unencrypted form. Alert if VS Code or webview processes access github.dev cookies/localStorage. Detect exfiltration of cookie contents to non-GitHub domains. Flag absence of expected github.dev cookie deletion on browser restart (persistent token storage).

suggestion.title: Crypto Mining Pool Communication from Client Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly cites 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Detection must key off command-and-control callbacks to mining pools (stratum protocol, port 3333/5555/9999).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound DNS queries or TCP connections to mining pool domains (mining.f2pool.com, antpool.com, ethermine.org, nanopool.io, mining.binance.com) from non-server endpoints. Include stratum protocol traffic patterns (JSON-RPC on alternate ports).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Minecraft Mod Download and Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain vector explicitly stated: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Attackers compromise or spoof Minecraft mod downloads from unauthorized sources; detection must chain download, extraction, and execution of malicious .jar files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .jar, .zip, .exe files from non-official Minecraft domains (exclude launcher.mojang.com, curseforge.com official CDN), followed by extraction to %appdata%\.minecraft\mods or game installation directory and subsequent .jar/exe execution.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Process Spawning Cryptominer Children
suggestion.rationale: Pirated Minecraft content executes embedded or downloaded crypto-mining payloads; javaw.exe (Minecraft JVM) should not spawn xmrig, claymore, or other mining tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when javaw.exe, minecraft-launcher.exe, or minecraft.exe creates child processes matching crypto-miner signatures (process name contains 'xmrig', 'claymore', 'ethminer', 'weedhack' family indicators, or has high CPU % sustained >15m).

suggestion.title: CountLoader Loader Process and Payload Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article names CountLoader as a discrete malware affecting '86K' hosts. Pipeline must detect CountLoader's process execution and secondary payload spawning (miners, info-stealers).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CountLoader execution by known hash signatures or behavioral pattern (unsigned PE spawning packed children, memory injection artifacts). Alert on command-line args indicative of unpacking or loader functionality.

suggestion.title: Weedhack Malware Initial Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Weedhack is the primary attack name in the article title; no detection hypothesis was generated. Must surface Weedhack process execution, registry/file persistence, and behavioral anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Weedhack process execution via hash/yara signature if available. Alert on writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or Startup folders linking to malicious mod directories. Monitor for parent-child process chains from game launchers.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Resource Consumption by Game Processes
suggestion.rationale: Pirated Minecraft with embedded miners will exhibit sustained high CPU/GPU/memory usage atypical of legitimate Minecraft gameplay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Minecraft/game-launcher processes consuming >70% CPU sustained for >15min, or GPU utilization spikes coinciding with mod load. Correlate with network traffic to mining pools for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Enumeration via Python or Scripting Engines
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' and 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks.' Pipeline missed primary attack objective despite explicit framework design discussion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe or powershell.exe with LDAP/ADSI query strings, Get-ADUser, Get-ADComputer, or adfind usage. Flag rapid sequences of directory queries from single process within <60s window. Correlate script parent (unusual paths or callers) with query targets (domain vs local scope).

suggestion.title: Telegram API Abuse for Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections.' No detection pattern for this infrastructure evasion technique despite novel threat-actor choice.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/S POST requests to api.telegram.org from non-browser processes (python, powershell, custom tools). Look for bot token patterns in query strings or POST bodies. Establish baseline of legitimate Telegram clients and flag anomalous usage from system accounts or scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' Core evasion technique of framework not represented in any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VirtualProtect + WriteProcessMemory sequences targeting legitimate executables (calc, notepad, explorer). Flag parent process anomalies (python, powershell spawning child processes) combined with cross-process memory writes. Alert on code caves or misaligned entry points in legitimate binary images.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Obfuscated Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables or DLLs intended to resist sandboxing, antivirus, and EDR detection.'
