No detection pattern for identifying heavily obfuscated/encrypted payloads characteristic of 80-module test corpus.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze executables for entropy >7.5 (encryption), packed stub markers, unusual section names, or invalid import tables. Flag execution of high-entropy binaries from user directories (Documents, temp). Correlate with EDR bypass toolkit signatures.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Communication with Custom Traffic Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' Customized traffic evasion not represented despite explicit framework component and victim indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/S traffic for beacon indicators masked as legitimate: predictable intervals (jitter analysis), high variance in User-Agent strings within single process, binary data in cookies/headers, DNS CNAME chains redirecting to C2. Detect Cobalt Strike JARM fingerprints and beacon metadata in traffic.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-Related Artifacts: Data Leak Site Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cobalt Strike operator logs of entries pointing to a ransom note and details on multiple organizations listed on a ransomware data leak site clarified that the framework was used for cybercrime operations.' No detection for HTTP requests to known leak sites or ransom-note staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/S requests from infected systems to known ransomware data leak sites (check OSINT feeds weekly). Monitor for ransom note file creation (.txt, .html, .bmp). Correlate leak-site visits with encryption activity and file staging in user directories.

suggestion.title: Beaconing to Legitimate Cloud Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'periodic outbound to small set of destinations' with beaconing signatures. Should detect C2 patterns against AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare IP ranges (T1071.001, T1071.004).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections to known cloud provider IP ranges with periodic timing pattern (30-600s intervals), low entropy in destination set, and consistency across multiple hosts. Filter out legitimate API calls by user-agent and certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Match — Installation Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article lists MD5 `1af33e1657631357c73119488045302c` as high-fidelity IOC but pipeline produced no file-matching hunt. Should detect file creation, process execution, or module load matching this hash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file creation, process execution, or DLL load with MD5 hash matching the provided IOC. Escalate if activity originates from cloud-hosted endpoint or occurs in suspicious directories.

suggestion.title: DNS-Over-HTTPS C2
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes abuse of Cloudflare and Google Cloud DNS services. T1071.004 (DNS protocol) suggests DNS tunneling over encrypted channels. Current beaconing hunt misses DNS-specific C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries to anomalous subdomains or high-entropy domain names, especially those resolving to Cloudflare or Google nameservers. Correlate with HTTPS traffic (port 443) that doesn't match certificate domains.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) listed but not operationalized into detection. Article describes malware hidden within cloud infrastructure traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process executions with encoded/base64 command-line arguments, unusual working directories, or parent-child relationships inconsistent with legitimate cloud tools (e.g., child of curl/wget/PowerShell executing obfuscated scripts).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated T3/IIOP Access to WebLogic Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit is 'remotely exploitable by threat actors with no privileges via T3, IIOP' protocols. No detection for network-layer protocol abuse to WebLogic ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for T3 (typically port 7001) and IIOP (typically port 9000) traffic to WebLogic endpoints from external or untrusted sources with no prior authentication session. Flag any sustained unauthenticated protocol handshake attempts.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server RCE Exploitation via CVE-2024-21182
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' as exploitation outcome. No detection for exploitation success indicators or post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic logs for ClassPathXmlApplicationContext or serialization gadget chain patterns; correlate with unexpected Java process spawns or shell command execution post-authentication-bypass. Flag if RCE indicators precede data queries on sensitive tables.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Access from Compromised WebLogic Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthorized access to critical data' and 'complete access to WebLogic accessible data' as impact. No detection for data exfiltration patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual volume of data queries or exports originating from WebLogic service accounts post-compromise. Flag if WebLogic process initiates outbound HTTPS/SFTP connections to external IPs not in allowlist, or if sensitive schema queries spike anomalously.

suggestion.title: Detection of Shodan-Enumerated Vulnerable WebLogic Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article cites '1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online, vulnerable to CVE-2024-21182' per Shodan. No proactive detection for internal assets matching vulnerable version signatures (12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for WebLogic Server instances with version 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 in network inventory. Cross-reference against patch calendar to confirm July 2024 or later patches applied. Alert on unpatched instances visible to external networks.

suggestion.title: Federal Agency WebLogic Patch Compliance Deadline Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA mandated 'patch by midnight June 4' via BOD 22-01. No use case for deadline-driven compliance monitoring or remediation verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track WebLogic patch deployments for CVE-2024-21182 with deadline of June 4 (BOD 22-01 mandated). Alert on federal agency assets still running vulnerable versions post-deadline. Verify patches via version checks and configuration audit trails.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Unpatched Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2022-0492 and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution. Federal due date 2026-06-05 establishes urgency. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear direction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unpatched Linux systems with CVE-2022-0492 present in vulnerability scanner results. Cross-reference against patch deployment timelines to identify systems with patch lag. Prioritize systems with external exposure.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release Agent Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact attack vector: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' Pipeline ignored this concrete exploitation path entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect write operations to cgroup v1 release_agent paths (typically /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent) from unprivileged contexts. Monitor for execution of arbitrary commands spawned via release_agent callback. Flag containers or user namespaces with direct cgroup filesystem access.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Cgroups v1 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes cgroups v1 release_agent vector which is a known container escape primitive. Pipeline failed to suggest container-specific detections for escape attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cross-namespace process execution initiated from containers. Alert on container processes spawning host-level system calls or accessing host cgroup hierarchy unexpectedly. Flag cgroups v1 usage in modern environments using cgroups v2.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Level Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'privilege escalation' but pipeline suggested no detection of the post-exploit state. Unprivileged process becoming root/kernel-level is high-fidelity signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate privilege transitions on Linux systems. Alert on anomalous uid/gid changes, especially unprivileged user → root or in-container process → host namespace privilege. Correlate with failed cgroups operations preceding success.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' substituting this CVE. Primary detection vector omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2025-48595 detections. Cross-correlate with patch deployment timelines. Flag unpatched Android Framework instances post-federal due date (2026-06-05) for escalation to compliance.

suggestion.title: Integer Overflow Exploitation Execution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'integer overflow vulnerability that allows for code execution' but pipeline supplied no execution-phase detection. OOB writes and heap corruption may leave forensic traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework process crash dumps for integer overflow signatures (heap corruption, stack smashing). Alert on SELinux denials from framework processes accessing unexpected memory regions. Correlate crashes with CVE-2025-48595 scanning results.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Local Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for local privilege escalation' but pipeline omitted privilege-escalation phase entirely. LPE represents critical post-exploitation detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uid/gid elevation syscalls (setuid, setgid, capset) from Android Framework or adjacent processes following memory-safety crashes. Flag capability escalation to CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: Federal Due Date 2026-06-05
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05' and 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Regulatory deadline tracking absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management systems for CVE-2025-48595 patch deployment across all Android Framework instances. Generate SLA report for unpatched assets as of 2026-06-05. Segment by federal contractor flag.

suggestion.title: Detect Brute-Force Attacks Against Dashlane Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack'—the primary attack vector. Pipeline should generate detections for rapid repeated failed authentications, which is both the attack mechanism and the first-stage indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag 5+ failed login attempts to Dashlane within 10 minutes from same source IP or user account. Brute-force tools exhibit retry patterns distinct from legitimate user behavior. Escalate alert if failed attempts are followed by successful login within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Detect Vault Download Following Successful Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—exfiltration phase. Pipeline missed detection for bulk password manager data retrieval post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers (50KB–50MB per user) from Dashlane API or client processes. Correlate successful login + vault download within 5 minutes from abnormal location/IP as high-confidence breach indicator.

suggestion.title: Detect Credentials Access from Password Manager Storage
suggestion.rationale: Dashlane is a password manager; downloaded 'encrypted vaults' means T1555.003 was executed. This MITRE technique directly applies but was not surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Host-based detection: processes accessing Dashlane vault files (%APPDATA%\Dashlane\*, ~/Library/Caches/Dashlane/*) or performing keychain/database queries on credential stores. Post-compromise indicator when paired with successful authentication from abnormal context.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Geographic Velocity in Dashlane Login Events
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies attacker-controlled authentication from non-user geography. Article implies 20 users compromised; geographic anomalies would be leading indicator of automated attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag user logins from IP ranges inconsistent with historical baseline (e.g., habitual US logins, sudden Eastern Europe origin). Escalate if same user logs in from 3+ distinct countries within 1 hour—indicative of successful brute-force followed by attacker exploration.

suggestion.title: WinRAR RCE Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Headline: 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR'—direct evidence of initial-access vector. No detection rule generated for WinRAR-based RCE or suspicious archive processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR (rar.exe, unrar.exe) spawning child processes with command-line execution (PowerShell, cmd, rundll32), particularly from %TEMP% or %AppData% directories. Alert on WinRAR loading unsigned or attacker-controlled DLLs. Detect archive extraction patterns consistent with malware delivery workflows.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel' as delivered payloads. Zero execution-phase detections generated despite malware families being clearly identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution matching GammaWorm or GammaSteel signatures: parent process WinRAR/explorer, file creation in extraction paths, registry modifications to RunOnce/CurrentVersion/Run, or network callbacks to known C2. Cross-reference against Gamaredon YARA rules and IOC feeds.

suggestion.title: Email-Delivered WinRAR Exploit (Phishing Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon historically delivers via email; article targets Ukraine (government/critical infrastructure). No phishing or email-attachment detection generated despite this being Gamaredon's primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email with RAR/RAR.exe attachments from external senders, especially spoofing Ukrainian government, utility, or defense entities. Correlate archived email samples with endpoint WinRAR execution within 5 minutes. Alert on multi-stage archives (RAR containing executables or Office docs).

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution Chain from RAR Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon malware is known to use PowerShell for post-exploitation execution. Article describes malware delivery but no scripting-based execution detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell spawned from WinRAR temp directories (%TEMP%\RAR*), or with Base64-encoded commands, or with suspicious parameters (-WindowStyle Hidden, -NoProfile, -NonInteractive). Alert on PS execution within 10 seconds of WinRAR completion.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery without any C2 detection. No network-based or DNS-based IOCs extracted despite Gamaredon being attributed to documented C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS/HTTP connections from WinRAR-infected hosts to known Gamaredon C2 domains (via threat feeds). Detect beaconing patterns: regular callback intervals, small request/response sizes, absence of legitimate protocol negotiation. Flag DNS queries to Gamaredon infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration (Ukraine-Targeted)
suggestion.rationale: Article context (Ukraine targeting) and Gamaredon's known objectives (data theft from government/critical infrastructure) imply collection/exfiltration phase. No detection rules generated for staging, archiving, or exfil activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large file copies to temp directories (staging), archive creation from sensitive paths (Documents, Desktop, shared drives), or bulk file access on network shares. Correlate with C2 exfiltration. Alert on unusual volumes from defense/critical infrastructure IP space targeting external hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-48595 is 'under limited, targeted exploitation'—a high-severity Android Framework zero-day allowing 'code execution and escalate privileges' on Android 14+. This is the primary IOC and attack vector; no detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework component for exploitation signatures tied to CVE-2025-48595: kernel memory access violations, unexpected capability grants to untrusted apps, Framework process crashes preceded by unusual system calls. Alert on these patterns on Android 14+ devices, especially high-profile/enterprise enrollments.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Critical Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the 'most severe' Framework flaw 'could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed'. Privilege escalation is the core attack outcome and should drive detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unexpected privilege transitions on Android 14+ devices, particularly unprivileged-to-privileged escalations. Monitor for SELinux policy violations originating from Framework or System components. Correlate rapid privilege escalations with preceding exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: Spyware Deployment Post-Zero-Day Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states that 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals'—exploits are post-exploitation vectors for spyware installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for installation of unsigned, sideloaded, or hidden applications on high-profile devices. Flag persistent background processes with network exfiltration patterns and C2 beaconing behavior on devices matching exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Display Component Exploitation (CVE-2026-21385)
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out a separate Qualcomm display zero-day 'under limited, targeted exploitation'. This is a distinct kernel-level attack surface referenced but not captured in threat intel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Qualcomm display driver subsystem (GPU, DPU) for memory access violations, driver crashes, and abnormal ioctl sequences. Alert on kernel panics or driver restarts preceded by suspicious graphics-related syscalls.

suggestion.title: Patch Lag Exposure for High-Risk Populations
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Google Pixel devices will receive these security updates immediately, other vendors will often take longer'—vendors' patch lag creates vulnerability window. High-profile targets (per nation-state targeting context) will remain exposed longest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track enrolled devices still running pre-2026-06-01 Android firmware after patch availability, prioritizing high-sensitivity accounts and VIP users. Flag devices with repeated multi-month patch lag—consistent with targeted attack infrastructure exploiting slow vendor rollout.

suggestion.title: Critical System Component Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists '18 critical vulnerabilities across System, Framework, and Qualcomm closed-source components' and identifies Framework as 'most severe'. Attackers may chain multiple criticals for defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid-sequence failures or exploits targeting System, Framework, and Qualcomm components in succession—signatures of multi-stage privilege-escalation chains. Alert when Framework or System component errors immediately precede unexpected capability grants.

suggestion.title: Android Critical Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states one flaw is 'actively exploited'; pipeline generated zero detections. Must monitor for exploitation signatures against patched CVEs—typically memory corruption, kernel module loading, or process privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal process execution, memory access violations, or kernel exploit patterns within seconds of suspicious app or system component loading. Correlate against CVE-specific indicators (shellcode signatures, gadget chains, ROP patterns).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation on Android Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'actively exploited' vulnerability; privilege escalation is the immediate post-exploitation objective. Pipeline surfaced no elevation-of-privilege detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for uid/gid transition from unprivileged app context to system/root, SELinux allow-rules violations, capabilities escalation (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE), or kernel module insertion.

suggestion.title: Malware Artifact Staging Post-Android Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies malware payload delivery; pipeline missed detections for persistence and artifact creation (dropped binaries, modified startup items, injected libraries).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file writes to /system/*, /vendor/*, or app-specific directories; unusual library injection into system processes; or modifications to init.rc / init.*.rc startup scripts.

suggestion.title: Android Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Actively exploited flaw most likely delivers functional malware payload; pipeline ignored network-based C2 detection despite high severity rating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual outbound connections from compromised Android to external servers, esp. non-standard ports, domains matching malware feed repos, or patterns consistent with mobile banking trojans/spyware.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Device Identification in Network Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states Google released patch for 124 flaws including one exploited; pipeline should generate detection for in-network vulnerable device versions (e.g., build numbers <June 2026 patch level).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference observed Android OS version/build number against Google Security Advisory; flag devices running Android versions matching known-vulnerable ranges or with build dates predating patch release.

suggestion.title: Suspicious System Service Hijacking on Android Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article refers to 'critical' flaw affecting system components; pipeline failed to suggest detection for compromised system services (common post-exploitation objective in mobile attacks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected spawning of system services (adbd, installd, mediaserver) with modified binary paths, injected parent processes, or network-accessible listeners on unexpected ports.

suggestion.title: Bulk Rewriting of Composer Package Repository Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—clear persistence mechanism. Pipeline missed detection rule for coordinated tag manipulation patterns in package registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk tag creation or modification events in Composer packages within compressed timeframes. Correlate git commit metadata (author, signature validity, timestamp) against known maintainer profiles. Flag tags introducing new post-install scripts or network callbacks without corresponding security announcements.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Credential Exfiltration via Package Lifecycle Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Title objective: 'Steal CI Secrets'. Attack leverages package installation hooks to extract CI environment variables. Pipeline surfaced zero credential-theft detection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update for post-install script execution exfiltrating CI environment variables (GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, deploy keys). Detect outbound connections from build environments to non-standard hosts during dependency resolution. Flag scripts containing base64-encoded payloads or credential-stealing patterns (env dumps, HTTP exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Repository Maintainer Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires repository access. Article indicates mass tag rewrites across 'multiple packages'—suggests account takeover or insider compromise. Pipeline omitted detection for anomalous maintainer behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package registry logins from geographically anomalous locations or rare IP ranges. Correlate successful authentication with bulk tag operations or file modifications. Flag mass publish events or version rollbacks deviating from historical maintainer patterns. Monitor for API token creation or permission escalation events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Package Installation Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'rewritten' packages indicates code modification. Supply chain attacks inject malicious logic into composer.json lifecycle scripts. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install/update executing scripts that spawn shell commands, make network calls, or access CI_* environment variables. Monitor for obfuscated payloads (base64, gzip), curl/wget to attacker infrastructure, or credential enumeration patterns. Flag scripts running outside expected package directories with elevated privilege context.

suggestion.title: Installation of Compromised Composer Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'every tag rewritten'—multiple malicious versions exist. Downstream users may inadvertently depend on poisoned releases. Pipeline lacked impact-phase detection for forced downgrades or version anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when composer.lock pins laravel-lang or related packages to versions predating last security update or diverging from latest stable. Correlate sudden version rollbacks with build anomalies or CI secret exfiltration events. Monitor for non-deterministic composer.lock changes across identical install commands.

suggestion.title: Non-Official Package Registry Mirror Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks sometimes redirect package resolution to attacker-controlled mirrors. Pipeline failed to detect repository spoofing or registry switching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json and global composer config for non-Packagist package sources or custom mirrors. Alert on DNS lookups for unofficial registry domains. Flag composer install attempts fetching packages from attacker-controlled IPs or domains. Cross-reference resolved package sources against known registry infrastructures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Clone or Bulk Code Export
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'securing code' across lifecycle. Implies threats of code theft or unauthorized access to repositories—a primary target in development supply chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume or anomalous Git clone, archive, or export operations from development repositories. Flag operations from unexpected accounts, IPs, or outside business hours; correlate with external data egress.

suggestion.title: Agent Framework Instantiation from Unexpected Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'securing agents' as pillar; Microsoft Agent 365 mentioned. Need detection for unauthorized agent spawning or hijacking, which represents execution and persistence in development environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on instantiation of agent frameworks (Microsoft Agent 365, LangChain, AutoGPT-style implementations) from unexpected parent processes, user contexts, or with suspicious parameter patterns (e.g., non-approved endpoints, credential injection).

suggestion.title: Model Artifact or Weight File Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'securing models' in development pipeline. Model poisoning is a critical threat vector during development and training phases that defenders must detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to model files (.onnx, .safetensors, .pt, .h5, .keras), training datasets, or ML artifact repositories outside of authorized CI/CD workflows. Flag modifications from unexpected user accounts or processes.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline or Build Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes securing 'across the development lifecycle,' including build stages. Supply chain attacks via pipeline configuration modification (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines) are a known escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to CI/CD configuration files, commits to protected branches bypassing approval workflows, unauthorized credential additions to pipeline environments, or changes to deployment approval chains.

suggestion.title: Development Service Principal Abuse Across Build Stages
suggestion.rationale: Development lifecycle security requires detection of lateral movement between build agents, artifact repositories, and staging environments using compromised service credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous cross-stage authentication by build service principals: token reuse, unexpected service-to-service calls, authentication to non-pipeline systems, or access to production infrastructure from build agents.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Review Bypass or Direct Push to Protected Branch
suggestion.rationale: Code integrity is central to 'securing code' across lifecycle. Attackers may attempt to bypass review controls to inject malicious changes into shipped code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits bypassing mandatory code review on protected branches, force-pushes to main/production branches, review dismissals from unexpected accounts, or modifications to branch protection rules.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Nx Console extension was compromised; expected supply-chain attack distributing malicious package versions to developer machines during compromise window
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/update, VS Code extension install, or package manager operations targeting Nx Console during known compromise date range. Alert on installation of version numbers matching advisory. Correlate with ProcessCreationEvents from code or npm CLIs.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from VS Code Extension Host
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension executes within VS Code ExtensionHost process; expected malicious code spawning shells for reconnaissance, exfiltration, or lateral movement
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh spawned as children of ExtensionHost.exe or node.exe running extension code. Flag unusual command-line arguments, encoded payloads, or suspicious binaries. Baseline legitimate Nx extension behavior first.

suggestion.title: Network Beaconing from VS Code Extension Process
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension code typically establishes command-and-control or exfiltration channels; monitor for unexpected outbound connections from extension runtime
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from ExtensionHost or Node.js processes to non-standard ports, newly-registered domains, or IPs with poor reputation. Baseline known Nx update servers and package registries to suppress FP.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Extension running under developer privileges has access to .ssh, .git credentials, npm tokens, and environment variables storing cloud API keys; expected exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads of ~/.ssh/*, ~/.git/*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/* by processes spawned from extension host. Flag cat/type/copy operations on credential files and environment variable access (env, printenv) outside normal editor workflow.

suggestion.title: Workspace Code Injection via Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: Extension with filesystem access can inject malicious code into developer projects, modify build configs, or plant backdoors in source trees
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk or rapid file write/modify operations within VS Code workspace directories (project roots, package.json locations) by child processes of extension host. Flag modifications to build files, package manifests, and source-code paths outside normal IDE edit patterns.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Account Compromise Indicator
suggestion.rationale: For supply-chain attacks on package repos, monitor account activity, release patterns, and version metadata anomalies on npm/NuGet during compromise window
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish, npm login, or package upload operations targeting Nx Console repository during suspected compromise dates. Cross-reference with known malicious version numbers from advisory. Alert on publish patterns inconsistent with normal release cadence.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Payload Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames Operation FlutterBridge as a 'malvertising campaign'—the initial access vector is poisoned ads from legitimate ad networks. Pipeline missed the entry point entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious executable downloads from ad network domains or CDN providers to macOS endpoints. Correlate unusual file types delivered from advertising infrastructure (DMG, PKG, ZIP containing Mach-O) with immediate process execution by browsers or system processes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Flutter Binary Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'FlutterShell backdoor, built using the Flutter framework'—novel malware likely lacks proper code signing/notarization. Detection must surface non-standard Flutter app execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned or invalid-signature Mach-O binaries embedding Flutter libraries. Alert on removal of com.apple.quarantine attributes, xattr manipulation, or Gatekeeper bypass patterns preceding Flutter process launch.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence via LaunchAgent
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell is described as a 'backdoor'—article implies persistent installation. Pipeline should surface LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon creation by suspicious processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of user-writable LaunchAgent plists (~/.local/share/LaunchAgents or ~/Library/LaunchAgents) by non-system processes. Detect plist entries referencing unsigned binaries, downloads folders, or /tmp paths. Correlate timing with malvertising ad clicks.

suggestion.title: Backdoor C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor functionality explicitly requires command-and-control communication. Pipeline failed to surface detection for outbound C2 traffic to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious outbound connections from unsigned or recently-executed Flutter processes to rare/non-standard ports or unusual domains. Detect periodic beaconing patterns (5-60s intervals) to infrastructure associated with FlutterShell samples.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise System Discovery Commands
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor access implies reconnaissance phase. Article emphasizes shell capability—typical first-stage post-exploitation spawns system enumeration commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid-fire execution of system profiling commands (system_profiler, uname, sw_vers, ifconfig, id) from the backdoor process or shell spawned by it. Flag multi-command enumeration within <30s window post-infection.

suggestion.title: macOS Ad-Targeting Malware Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Operation FlutterBridge specifically targets macOS via ad ecosystem—detection should identify the cross-domain pattern of ad-click → malware delivery → backdoor execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequence: (1) network request to ad/marketing domain from browser, (2) redirect to attacker CDN or malvertiser, (3) download of executable (DMG/PKG), (4) user execution, (5) outbound C2. Multi-event correlation reduces FP from legitimate ad traffic.

suggestion.title: WeedHack JAR execution from suspicious domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'distributed through Minecraft-related malicious mods, clients, cheats, and utilities' via '240 distribution URLs' and '3,820 unique malicious JAR files.' No detection for abnormal JAR sourcing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JAR file execution originating from domains not matching official Minecraft client GitHub repos (Meteor, Wurst, Impact, LiquidBounce official sources). Flag child process spawns from Java/javaw.exe with CLR/COM abuse patterns. Correlate with downloads from domains containing impersonated client names.

suggestion.title: Minecraft session token and browser credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets Minecraft session ID theft, cookies, and saved passwords across 36 browsers, 56 cryptocurrency add-ons, 12 desktop cryptocurrency wallet apps, Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials.' No detections for credential store enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JAR-spawned processes accessing credential stores: Minecraft launcher config (%appdata%\Roaming\.minecraft), browser local storage/SQLite DBs, crypto wallet app directories. Detect process handle opens to LSASS or credential manager from Java child processes. Alert on bulk file access to AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data after JAR execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Minecraft mod impersonation via fake security warnings
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious website displays a security notice warning visitors...only download Skytils from official site' while hosting malware. Represents T1036.005 masquerading with social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads from domains with typosquatted or near-legitimate names of Minecraft client projects (Meteor, Wurst, Impact). Cross-check downloaded JAR signatures against known good from official GitHub releases. Alert if JAR comes from domain showing legitimate GitHub/Discord links but serves different binary.

suggestion.title: WeedHack premium tier remote access activation (webcam, keylogger, shell)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'premium tier...remote control with input access (mouse and keyboard), webcam access, keylogger, remote shell, and remote file management.' No detections for these advanced capabilities post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-JAR execution, detect: (1) unusual process accessing camera/webcam drivers (WinRT Camera, MediaFoundation); (2) cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as child of Java process; (3) new registry entries in HKCU\Software with suspicious scheduled tasks; (4) input hook DLL injection into Java processes.

suggestion.title: SEO poisoning landing page downloads of WeedHack malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SEO poisoning distribution method targets keywords...Meteor Client, Radium Client, Wurst Client...McAfee explains that many of those projects do not have official websites, only GitHub pages.' No detections for SEO-poisoned domain traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP GETs for domains with keyword patterns matching known Minecraft client names where legitimate projects only have GitHub repos. Flag domains registered recently (< 6 months) that rank high in search results for these keywords. Detect JAR downloads from search-engine-referring traffic with no prior user interaction history.

suggestion.title: YouTube malicious link promotion in video descriptions and comments
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'reaches victims mainly through YouTube videos...attacker drops download links in descriptions and comments. Some videos are well-made...have accumulated more than 7,500 views.' Distribution vector not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP referrer chains from youtube.com to suspicious JAR download domains. Alert if user clicks link in YouTube video description/comments and downloads executable. Cross-reference with known malware distribution domains. Monitor for patterns of multiple users clicking same malicious YouTube links within short time window.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution and Child Process Tree
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Xeno RAT' as the delivered payload. No detection use case for RAT execution patterns. Phrase: 'Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Xeno RAT process spawning or reconnaissance commands (whoami, systeminfo, tasklist, ipconfig) immediately post-execution. Look for parent-child process relationships where a non-standard parent (e.g., msiexec, rundll32, Office process) launches a process with RAT-like behavior (network connections, file enumeration).

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Beacon and Network Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article implies delivery of a remote access trojan but no detection for C2 communication. Expected communication to attacker infrastructure. Phrase: 'Xeno RAT' as deployed malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Finance Ministry hosts to non-whitelisted external IP addresses or domains, especially over HTTP/HTTPS and non-standard ports. Flag DNS lookups to unusual domains immediately after suspicious process execution. Alert on repeated connection attempts to single external IP from multiple internal hosts (lateral movement via RAT).

suggestion.title: Phishing Attachment with Xeno RAT Payload
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy is known for spearphishing campaigns; article targets Finance Ministry suggesting email-based initial access. Phrase: 'SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry'—SideCopy historically uses phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with .exe, .scr, .bat, .cmd, .zip, .rar, or .ps1 attachments sent to Finance Ministry staff. Correlate with sender reputation, domain spoofing attempts (look for Pakistan-based infrastructure or similar TLDs). Monitor for attachment execution by endpoints shortly after email receipt.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT System Reconnaissance Commands
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically execute discovery commands post-execution; no detection for Xeno-specific reconnaissance. Article indicates targeted access to Finance Ministry system data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of native Windows reconnaissance tools (whoami, systeminfo, tasklist, net user, net group, dir, wmic logicaldisk) within 1-5 minutes after Xeno RAT execution. Flag sequences of these commands from a single process tree as lateral movement or privilege escalation probing.

suggestion.title: Finance Ministry Data Exfiltration via RAT
suggestion.rationale: Target is Finance Ministry, implying sensitive financial/operational data at risk. No detection for data collection or exfiltration patterns. Phrase: 'Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file operations (copies, archives, reads) targeting Finance Ministry-specific directories (payroll, budgets, contracts) initiated by RAT-spawned processes. Correlate with egress network traffic (high byte volume to external C2). Alert on unusual file compression (7z, rar, zip) of sensitive documents.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Behavioral Indicators: Registry Persistence and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy is known for registry-based persistence and remote desktop abuse. No detection for lateral movement or persistence mechanisms. Phrase: 'Pakistan-Linked SideCopy'—actor-specific TTPs missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry writes to Run, RunOnce, or ScheduledTask keys from Xeno RAT process or child processes. Flag RDP connection attempts (port 3389) or PsExec-like lateral movement (ADMIN$ share access, service creation) originating from compromised Finance Ministry host to other internal systems.

suggestion.title: Maven/Gradle Dependency Resolution - jqwik-engine 1.10.0 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names affected package 'net.jqwik:jqwik-engine' version '1.10.0'. States 'Any project that pulled net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at 1.10.0, directly or transitively' was impacted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Maven Central and Gradle dependency resolution for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at version 1.10.0. Alert on pom.xml, gradle.build, or lockfile entries matching this package-version pair. Check Maven local cache and CI build logs for resolution of 1.10.0.

suggestion.title: ANSI Erase Code Sequences in CI/Test Output Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice' to hide from terminals but remain in logs. Specifies 'ESC is the control byte 0x1B', '[2K means erase the entire current line', 'CR sends the cursor back to column zero'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search CI/CD logs for sequence ESC[2K (hex 0x1B5B324B) combined with carriage returns (0x0D) in proximity to test execution output. Anomalous in raw logs; indicates intentional line hiding. Cross-reference with decompiled JAR inspection for printMessageForCodingAgents method.

suggestion.title: JVM Bytecode Inspection - printMessageForCodingAgents Method Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malicious code in 'a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents(), inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class'. Recommends 'decompile the 1.10.0 JAR. The printMessageForCodingAgents() calls in JqwikExecutor are right there.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decompile net.jqwik:jqwik-engine:1.10.0 JAR files in build artifacts. Detect method 'printMessageForCodingAgents' in class 'net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor'. Compare bytecode signature against 1.10.1 baseline to establish maliciousness.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Prompt Injection Payload - Disregard Instructions + Delete Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article documents payload 'told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' Recommends 'Grep your CI and IDE logs for the phrase about disregarding instructions and deleting jqwik tests and code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI coding agent logs (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot agent, Cursor) for phrases matching 'disregard.*instruction' and 'delete.*jqwik.*test' appearing in same context. Alert when these phrases appear in raw test output fed to agents. Correlate with jqwik 1.10.0 dependency detection.

suggestion.title: SHA-256 Hash Validation for jqwik-engine 1.10.0 JAR Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides detection method 'Check suspect JARs against the SHA-256 above' with specific hash value. Enables artifact-level detection independent of version metadata or string-based identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compute SHA-256 of jqwik-engine JAR files in build artifacts and Maven local repositories. Alert on match to known-malicious 1.10.0 release hash. Validate against Snyk advisory database and Maven Central official checksums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Bulk File Deletion Following Test Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of potential impact 'losing your source and test files with no useful audit trail' if agent follows injected instruction. Documents destructive payload intent: 'delete all jqwik tests and code'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate jqwik test execution (mvn test, gradle test, mvn clean test) with subsequent bulk file deletion operations. Alert on rm -rf or del /s commands targeting .java or test-related files following jqwik 1.10.0 test runs, especially if spawned by CI/agent process.

suggestion.title: JavaScript execution via npm preinstall hook spawning child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install' — core execution vector not operationalized. No hunt exists for the preinstall script execution pattern itself despite T1546.016 being listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by npm, yarn, pnpm, or node during package install phase where parent command contains 'preinstall' or 'prepare' lifecycle hook. Correlate with unexpected JavaScript execution from node_modules/.bin or package installation directories.

suggestion.title: Credential environment variable enumeration by JavaScript runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, CircleCI' — no hunt operationalizes detection of this credential access despite T1552.001, T1552.005, T1528 being listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node/JavaScript process arguments and child spawns for patterns matching environment variable harvesting: process_command_line contains GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GCP_*, VAULT_ADDR, npm_* or spawns of env, printenv, or sh -c with variable expansion. Alert on variable exfiltration to HTTP/DNS destinations.

suggestion.title: Outbound credential exfiltration from npm install process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multi-stage' harvester implying command-and-control or exfiltration phase, but kill-chain reconstruction is empty and no UC detects credential data leaving the host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node initiating unexpected HTTP POST or DNS queries to external hosts during package installation window. Flag requests with high-entropy payloads or API patterns suggesting credential dumps. Correlate with known malicious infrastructure or private IP ranges accessing public internet.

suggestion.title: Clustered installation of @redhat-cloud-services packages across multiple hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'multiple packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope' compromised. UC_20_7 detects single-host installs; need fleet-wide aggregation to detect incident response or uncontrolled blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate npm installs of @redhat-cloud-services/* across all hosts. Alert when 5+ distinct @redhat-cloud-services packages installed on same host within 30 minutes, or when >10 hosts install any @redhat-cloud-services/* within 1 hour window.

suggestion.title: Obfuscation patterns in npm preinstall script content
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sophisticated multi-stage' payload that 'fire[s] via a preinstall hook' — behavioral detection of obfuscated script content before execution. Article notes T1027 (Obfuscation) but no hunt operationalizes content analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json preinstall field and .npmrc scripts for hallmarks of obfuscation: base64-encoded blocks, eval/Function constructor usage, atob/btoa calls, binary-like entropy spikes, or hex-encoded strings. Flag preinstall scripts with content entropy >6.5 bits per byte.

suggestion.title: npm Install with Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'payload' and article describes multi-stage attacks in npm. Post-install scripts are the execution vector for npm worms and credential harvesters (inherent to npm attack model but not surfaced by pipeline).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/yarn package manager spawning child processes (node, bash, powershell) during install phase. Wormable npm attacks execute post-install scripts; correlate process trees npm → subshell → network calls or file writes to %APPDATA% or .npm cache directories.

suggestion.title: npm Package Dependency Tree Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'supply chain' attacks and 'worm propagation' in npm ecosystem. Pipeline missed the detection for typosquatting and legitimate package masquerading variants that define npm supply chain risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json and lock files for version mismatches, published-to-resolved gaps, and packages fetched from registries other than npm.js. Correlate package install events against baseline dependency trees.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Description explicitly mentions 'CI/CD persistence' as a post-Shai Hulud attack vector. Pipeline produced no use cases for detecting malicious npm packages in CI runners that establish persistence across builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm package installations in CI/CD contexts (GitHub Actions runners, Azure DevOps agents, Jenkins agents). Flag packages with new or modified preinstall/postinstall/prepare scripts; correlate with subsequent cron additions, ~/.bashrc modifications, or ssh key generation in CI job context.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via npm Preinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'Credential Harvesting' and 'obfuscation'. Malicious npm packages exfiltrate environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, GitHub tokens) during install via hooks. Pipeline surface no specific detection for this common npm attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl/wget/powershell spawned during npm install phases exfiltrating to external domains. Monitor for base64-encoded environment variable exfiltration, particularly npm tokens and cloud credentials, sent to attacker C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code in npm Package Manifests
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly cite 'obfuscation' as an npm malware characteristic. Pipeline produced no detection for identifying obfuscated JavaScript payloads (UglifyJS, base64 encoding) embedded in package.json scripts or build tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect package.json 'scripts' field and extracted tarball contents for obfuscation markers: excessive unicode escapes, base64 blobs in script fields, suspicious npm-cli-login patterns. Flag packages where source entropy or byte patterns indicate obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: npm Worm Self-Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords and description emphasize 'worm propagation' in npm supply chain. Pipeline missed detection for compromised packages modifying package.json or lock files to inject themselves as dependencies in downstream projects, enabling auto-propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to package.json, package-lock.json, or .npmrc during npm execution. Detect package installation steps that append new dependencies or modify dependency versions. Correlate with subsequent package publishes by developer accounts.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'device code phishing, which abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild.' This is a named, quantified, and active attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth device code grant flows in sign-in logs, especially those without matching corporate device registration or from unexpected geolocations. Alert on successful device code auth immediately followed by token refresh, unusual OAuth app consent, or MFA bypass indicators. Monitor for clusters of device code attempts across multiple user accounts within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Shadow AI Tool File Exfiltration (Non-Corporate Account)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Of file uploads to AI tools, 38% are made from personal shadow accounts rather than organizational ones' and '67% using non-corporate accounts.' Explicitly quantified exfiltration behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud app activity for file uploads to public AI services (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) when accessed via personal accounts on corporate devices. Correlate with clipboard paste events and document classification to infer sensitive data exfiltration. Flag accounts showing patterns of data staging and upload to out-of-policy services.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Search-Result Malvertising Click-Through
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'ClickFix is an even clearer example, where 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results' with 'InstallFix and ConsentFix' variants. Specific delivery mechanism and family variants named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect search-engine-referred clicks that land on suspicious clone pages or malware-hosting domains. Flag on rapid sequential clicks to search results followed by executable download prompts, browser overlay consent dialogs, or JavaScript `document.write()` calls. Correlate referrer (search) with landing domain reputation.

suggestion.title: LLMShare Legitimate AI Link Abuse Malvertising
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers were malvertising the links via search engine ads... using legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL.' Technique leverages legitimate AI infrastructure as delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search engine referrals to known AI chat sharing domains (chat.openai.com/share, etc.) that contain embedded malicious shared chats or redirect chains. Detect via TLS inspection of shared chat content or inspection of secondary HTTP redirects from within the shared context. Flag if shared chat contains malicious prompt injection or credential harvesting mechanics.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI Browser Extension Installation & Context Exfil
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.' Explicitly identified as unmonitored exfiltration vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of AI-labeled or AI-related browser extensions with high outbound network volume. Correlate extension network activity with browsing history (visits to internal apps, cloud services) to infer context exfiltration. Flag if extension uploads high-entropy or structured data to external hosts not on allow-list.

suggestion.title: Doko's Panel / ShinyHunters / BlackFile AitM Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names: 'Doko's Panel and derivative kits, used extensively by ShinyHunters and BlackFile.' These are attributed, tracked threat actors with named tooling producing industrialized account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious TLS certificates on common SaaS/OAuth domains or unusual reverse-proxy patterns indicative of AitM phishing kits. Detect via certificate pinning violations, mismatched TLS issuer chains, or re-submission of credentials within a single session. Alert on IPs/ASNs known to host derivative Doko panels or ShinyHunters infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Steam Profile C2 Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hiding command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments' and 'turning a popular gaming platform into a covert control channel'—detection must target HTTP/HTTPS connections to steamcommunity.com/profiles or /id/ endpoints with parsing of response bodies for command injection patterns, not just connection frequency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections to steamcommunity.com/profiles/* or steamcommunity.com/id/* URLs originating from WordPress servers, particularly with response payloads containing command-like syntax (base64, hex, script fragments). Correlate to malware execution events on same host.

suggestion.title: WordPress Malware Execution Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware campaign targeting WordPress websites'—but no detection for the infection/execution phase itself. Pipeline missed T1189 (Service Exploitation) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WordPress child process spawning (apache/nginx → php → cmd.exe/bash), suspicious file modifications under /wp-content/, /wp-plugins/, or wp-config.php, or PHP eval() execution triggered from web requests. Correlate with outbound connections to hello-mywordl.info.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Registration Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'hello-mywordl.info' as malware C2 infrastructure. Pipeline must link domain registration timestamps/registrar patterns to WordPress malware campaigns and track first-contact with infected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new domain registrations matching patterns of malware C2 infrastructure (typosquatted domains, newly registered with generic registrars, bulk registration with identical privacy settings). Correlate to compromised WordPress site IPs within 7 days of registration.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from WordPress Admin
suggestion.rationale: Article implies data exfiltration via malware but does not specify mechanism. Common WordPress malware pattern is stealing admin credentials or database access. Pipeline should infer T1110 (Brute Force) or T1040 (Sniffing) variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed WordPress login attempts from single source IP followed by successful auth; or detection of database.php access patterns indicating credential exfiltration; or wp-admin POST requests with suspicious parameters typical of credential-stealing plugins.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking Registry Modification for InprocServer32
suggestion.rationale: The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in, effectively allowing the malware to run at startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications to HKLM/HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 where data points to non-System32 locations. Correlate with DLL load events and logon timing to identify startup persistence.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from Injected DLL
suggestion.rationale: natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded. The PowerShell script performs basic checks for controlled environments before downloading Stage 2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell invocation with Base64-encoded parameters from DLL parent process or game directory context. Include query for WMI/registry sandbox detection patterns in script content.

suggestion.title: Modified FFmpeg DLL with Malicious Native Import
suggestion.rationale: Modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) imported the DllGetClassObject function from natives2_blob.bin. The legitimate game requires ffmpeg.dll to run, guaranteeing execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FFmpeg.dll file hash mismatch against known-good versions. Flag DLL import of suspicious .bin files (natives2_blob) from game process. Correlate with abnormal child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment Enumeration Before Malware Activation
suggestion.rationale: The Stage1 PowerShell script performs basic checks for controlled environments before the implant downloads the Stage 2 Trojan, indicating sandbox evasion logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell queries to WMI classes (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BaseBoard) or registry paths (VirtualBox, VMware, Xen) before outbound network activity. Temporal gap between execution and first C2 suggests evasion delays.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Download Several Days After Initial Infection
suggestion.rationale: After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities. Clear two-stage attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executable downloads from persistent process (InprocServer32 context) after multi-day lag. Flag outbound connections from logon-triggered DLL execution; correlate absence of user action with network I/O.

suggestion.title: Hentai Game Archive Distribution via File-Sharing Services
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized games distributed via PixelDrain file transfer service and torrent trackers (AniRena). Archives contained legitimate game files alongside malicious DLLs, blending payload with legitimate content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on downloads from known adult file-sharing infrastructure (PixelDrain, AniRena) of game archives. Post-extraction, scan for natives2_blob.bin or hash mismatch on bundled ffmpeg.dll.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'preinstall' attack vector; article describes malicious scripts executing during package installation. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node processes spawning shells (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) or curl/wget during package install phases. Preinstall scripts should have limited process spawning; flag deviations from baseline npm install behavior.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—credential access is core objective but zero CA-phase detections exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes accessing ~/.git, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.ssh, HKEY_CURRENT_USER registry hives during package installation. Timestamp correlation with preinstall execution and credential exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Republishing Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack spreading 'like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—persistence and lateral-movement via supply-chain injection. Zero detections for abnormal package registry activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish/push API calls to registries from CI/CD or developer environments. Flag version bumps on established packages with minimal deltas, re-publishes from new accounts, or registry authentication from unusual locations.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secret Exfiltration via npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'silently infects CI/CD environments'—no detections for env-var harvesting in CI/CD context where secrets are injected by build systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD pipelines, detect npm/node processes accessing GITHUB_TOKEN, CI_COMMIT_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CREDENTIALS, or other injected secrets, followed by unexpected outbound HTTPS connections.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Republishing malicious packages requires stolen npm auth credentials. Article implies token exfiltration but pipeline captured zero credential-access detections for .npmrc files or npm auth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to ~/.npmrc, in-memory reads of npm_authtoken or _authToken from npm config, and processes enumerating npm registry credentials. Correlate with subsequent npm publish operations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal package.json/lock File Modification During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like spreading implies package manifest manipulation. Pipeline should detect preinstall/postinstall scripts modifying dependency files—a clear supply-chain escalation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock occurring during npm install phases. Detect when installation scripts alter manifests, add transitive dependencies, or change registry URLs.

suggestion.title: Forced NTLM Authentication via Malicious URI Scheme
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' via URI—classic forced-auth pattern. Pipeline missed T1187 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Search (searchindexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) initiating outbound connections to non-Microsoft hosts or making unauthenticated NTLM requests to unexpected shares/IPs. Alert on credential submission events tied to URI-handler invocations, especially if followed by NTLM Type-2/Type-3 exchanges over port 445 or 139.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Process Accessing Malicious UNC Paths
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerability likely triggers Windows Search to access attacker-controlled UNC paths (\\attacker-ip\share). Article mentions 'URI Vulnerability' but pipeline identified no file-access baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows Search processes (searchindexer.exe, Windows.Search.exe) connecting to unknown or untrusted UNC paths, especially paths with high entropy names or IPs outside internal ranges. Baseline normal Search Index locations and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: NTLM Relay Attack from Windows Search Context
suggestion.rationale: NTLMv2 hash capture is a pre-cursor to relay attacks (T1557.002). Pipeline did not surface lateral-movement or C2 follow-on implications.
log_sources: SecurityEvent (4624: Logon, 4625: Failed Logon with NTLM)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If captured NTLMv2 hashes are relayed, watch for: (1) NTLM authentication from unexpected source IPs tied to Windows Search machine, (2) lateral logons using accounts that don't normally traverse network paths, (3) repeated NTLM auth attempts to multiple targets in short window (SMB relay footprint).

suggestion.title: Process Hooking / Handler Registration for URI Schemes
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'URI Vulnerability'—attacker likely registers malicious handler or triggers Search to parse specially-crafted URI. No detection for handler manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\URL Handlers and HKCU equivalents for new or suspicious URI scheme registrations. Alert on handler commands pointing to writable paths, LOLBins, or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Credential Material in Windows Search Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is hash theft—hashes may be cached in Search index, temp files, or event logs. Pipeline missed data-at-rest detection angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Windows Search index and temporary directories for plaintext or weakly-encoded NTLM hashes, UNC paths with credentials, or auth material. Compare captured hashes against known corporate password lists to gauge breach scope.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from searchindexer.exe
suggestion.rationale: Exploited vulnerability may achieve RCE through Windows Search. Article doesn't rule out code execution; pipeline ignored execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by searchindexer.exe, Windows.Search.exe, or SearchProtocolHost.exe—especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, or outbound-capable tools. Baseline normal child processes and treat deviations with suspicion.

suggestion.title: Phishing to github.dev Exploitation Landing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers to steal GitHub authentication tokens by tricking users into clicking a link' — initial vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails/messages with github.dev URLs or redirect chains to github.dev. Alert on github.dev access from users without recent GitHub repository interaction history or from geographies inconsistent with baseline.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Simulation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension' — core execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension installations triggered shortly after postMessage() calls from webview contexts or untrusted origins. Alert when extensions install to %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions without preceding user consent dialogs or when installation follows synthetic input event sequences.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev...the token...has full access to every other repo that you have access to' — describes token interception and scope abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests from Chromium/VS Code processes to github.com/github.dev containing Authorization headers or bearer tokens. Alert on unscoped or full-scope GitHub tokens transmitted to unexpected destinations immediately after webview activity.

suggestion.title: GitHub Private Repository Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access' — post-compromise discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls to /user/repos, /user/installations endpoints from new source IPs or user-agents. Alert on bulk repository enumeration within short timeframes using full-scope tokens, especially from unexpected geographies.

suggestion.title: Synthetic Keypress Injection from Webview Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses' — technique abuses webview-to-parent process communication for input spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for postMessage() API calls from webview frames sending synthetic keyboard/mouse event payloads to parent VS Code process. Alert when keystroke sequences match known UI navigation patterns (extension installation, authentication).

suggestion.title: github.dev Cookie/Token Persistence Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev' is the recommended mitigation, indicating tokens stored in clearable browser storage despite sensitivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code or Chromium processes accessing browser cookie/localStorage directories for github.com/github.dev domains. Alert on reads of sensitive storage locations from JavaScript contexts or unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' as impact—miners generate detectable process creation, resource exhaustion, and C2 patterns; pipeline generated zero mining-related detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events associated with known cryptocurrency miner families (xmrig, monero miners, etc.) spawned from Minecraft or user-writable directories. Correlate with sustained high CPU usage (>80%) and network egress to mining pool IPs. Flag any Minecraft process spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Pirated Content Download and Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial access as 'Spread via Pirated Content'—should detect suspicious file sources (torrent, warez sites, forums) followed by execution; pipeline provided no initial-access or execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads from known piracy hosting/torrent infrastructure followed within 10 minutes by execution of downloaded files. Monitor for Minecraft mod installers or 'game cracks' downloaded to AppData or Downloads, then immediately executed. Alert on parent-child relationships where browser spawns unsigned executable with randomized name.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headlines 'CountLoader Hits 86K'—a named malware family; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or signatures; should include file hash, registry, process-name, and C2-domain patterns for CountLoader specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create malware artifact catalog for CountLoader: file names, mutation signatures, registry run-keys, mutex names, C2 domains/IPs. Hunt for process trees where CountLoader downloader creates child processes (miners, backdoors). Cross-reference file hashes against public AVs and sandbox detonations to identify variants. Escalate any direct hits or behavioral near-matches.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Process Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'—pirated mods or compromised launcher; should detect anomalous Minecraft process behavior (unexpected network egress, child processes, parent process mismatches).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when javaw.exe (Minecraft launcher) initiates outbound connections to non-Mojang IPs, spawns non-Java children (powershell, cmd, miner executables), or reads/modifies registry outside game directories. Baseline Minecraft network behavior per user; flag deviations. Monitor for modified game JAR files with suspicious embedded libraries.

suggestion.title: Mining Pool Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Miners exfiltrate value via mining pools; article implies C2/mining-pool communication but pipeline generated no network detection; should flag connections to known Monero/Bitcoin mining pools by IP/domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of known Monero and Bitcoin mining pool FQDN/IP ranges (pools.supportxmr.com, etc.). Alert on any process (especially from Minecraft directory or launched by unprivileged user) connecting to mining pools. Correlate with sustained egress volume and DNS requests to mining-pool infrastructure. Exclude corporate mining operations via allow-list.

suggestion.title: Launcher/Installer Tampering via Compromised Pirated Distributors
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malware packaged in fake or compromised Minecraft installers; should detect file-replacement, directory-traversal, or supply-chain poisoning indicators in game launcher/mod directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Minecraft installation directories (.minecraft, game launcher paths) for unexpected file modifications, new DLLs, or INI/config tampering. Alert on game launcher modifications that alter CLASSPATH, JVM args, or spawn wrapper processes. Detect when game shortcut or launcher registry entry points to non-standard executable or contains malicious parameters.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Pipeline extracted zero C2-related use cases.
