suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes initiating HTTPS POST requests to api.telegram.org with bot tokens or chat identifiers. Flag unusual parent processes (Python, Go, Rust binaries) making Telegram API calls, especially with repeated beacon intervals or large serialized data in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Front-End Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' Proxy-layer C2 infrastructure was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect C2 beacon patterns through workers.dev or Cloudflare-proxied domains: repeated POST/GET requests at regular intervals, characteristic request/response sizes, or anomalous data volume for legitimate Cloudflare use.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Reconnaissance via Staged Agent Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'an automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.' Iterative reconnaissance pattern was not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire LDAP queries or PowerShell Get-AD* commands in sequence (Users → Groups → Computers → SPNs), especially when interspersed with pauses suggesting remote task coordination. Flag bulk enumeration of domain admins, service accounts, and cross-forest trusts.

suggestion.title: Python Payload Generator Spawning Rust/Go Obfuscated Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a Python tool that generates payloads, mostly in Rust and Go' and 'Close to 80 modules were generated and tested.' Parent-child process pattern (Python → compiled binary) was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes spawning Rust or Go compiled binaries, particularly from non-standard locations (temp dirs, user profiles). Monitor for unusual argument patterns, absence of expected command-line flags, or execution following file-write activity in the same directory.

suggestion.title: EDR Product Detection and Conditional Payload Selection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malware 'tested in virtual environments against EDR tools from Sophos, CrowdStrike, and Microsoft' with framework agents for 'testing' and 'OPSEC hardening.' Detection-aware evasion logic was not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process queries of running services/drivers tied to Sophos/CrowdStrike/Defender (WmiPrvSE checking for SophosED.exe, falcon-sensor, or Sense.exe). Detect branching execution logic: processes that load different modules or DLLs conditionally based on EDR product detection.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Binaries via Python
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' Process hollowing / code injection pattern was not surfaced as a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes calling VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, or SetThreadContext on legitimate system binaries (calc.exe, notepad.exe, explorer.exe). Flag legitimate executables spawned with empty or minimal command-line arguments when they normally require options.

suggestion.title: C2 traffic from AWS/Google Cloud/Azure/Cloudflare IP space
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Cloudflare, and GitHub, to camouflage malicious traffic, evade detection, and sustain long-lived Command and Control.' This is the primary attack vector. No UC addresses C2 from legitimate cloud provider ASNs and IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from endpoints to AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and Cloudflare IP CIDR blocks with C2 indicators: small payloads, periodic intervals, anomalous ports for the provider. Baseline legitimate cloud API traffic first.

suggestion.title: DNS exfiltration via cloud DNS services
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1071.004 (DNS) as attack technique. Explicitly mentions DNS abuse through trusted cloud providers for command and control. No DNS-specific UC exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries with high-entropy domain labels, large TXT/NULL record payloads, or rapid sequential queries targeting AWS Route53, Google Cloud DNS, or Cloudflare DNS endpoints. Decode attempts should trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: HTTPS C2 via CDN/cloud proxy masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1071.001 (Web Protocols) combined with Cloudflare/AWS abuse. Attackers proxy C2 through CDNs to appear legitimate. No UC addresses this channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to Cloudflare, CloudFront, or Azure CDN with C2 signal: small payloads, regular timing, unusual URI paths, mismatched SNI/certificate issuer, or certificate pinning anomalies.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated payload delivery via cloud infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and emphasizes cloud services as delivery channel. No UC addresses obfuscated content flowing through AWS/Google Cloud/Cloudflare IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads originating from AWS/Google Cloud/Azure/Cloudflare IPs with obfuscation markers: high entropy, known packer signatures, Base64-encoded streams, or suspicious MIME type mismatches. Correlate with process execution of decoded content.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts on Oracle WebLogic T3 Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2024-21182 is exploitable 'via T3, IIOP' protocols and is 'actively exploited in attacks.' Pipeline generated no detection for this explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious T3 protocol handshakes or malformed T3 packets targeting port 7001 or non-standard WebLogic ports. Baseline legitimate WebLogic-to-WebLogic T3 communication and alert on unauthenticated clients establishing T3 streams.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed Oracle WebLogic Server Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Shodan now tracks over 1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online' and identifies specific vulnerable versions (12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0). Pipeline missed inventory monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly accessible Oracle WebLogic instances via port scanning telemetry, cloud security posture tools, or version fingerprinting. Correlate with Shodan/Censys data to surface unexpectedly exposed WebLogic services; flag vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0 for urgent remediation.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Oracle WebLogic Admin Console

suggestion.title: Monitor for CVE-2024-21182 Specific Exploitation Signatures

Monitor for known PoC payloads or characteristic bytecode sequences in network captures; correlate IDS alerts with WebLogic process injection or child-process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Compromise Data Access on Compromised WebLogic Instances

suggestion.title: Detect Reconnaissance Scanning for Vulnerable WebLogic Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Shodan scanning as the reconnaissance vector ('Shodan now tracks over 1,592 instances'). Pipeline failed to create detection for version-enumeration or banner-grabbing attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: CVE-2022-0492 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution and federal due date 2026-06-05. Pipeline should have generated patch-compliance UC for vulnerability scanners and asset management logs.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Unauthorized Manipulation

suggestion.title: Kernel Privilege Escalation to Root from Unprivileged Context

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation: Integer Overflow Post-Exploitation

suggestion.title: Brute-force attack against password manager accounts

suggestion.title: Bulk encrypted vault download from compromised password manager session

suggestion.title: WinRAR Remote Code Execution Exploitation

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation from Compromised Tag

suggestion.title: CI Secret Exfiltration via Composer Hook Execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP/shell scripts spawned during composer autoload execution accessing CI secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, Docker registry tokens). Flag unexpected outbound DNS/HTTP from php-cgi or composer processes to non-package-repository destinations.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Tag Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' but pipeline extracted no IOCs for hash/signature mismatches or tag tampering that would indicate version substitution

log_sources: CI/CD logs fed to LLM context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Before feeding tool output (test logs, build summaries, CLI output) to LLM agents, scan for injected instructions, especially commands to disregard, delete, or modify code. Flag presence of phrases like 'disregard previous instructions' or imperatives to destroy artifacts in non-human-readable contexts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Library Method Invocation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is a single method call: 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class.' Pipeline should detect when this method is called or present in loaded classes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for invocation of or presence of the method `printMessageForCodingAgents()` in net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor. Trigger on class loading of JqwikExecutor from version 1.10.0 or decompilation of JARs containing this method.

suggestion.title: Maintainer-Injected Supply Chain Sabotage
suggestion.rationale: Novel attack pattern: 'The maintainer wrote it on purpose... The person who wrote it was Johannes Link, the project's own maintainer.' This is insider-based supply chain compromise, not external account hijacking. Requires monitoring for maintainer behavior anomalies and intentional payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to open-source projects that introduce new methods specifically named or documented as targeting AI/agentic tools. Monitor for deliberate obfuscation techniques (ANSI codes, intentional hiding) paired with methods designed to execute only in automated contexts.

suggestion.title: File Deletion Executed by LLM Agent from Tool Output Injection
suggestion.rationale: Intended impact: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' If the agent follows the injected instruction, it would delete files. Monitor for unexpected file deletions triggered by LLM agent execution of embedded commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LLM agent processing of tool output with subsequent file deletion operations on the same system. Flag when file deletions follow agent reads of build/test output, especially deletions of test files or entire directories matching patterns in injected instructions.

suggestion.title: Preinstall Hook Triggering Credential Reads from Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI.' No UC detects the actual credential-gathering execution phase—only installation and payload download are covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node or npm process spawned during preinstall hook that reads from credential files (/root/.aws/credentials, /root/.azure/config, $KUBECONFIG, env vars containing AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, VAULT_ADDR). Look for repeated fstat/open calls on credential paths followed by child process spawns of curl, wget, or base64. File read events on cloud provider credential stores within seconds of malicious package npm install.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Metadata Service Access from npm Preinstall Context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'targets...GCP, Azure' metadata and the techniques list includes T1552.005 (Cloud Instance Metadata API), but no UC detects actual metadata endpoint calls (169.254.169.254, 'metadata.google.internal', etc.) from node processes during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process (spawned as child of npm/preinstall) initiating DNS queries or HTTP connections to cloud metadata endpoints: 169.254.169.254/metadata/v1/* (GCP), 169.254.169.254/api/token (Azure), 169.254.169.254/ (AWS), 'metadata.google.internal', 'instancemetadata.service.consul'. Correlation with @redhat-cloud-services package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Exfiltration via DNS or HTTP from Node Preinstall Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1071.001 (HTTP) and T1071.004 (DNS) usage for exfil but no UC detects outbound C2 or data exfil patterns. The credential harvester must communicate stolen data; current UCs stop at execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node or child process (spawned from preinstall hook) initiating outbound HTTP POST/PUT to anomalous domains or high-volume DNS queries (DNS tunneling signatures) within 60 seconds of credential reads. Look for command-line curl/wget with base64-encoded payloads, or node spawning bash to execute network commands. Exfil timing correlation with credential access events.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution with Network/File Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install.' Current UCs detect installation and bun downloads separately but miss the preinstall trigger event itself—the moment npm lifecycle script execution begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm or node process invoking a script at lifecycle phase 'preinstall' (visible in command line or parent process args). Correlate with child process spawns (bash, sh, node, curl, wget) and file system writes to /tmp or node_modules within 2 seconds. Look for npm parent with --script flag or package.json preinstall entry parse patterns.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Payload Execution in node_modules Preinstall Context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1027 (obfuscated payloads) and T1059.007 (JavaScript execution) but no UC detects highly obfuscated or minified JavaScript code being sourced and executed from package.json or installed modules during preinstall.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Preinstall hook or npm lifecycle script execution that sources obfuscated JavaScript from node_modules or installs a package whose index.js or preinstall.js contains high entropy, minified, or base64-encoded payloads (entropy > 6.5 bits/byte). Detect via file content analysis of JavaScript written to node_modules during package install, or node invocation of highly obfuscated scripts with regex `node.*-e.*[A-Za-z0-9+/=].*==` patterns.

suggestion.title: Multiple @redhat-cloud-services Packages Installed Across Dev/CI Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multiple packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope'—supply chain breadth suggests hunting across multiple related packages and environments. Single-package installs miss the scope of potential exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate across multiple @redhat-cloud-services packages (host-inventory-client, notifications-client, frontend-components, rbac-client, etc.) installed in the last 7 days. Count unique hosts/users installing 3+ affected packages from the same scope. Correlate with CI/CD environment context (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, CI=true env vars). Flag broad supply chain compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage attacks' and 'post-install script' vectors in npm package exploitation. Pipeline missed detection for execution of arbitrary code via install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or npm.exe spawning unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, curl, wget) during package installation. Flag processes spawned from npm cache or node_modules directories with egress network activity or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from npm Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential harvesting' as an attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection for exfiltration of npm tokens, registry credentials, or GitHub tokens from build environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exfiltration of npm_token, NPM_TOKEN, .npmrc contents, or GitHub tokens by monitoring environment variable dumps, base64-encoded credential leakage to external domains, or authentication header anomalies in outbound HTTP traffic from CI/CD runners.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'supply chain' attacks and package-level compromise. Pipeline should flag detection of unexpected package.json modifications or dependency version downgrades introducing vulnerable/malicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to package.json or package-lock.json files, sudden introduction of unknown or typosquatted package names, or installation of packages from non-standard registries. Correlate with CI/CD pipeline triggers.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Persistence via npm Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CI/CD persistence' as a primary attack goal. Pipeline missed detection for installation of persistent malware disguised as legitimate build dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated installation of the same suspicious npm package across multiple CI/CD runs, persistence mechanisms in post-install scripts (cron jobs, scheduled tasks, shell rc files), or modification of CI/CD configuration files by processes spawned from npm modules.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Propagation via npm Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'worm propagation.' Pipeline should detect when a single malicious package rapidly infects downstream consumers, indicated by cascading installations and lateral movement patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid spike in installations of a specific npm package version, followed by outbound connections from infected systems to download additional payloads or propagate to other systems. Monitor for beaconing patterns or bulk credential exfiltration across multiple endpoints simultaneously.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Detection in npm Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'obfuscation' and 'payload.' Pipeline should detect use of code obfuscation, string encoding, or Base64/gzip payloads embedded in node modules to evade static analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source for obfuscated JavaScript patterns (minified, base64-encoded strings, hex payloads), encrypted or gzip-compressed binaries embedded in node_modules, or dynamic code evaluation (eval, Function constructor) that loads payloads at runtime. Correlate with YARA or pattern-matching rules for known malware families.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Flow Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'device code phishing...has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked.' Explicit attack surface with industrial tooling documented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth device_code grant_type flows where device code was requested but never successfully authenticated, or where authentication occurs from geographically inconsistent IP. Flag multiple failed device code attempts for same user within 1 hour or device code scopes requesting mail.read, mail.send, or files.read on first-time consent.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Browser Clipboard and Session Data Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'analyzing page behavior, script execution, and malicious mechanics (session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads) rather than matching domains against a feed — particularly where many attacks now take place entirely inside the browser session without touching the endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser process clipboard API invocations (navigator.clipboard.read* methods) in non-approved domains followed by exfiltration. Alert when script execution (eval, Function() constructor) in untrusted origins precedes clipboard access. Flag repeated clipboard reads within <5 second window.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI SaaS OAuth Consent and Shadow Account Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'average organization has 16 unique AI apps, 17 AI browser extensions, and 17 AI-connected OAuth integrations — most of them unapproved...Of file uploads to AI tools, 38% are made from personal shadow accounts rather than organizational ones.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag OAuth consent grants to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot (personal tier) or file upload API calls to openai.com, claude.ai, google.com/colab from corporate IP ranges. Alert on sign-ins from corporate device to personal Microsoft/Google account followed by AI service access. Monitor CloudAppEvents for uploads to OneDrive personal accounts followed by AI service API calls.

suggestion.title: AI Browser Extension Unauthorized Data Collection and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.' Average org has 17 unapproved extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when unapproved browser extensions (classified as AI-related or low-trust) invoke tabs.query or webRequest APIs to capture navigation to sensitive domains (intranet, HR, finance systems) then exfiltrate to external extension infrastructure. Flag extensions requesting 'all_urls' permission on non-whitelisted publishers. Monitor for unusual extension install events from non-official stores (sideloaded XPI/CRX).

suggestion.title: Search Engine Result and Malvertising-Delivered Phishing Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ClickFix is an even clearer example, where 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results' and 'malvertising, social media, SEO poisoning' are primary delivery. Email security is 'structurally blind to the delivery channels that are growing fastest.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee browser navigation: search.google.com or search.bing.com → landing page within 30 seconds → redirect to newly-registered or suspicious domain with phishing signals (OAuth form, device code prompt, MFA bypass). Flag malvertising patterns: SRP click on paid search result (ads.google.com) bypassing organic results. Detect LLMShare abuse: clicks to chatgpt.com/share/*, claude.ai/share/*, etc., redirecting to external phishing kit.

suggestion.title: Rapid Phishing Domain Rotation and Zero-Day Delivery Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Spamhaus: '89% of phishing domains are active for fewer than two days. For organizations relying on blocklists and IOC feeds, every phishing attack is effectively a zero-day.' Pattern detection required when IOC-based is 'degraded.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS A-record creation timestamps with first-seen UrlClickEvents to same domain (delta <1 hour). Flag domain clusters: 3+ homograph/typosquat variants (similar Levenshtein distance) resolving to fresh ASNs within 24 hours. Alert on subdomains reusing phishing-campaign templates detected via DOM similarity (OAuth prompt layout, certificate validation bypass patterns) on previously-flagged kits (ClickFix, InstallFix variants).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound to Steam Community by Non-Gaming Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'communicates with infected sites' via 'Steam Community profiles.' Detection should flag WordPress processes, PHP engines, or typical malware-process parents initiating HTTPS to steamcommunity.com outside of user-initiated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound TLS connections from WordPress process spaces (php.exe, apache, httpd) or suspicious parent processes to steamcommunity.com on port 443. Correlate with presence of injected malware code in WordPress files to confirm C2 rather than legitimate gaming use.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Profile Comment Fetch Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments.' Detection should identify repeated programmatic fetches of specific profile comment threads at regular intervals or correlated with malware execution windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET requests to steamcommunity.com/profiles/<numeric_id> or steamcommunity.com/id/<username> endpoints at regular intervals from compromised WordPress hosts. Look for User-Agent anomalies (not browser-like) and absence of session/cookie context typical of human browsing.

suggestion.title: WordPress Malware Injection Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'targeting WordPress websites' with 'malware campaign.' Detection should identify post-compromise artifacts: suspicious PHP code injection, unauthorized theme/plugin modifications, or file-write patterns consistent with web-shell deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress root and plugin directories for creation or modification of .php files outside of expected updates/deployments. Correlate file write events with suspicious process parents (php, apache) and presence of obfuscated code or base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Domain Resolution to hello-mywordl[.]info
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'hello-mywordl.info' as registered IOC. Detection should identify DNS queries and successful resolution from WordPress hosts or internal network to this known malware C2 domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all DNS queries for hello-mywordl.info and subsequent TCP connections to resolved IPs. Prioritize alerts from WordPress process spaces or from internal systems not expected to contact external C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Beaconing to Small Set of C2 Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies C2 communication pattern. Detection should flag periodic outbound connections from compromised hosts to the IOC list at regular intervals with low variance in timing, consistent with automated beacon behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic connections from WordPress hosts to hello-mywordl.info or Steam profile endpoints with consistent inter-beacon timing (average 30–600s), low standard deviation (<5s), and >30 total connections over observation window.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via Windows Color System Registry Modification at Logon
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' Critical persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID entries related to Color System Loader. Correlate with suspicious DLL loads from game directories at logon. Monitor for InprocServer32 entries pointing to non-standard DLL paths.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via Modified FFmpeg in Game Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) imported the DllGetClassObject function from natives2_blob.bin.' Game load triggers exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ffmpeg.dll loads from game installation directories with suspicious SHA1. Monitor for DLL import resolution to .bin files (natives2_blob.bin). Alert on sideloading chains from game executables.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from Binary Blob
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Stage1 mechanism: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' Direct payload deobfuscation and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell instantiation with Base64-encoded arguments. Alert on PS spawned from game processes or DLL load contexts. Decode and inspect Base64 command blocks for obfuscated malicious logic.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game Distribution via PixelDrain and Torrent Trackers
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'links redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service' and 'distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena.' Primary initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on downloads from PixelDrain domains and AniRena tracker IPs. Inspect game-archive file structures for non-standard DLL presence. Correlate archive download + game binary execution on same host.

suggestion.title: Delayed Multi-Stage RAT Payload Download After Persistence Established
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Delayed payload download suggests C2 check-in and staged delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections 2–7 days post-infection. Monitor for executable downloads from non-reputable domains. Correlate network IOCs with presence of COM hijacking or natives2_blob.bin artifacts on disk.

suggestion.title: Sandbox Evasion via Environment Detection in Stage1 PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article states Stage1 'performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Indicates anti-analysis capabilities designed to evade detection sandboxes and analysis infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VM/hypervisor detection patterns (WMI Win32_ComputerSystemProduct queries, CPUID checks). Alert on debugger or analysis-tool detection attempts. Suspicious environment checks in PowerShell Stage1 logs indicate evasion.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Malformed Frame DoS Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'HTTP/2 Bomb Vulnerability Allows Remote DoS'—directly describes malformed frame-based attack. No frame anomaly detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 frames with abnormal sizes, missing mandatory fields, or violations of RFC 7540 frame format. Correlate frame anomalies from single source IP with server-side connection resets or 5xx errors.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 RST_STREAM Flood
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 bomb attacks characteristically flood RST_STREAM control frames to exhaust resources. Article describes 'bomb' mechanism but pipeline surfaced no control-frame abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >100 HTTP/2 RST_STREAM frames per minute from single source IP. Correlate with server latency increase or process memory growth spikes.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Stream/Connection Exhaustion
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies impact on NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare—indicating resource exhaustion at connection/stream layer. Pipeline missed resource-depletion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained spikes in concurrent HTTP/2 streams from single source exceeding baseline by 5x+ within 30s window. Alert if coincident with memory pressure or file descriptor exhaustion on web server.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Restart or Unavailability Post-HTTP2-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Remote DoS'—impact must include service unavailability. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase or process-health detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/2 protocol anomalies (malformed frames, RST floods, stream exhaustion) with subsequent web server process crashes, restarts, or availability metric drops (uptime alerts).

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Protocol Conformance Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'HTTP/2 Bomb'—implicitly a protocol-level attack. Pipeline should flag RFC 7540 violations: invalid frame sequences, missing connection preface, forbidden header combinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 connections failing RFC 7540 conformance checks: connection preface missing/malformed, frame ordering violations, or invalid magic number. Log source should include WAF protocol inspection logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Post-Install Script Execution in Build Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack via preinstall/post-install malicious code in npm packages. Pipeline failed to suggest behavioral detection for script execution anomalies during package installation despite this being the initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node processes executing shell/PowerShell child processes from node_modules/.bin or .scripts paths. Detect post-install hooks spawning interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) with command-line arguments not declared in package.json. Alert on network connections initiated by child processes spawned during npm install/ci phases.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Environment Variables and Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines—detecting access to .aws, .azure, .ssh directories and environment variable enumeration is critical yet completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node/npm child processes attempting file access to credential stores (~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.ssh, ~/.git, %APPDATA%\.aws). Detect environment variable enumeration (env, printenv, Get-ChildItem Env:) spawned from npm contexts. Alert on reads of .git/config, .npmrc, or cloud credential files from post-install script parents.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Package Republishing and Version Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm-like spread through republishing infected packages to further victims. Pipeline missed lateral movement detection for anomalous npm registry interactions (npm publish, version bumps) from compromised CI/CD environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish/npm version commands from non-designated release agents or developer workstations. Detect HTTPS connections to registry.npmjs.org or private registries from CI/CD environments during non-scheduled release windows. Alert on version increments to @redhat-cloud-services packages lacking corresponding git commits or CI pipeline triggers.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Infection and Persistence via npm Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes silent infection of CI/CD environments as a key impact. Pipeline failed to suggest detections for persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, cron entries, shell profile modifications) established during package installation phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of .bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile, or scheduled task/cron entries during npm install execution contexts. Detect persistence setup via init scripts or shell rc-file manipulation from Node processes. Flag entries created in ~/.npm or CI agent user's home directories linking to external URLs or C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials to Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Harvested GitHub/cloud credentials must be exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure. Article describes credential theft but pipeline generated no detection for credential transmission despite this completing the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS/HTTPS traffic from npm/Node processes with high-entropy or encoded subdomains (credential staging). Detect HTTP POST requests to unknown/suspicious domains with base64-encoded payloads from npm child processes. Alert on data exfiltration patterns matching credential formats (JWT tokens, API keys, AWS key IDs) leaving developer/CI machines.

suggestion.title: npm Package Integrity Mismatch: Version Downgrade Followed by Unexpected Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack introduces malicious versions of legitimate packages. Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection combining version manipulation (downgrade, rollback) with obfuscated post-install script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install/update events showing version downgrades or hash mismatches against package-lock.json or npm registry checksums. Detect when packages with tampered versions immediately spawn shell commands or network connections. Cross-reference package SHAs with npm registry to identify tampering, flag obfuscated post-install scripts using base64 decoding or string concatenation.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension.' No detection for webview-originated extension installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension installation (registry/filesystem writes to %LOCALAPPDATA%/Code/User/extensions) preceded by webview or github.dev URL access within the same parent process. Correlate with synthetic input injection (SendInput, user32.dll calls) from non-user-interaction contexts. Flag extensions installed outside normal marketplace authentication workflows.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Credential Harvesting from VS Code Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev.' No detection for token extraction from developer tool credential caches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code or child processes accessing token storage paths (%APPDATA%/Code/User/globalStorage, browser profile credentials). Alert on non-VS Code processes reading these locations. Correlate file access with unexpected GitHub API calls or token usage from the same machine within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub API Repository Enumeration Post-Token-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access.' Discovery phase needs discrete detection from token theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GitHub API call patterns per user/machine. Alert on sudden spike in /user/repos, /repos, or GraphQL repository enumeration queries. Flag API calls from new/unusual authenticating tokens. Correlate with github.dev session anomalies or VS Code extension activity on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Phishing-Link-Triggered VS Code Zero-Day Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tricking users into clicking a link' to github.dev. Initial access vector via social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious github.dev links in email/chat (especially shortened URLs or obfuscated paths). Correlate with recipients' subsequent VS Code extension installation or github.dev authentication sessions. Alert if same recipient machine executes GitHub API queries within 30 minutes of clicking link.

suggestion.title: Synthetic Input Injection Originating from VS Code Webview Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'simulate keypresses in the main editor' via malicious JavaScript in webview sandbox. Keystroke simulation specific to exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SendInput or equivalent input synthesis (Windows.Devices.Input API, user32 SendInput, keybd_event) originating from JavaScript/script execution within VS Code webview. Correlate with extension installation command initiation. Flag absent legitimate HID device events paired with synthetic input API calls.

suggestion.title: github.dev Session Token Theft and Unauthorized Cookie/Local Storage Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: mitigation involves 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev'; tokens are 'POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev.' Session persistence and theft must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code or subprocesses accessing github.dev session storage (browser IndexedDB, localStorage, Cookies folder). Alert on automated/bulk read operations on session tokens outside normal VS Code authentication workflows. Correlate browser data access with subsequent API token usage or cross-domain requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Delivery from Piracy Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' — establishes supply-chain compromise as initial-access vector with explicit distribution mechanism. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs, file hashes, or detection logic for this critical entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads from known piracy domains or untrusted software repositories, followed by execution within 300 seconds. Monitor write-then-execute sequences in user download directories. Correlate suspicious executable source with subsequent process spawning to command-and-control addresses.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Malware Execution and Persistence Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CountLoader Hits 86K' — documented malware with significant infection scale. Pipeline failed to extract hash indicators, execution signatures, or persistence patterns despite 86K figure implying available threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create rules for CountLoader execution chains: process injection patterns, unsigned child spawning, registry Run-key modifications. Alert on command-line obfuscation or reflective DLL injection signatures post-file-execution. Monitor for C2 callback network connections within 30 seconds of loader initialization.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Launcher and Mod Directory Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users' — specialized attack surface targeting game ecosystem. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for Minecraft-specific initial-access vectors (launcher hijacking, mod repository poisoning, version-manifest tampering).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Minecraft launcher process spawning and child processes. Detect modifications to Minecraft config files, game directories, or mod folders without corresponding legitimate update events. Alert on unsigned .jar file additions to game directories and suspicious launcher registry entries.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Resource Hijacking and Pool Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Miners Spread' — explicit impact-phase resource hijacking (T1496) with network exfiltration to mining pools. Pipeline provided zero CPU/memory signatures, miner process patterns, or pool connection detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained elevated CPU usage by non-system processes. Alert on memory-intensive processes spawned from pirated-content execution chains. Monitor for network beaconing to known cryptocurrency mining pool addresses and non-standard port connections to mining infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Telegram API Abuse for Ransomware C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections'—primary C2 infrastructure indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS requests to api.telegram.org from systems not typically using Telegram. Detect process-to-network patterns where Cobalt Strike beacons or Python-spawned processes make API calls to Telegram servers. Flag connections from unexpected executables with suspicious command patterns.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker Abuse as C2 Redirector
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server'—distinctive infrastructure evasion pattern used for C2 obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS connections to *.workers.dev domains from compromised hosts. Detect Cloudflare Worker traffic paired with Cobalt Strike beacon signatures or originating from unexpected processes. Flag TLS SNI or HTTP header patterns consistent with proxied C2 redirection.

suggestion.title: Python-Based Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality'—core execution technique of the toolkit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python.exe/python3.exe spawning unexpected child processes or accessing kernel32/ntdll regions via CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx, or WriteProcessMemory. Detect legitimate executables (calc.exe, notepad.exe, svchost.exe) suddenly loading suspicious DLLs post-Python execution. Flag in-memory code execution patterns after Python script activities.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery via AI-Driven Iterative Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices'—distinctive reconnaissance pattern suggesting autonomous scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid automated sequences of LDAP queries, WMI AD calls, or Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer commands spawned from Python subprocesses. Detect iterative command-line patterns (dsquery, adfind, nltest) suggesting agents re-evaluating results to select next discovery actions. Flag high-frequency AD enumeration from unexpected source processes.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Traffic Masquerading as Legitimate Web Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests'—core EDR evasion technique explicitly deployed by the toolkit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS beacon patterns with spoofed User-Agent strings, legitimate-looking Host headers, or common web asset paths (jquery.js, bootstrap.css). Detect Cobalt Strike command patterns in HTTPS traffic using TLS metadata or decrypted payload analysis. Flag process anomalies (rundll32, regsvcs making outbound web requests when unexpected).

suggestion.title: Iterative Malware Variant Testing and EDR Evasion Module Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Close to 80 modules were generated and tested against more than 70 techniques' using 'iterative approach to developing and testing malware against Sophos, CrowdStrike, and Windows Defender EDR agents'—high-frequency variant generation and testing behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency binary execution and variant generation (many file hashes executed in rapid succession). Detect payloads testing EDR hooks (ntdll syscall variation, AMSI bypass attempts, Defender exclusion queries). Flag suspicious file creation/deletion patterns in Documents or temp directories suggesting test payload staging and cleanup.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic T3 Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'via T3, IIOP' protocols with 'network access' and 'no privileges.' Pipeline failed to flag T3/IIOP as a detection vector despite it being the attack transport layer explicitly named in the article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual T3 protocol traffic (port 7001/7002 by default) or IIOP connections to Oracle WebLogic servers from unexpected sources. Flag rapid connection attempts, malformed handshakes, or connections from IPs not in established management ranges.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 Version Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0 with 1,592 exposed instances. Pipeline did not generate use case to detect or track these versions in enterprise inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query process command-line args, listening ports, and application metadata for Oracle WebLogic Server version identifiers matching 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0. Correlate with network exposure scans (e.g., Shodan data) to identify unpatched inventory.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Access from WebLogic Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation results in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Pipeline missed detection for anomalous file read/database query activity spawning from the WebLogic process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal file or database read operations initiated by Oracle WebLogic Server processes (e.g., java.exe or setDomainEnv.cmd children) accessing data directories outside typical application paths or querying database schema objects at scale.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WebLogic Server RCE via T3 Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker' with 'no privileges' and 'low-complexity attacks.' Pipeline did not map the unauthenticated exploit path or identify deserialization/gadget-chain indicators typical of Java RCE payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned directly by or as a child of WebLogic process (java.exe) without prior authenticated session. Flag if timing correlates with inbound T3 connection or unusual environment variable inheritance.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-Related Oracle Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states '12 [Oracle flaws] have been abused in ransomware attacks' and describes WebLogic as 'a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors.' Pipeline should have flagged ransomware-specific kill-chain indicators and actor TTP associations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebLogic exploitation signals with ransomware behavioral indicators: large-scale file encryption, volume shadow copy deletion, event log clearing, or deployment of encryption tools. Alert on WebLogic compromise within 24 hours of ransomware tooling execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Detection via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states under 'Indicators of Compromise': 'CVE-2022-0492 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the baseline detection to identify at-risk systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, kernel version inventories, and patch management systems for Linux systems running unpatched kernel versions susceptible to CVE-2022-0492. Cross-reference against CISA KEV due date (2026-06-05) to flag overdue remediation.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Exploitation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the specific exploitation mechanism: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' This is a precise behavioral indicator for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to cgroups v1 release_agent paths (typically /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent), execve() calls from cgroup hierarchies, and unusual process spawning from cgroup controllers. Prioritize on Linux systems in kernel versions prior to patches for CVE-2022-0492.

suggestion.title: Linux Privilege Escalation from Restricted Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'improper authentication vulnerability which could allow for privilege escalation' through cgroups mechanism, implying processes escalating from unprivileged to privileged context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege boundary violations: unprivileged process (uid > 0) writing to kernel structures, container processes spawning host-level shells, or capability grants via cgroups. Correlate with cgroups controller manipulation and release_agent invocation.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attack on Cloud Vault Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Brute-Force Attack' as the attack vector. This is the primary threat mechanism and requires detection of failed authentication attempts against Dashlane or similar credential-storage services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal spike in failed sign-in attempts against password-manager services within a short timeframe. Alert on single source attempting multiple credentials or single credential across multiple accounts. Threshold: >10 failed logins in 15 minutes from same source or to same account.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Vault File Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—indicating successful data exfiltration after brute-force compromise. Requires detection of vault/archive downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk download or export of encrypted vault files from password-manager cloud storage. Flag unusual download sizes (>10MB for vault data), downloads to new geographies, or downloads outside business hours from compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Vault Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms vaults were accessed and downloaded by unauthorized actors. Requires detection of unusual access patterns after credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication spike with subsequent successful login from same source and immediate large file access/download. Baseline normal vault-access patterns and alert on deviations: multiple vaults accessed by single session, access from new device/location post-compromise, rapid sequential vault opens.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Exploitation — Suspicious Child Process Execution Post-Extract
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR'; this is the attack vector but no detection logic provided for weaponized archive decompression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinRAR.exe or WinRAR processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, regsvcs.exe, or unsigned binaries within 10 seconds of archive extraction. Enrich with parent-process context (email, Downloads folder, %temp%, network shares).

suggestion.title: GammaWorm Malware Execution and Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: GammaWorm explicitly named as delivered payload in title; no detection hypothesis for post-exploitation runtime behavior or C2 signaling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution from extraction or temp directories matching GammaWorm naming/behavioral signatures (Registry modification, WMI activity, service creation). Correlate parent chain: email/archive → WinRAR → unknown process. Monitor for DNS/HTTP beaconing patterns.

suggestion.title: GammaSteel Data Stealer — Sensitive File Access
suggestion.rationale: GammaSteel identified as stealer malware in title; no detection logic for credential access, file enumeration, or exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unknown processes reading LSASS, SAM registry hives, browser credential stores (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Chrome\User Data), Outlook PST files, or SSH keys. Correlate with GammaWorm execution or post-WinRAR exploit timeline.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Infrastructure & Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon actor named in title but no C2 infrastructure attribution or post-compromise dwell-time detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain Gamaredon C2 domain/IP list from CISA, Mandiant, or sector ISACs. Alert on Ukrainian-scoped networks or organizations with historical Gamaredon targeting connecting to attributed infrastructure. Include historical domains for retroactive search.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign with Malicious WinRAR Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine-specific targeting + WinRAR delivery vector + Gamaredon attribution strongly implies spear-phishing campaign; typical for this actor. No email-layer detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Ukraine-based organizations: detect inbound emails with .rar/.zip/.7z attachments from external senders, especially spoofed internal domains. Flag downloads and extraction of archives to user directories. Cross-reference with known Gamaredon phishing patterns.

suggestion.title: Android Framework CVE-2025-48595 Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Local attackers can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability (tracked as CVE-2025-48595) to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' This is actively exploited; pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected privilege escalation on Android 14+ devices post-June 2026 patch. Correlate low-privilege processes (WebView, media renderer) with system_server code injection attempts, unexpected child process spawning from Framework components, or writes to sensitive Android system paths.

suggestion.title: Targeted Commercial Spyware Deployment via Android Framework Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware'—indicating known actor category. Pipeline generated no detection for spyware-specific exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK installation anomalies preceded by Framework or WebView crashes. Spyware delivery correlates with exploit staging: watch for code injection into system daemons, unexpected dex loading in high-privilege contexts, and network callbacks to attacker infrastructure immediately post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Nation-State Precision Targeting of High-Value Individuals
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'nation-state operations [have] target[ed] high-profile or high-interest individuals' using Android Framework flaws. This threat actor profile has zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For high-value targets, monitor for precision exploitation: one-off exploit payloads, targeted messaging app crashes preceding system changes, C&C beacons to nation-state infrastructure, and anomalous system_server behavior on specific device identifiers. Nation-state attacks are low-volume, high-fidelity.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Android Framework (CVE-2025-48595 RCE Path)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed.' This RCE vector is unmapped in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor system_server process for out-of-band child spawning, unexpected IPC handler registration in MediaServer/system frameworks, or code injection indicators. RCE via Framework manifests as mismatch between parent context and privilege level of resulting process.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Closed-Source Component Vulnerability Chain (CVE-2026-21385)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'vulnerabilities in...Qualcomm closed-source components' and specifically CVE-2026-21385 in display driver ('under limited, targeted exploitation'). No vendor-specific component detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor graphics subsystem (surfaceflinger, hwcomposer, vendor.display services) for unexpected privilege escalation, abnormal GPU memory access patterns, or DMA controller manipulation. Qualcomm driver exploits target GPU context management and DRM boundaries.

suggestion.title: Chained Privilege Escalation: Local Execution to System Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes two-stage attack: 'Local attackers can exploit...to gain code execution and escalate privileges'—sequential privileged transition with zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ordered patterns: low-privilege process writes exploit payload to /tmp or /data/local/tmp, terminates abnormally, followed by unexpected root or system_server process spawning with inconsistent parent/user context and abnormal execution path or memory maps.

suggestion.title: Android Memory Corruption Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly signals 'one actively exploited' vulnerability in critical Android components; pipeline failed to map exploitation phase. Memory corruption (CVE class typical in Android kernel/mediaserver) should trigger detection on unexpected process termination + privilege boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid process crash + immediate follow-up activity in system/kernel context. Correlate with known Android memory-corruption CVE signatures (heap spray indicators, ROP gadget execution, null-deref in privileged drivers).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation via Android Syscall Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation of kernel/driver vulnerabilities directly enables privilege escalation—article describes 'one actively exploited' flaw but pipeline missed privilege-escalation kill-chain link and detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged→root/system transitions in mediaserver, system_server, or kernel processes without user interaction or legitimate service restart. Flag SELinux policy violations preceding UID/GID change.

suggestion.title: Android Security Patch Installation Failure or Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'patches 124 flaws' but pipeline ignored remediation-coverage detection gap. For active 0-day, tracking patch-installation status and blockers is critical for impact assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on devices reporting Android API level ≤ vulnerability-patched-build-number after patch-window closure. Flag update-denial events, failed OTA installations, or rollback to unpatched builds within 30 days of advisory.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Tag Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' — core attack vector. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for unexpected git tag modifications without corresponding legitimate commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git repositories for tag creation or force-push events that modify package version tags. Alert when tag timestamp predates commit log entry or when rewritten tags contain source code changes not traceable to legitimate development branches.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Access from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title claims attack 'Steal CI Secrets' — malicious code in compromised packages reads and exfiltrates CI environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS credentials, etc.) during installation. Pipeline missed credential access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/bash child processes spawned by composer install accessing environment variables (via env, printenv, or $_ENV). Alert when process immediately follows with HTTPS POST to non-repository domains, or curl/wget commands with base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Package Coordinated Composer Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Multiple Composer Packages' rewritten, suggesting coordinated maintainer account compromise or repository-level breach. Pipeline should detect unusual access patterns across multiple package repos from single source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository write operations (git push, tag creation) from single IP or user account targeting multiple distinct Composer packages within 24-hour window. Flag if operations occur outside normal business hours or from geolocations inconsistent with historical maintainer behavior.

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Install Script Execution in CI Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package tags execute arbitrary code via composer post-install hooks. Article implies code injection without explicitly naming it. Detection should focus on unusual command execution patterns spawned from package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP or shell processes spawned as children of composer with command patterns indicating credential exfiltration: env variable enumeration, output redirection to network streams, or execution of curl/wget with piped shell arguments.

suggestion.title: Composer Lock File Unexpected Package Version Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Attack operates by 'rewriting tags' — composer.lock must reflect these malicious versions. Detection should alert when lock file specifies package versions or commits not explicitly declared in composer.json, or commits not findable in official repository branches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on composer.lock modifications where package entries reference git commits that do not exist on main/master/release branches, or where referenced commit is younger than the tag it is bound to.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Integrity Verification Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Attack succeeds by rewriting git tags — implies package signature/hash verification either disabled or bypassed. Detection should identify installations skipping integrity checks or from unsigned/untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer or package manager execution with flags that disable signature verification (--no-verify, --ignore-signatures, etc.), or installation of packages from non-canonical Packagist sources without corresponding upstream mirror configuration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Agent Service Principal Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Microsoft Agent 365' and 'securing agents across the development lifecycle' — indicates agents as first-class security targets. Pipeline missed coverage for unusual service principal access, privilege escalation on agent identities, or unauthorized agent invocations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service principal sign-ins from unfamiliar IPs, unusual resource access patterns by agent-owned identities, or privilege grants to agent-controlled accounts. Flag attempts to elevate agent permissions or add new credentials to agent identities.

suggestion.title: Development Lifecycle Tool Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'securing code...across the development lifecycle' — implies threats to dev tools. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for compromised build agents, tampered CI/CD configurations, or unauthorized modifications to pipeline definitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous modifications to Azure Pipelines YAML, GitHub Actions workflows, or build definitions outside normal change control. Flag execution of unsigned build artifacts or execution of build tools from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Model Weight/Training Data Exfiltration from Development Env
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'securing...models across the development lifecycle' — suggests threat model includes model IP theft. Zero UCs for unusual model file access, training data staging, or model weight checkpoint downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large, unexpected exports of model checkpoint files (.pth, .ckpt, .safetensors) from development environments, especially to external cloud storage or personal accounts. Flag data preparation scripts dumping training datasets to accessible shares.

suggestion.title: GitHub / Version Control Repository Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'GitHub' and code security is core message. Pipeline extracted zero detections for branch protection bypass, malicious dependency injection into code repos, or credential theft from CI secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository protection rule disablement, force-pushes to main/production branches, mass additions of new collaborators to sensitive repos, or commits signed with non-organizational keys. Flag commits that add hardcoded credentials or suspicious package dependencies.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvest from Developer Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Development lifecycle security inherently involves protecting API keys, tokens, and secrets in dev environments. Article mentions agents and models — common targets for credential scraping. Zero UCs for env var exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading .env files, environment variable dumps via 'env' commands, or clipboard access in development contexts. Flag PowerShell scripts enumerating %APPDATA% or /home directories for secrets databases.

suggestion.title: Detect Installation of Compromised npm Packages from Non-Standard Registry
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack article; npm registry substitution or unauthorized package installation is core attack vector. No detection use case was generated despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci invocations with --registry flags pointing to non-standard domains, or detect npm_config environment variables pointing to attacker infrastructure. Flag installations of @redhat-cloud-services packages from sources other than official npm registry (registry.npmjs.org).

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Code Execution from Compromised npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Once installed, malicious npm code executes in node processes. Article title and context imply code execution; no detection for node process behavioral anomalies was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js processes spawning unexpected child processes, making outbound network connections to non-standard ports/domains, or writing to sensitive directories (AWS credentials, SSH keys, git config). Correlate with recent npm install events.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Lockfile Tampering or Package Version Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often involve version downgrades to vulnerable packages. Article context suggests versioning is relevant; no detection for lockfile anomalies generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to package-lock.json or yarn.lock with timestamps inconsistent with developer activity. Detect requests for older/vulnerable @redhat-cloud-services package versions that contradict semver upgrade expectations.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Metadata Spoofing or Registry Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise may involve poisoned registry metadata or redirects. No IOC extraction or detection for registry-level anomalies was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to registry.npmjs.org with unexpected resolutions or man-in-the-middle indicators. Detect npm metadata requests (package.json downloads) with mismatched integrity hashes or suspicious author/maintainer fields.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration of Source Code or Credentials via Compromised npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article title does not specify payload; supply-chain compromises typically exfiltrate credentials or source. No detection for suspicious outbound data transfer from node processes generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node processes for unexpected HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to external domains with suspicious content (base64-encoded files, credential patterns, or large data transfers). Flag connections to attacker C2 infrastructure correlated with package install timing.

suggestion.title: Detect npm CI/CD Pipeline Poisoning via Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages in CI/CD environments can poison builds. Article context implies developer/production environments; no CI/CD-specific detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install commands in CI/CD pipelines executed with non-standard node modules or post-install scripts that invoke shell commands, curl, or attacker infrastructure. Monitor for unexpected environment variable exfiltration (CI_TOKEN, API_KEY) in build logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VS Code Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article covers compromised Nx Console extension; attackers distribute malicious extension via official channels. No detection for extension installation/version changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory for unexpected additions or modifications, or track extension-store API calls and manifest downloads. Correlate suspicious VS Code process spawns with recent extension installations. Alert on version rollbacks to known-compromised builds.

suggestion.title: Malicious Child Process Spawned by VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension likely executes arbitrary code; pipeline missed execution-layer detections. Article implies code execution post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by Code.exe or code-insiders.exe pointing to unusual executables (curl, powershell, cmd, wget, script interpreters). Flag reverse-shell patterns or encoded command execution. Correlate timing with extension load.

suggestion.title: Network Communication from VS Code Extension Process
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain payload likely includes C2 callback. Pipeline ignored network IOCs entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP from Code.exe or extension worker process to non-Microsoft/non-repo domains, especially with encoded query strings or suspicious User-Agents. Flag DNS requests for freshly registered domains originating from extension code paths.

suggestion.title: Extension File Modification or Injection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension persists via modified extension files or malicious injected code. Article describes compromise at source; no file-integrity detections offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.vscode/extensions/ (or equivalent per OS) for unauthorized file writes, additions of suspicious .js or .json files, or modification of entry-point manifest files (package.json, activate scripts). Flag entropy spikes in extension bundles.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension with access to developer IDE can harvest credentials from git config, environment variables, or IDE settings. No pipeline coverage for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads from ~/.ssh/, ~/.git/config, ~/.bash_history, IDE settings/secrets storage by VS Code processes. Alert on environment variable reads (GIT_AUTHOR, SSH_KEY, TOKEN_*) followed by suspicious network egress.

suggestion.title: Rollback or Removal Bypass of Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: Users attempting to remove or downgrade the extension may trigger uninstall hooks that prevent removal or restore payload. Pipeline missed persistence/anti-remediation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed VS Code extension uninstalls or reinstalls immediately after removal attempts. Detect File/Registry locks held by extension processes after uninstall command. Alert on extension .zip re-extraction or manifest rollback during cleanup.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Delivery Chain Detection—Suspicious Ad Redirect Cascade
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malvertising campaign' as infection vector: 'Operation FlutterBridge is a malvertising campaign targeting macOS users.' Pipeline generated zero UCs for ad-network-based initial access or redirect anomalies typical of drive-by downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP redirect chains (≥3 hops through ad/affiliate domains) concluding with executable downloads. Correlate redirect source reputation and landing domain age (<30 days) with subsequent suspicious process execution from Downloads folder on macOS.

suggestion.title: Flutter-Compiled Backdoor Execution—FlutterShell Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor is 'built using the Flutter framework'—novel delivery mechanism for macOS. No UC captures Flutter runtime execution patterns or CLI invocations suspicious for backdoor initialization.
