suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM container source code for 'new Function(' or eval() patterns. Alert on containers referencing Stripe customer record IDs (cus_ prefix) or metadata parsing. Track container hash changes and review creation/modification timestamps.

suggestion.title: Legitimate API Domain Abuse for CSP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters that would otherwise flag traffic to an unknown skimmer domain.' Defense evasion via trusted domains (api.stripe.com, googletagmanager.com).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline api.stripe.com traffic patterns from checkout pages (normal POST size, frequency, request body schema). Alert on anomalous metadata writes, unusual request sizes, or non-standard JSON structures. Monitor for requests originating from unexpected geographies.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Fields Harvested from Checkout Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.' Collection phase before obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript access to credit card form fields by selector (name*=card, name*=cvv, name*=exp). Alert on repeated field enumeration, form data concatenation, or regex patterns targeting payment attributes. Correlate with subsequent localStorage writes on same page load.

suggestion.title: Firestore Exfiltration to braintree-payment-app Project
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant: 'Google Firestore...is used instead of Stripe...stored in a different localStorage key (_d_data_customer_)' with document path 'tracking/captcha' in project 'braintree-payment-app.' Alternate exfiltration backend.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firestore write operations to documents matching 'tracking/*' or 'captcha/*' in projects with payment-related names. Alert on binary or base64 content in document fields. Cross-correlate with localStorage key '_d_data_customer_' updates on e-commerce checkouts.

suggestion.title: Massive Outbound Data Transfer to External Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states '234 GB of data' stolen; such volume requires sustained high-bandwidth exfiltration. Detection needed for bulk outbound transfers typical of data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained outbound data transfer >50 GB to single external IP or domain within 24-hour window. Correlate with compression tool execution (7z, WinRAR, tar). Baseline against legitimate backups and sanctioned cloud sync.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Query for Bulk PII Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 2.6 million records with email, names, SSN, govt IDs, health insurance, DOB extracted—indicating targeted queries against customer tables. 'Unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' directly implies credential compromise or network foothold used to query sensitive data stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for: (1) large OFFSET/LIMIT queries against customer_demographics, health_claims, or member_ids tables; (2) service account login followed by bulk SELECT returning >10k rows; (3) query patterns inconsistent with known application behavior.

suggestion.title: Long-Dwell Persistence Indicative of Multi-Stage Attack
suggestion.rationale: Breach 'came to light last month' yet data was stolen and leak negotiation failed—minimum 4+ weeks of attacker presence. 'Limited disruption' suggests stealth; requires persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag service accounts created or modified during incident window. Hunt for RDP/SSH sessions >4 hours duration, disabled-account re-enablement, or scheduled tasks executing with SYSTEM privilege. Correlate with lateral-movement indicators (process creation from unusual parent, UAC bypass attempts).

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Compression Prior to Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: To move 234 GB covertly implies staging/compression. Article mentions 'took immediate action to contain' but breach was live ≥4 weeks, suggesting attacker compressed and staged data before exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of compression (WinRAR, 7-Zip, gzip), archival tools, or bulk export utilities (sqlmap, mysqldump) targeting PII directories. Monitor for temporary file creation on network shares >500 MB, then rapid deletion.

suggestion.title: Threat Intelligence: ShinyHunters Infrastructure & Leak Site Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'infamous extortion group ShinyHunters' and references public leak site; any internal resolution/access to ShinyHunters C2/leak domains is breach indicator or attacker coordination signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index ShinyHunters known leak-site domains and C2 IPs. Alert on: (1) internal DNS queries for these domains; (2) successful proxy/firewall traversal to leak site; (3) HTTP POST/PUT requests consistent with data upload to extortion site.

suggestion.title: Healthcare Credential Theft: SSN and Government ID Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Explicit extraction of 'government-issued IDs' and 'health insurance information' indicates targeted credential-access phase. High-value identity data requires targeted querying.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag queries returning SSN, driver-license, passport, or health-plan identifiers. Alert if executed by non-application service accounts or from new source IPs. Correlate with bulk export operations.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Detection: Fake Open-Source Tool Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google.' Pipeline extracted zero domains despite this being the core IOC type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when users resolve or visit domains containing common open-source tool names (e.g., python-xyz.com, nodejs-mirror.com) that differ by typo, TLD swap, or subdomain from canonical repositories (github.com, pypi.org, npmjs.com). Cross-reference DNS queries against known fake-site IOCs.

suggestion.title: TDS Traffic Redirection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deliver malware via TDS' — Traffic Direction System is a stateful redirection tool. Pipeline did not surface TDS-specific detection or behavioral patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid HTTP 302/307 redirects from a single source IP to multiple destination IPs (hallmark of TDS behavior). Monitor for requests to domains matching tool names followed by redirect to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Open-Source Tool Download Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake sites masquerading as package repositories. No detection logic for downloads initiated from non-canonical sources (e.g., package installation from fake pypi, npmjs, or golang.org mirrors).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package managers (pip, npm, go get) or direct downloads target domains not matching canonical open-source repositories. Correlate with previous user web history to establish if visit to fake site preceded package install.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery Post-Redirect Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malware is the endpoint payload after TDS redirect. Pipeline should alert on unexpected executables downloaded from tool-impersonation domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on executable/MSI/DMG/tar.gz files downloaded from domains flagged as fake-tool sites. Correlate file metadata (hash, signer, submitter reputation) against malware databases and alert if hash is unknown or known-malicious.

suggestion.title: Search Result Click-Through to Attacker Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Rank High on Google' — attack relies on search-result spoofing. No detection for users clicking through from search results to attacker-controlled tool sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Referer headers from search engines (google.com, bing.com) followed by navigation to newly-registered or suspicious domains containing tool keywords. Combine with certificate-transparency logs to identify domains registered near article publication date.

suggestion.title: macOS Process Execution from Untrusted Downloaded Binary
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'FlutterShell Backdoor'; pipeline omitted execution-stage detection despite explicit malware reference and macOS platform indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation of unsigned or recently-timestamped executables on macOS following downloads from ad-serving domains. Monitor for Archive Manager decompression followed by immediate execution.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Malicious Advertisement Click
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' as delivery vector; pipeline created no initial-access detection for ad-network exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads initiated from Google Ads or YouTube domains where file type is executable, script, or suspicious archive. Correlate timing and user context against normal browsing patterns.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Communication from FlutterShell Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Named malware is a 'backdoor' requiring active C2; pipeline failed to surface command-and-control detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS for outbound connections on non-standard ports to recently registered domains. Alert on encrypted traffic to known Flutter-malware C2 infrastructure or suspicious TLS certificate issuer patterns.

suggestion.title: Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron for macOS Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor malware requires persistence mechanism; 'backdoor spreads' indicates active propagation and survival post-reboot, yet persistence phase was entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, and /var/spool/cron/tabs/ for new entries pointing to unsigned executables. Alert on plist modifications or cron job creation by unknown processes.

suggestion.title: MCP-for-Stata API calls with shell metacharacters in log_file_name parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'log_file_name parameter...directly interpolated into a Stata command string without sanitization' and lists injectable Stata commands (shell, python, erase). A direct hunt for API/CLI invocations with shell metacharacters in the parameter value would detect pre-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/API requests to stata_do endpoint or CLI invocations of stata-mcp with log_file_name parameter containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $, backticks, newlines). Check for patterns like %0d%0a (URL-encoded newline) or unencoded \n in POST bodies. Baseline: benign log file names are filesystem-safe (alphanumeric, dash, underscore only).

suggestion.title: Stata GuardValidator bypass — do-file content clean but injected parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'GuardValidator only scans the do-file content but does not validate this parameter.' A hunt for requests where the do-file is benign but the log_file_name is malicious would directly target the vulnerability design flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor stata_do API/CLI calls where (a) the do-file parameter passes GuardValidator (no suspicious shell keywords), AND (b) the log_file_name parameter contains shell keywords or metacharacters. This combination signals exploitation of the known bypass.

suggestion.title: Stata executing python or shell commands injected via log_file_name
suggestion.rationale: Article lists example injected commands: 'shell', 'python', 'erase'. If parameter injection succeeds, Stata logs should contain these commands executed in sequence. Log-level detection for these specific Stata keywords in suspicious context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stata execution logs (.smcl or .log files) for shell or python commands appearing _after_ a log file name parameter that contains shell metacharacters. Baseline: legitimate do-files do not inject commands via filename parameters. Alert on shell/python blocks immediately following suspicious log_file_name evaluation.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure — MCP-for-Stata version inventory and CVE-2026-47708 affection check
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' as a recon-phase hunt. Pipeline should surface vulnerability-to-asset mapping: find all installed MCP-for-Stata versions, cross-reference against CVE-2026-47708 affected versions (implied: all pre-patch versions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search software asset databases, pip/npm package registries, conda environments, and process listings for mcp-for-stata or stata_mcp installations. Flag any version <[patch version] as vulnerable to CVE-2026-47708. Correlate with internet-facing MCP servers or API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated YPTSocket WebSocket Handshake with XSS Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker' and 'YPTSocket plugin' broadcasts metadata. Pipeline missed WebSocket traffic as attack vector. Article: 'lets any unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket connections to `/plugin/YPTSocket/` endpoints without prior authentication handshake. Flag connections where WebSocket upgrade request includes malformed page_title or webSocketSelfURI parameters containing URL encoding of angle brackets, event handlers, or script tags.

suggestion.title: Browser DOM Tree Mutation Injection via YPTSocket Page Title
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'page_title' as broadcast vector: 'metadata broadcast in YPTSocket'. Pipeline missed monitoring the actual DOM manipulation vector where payload lands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on browser (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, firefox.exe) child processes or DLL loads spawned during active YPTSocket WebSocket communication, or on abnormal network callbacks from script evaluation. Monitor for setTimeout/setInterval/eval invocations from WebSocket message handlers.

suggestion.title: Admin Session Cookie Exfiltration Post-YPTSocket XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'every administrator currently viewing' and techniques list T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie). Pipeline did not map the attack-to-impact chain: XSS → cookie theft → admin compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser HTTP requests to YPTSocket pages (with XSS signatures) with subsequent unusual egress to attacker-controlled domains or anomalous auth token transmission. Flag if authenticated admin session cookies appear in cleartext HTTP headers or POST bodies to non-AVideo-internal destinations.

suggestion.title: YPTSocket Online Users Pane Accessed by Non-Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'administrator' as target but payload is 'unauthenticated'. Detection gap: pipeline missed recognizing that an unauthenticated user crafting the XSS will show up as one actor (attacker), but payload executes in admin context (victim). Monitor for privilege-escalation between request originator and execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if /plugin/YPTSocket/ requests originate from IP/user not in admin group or marked as unauthenticated, yet the subsequent JavaScript payload execution context is tied to admin credential tokens or cookies. Check for mismatched authentication levels between request initiation and payload result.

suggestion.title: Stored XSS Payload Persistence in AVideo Plugin State
suggestion.rationale: Article says 'Stored DOM XSS'—keyword 'stored' indicates payload is persisted server-side. Pipeline generated no persistence or storage-layer detection. Article: 'lets any unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AVideo database writes or filesystem updates to YPTSocket plugin state files for inclusion of unencoded HTML/JavaScript keywords (<img, <script, onerror, onload, javascript:). Flag if page_title or webSocketSelfURI parameter values stored without HTML entity encoding or sanitization.

suggestion.title: Package version downgrade to @cap-js/openapi 1.4.1 specifically
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'compromised version of @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 was published on May 19, 2026.' Pipeline does not hunt for downgrades to or forced installations of this specific version, which is the primary vector. Recommend detection of package.json or package-lock.json specifying version 1.4.1.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of package.json or npm install/ci commands specifying @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 post-May-19-2026. Correlate with accounts performing dependency updates. Alert if version pin matches compromised release and timestamp falls within known infection window.

suggestion.title: Credential file reads immediately followed by outbound network to t.m-kosche.com
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious packages harvested credentials.' Pipeline detects credential file access and exfil separately but does not correlate file reads to subsequent network callbacks. This temporal+spatial linkage is critical for distinguishing harvest-and-exfil from coincidental access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For any process (node.exe, bun.exe, npm.exe) that touches >= 2 credential files (AWS/GCP/npm/SSH), create timeline window (5 minutes). Flag if same process or parent spawns network connection to t.m-kosche.com or any external IP within that window. Confidence increases if multiple credential stores are read in single session.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook executing non-npm, non-node binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attempted self-propagation' and 'malicious packages.' The current UC_7_4 detects bun spawning from npm contexts, but does not detect other unusual runtime executables (curl, wget, powershell, bash, sh) that could indicate reconnaissance or payload fetch. Needs broader execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/preinstall/postinstall hooks spawning child processes other than node, npm, yarn, pnpm, bun. Flag invocations of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh), HTTP clients (curl, wget), or archive utilities (tar, unzip) during package install. High-confidence signal if invoked with URLs or remote targets in command line.

suggestion.title: Package self-propagation: npm package adding itself to dependencies of sibling packages
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'attempted self-propagation.' Pipeline has no detection for horizontal spread—e.g., compromised package injecting itself into package.json of other installed packages or adding new dependencies. This is a persistence and lateral-movement vector within the development environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned during npm install modifying package.json files in sibling directories or parent node_modules. Flag if @cap-js/openapi process (or any npm-triggered child) creates, edits, or appends to package.json outside its own installation directory. Anomaly: package count in package.json increasing post-install.

suggestion.title: Package integrity mismatch: installed @cap-js/openapi hash differs from npm registry
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 and SHA1 of malicious payload, but no detection compares installed file hash to official npm registry manifest. Package-lock.json or shrinkwrap integrity field should contain expected hash; deviation indicates either supply-chain compromise or man-in-the-middle. Pipeline missed this verification-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During or post-npm install, extract SHA256/SHA1 of installed @cap-js/openapi files. Compare to npm registry integrity field in package-lock.json or to baseline of known-good @cap-js/openapi@1.4.2 (patched version). Flag hash mismatch, especially against known-malicious hashes from GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv.

suggestion.title: Executable downloaded from lookalike/fake-tool domain with matching known-malicious hash
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'create convincing fake websites that impersonate popular security tools' (Ghidra, dnSpy, SpiderFoot). Core attack is domain impersonation + file delivery. Pipeline lists SHA256 hashes and malicious domains but generates no detection correlating them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads from known-malicious domains (IOC list) or lookalike domains (register.edu vs registeredu.com patterns) where file SHA256 matches known-malicious hash. Correlate to immediate execution within 30s as high-confidence indicator of unwanted payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Trusted security tool filename or certificate spoofed in downloaded file metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes hackers impersonate legitimate tools by 'complete with professional designs.' Detection should hunt for file metadata claiming to be Ghidra.exe, dnSpy.exe, SpiderFoot.exe but coming from suspicious sources or with mismatched signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for executables with names or internal resources matching legitimate tools (Ghidra, dnSpy, SpiderFoot, ilspy) but absent valid Microsoft/original-publisher signature or downloaded from non-official domain. High-confidence indicator of spoofed tooling.

suggestion.title: Domain reputation + lookalike detection for security tool brands
suggestion.rationale: Attacker creates 'ghidralite.com' (article) and 'dnspy.org'/'ilspy.org' (IOCs). Domains are intentional typosquats of Ghidra, dnSpy, ilSpy. Pipeline lists these IOCs but does not generate hunt for similar patterns or new lookalikes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and web access to domains containing substring matches or Levenshtein-distance variants of known security tools (ghidra, dnspy, spiderfoot, ilspy, burp, metasploit, etc.). Combine with WHOIS age (recently registered) and SSL certificate anomalies (self-signed or mismatched CN) to flag potential typosquats.

suggestion.title: Downloaded file execution from user-writable temp or AppData path
suggestion.rationale: Article describes users clicking download buttons on fake sites. Most browsers save to Downloads; malware payloads typically execute from temp locations. Detection should correlate browser-initiated file write to execution from suspicious path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executable file is written by browser process (chrome.exe, msedge.exe) to user-writable path (Downloads, Temp, AppData\Local\Temp) and executed within 30 seconds with suspicious child processes (powershell, cmd, rundll32, regsvr32, wmi).

suggestion.title: Certificate pinning bypass or HSTS bypass to lookalike domain
suggestion.rationale: Attackers register 'ghidralite.com' to appear legitimate. Detection should flag HTTP or self-signed HTTPS connections to domains that claim to be security tools but lack proper certificate chain or pinning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS connections to lookalike tool domains with self-signed or mismatched certificates (CN does not match domain, issuer is not trusted CA, or certificate age < 30 days and domain is lookalike of known tool).

suggestion.title: Outlook Mail Forwarding or Transport Rule Created Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'spied on' mailbox for 5 months; mail forwarding rules are the canonical persistence mechanism for silent email exfiltration. Pipeline missed foundational persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on New-InboxRule or Set-InboxRule operations creating forwarding rules to external domains. Baseline rule creation frequency per executive; flag rules with ForwardingAddress property pointing outside organization during or immediately after suspected initial access window.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Accessed via IMAP/POP3 or Unusual Geography Post-Password Reset
suggestion.rationale: Five-month persistent access implies either stolen credentials or token compromise persisting across password resets. Title emphasizes monitoring over extended period; detect anomalous logon patterns (impossible travel, off-hours, non-corporate IPs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for executive's Outlook/IMAP access (time-of-day, geography, device). Alert on IMAP logins from non-corporate ASN or impossible-travel distances. Correlate logon anomalies with mail rule creation or search spikes within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: OAuth Application Consent Granted to Unvetted App Targeting Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Modern email breaches often persist via OAuth tokens granted to third-party apps, surviving password resets. Article does not specify initial access method; OAuth token theft is prevalent in stock-exchange-targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new OAuth application consents targeting Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, or Calendar permissions. Alert on grants to rarely-seen applications or those with suspicious publisher; cross-reference with concurrent mailbox access anomalies. Baseline acceptable apps for executive role.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegated to Unfamiliar Service or User Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers grant mailbox delegation to maintain persistent, audit-trail-light access. Article indicates sustained surveillance; delegation is less detectable than direct logons and enables email exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MailboxPermission changes granting FullAccess, SendAs, or SendOnBehalf to accounts outside executive's department. Flag delegation to service accounts created after suspected compromise start date. Cross-reference against org chart.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Email Search or eDiscovery Export from Target Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: "Spied on" mailbox for 5 months suggests systematic collection of sensitive emails. eDiscovery searches and bulk exports are common exfiltration vectors post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on New-ComplianceSearch or Search-Mailbox targeting executive's mailbox with large result sets (>10k items). Flag eDiscovery exports to PST or suspicious recipients. Establish baseline; flag anomalies in search frequency, keywords queried (e.g., M&A, contracts, board minutes), or export volume.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Login from Suspicious User-Agent or IMAP/POP3 After Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers accessing stolen credentials via IMAP or legacy protocols avoid modern Outlook clients and MFA. Five-month surveillance likely leveraged programmatic access to avoid behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IMAP/POP3 logons to executive mailbox, especially from non-standard user-agents (raw IMAP clients, curl, etc.) or non-corporate IP ranges. Flag sustained IMAP sessions with unusual folder access patterns (systematic enumeration, large attachment downloads). Baseline acceptable IMAP clients.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Infostealer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'fileless .NET Infostealer' in the title and threat profile, but pipeline generated no detection for in-memory .NET execution, CLR injection, or obfuscated assembly loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rundll32.exe or PowerShell.exe spawning unusual .NET assemblies, dotnet.exe with obfuscated command lines, or CLR profiler environment variables. Fileless execution avoids disk I/O, so focus on process creation, loaded module paths, and CLR ETW event sources.

suggestion.title: Masquerading as Legitimate Software Vendor
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'fake Claude Code install page' and 'spoofed Anthropic install page' — direct masquerading of a legitimate vendor's installer. Pipeline should flag domains impersonating software vendors, particularly those with version-number keywords mimicking official infrastructure (e.g., 'download.version-*').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains registered with patterns ('*-version-*.com', '*download*', '*install*') that closely match legitimate vendor domains, especially with domain-age < 30 days and SSL certs issued to entities not matching domain names. Correlate with high-volume organic search referrers.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning for Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'SEO poisoning to push a spoofed Anthropic install page to the top of search results.' This attack-infrastructure setup (T1583.002) enables initial access via organic search rather than emails or ads and should be hunted separately at DNS/network boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains with high keyword-stuffing similarity to 'Claude Code install' or 'Anthropic download' registering and receiving organic search traffic (Referer contains google.com, bing.com) within days of registration. Cross-correlate with malware-hosting infrastructure indicators (ASN reputation, passive DNS).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to C2 Domains
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline flagged T1539 and T1555.003 (credential access) but omitted the exfiltration leg. Article describes attackers 'silently steal credentials' — the downstream transmission to C2 (oakenfjrod.ru, download.version-516.com) must be hunted as a separate event correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate non-browser process (e.g., rundll32.exe, powershell.exe) file access to browser credential databases (Login Data, Cookies) with subsequent DNS/HTTP beaconing to oakenfjrod.ru or download.version-516.com. Alert on short time delta (< 30 seconds) between credential-store access and outbound C2 connections.

suggestion.title: macOS FlutterShell Malware Hash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates 9 SHA256 hashes (e.g., '021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845') as 'high-fidelity' indicators of the actual malware payload. Pipeline extracted zero hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file creation, execution, or process hash matching the 9 known FlutterShell SHA256 values. Correlate with immediate parent process (browser, download utility) for phishing confirmation. High confidence if combined with C2 domain connectivity.

suggestion.title: Connections to FlutterShell C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Eight C2 domains explicitly listed as attack infrastructure (atsheisdomestic.org, etoftheappyrince.org, etc.). Pipeline extracted zero. T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) indicates non-standard C2 channel—monitor for anomalous protocols on these IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on DNS and network egress to the 8 C2 domains. Elevated confidence if process matches malware hashes OR if app execution precedes outbound connection within 5 minutes. Monitor for non-HTTP protocols (obfuscated, binary) consistent with T1071.

suggestion.title: Download and Execution of Fake macOS Applications
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'threat actors using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications.' Article states users 'download and run the fake application'—this is user-initiated execution (T1204.001) following malvertising (T1598), but pipeline captured neither technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or dubiously-signed macOS app bundles executed shortly after browser tab closure or click event. Correlate browser history with bundle identifier and code signature; flag if bundle claims to be (e.g.) 'XCode' or 'Chrome' but has empty/mismatched signature. High-entropy or obfuscated bundle contents (T1027) amplify risk.

suggestion.title: Masquerading as Legitimate macOS Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Fake applications disguise themselves as legitimate tools ('fake desktop applications'). No detection for T1036/T1036.004. Attack description implies spoofed app icons, names, and code-signing to bypass Gatekeeper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify macOS processes with bundle IDs mimicking Xcode, Homebrew, Git, or other developer tools, but with unsigned or invalid code signatures. Compare bundle CFBundleVersion against known versions; flag if newer than latest public release (possible trojanization). Monitor for bundle execution from unusual paths (~/Downloads, /tmp).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Flutter Backdoor Binary Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes T1027 (Obfuscated Files) as technique. Pipeline did not generate behavioral detection for de-obfuscation or runtime payload loading typical of Flutter binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes with abnormally high entropy strings, dynamic library injection via dlopen(), or unusual Framework loading (esp. non-standard Flutter runtimes). Correlate process spawn chains: parent=legitimate app, child=system utilities (curl, sh) spawned with obfuscated arguments. Flag suspicious fork/exec patterns.

suggestion.title: Google Ads Ecosystem Abuse for Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is malicious Google Ads delivering payloads. Article does not name specific ad network IOCs or fake domain names, only C2. Pipeline should surface ad-click patterns and domain registration patterns consistent with ad network impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users who visited ads-parkpro.com, adsparkpro.top, adsparkpro.net (ad network lookalike domains) with subsequent downloads of suspicious bundles within the same session. Alert on browser activity to these domains followed by macOS app execution within 10 minutes. Cross-reference with web proxy logs for click-through patterns.

suggestion.title: Cmd.exe spawning PowerShell with -EncodedCommand
suggestion.rationale: Article documents exact attack sequence: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload' — child process relationship + obfuscated command execution is unambiguous payload delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or explorer.exe launching powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand, -enc, or -e flags present in command line. Baseline legitimate admin automation, flag interactive user launches at unusual hours.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest to C2 + curl.exe to same destination
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly correlates Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe both connecting to 144.31.221.82:6060 — dual-executable C2 handshake confirms beaconing. 'Together, they told a complete story.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl.exe or Invoke-WebRequest process spawned post-PowerShell execution with outbound connections to IPs flagged as malicious ASN ranges or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate process tree + network destination.

suggestion.title: File deletion via Remove-Item post-execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script' — anti-forensics cleanup is explicit post-C2 indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe or cmd.exe executing Remove-Item or del commands targeting ApplicationData, Temp, or recently-created files within minutes of Invoke-WebRequest activity. Flag when cleanup follows scripted execution.

suggestion.title: Python HTTP client to malicious/reputation-poor ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hunt hypothesis: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure...Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Python user-agent traffic in environment; alert on python.exe or python3 spawning requests to ASNs with poor reputation scores, newly registered, or flagged C2 hosters. Exclude CI/CD pipelines and package managers.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC to suspicious ASN (Living-off-the-Land payload fetch)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies LOTL technique: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MSIEXEC user-agent in firewall logs connecting to malicious/untrusted ASN ranges or C2-associated IPs. User-agent persistence in encrypted sessions makes this high-signal. Correlate with executable activity on source host.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges. Certain autonomous systems have a long, documented history of hosting command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. Outbound connections to these ranges warrant investigation regardless of the specific destination IP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain curated ASN allowlist of known C2 hosters (EVILEMPIRE and equivalents). Alert on ANY outbound connection to these ASN ranges from internal hosts. High-fidelity given historical hosting correlation; minimal FP surface.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes 'self-spreading worm via Phantom Gyp'—binding.gyp files execute arbitrary code during node-gyp rebuild (postinstall phase); malicious scripts would trigger during 'npm install' with no user interaction required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell processes (bash, cmd, powershell) spawned as children of npm or node-gyp with suspicious arguments (curl/wget, environment variable manipulation, chmod +x). Flag process chains indicating build-time code execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Injection into package.json
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading worm behavior implies lateral propagation through compromised package forcing installation of further malicious dependencies; requires monitoring of unexpected dependency graph mutations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new dependencies added to package.json/package-lock.json without user action, especially version range operators (^, ~) permitting automatic updates. Correlate across multiple project directories for worm-like propagation patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp File Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Phantom Gyp' directly references binding.gyp as attack vector; gyp build system executes arbitrary 'actions' and 'variables' during native module compilation—no prior execution required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor binding.gyp files in installed packages for suspicious 'actions' keywords invoking shell commands (sh -c, python -c, gcc -E). Trigger on node-gyp process spawning unexpected child processes (network utilities, encoders, remote downloaders).

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Network Activity from npm Build Processes
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like behavior requires C2 communication for command dispatch and victim coordination; malicious postinstall or gyp actions initiate network requests during installation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and alert on DNS/HTTPS traffic from node, npm, python, or compiler processes during package installation. Flag connections to non-standard TLDs, newly-registered domains, or IP ranges outside npm/GitHub infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Recursive Lateral Spread via Transitive Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Title's 'self-spreading worm' characteristic implies automatic propagation through dependency trees; malicious package installed in one project may automatically trigger further infections in dependent projects via shared node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect correlated npm install events across multiple distinct project directories with identical malicious package versions. Monitor for transitive dependency chains that spike in adoption velocity across unrelated projects.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Environment and Build Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks harvest environment data (CI/CD secrets, source repo URLs) during build; postinstall/gyp actions can enumerate and exfiltrate .env, package.json, and git configuration without user awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads of sensitive patterns (*.env, .git/config, package.json) from node/npm processes, followed by network egress (DNS TXT lookups, HTTP POST to external domains). Correlate timing with postinstall execution phase.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Preinstall Hook Execution with ELF Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'published package versions containing the Rust ELF binary executed via 'preinstall,' pushing malicious commits into repositories.' Preinstall hooks are event-triggered execution vector not typically used legitimately in CI contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/Node package installations for preinstall scripts executing binary artifacts or architecture-specific ELF files. Baseline expected preinstall behavior per environment; flag direct binary execution from package manager context rather than script interpreter invocation.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Module Installation from Package Manager Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IronWorm is written in Rust, hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' eBPF program loading from package installation contexts is anomalous kernel-level persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on eBPF program registration (bpf_prog_load, bpf_map_create syscalls) temporally correlated with npm package installation. Cross-correlate kernel module loading with package manager process hierarchy. Kernel rootkit installation is anomalous post-installation behavior in CI/dev environments.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential File Access Pattern Targeting Multiple Secret Types
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malware targets 86 environment variables (key-value pairs) and 20 credential files that may contain OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials, vault configuration files, SSH keys, and Exodus cryptocurrency wallet files.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single processes accessing 5+ distinct credential file types within 60 seconds: ~/.aws/*, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.vault-token, ~/.anthropic*, ~/.openai*, cryptocurrency wallet directories. Flag sequential reads from environment variables combined with credential file enumeration.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Upload Containing Serialized Credential Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware serializes the secrets into a single value and then writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output...uploading the file as a build artifact.' Uses CI artifacts to exfiltrate without C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for artifact uploads immediately following credential harvest activity. Flag uploads with innocent names (lint, coverage, formatting reports) that are abnormally large or contain serialized/encoded credential patterns. Alert on artifacts uploaded outside standard CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating npm Package Publication Using Stolen Trusted Publishing Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The Rust-based malware self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow...publish trojanized versions of packages owned by the victim.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package version publications for anomalies: new versions from unusual CI runners, Trusted Publishing tokens used outside normal deployment pipelines, rapid successive publishes from compromised accounts, version publishes from geographic/network contexts inconsistent with account history.

suggestion.title: Git Commits with Backdated Author Timestamps (Defensive Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The commit author appears as "claude," and the timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag git commits with authorship timestamps >1 year in past that are pushed to repositories on current date. Monitor for 'claude' commit author across multiple malicious repositories within short timeframe. Alert on bulk push operations containing backdated commits from single account.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Shell Command Expansion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(…) form runs a shell command during the configure phase…The compromised packages abuse this directly.' This is the core attack vector; no detection use case was generated for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binding.gyp files containing shell command expansion syntax `<!(` or backticks. Flag when npm install triggers node-gyp rebuild on packages whose binding.gyp contains executable commands rather than legitimate build configurations. Correlate with process creation of shells (bash, sh, zsh) spawned as children of npm or node-gyp.

suggestion.title: Credential Access During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The payload harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes.' No detection for credential file access by processes spawned during npm install was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned during npm install (node-gyp, npm, bun) attempting to read sensitive credential files: .npmrc, .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .docker/config.json, GitHub SSH keys, Vault tokens. Flag file access patterns where a single npm install session touches multiple credential storage locations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection by Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence.' The pipeline missed detection for workflow files created or modified by processes originating from npm package installation contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .github/workflows/ directory for new or modified YAML files created by processes spawned during npm install or by child processes of the package installation context. Correlate with git commit/push activity from the same process tree. Flag workflows that schedule on common triggers (push, pull_request, schedule) without prior baseline.

suggestion.title: Package Version Bombing from Single npm Account
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4' and 'Many of the inflated version numbers… are themselves a side effect of the worm's automated republishing.' No registry-monitoring use case was generated for this worm-behavior fingerprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for single maintainer accounts publishing multiple distinct versions of the same package within short timeframes (e.g., >3 versions in <5 minutes), especially with semantic version jumps (1.x → 3.x or unusual increments like 2.26.4). This indicates automated worm republishing, not legitimate releases.

suggestion.title: Bun-Based Multi-Stage Payload Execution During npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The payload: a multi-stage Bun-based loader.' No detection was generated for Bun runtime execution in the context of package installation, which is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Bun runtime (bun.exe, bun CLI) spawned as a descendant of npm install, node-gyp, or node processes. Flag unusual command-line arguments, network connections to external IPs/domains, or file writes outside the package directory. Bun is uncommon as an install-time dependency; its presence during package installation warrants escalation.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Unexpected GitHub Repository Pushes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' No detection use case for credential data appearing in git commits or being pushed to external/unusual repos during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git push operations initiated during or immediately after npm install contexts. Flag pushes to repositories not in the organization's allowlist, or commits containing patterns matching credential formats (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.). Correlate with process lineage from npm/node-gyp to git to identify the injection point.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon to TA4922 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 5 C2 IPs and 3 C2 domains from TA4922 campaigns ('deploying a growing arsenal of malware against organizations'). Network connections to these should be hunted immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound TCP/UDP connections to C2 IPs (206.238.115.58, 154.211.86.110, 43.156.77.97, 103.214.172.33, 18.139.83.110) and DNS resolutions to C2 domains (aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com). Alert on successful connections from internal hosts.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Malware Execution by File Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 13 SHA256 hashes attributed to TA4922 malware (Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, ValleyRAT). Hash-based detection is highest-confidence for known samples.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match process creation, file write, and module load events against the 13 provided SHA256 hashes. Flag execution of any hash; correlate with web proxy logs for download source.

suggestion.title: RAT Persistence via Autostart Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: RAT families (Atlas, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, ValleyRAT) typically establish persistence. Article does not detail mechanism, but registry run-key and scheduled task abuse are standard for these tool families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for suspicious executables matching file hash IOCs or unsigned binaries launched by unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: TA4922 RAT Discovery Behavior Clustering
suggestion.rationale: RATs characteristically perform host enumeration: 'System Information Discovery (T1082), File and Directory Discovery (T1083), Software Discovery (T1518)'. Article states Atlas and Valley are RATs; behavioral cluster can catch variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid execution of discovery commands (whoami, ipconfig, systeminfo, dir, tasklist, Get-Process) within short time window from a single process parent, especially if process also matches obfuscation signature (T1027) or hash IOCs.

suggestion.title: Delivery of Loaders (RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader) via Email
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'campaigns' against regions; loader malware historically delivered via phishing. Article phrase 'campaigns are financially motivated and show a level of planning' suggests targeted delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails containing attachments matching the 13 file hash IOCs or linking to C2 domains. Cross-reference with user clicks on malicious links; correlate with proxy logs for downstream C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Loader File Detection (T1027)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as an observed technique. RomulusLoader and SilentRunLoader names suggest obfuscated/packed payloads; entropy and section-name anomalies should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag executables on disk with suspicious entropy (>7.0), .text section heavily packed, or missing standard sections. Correlate with process injection (CreateRemoteThread, SetWindowsHookEx) if executed; cross-check against the 13 file hash IOCs for known obfuscated variants.

suggestion.title: Finance Executive Email Compromise via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' No detection UC was generated for this common living-off-the-land email harvesting pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process execution with command-line arguments referencing email protocols (IMAPX, MAPI, Exchange Store) or Outlook data files being accessed via cmd.exe or powershell.exe from non-administrative users. Correlate with outbound network connections to mail infrastructure from unexpected processes. Alert on registry modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\*\Outlook\AutoDiscover or similar email configuration keys.

suggestion.title: VS Code GitHub OAuth Token Extraction via Webview Message Passing
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exploit a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews' to steal GitHub OAuth tokens. No detection for this development-environment credential theft vector was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension installation from non-official marketplaces or suspicious extension updates that correlate with subsequent GitHub.dev or GitHub API authentication. Detect token-like strings (github_pat_, ghp_, ghu_) in process memory or network egress from code editor processes. Alert on VS Code webview processes spawning with unusual parent-child relationships or command-line switches indicative of extension loading.

suggestion.title: Kali365 Device Code Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Once targeting just Microsoft 365, the phishing-as-a-service platform now aims at AWS, Okta, and Russian platforms, while relying on device code phishing.' This attack pattern—device code OAuth flows—was not covered by any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with URLs redirecting to device code consent screens or oauth.com variations. Correlate unusual device registration (GET /device_authorization) with user-agent strings typical of headless scrapers or non-browser clients. Alert on successful user code entry followed immediately by token acquisition from a different IP or geography. Monitor for MFA bypass indicators post-device code authentication.

suggestion.title: Red Hat NPM Supply Chain Worm—Credential Theft Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, where it pilfers sensitive credentials.' No detection was proposed for this supply-chain-sourced lateral movement and credential harvesting pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected npm package version changes or new account activity on package ownership. Monitor for process execution spawning credential-access patterns (reg query hklm\sam, mimikatz-like behavior, LSASS.exe access) from npm/node child processes. Alert on worm-like propagation: repeated process spawning with credential-theft signatures across multiple user/machine contexts within short time windows.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Resource Exhaustion Detection—Rapid SETTINGS/RST_STREAM Frames
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'The attack potentially affects over 880,000 websites that support HTTP/2' via HTTP/2 Bomb exploit. No use case was proposed to detect this availability attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormally high frequency of HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames or RST_STREAM messages from a single source IP within short time windows. Threshold: >1000 SETTINGS frames per second or >500 RST_STREAM per connection lifecycle. Correlate with server-side resource exhaustion metrics (open connections, memory, thread count spikes). Alert on patterns consistent with HTTP/2 Bomb variants (Pingora, NGINX, Apache HTTPD, IIS).

suggestion.title: KongTuke C2 Discovery—Beaconing and Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites: 'recent KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery' through hypothesis-driven threat hunting. This is a named threat actor artifact with no corresponding detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KongTuke C2 beaconing by identifying repeated connections to known C2 infrastructure with regular time intervals or unusual application-layer protocol patterns. Correlate beaconing IPs/domains with command execution events (PowerShell, cmd.exe spawning) at intervals matching beacon timing. Monitor for encoded command payloads typical of KongTuke C2 protocol.

suggestion.title: MCP Server or External Tool Injection via Agent Runtime Selection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'they continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs, reusable skills, open source components, plugins, and third-party tools — any of which may be vulnerable, malicious, or misconfigured. These components are selected and invoked at runtime and not pre-approved.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on agent processes dynamically resolving and invoking MCP servers or tools not in an approved whitelist. Monitor for novel external module loads by agent runtimes in near real-time. Baseline approved tool registries and flag deviations within agent execution environments.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Command Execution Outside Baseline Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once given a goal, they can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments — often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' Replit incident exemplifies this: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of commands, file paths, and API targets permitted for each agent class. Alert on commands outside baseline, file modifications in restricted directories (prod databases, config stores), or subprocess spawning with unusual frequency or privilege elevation patterns.

suggestion.title: Agent Defense Evasion: Post-Incident Cover-Up and Fabrication
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: agent 'fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Article emphasizes agent behavior 'was not governed at the moment of action,' describing post-breach cover-up operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk database inserts/updates immediately following agent errors, deletions, or anomalous actions. Flag synthetic or repeated-pattern records created post-incident. Monitor for agents reversing or obfuscating their own prior operations. Enforce immutable audit logging for all agent actions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Code and Secrets in Agent-Generated Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'That output may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations' and 'By the time post-commit scanning runs, the vulnerable output may already be in the repository.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement inline scanning of agent-generated code at creation time, not post-commit. Flag hardcoded credentials, API keys, and dependency versions with known CVEs. Alert on agent commits bypassing code review workflows. Correlate generated artifacts against secret stores.

suggestion.title: Agent Unauthorized Production Data Access and Exfiltration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the production agent that's about to forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go' and agents that 'call APIs, and chain workflows across environments.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline agent API calls by destination, data classification, and payload size. Alert when agents invoke external APIs with sensitive data in request body. Monitor for agents chaining unrelated API calls to exfiltrate data via side channels. Enforce API allowlisting before agents access production data endpoints.

suggestion.title: Workflow Composition: Benign Actions Chained into Dangerous Compound Outcome
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It won't stop an autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement workflow-level risk assessment, not action-level approval. Alert when benign actions (read config, modify RBAC, delete backups, exfiltrate logs) are sequenced by the same agent within minutes, producing dangerous compound effects. Require human approval for multi-step workflows involving sensitive resource chains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to SRA Self-Registration Application
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers breached its systems on May 14' targeting the 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine'—requires detection of initial unauthorized access to this web-facing application before data exfiltration occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous authentication patterns to SRA: failed login spikes, geographically impossible logins, out-of-hours access from service accounts, or rapid authentication sequences. Monitor for authentication bypass attempts, SQL injection payloads in request logs, or exploitation indicators against web application input fields.

suggestion.title: Bulk Exfiltration of Household PII Records
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information'—detection requires monitoring for mass PII extraction patterns from the SRA database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries extracting ≥1k records containing combined PII fields (name+ID+phone+location), unencrypted bulk exports from SRA, large file transfers from application servers, or simultaneous download sessions matching record-count patterns. Correlate query volume spikes with authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Using Stolen Beneficiary Data
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money'—indicates active phishing exploitation of the 600k stolen records with personal details enabling targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spoofed WFP sender domains, phishing URLs requesting re-registration or account confirmation, and messages sent to Gaza-based beneficiaries using personal identifiers (names, neighborhood data) from the breach. Correlate email volume spikes post-May-14 with Gaza geographic targeting and credential-harvest patterns.

suggestion.title: Database Query Reconnaissance for PII Schema Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Attackers stole structured PII from 600k records—likely preceded by schema reconnaissance queries to identify which tables/columns contain names, IDs, phone, and location data, detectable via SQL audit logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-standard SQL queries against SRA databases using INFORMATION_SCHEMA access, SELECT * patterns on beneficiary tables, or queries joining PII columns not typically accessed by application. Flag queries from database accounts with read-only or limited scope accessing unrestricted PII field combinations.

suggestion.title: Emergency SRA Platform Suspension and Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements'—emergency platform shutdown during active breach indicates containment actions or potential attacker persistence infrastructure modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unscheduled SRA service shutdowns, emergency configuration rollbacks, firewall rule changes, or security module activations during/after May 14 breach window. Alert on administrative access disabling application logging, authentication bypass modifications, or database password resets during incident response period.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Load from Game Directory with Suspicious Binary Import
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85), that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' This is direct DLL hijacking via game loader. Zero use cases generated for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect game executables (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) loading modified system DLLs (ffmpeg.dll) that in turn load suspicious .bin files with COM-related exports (DllGetClassObject). Monitor parent-child relationships where game process → DLL load → undocumented binary import.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Base64 Script Execution from Game Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded. The PowerShell script...performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Game-spawned PowerShell with obfuscation is high-signal. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell child processes spawned by game executables or game-loaded DLLs. Flag Base64-encoded command lines (presence of -EncodedCommand or suspicious IEX patterns) executed in game context, especially with anti-sandbox logic.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking: InprocServer32 Registry Modification for ColorCal DLL
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' Specific COM target named; classic persistence overlooked entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID and HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID for modifications to Windows Color System Calibration (ColorCal/wcscaling) InprocServer32 entries. Flag redirection to non-system paths or .bin files. Alert on logon-triggered execution via modified COM objects.

suggestion.title: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion in Game Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PowerShell script...performs basic checks for controlled environments. For example, it...[truncated].' Defensive evasion pattern indicated but incompletely documented. Still detectable via behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell commands from game process tree querying WMI for VM/sandbox artifacts (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BIOS, Registry VM checks). Flag scripts that conditionally exit or alter behavior based on environment checks; anomalous termination of game process post-check.

suggestion.title: Delayed RAT Payload Download and Execution Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Multi-stage delivery with days-long delay. Requires correlation between initial game infection and late-stage RAT network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate game process infection (Stage 1 PowerShell) with network beaconing 1-10 days later from same user/host. Detect HTTP/HTTPS downloads of executable or DLL artifacts initiated by COM-hijacked persistence mechanism (ColorCal-triggered process spawning). Monitor for Argamal detection signatures post-download.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Trojanized Hentai Game Distribution via File Sharing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL' and 'delivered via PixelDrain...torrent trackers, including AniRena.' Initial access vector—legitimate games + malicious payload. Threat hunting use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of hentai/adult games (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) from non-official sources (PixelDrain, torrent trackers). Monitor for game archives containing both legitimate game files AND unsigned/mismatched DLL files (ffmpeg.dll hash mismatch against known-good hashes). Flag first execution of trojanized game + subsequent Stage 1 PowerShell.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)' — no use case generated for detecting exploitation attempts against this known vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis ports (6379, 6380) for malformed RESP protocol packets, script injection payloads, or module-load exploitation attempts. Baseline legitimate admin tool signatures and alert on deviations targeting known CVE-2026-23479 attack vectors.

suggestion.title: Redis Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE impact but offers no detection for actual code execution via EVAL, SCRIPT LOAD, or MODULE LOAD commands that would follow successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from redis-server with system binary names or suspicious command lines. Flag EVAL/SCRIPT LOAD redis-cli commands followed by immediate child-process creation or unexpected network egress.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Redis Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: RCE compromises typically lead to discovery phase — missing detection for command sequences like INFO SERVER, CLIENT LIST, CONFIG GET that reveal Redis configuration and connected clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire Redis admin commands (INFO, CONFIG GET, CLIENT LIST) from single source within 2-minute window. Baseline expected admin patterns; flag sequences matching post-compromise reconnaissance profiles.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Anti-Sandbox Registry/Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malware features several anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the "CExecSvc" service, and OS UUID.' Direct evasion tactic requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process calls checking CExecSvc service status or enumerating Defender Application Guard registry paths (HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Hvci, services enumerations). Flag WMI queries for OS UUID on suspicious parent processes. Correlate with known malware process names or loader DLLs.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection (RomulusLoader)
suggestion.rationale: Article: RomulusLoader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' No detection coverage for these core execution techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child relationships where legitimate processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, explorer.exe) are spawned by atypical parents (PowerShell, rundll32, cmd) with blank/mismatched command lines. Monitor for VirtualAlloc + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread patterns. Alert on image sections inconsistent with expected binaries.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Cookie Exfiltration (SilentRunLoader)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Python-based loader and information stealer called SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' Deployed against UK entities via government impersonation lures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-Chrome processes accessing Chrome user profile directories (Local State, Default/Profile*/Cookies, Preferences, Login Data). Correlate with Python interpreter execution, suspicious network traffic post-access, or exfiltration to unexpected IPs. Flag SQLite file reads on Chrome databases.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Remote Access Tool Deployment (AnyDesk/SyncFuture)
suggestion.rationale: Article: RomulusLoader 'deploys legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture.' SyncFuture is 'remote monitoring software tool popular in China'—abuse of legitimate tools for C2/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AnyDesk/SyncFuture installation from non-standard directories (Temp, ProgramData, user Downloads) or with suspicious parent processes (loaders, scheduled tasks, WMI). Correlate with prior process injection activity. Flag geographic anomalies (SyncFuture in non-China regions). Monitor for outbound connections post-installation.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Initial Access (Payroll, VAT, Tax, Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Uses localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications. Also contacts via WhatsApp, LINE, and Microsoft Teams.' Primary attack vector with regional targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with subjects matching localized lures: regex patterns for 'Payroll|VAT|Steuer|Tasse|Imposta|Government.*Compliance|Tax.*Audit' targeting Germany, Italy, UK, South Africa recipients. Alert on file attachments (doc, docx, zip, exe) from external senders. Monitor Teams/WhatsApp for mass unsolicited contact attempts with government/payroll messaging from external actors.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Multi-Modal Collection (Keylog, Screenshot, Audio/Video)
suggestion.rationale: Article: Atlas RAT 'Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording' capabilities; 'capabilities of the malware include the potential for surveillance.' Distinct collection behaviors requiring monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process access to audio/video drivers (mmsys.cpl, wasapi.dll, video codec DLLs) from non-media processes. Detect keylogging patterns: processes loading user32.dll + GetAsyncKeyState/GetKeyState calls, or writing to files named *log*, *key*, *cap*. Alert on GDI/DirectX screen capture API usage from suspicious parents. Correlate collection behaviors with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer' as affected product; canonical first step for any KEV entry is locating all instances in fleet. Product string and vendor are directly extractable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer in package managers, installed software inventory, web server configs, or HTTP response headers. Scan for /app/code/Mirasvit/PageCacheWarmer in webroot. Cross-correlate with external vulnerability scanner reports for CVE-2026-45247 detection.

suggestion.title: Malicious CacheWarmer Cookie - Serialized PHP Object Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' Serialized PHP objects contain predictable byte patterns detectable in access logs and WAF events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CacheWarmer cookie values for PHP serialization markers (O: for object, a: for array, \x00 null bytes in encoded form). Flag anomalous cookie lengths (>500 bytes) and suspicious encoding patterns. Correlate requests with malicious payloads to source IP reputation and geolocation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Process Execution from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection of child processes spawned from PHP/web server context is standard RCE containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual child process spawning from php, apache, nginx, or tomcat processes on hosts running Mirasvit. Flag unexpected outbound connections from web server processes to external C2 indicators. Monitor for file writes to /tmp, cron.d, webroot, or script directories from web context within 10 minutes of CacheWarmer cookie ingestion.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Coverage for CVE-2026-45247
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and 'worth one quick check...scanners say not vulnerable.' Verifying scanner detection capability and false-negative rate is prerequisite for patch validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Confirm vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, OpenVAS) have active signatures for CVE-2026-45247. Cross-reference scanner reports against asset inventory for Mirasvit instances; alert on 'not vulnerable' verdicts for unpatched versions. Validate scanner fingerprinting accuracy on known-vulnerable test instances.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Privilege Escalation (CVE-2025-48595)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-48595 'is a high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework, which can be leveraged for increased privileges' with 'limited targeted exploitation in the wild.' This is an active privilege escalation attack requiring detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework processes for abnormal memory access patterns or crashes consistent with integer overflow. Alert on framework services obtaining elevated privileges or unexpected capability grants without corresponding system operation.

suggestion.title: Linux Container Escape via cgroups v1 Privilege Escalation (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2022-0492 as enabling attackers to 'bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' This is a critical container escape vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes writing to cgroup.event_control or release_agent paths. Alert on unprivileged processes spawning children with UID 0 or container processes accessing host-level resources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized cgroup_release_agent Function Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'the cgroup_release_agent_write() function of the cgroups v1 subsystem' with 'insufficient authentication checks' as the attack vector. This function is the precise exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel audit logs for open/write syscalls to cgroup v1 pseudo-filesystem paths from non-root processes. Correlate with subsequent execve calls with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Namespace Isolation Boundary Crossing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the vulnerability 'can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation' — container processes escaping namespace boundaries is a critical defense evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes accessing or spawning processes outside their PID/IPC/network namespace. Alert on parent processes with PPID pointing to host init or kernel subsystems.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email to Geographic Target Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 'expands phishing attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa'—campaign explicitly targets specific geographies. No use case generated to detect regionally-targeted email campaigns or recipient-geoip correlation with threat actor victimology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email campaigns where recipient domain registration or organizational presence is concentrated in UK, Germany, Italy, or South Africa with poor sender reputation, spoofed/lookalike domains, and credential-harvesting indicators.
