suggestion.title: Office Macro Execution Post-Phishing Email
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns typically deliver Office attachments; article mentions 'phishing attacks' but no detection rule for malicious macro execution or child-process spawning from Office applications following external email receipt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerShell ISE) opening files from external email and immediately spawning shell processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, certutil.exe). Flag execution within 5 minutes of file open as high-confidence phishing-driven compromise.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Phishing inherently targets credential harvesting; no use case for detecting fake login-form submissions or credential input to external/untrusted authentication pages post-email click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate URL clicks from phishing emails with submissions to credential-harvesting domains (typosquatted Office 365/SSO pages, form-based phishing kits). Alert on POST requests to external domains containing 'username', 'password', or 'email' parameters within 30 minutes of phishing email receipt.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Login Activity from Phishing-Targeted Accounts
suggestion.rationale: TA4922 phishing campaign implies credential compromise; no detection for post-compromise login anomalies (impossible travel, off-hours access, unusual geolocations) from targeted users within 24-72 hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify accounts targeted in TA4922 geographic scope and flag logins from UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa with impossible-travel distances from user baseline, multi-failed RDP/IMAP attempts, and concurrent session anomalies.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Phishing-Delivery Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Phishing is a delivery vector; no detection for secondary-payload command-and-control communication. Article describes attacks but not detection for infected-host callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from hosts that opened phishing attachments to suspicious external IPs/domains (non-white-listed ASNs, newly registered domains, fast-flux indicators). Correlate DNS queries for unusual domains with Office process execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: Magento Cache Warmer RCE - Exploitation Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited in real-world attacks'; attackers must make HTTP requests to the vulnerable endpoint
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento web servers for POST/GET requests to Cache Warmer paths (e.g., /mirasvit/cache/warmer, /cache/warmer). Correlate request timestamps with process creation events on the same host. Alert if request patterns match known exploit payloads or unusual HTTP methods/content-type headers.

suggestion.title: PHP Insecure Deserialization - Untrusted Object Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'insecure deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism; this is the execution pathway
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes executing unserialize() calls with untrusted input following HTTP requests to Mirasvit endpoints. Flag PHP spawning child processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe) within milliseconds of suspicious deserialization. Correlate web request timestamps with unexpected child process creation under web server UID.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution - Post-Exploitation Shell Activity
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45247 explicitly enables RCE; real-world exploitation necessarily involves command execution post-vulnerability trigger
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections initiated by PHP/Apache processes following Cache Warmer endpoint access. Monitor for suspicious command-line arguments (curl, wget, nc, whoami, id) executed by web server processes. Flag cron/at job modifications originating from web server context.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Extension Suspicious Parameter Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension' by name; exploitation likely passes malicious serialized objects via request parameters
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Mirasvit extension paths containing PHP serialization markers ('O:', 's:', 'a:' prefixes) in query strings or POST bodies. Baseline legitimate Cache Warmer request patterns; alert on requests with unusual parameter names, excessive payload sizes, or suspicious object class names.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against CVE-2026-20230 Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—requires detection of attack traffic matching known payload signatures against Unified CM endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco Unified CM (ports 8080, 8443, 6970) for POST requests containing CVE-2026-20230 exploit payloads. Alert on requests to vulnerable administrative endpoints with malformed or injected parameters matching known POC signatures.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Cisco Unified CM Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article references unpatched systems as attack surface. Detect inventory of vulnerable versions before exploitation window closes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Unified CM systems running affected versions (pre-patch baseline TBD from CVE details). Flag systems with version strings matching vulnerable range; escalate based on network exposure and time-since-patch-release.

suggestion.title: Public Exploit Repository Activity for CVE-2026-20230
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes public exploit availability. Threat intel must track exploit repository commits, Metasploit module updates, PoC GitHub repos to measure threat maturity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily query for CVE-2026-20230, variant spellings, and product keywords across ExploitDB, Metasploit, GitHub. Capture POC publication date, update frequency, and functional claims. Correlate with org patching velocity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Patch Application Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article announces patch availability ('Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230'). Track deployment to measure remediation effectiveness post-disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on absence of patch installation >30 days after advisory publication. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results (e.g., Nessus) against deployed versions. Flag systems in high-risk zones (DMZ, customer-facing) that remain unpatched.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Behavior on Compromised Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit availability raises risk of post-compromise activity (persistence, lateral movement, data exfil). Standard post-breach indicators should apply to Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For systems showing successful exploitation, monitor outbound connections to uncommon destinations, internal port scanning activity, suspicious logons to adjacent VoIP/collaboration servers, and extraction of call recordings or user credentials from Unified CM database.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Remote SSRF Exploitation via WebDialer
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device' and explicitly names SSRF as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection for the HTTP attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoints for SSRF indicators: malformed Host headers, file:// protocol references, internal IP addresses in request parameters, or requests attempting to access local files or internal services. WebDialer is disabled by default; any traffic to /webdialer/* paths warrants investigation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Writes from Unified CM Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allowing attackers to 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' Pipeline missed the file write phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file write activity originating from Cisco Unified CM service processes (java, tomcat) to directories outside normal application scope: /tmp, /var/spool, /etc, or other system paths. Baseline normal CM file write patterns and flag deviations, particularly writes to executable or script directories.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Cisco Unified CM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes exploit 'could result in an attacker elevating privileges to root' and describes written files as mechanism for privilege escalation. No detection use case for the privilege elevation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation to root originating from Unified CM-related processes, including setuid execution, sudo invocations, or exploitation of written scripts/binaries in world-writable directories. Correlate with prior file writes from CM processes to establish exploit chain.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WebDialer Service Enablement on Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WebDialer is disabled by default' and provides remediation: 'disable the WebDialer service.' Pipeline should detect enablement of this normally-disabled, vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any enablement of Cisco WebDialer service (CTI Services > Cisco WebDialer Web Service) on Unified CM systems. Establish baseline of which systems should have WebDialer enabled and flag unexpected activations. Monitor Cisco Unified Serviceability logs for service state changes.

suggestion.title: HTTP to Root Escalation Chain - CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes continuous attack flow from HTTP request through file write to root access. Pipeline failed to map the correlated chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious HTTP requests to WebDialer endpoints with subsequent unexpected file writes from Unified CM processes and root-level privilege escalation attempts within a 5-minute window. This three-stage correlation (HTTP anomaly → file write → privilege escalation) is characteristic of CVE-2026-20230 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded SSH Credential Access to Unified CM Root
suggestion.rationale: Article cross-references: 'Cisco warns that Unified CM has hardcoded root SSH credentials.' Pipeline should capture SSH-based compromise of root account via default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH authentication attempts to Unified CM systems using default/hardcoded root credentials. Flag successful root SSH sessions from unusual source IPs or time-of-day patterns. Correlate failed SSH attempts followed by successful escalation as potential exploitation pattern.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Action Triggered by External Issue
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'One Malicious Issue Hijack Repositories' — external actors create issues triggering workflows with elevated permissions. Pipeline missed the initial-access vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Action workflow executions triggered by issues or pull requests from external/untrusted identities. Correlate with actions that access or export GITHUB_TOKEN, modify repository settings, or write to protected branches.

suggestion.title: GITHUB_TOKEN Exfiltration via Action Environment
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking implies credential theft. Workflow 'flaw' enables token leakage — article context implies GITHUB_TOKEN compromise as the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Action jobs exporting GITHUB_TOKEN to env, logging secrets, or exfiltrating tokens via curl/wget to external URLs. Monitor for unusual network calls from action runners to unauthenticated endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Hijacking via Compromised Action
suggestion.rationale: Explicit threat in title — repository hijacking. Pipeline failed to flag repository mutation patterns: branch rule bypass, admin role grants, deployment key injection, or secret modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or deletion of branch protections, admin role assignments, deploy key additions, or secret modifications executed by GitHub Actions workflows immediately after or during issue-triggered runs.

suggestion.title: Workflow File Injection via Issue or Pull Request Comment
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking mechanism implies action flaw in parsing user input. Article phrase 'one malicious issue' suggests issue-template or workflow YAML manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to `.github/workflows/*.yml` files or issue templates immediately before/after malicious issue creation. Flag action jobs executing `run:` steps with curl, script injection, or command substitution patterns.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via GitHub Secrets Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking requires exfiltration of deployment credentials, API keys, or OIDC tokens stored in repository secrets. Pipeline omitted secrets-access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows listing secrets via `secrets` context object, GitHub API enumeration, or environment variable dumping. Correlate with network egress to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Poisoning via Compromised GitHub Action Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Flaw 'lets one issue hijack repositories' — likely affects shared actions or workflows imported by other repos. Pipeline missed the supply-chain amplification vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repositories importing vulnerable actions for unusual downstream workflow modifications, token usage, or repository access after the vulnerability date. Track action version pinning changes and unexpected step additions.

suggestion.title: GTM Container Loads Malicious Function Code
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code is 'embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page' and uses 'new Function()' to execute reassembled JavaScript from Stripe metadata. This is explicit code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM containers for loader scripts that execute unfamiliar Function() calls or reassemble code from external metadata. Alert when GTM script loads payload that queries specific Stripe customer records (pattern: api.stripe.com/v1/customers/cus_*) and extracts metadata for code execution.

suggestion.title: Stripe Customer Record Abuse for Data Exfiltration Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'creating a new Stripe customer object and storing the stolen data in metadata fields. Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend.' Customer ID cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR created Dec 24, 2025.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Stripe account activity showing rapid sequential customer record creation with no associated transactions or purchase context. Flag metadata fields containing obfuscated binary or XOR patterns. Correlate with checkout page skimming if possible.

suggestion.title: XOR-obfuscated Payment Data in Local Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally instead of immediately exfiltrated.' localStorage keys include _d_data_customer_ variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor checkout page context for suspicious localStorage writes immediately after payment form interaction. Flag keys matching _d_data* or similar patterns. Detect XOR byte patterns (repeating key material XOR'd with consecutive bytes produces predictable entropy signatures).

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Abuse for Malware Payload Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article documents variant using 'Google Firestore, a cloud database service, where the payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' Names crafted to 'blend in with legitimate payment and bot-protection traffic.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Firestore read patterns where payment/checkout JavaScript initiates reads to documents in projects named *payment-app, especially paths matching tracking/* or captcha/*. Flag documents returned with 140+ byte binary blobs in fields that normally contain minimal config.

suggestion.title: Trusted Domain Abuse – Stripe/GTM Pass Through Network Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Both the payload and the stolen cards move through api.stripe.com. Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters that would otherwise flag traffic to an unknown skimmer domain.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to api.stripe.com that deviate from normal payment-flow patterns: payloads containing serialized customer records, metadata updates without associated transaction initiation, or requests from non-Stripe-integrated checkout contexts.

suggestion.title: Checkout Page Credential Harvesting – Form Interception Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.' Activation 'when a shopper reaches a checkout page.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor checkout JavaScript for DOM listeners attached to payment form fields post-load. Flag scripts that fire on form submit events and collect input values matching PAN, expiration, CVV, name patterns, then POST to external URLs (especially Stripe/Firestore). Cross-reference with GTM container load timing.

suggestion.title: Database Bulk Export Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 234 GB of data stolen—a massive exfiltration requiring abnormal database access patterns. No detection rule generated for this critical activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database systems for unusual SELECT queries returning abnormally large result sets, bulk exports of patient records (names, IDs, government-issued IDs, insurance data), and execution of export utilities. Alert on non-standard service accounts or admin accounts exporting data outside normal business patterns.

suggestion.title: Large Outbound Data Transfer Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: 234 GB exfiltration indicates massive sustained data movement. Article implies transfer out of network but no detection for unusual outbound volume is captured: 'took immediate action to secure our environment, contain the attack.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for typical outbound volume from healthcare systems. Alert on sustained high-volume connections to non-approved cloud storage, file-sharing services, or known ShinyHunters/exfiltration infrastructure. Track for anomalous data staging followed by rapid transfer.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Patient Data Systems
suggestion.rationale: Attackers achieved 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' then accessed PII databases. Attack step from initial foothold to data repositories is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual login patterns to database servers and healthcare applications (DentaQuest patient records systems). Alert on privilege escalation, service-account abuse, or admin tools accessed from non-admin machines. Track for access to systems outside user baseline.

suggestion.title: Initial Public-Facing Application Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach via 'unauthorized access' but does not detail entry vector. For a company serving 35M customers with public patient portals, initial compromise likely exploited public-facing app. This attack phase is unrepresented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor patient portals, provider APIs, and web-facing applications for exploitation attempts: SQL injection patterns, unexpected file uploads, path traversal probes, authentication bypass attempts, and anomalous API call sequences. Track for high failed login attempts followed by successful access.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Transfer of 234 GB requires pre-exfiltration staging. Article implies multi-step process but no detection for file staging, compression, or aggregation activities is captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of unusually large temporary files, invocation of compression utilities (7z, rar, tar, zip) on non-standard accounts, and movement of data to staging directories. Alert on archive activities on database servers or healthcare data repositories, especially outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: DNS/Web Query – Typosquatted Open-Source Tool Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google'—homographic/homophonic lookalike domains are the primary attack entry point. Pipeline should have generated detection for lookalike registrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS requests and web proxies for queries to domains similar to popular open-source repos (pip, npm, cargo, golang) using character substitution (0 for O, 1 for I, etc.), homograph abuse, or homophone variants. Flag requests with high edit distance from known legitimate domains.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System (TDS) – Conditional Malware Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Deliver Malware via TDS'—TDS is the delivery mechanism. Pipeline should have generated detection for 30x redirect chains and device-fingerprinting-based payload selection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious HTTP redirect chains (301/302) from lookalike domains with User-Agent probing patterns, OS/browser version checks in request headers, and conditional payloads. Flag rapid redirects to different endpoints based on device fingerprinting parameters.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution Post-Download from Fake Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery to end users. Should detect process execution of files downloaded from typosquatted domains, especially script interpreters or installers spawned from Temp/Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web-download events (proxy/AV logs) from lookalike domains with subsequent process creation events. Flag execution of installers, script interpreters, or LOLBins (certutil, msiexec, powershell) spawned within 5 seconds of downloads from fake open-source sites.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning – Bulk Domain Registration with Rapid Google Indexing
suggestion.rationale: For sites to 'Rank High on Google', attackers must register domains in bulk and accelerate indexing. Pipeline should detect SEO-poisoning infrastructure: new domain cohorts, Search Console abuse, backlink injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clusters of newly registered domains (within 30 days) with typosquatted open-source tool names. Correlate with bulk URL submissions to Google Search Console, botnet SEO-traffic patterns, and hosting on known bulletproof hosters.

suggestion.title: Phishing via Google Search Results – SERP Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes users finding malicious sites through Google search results (via ranking manipulation). Should detect Google Search Console account abuse, bulk indexing requests, and anomalous referrer traffic from search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Search Console for suspicious account activity: bulk URL indexing requests for newly registered domains, subdomain takeover attempts, and Search Analytics queries for terms matching real open-source tool names. Correlate with spike in organic-referrer web traffic to lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Malvertising redirect chain to malware download
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' as delivery vector—this is initial access T1598.003. Pipeline ignored the ad-network-as-attack-surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network redirects from legitimate ad networks (Google, YouTube) to unknown/suspicious domains, especially when followed by file download. Correlate with subsequent process execution of unusual binaries in temp directories or user cache folders.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell process execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Malware name and platform are clear from title; no detection generated. Pipeline should map malware family name to process/binary signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of FlutterShell binary or variants by unusual parent processes (browsers, downloaders). Look for suspicious dylib loading, code injection into legitimate macOS processes, or unsigned/untrusted code execution.

suggestion.title: macOS logon item or LaunchAgent persistence by FlutterShell
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates backdoor spread on macOS but pipeline omitted persistence tactics. macOS-specific: Login Items, LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons (T1547.001, T1547.014).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of ~/.config/autostart, ~/Library/LaunchAgents, or /Library/LaunchDaemons by processes spawned from browser or download locations. Monitor for plist files with suspicious command lines or dynamic linker hijacking (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES).

suggestion.title: Suspicious browser plugin or extension installation from malvertising
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising frequently leads to browser extension/plugin injection for persistence and data exfiltration. Article silent on this but standard for ad-driven malware on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected writes to browser extension/plugin directories (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) immediately after suspicious ad-domain visits. Correlate parent process (browser) and child process (installer/downloader).

suggestion.title: C2 callback from FlutterShell backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'backdoor' but no C2 detection use case generated. Pipeline must map malware family to expected command-and-control signatures (domains, IPs, protocols).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from processes spawned by malvertising or with FlutterShell indicators to non-standard ports or obfuscated domains. Watch for beaconing patterns, unusual protocols over HTTP/HTTPS, or DNS queries to suspicious TLDs.

suggestion.title: Browser/downloader child process spawning elevated/unsigned binaries
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising delivery typically ends with process execution from user-writable locations. Pipeline should detect browser→download→execute chain without whitelisting typical executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation chains where browser or downloader utility spawns unsigned or minimally-signed binaries from /tmp, ~/Downloads, ~/Library/Caches, or /var/folders. Elevated child processes from user-spawned parents are high-risk.

suggestion.title: Stata command-injection signature in process arguments (log_file_name parameter with escape sequences)
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'log_file_name parameter... directly interpolated into a Stata command string without sanitization.' Pipeline generated zero UCs detecting the actual injection artifact—the parameter itself containing quotes, semicolons, or escaped newlines (\n, \r) that break out of Stata string context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Stata or stata_mcp/stata_do process spawned with command-line arguments containing log_file_name followed by values with shell metacharacters, quote-nesting patterns, or newline escape sequences. Example: log_file_name=test.log'; shell 'whoami'# This is the actual exploitation vector before downstream shell/python spawning.

suggestion.title: Malicious Stata do-file execution or delivery (T1204.002 User Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1204.002 as mapped MITRE technique but generated zero UC for it. Vulnerability impacts any user executing a Stata do-file (.do script) with injected log_file_name—yet pipeline has no detection for suspicious do-file delivery, unusual execution context, or do-file content with injection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .do files created in temp directories (/tmp, %TEMP%), by web application processes, or with names containing special characters; or Stata processes invoked with do-file arguments pointing to suspicious paths. Correlate with process creation timing and source process context to identify social-engineering or delivery scenarios.

suggestion.title: File discovery/enumeration via Stata shell injection (T1083 detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) and states attacker can inject 'shell' commands, yet pipeline generated no UC detecting shell execution with enumeration intent (dir, ls, find, stat, glob patterns) spawned from Stata context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell processes (cmd.exe, bash, sh) spawned as children of Stata processes with command lines containing directory listing or file-find keywords (dir, ls, ls -la, find, stat, glob, list, dir /s). This post-exploitation reconnaissance pattern indicates successful injection leading to filesystem reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Stata process spawning Python with command-injection patterns in arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can inject 'python' commands via log_file_name. UC_4_2 detects shell spawning but misses Python—a common attack path for data exfiltration or secondary payload execution. Pipeline should detect python processes with suspicious parentage or argument patterns indicating injected code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python process spawned as child of Stata with command-line arguments containing shell operators (subprocess.call, os.system, shell=True), quoted/escaped strings suggesting injected payloads, or unusual import statements (socket, requests, subprocess). Correlates with CVE-2026-47708 exploitation for secondary code execution.

suggestion.title: Stata command injection kill-chain reconstruction (initial attack parameter → execution → impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article contains no kill-chain reconstruction despite describing complete exploitation sequence. Pipeline listed blank kill chain while article clearly describes: (1) attacker-controlled input (log_file_name parameter), (2) unsafe interpolation into command string, (3) arbitrary command execution. This should map to exploitation → command execution → potential file destruction or data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Synthesize kill chain from: (1) Stata process spawned with suspicious log_file_name argument (exploitation), (2) shell/python child process spawned (execution), (3) subsequent file operations (erase/rm) or data-read operations. Multi-stage detection improves confidence and filters noise from single-stage alerts.

suggestion.title: Typosquat domain access by impersonated tool name
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creating convincing fake websites that impersonate popular security tools' + domains like 'ghidralite.com', 'dnspy.org', 'ilspy.org'. Pipeline missed the impersonation pattern entirely. Should detect web access to known typosquats of Ghidra, dnSpy, SpiderFoot in near real-time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag web requests (DNS, HTTP/HTTPS) to domains that are character-similarity matches or typosquats of known security tools (Ghidra, dnSpy, SpiderFoot). Correlate to external source (non-org OSINT tools). High fidelity if user has no legitimate reason to access obscure tool mirrors.

suggestion.title: Download-to-execution correlation from non-trusted domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The moment a user clicks the download button, something very different happens behind [...]'. Pipeline provided generic UC but no specific hunt for: file downloaded from phishing domain → executable spawned within seconds. This is the core malware delivery pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: HTTP GET/download from phishing domain → FileCreated event → Process execution of that file within 30 seconds on same endpoint. High fidelity if domain is not whitelisted and executable is not digitally signed by known publisher.

suggestion.title: Mismatch between downloaded tool binary and legitimate project hash
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'links pointing to actual GitHub repositories' suggests attacker misdirects to fake binary. Could detect: user downloads 'Ghidra.exe' from ghidralite.com, but hash does not match official NSA Ghidra distribution hash on GitHub/VirusTotal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract SHA256 of downloaded files with tool-like names (ghidra, dnspy, spiderfoot) and compare against known-good hashes from official GitHub/SourceForge releases. Flag if hash does not match and file was downloaded from suspicious domain. Requires maintained hash baseline.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to typosquat security-tool domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: fake sites have 'professional designs' and likely lure users to 'login' or enter credentials to download. No detection suggested for credential harvesting on fake project sites. Would be high-value signal of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to phishing domains with body containing 'password', 'credentials', 'token' parameters, or requests to fake login pages (e.g., /login, /signin) on typosquat domains. Correlate POST to domain access from earlier UC. Very high fidelity.

suggestion.title: Outlook Mailbox Accessed from Unusual Geolocation or IP
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker maintained access for 'five months'—persistent mailbox intrusion requires initial compromise followed by ongoing access. Anomalous login detection is foundational. Cite: 'Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful Outlook/OWA logins from IP addresses or geographies inconsistent with the executive's known patterns, especially if preceded by failed login attempts. Correlate with multi-factor authentication bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Forwarding Rule Creation or Modification (Attacker-Controlled)
suggestion.rationale: Five-month access suggests persistence mechanism beyond initial credential theft. Forwarding rules are a classic mailbox persistence technique used to exfiltrate emails automatically. Cite: 'Hackers Spied' implies ongoing, automated collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of mailbox rules that forward emails outside the organization, especially when created from a non-standard client or during off-hours. Correlate with new delegated access grants.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Export or Unusual Mailbox Search Activity
suggestion.rationale: The intrusion sustained for five months suggests systematic collection of sensitive communications. Stock exchange executive emails likely contain material non-public information. Cite: 'Spied on' implies comprehensive email theft, not isolated access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk mailbox exports, mass message searches (e.g., SearchQueryInitiatedEx events with large result sets), or downloads of archive PST files. Flag activity performed by the compromised account at atypical times or from new clients.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Theft via Phishing (Mailbox-Specific)
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated mailbox intrusion targeting a senior executive likely involved initial phishing for credentials or OAuth tokens rather than brute force. Cite: 'Hackers' succeeded in targeting a named, high-value individual.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious OAuth consent grants or unusual service principal activity accessing mail resources. Correlate with phishing email campaigns to the executive or adjacent accounts. Flag token refresh from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Delegate Access Granted to Executive Mailbox by Attacker
suggestion.rationale: Alternative to forwarding rules, attackers may grant mailbox access to attacker-controlled accounts to maintain persistence and access. This requires mailbox permission modification. Cite: 'Five months' persistence suggests multiple access mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Add-MailboxPermission or Set-MailboxPermission events that grant SendAs, SendOnBehalf, or FullAccess rights to the executive's mailbox from unexpected admin accounts or during off-hours. Cross-reference with user lifecycle data.

suggestion.title: Multi-Account Mailbox Compromise within Same Timeframe (Campaign Scope)
suggestion.rationale: A five-month campaign against a single high-value target suggests part of a broader operation. Detect other compromised mailboxes in the organization with overlapping access patterns. Cite: 'Stock Exchange Executive' implies organizational context where other accounts may be compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate mailbox audit logs across the organization to identify clusters of accounts with anomalous access patterns (unusual IPs, failed logins followed by success, forwarding rule creation) within the same 5-month window. Flag coordinated campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download from Malicious Installer Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attack entry point: 'fake installer pages' and 'spoofed Anthropic install page,' yet pipeline generated no detection for malicious downloads from documented domains (download.version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of executable files (.exe, .msi, .zip, .ps1) from domains matching suspicious patterns (typosquatting legitimate vendors, .ru TLDs with suspicious registrations, version-number naming schemes). Correlate with HTTP referrer logs to identify users following SEO-poisoned search results to malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication via Malicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article documents infostealer must exfiltrate stolen credentials to C2; three domains provided (download.version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru, 185.177.239.255) but pipeline generated zero network IOC hunts despite article explicitly recommending them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from internal systems to known malicious IPs (185.177.239.255) and C2 domains (download.version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru). Inspect HTTPS traffic for SNI hostname mismatches. Monitor for suspicious DNS queries to newly-registered .ru domains or typosquatting patterns.

suggestion.title: .NET Runtime Suspicious Execution in Non-CLR Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'fileless .NET Infostealer' but pipeline generated no behavioral detections for .NET malware execution or in-memory CLR loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .NET Framework DLLs (clr.dll, clrjit.dll, System.dll) loading into processes where they are not expected (e.g., non-.NET host processes). Detect use of Living-off-the-Land compilers (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, roslyn) launching child processes or invoking suspicious PowerShell. Monitor for suspicious assembly reflective-loading patterns.

suggestion.title: Search Engine Referrer to Malicious Installer Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'SEO poisoning to push spoofed Anthropic install page to top of search results' — distinct from generic phishing, this is a search-engine-driven malware delivery mechanism not covered by existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web proxy logs for requests originating from legitimate search engine referrers (google.com, bing.com referrer headers) to suspicious domains (download.version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru). High-volume traffic from search referrers to newly-registered or suspicious domains in short time window indicates SEO poisoning campaign.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Campaign — Suspicious Download Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications' — initial access vector requires rules to detect suspicious ad campaigns and malware delivery landing pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on ads promoting desktop applications, particularly those linking to adsparkpro.* or sinterfumesco.com domains. Alert on rapid sequence of ad click → landing page load → executable download. Flag ads promoting well-known applications (Slack, Discord, etc.) with uncommon download sources.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Malformed Application Bundle Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake desktop applications' being executed — T1036 masquerading requires macOS-specific rules detecting spoofed applications with mismatched code signatures or suspicious bundle structure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned Mach-O binaries or application bundles with code-signing certificates from untrusted developers. Flag processes where bundle name matches legitimate software (Slack, Zoom, Chrome) but code signature or bundle identifier differs. Monitor for execution from nested Contents/MacOS paths within recently-downloaded applications.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Hits — FlutterShell Backdoor SHA256 Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article provides nine specific SHA256 hashes but pipeline generated no file-based detection rules matching these hashes despite 'high-fidelity' IOC label.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create detection rules for all nine provided SHA256 values: alert on file hash matches anywhere on macOS systems, with priority on Downloads/Caches/temp directories. Correlate file presence with parent process execution (browser, installer, application bundle). Escalate if hash appears in process memory or loaded modules.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation — LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'secretly install a powerful backdoor' implying persistence mechanisms, but no rules generated for detecting persistence installation typical of macOS backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation in ~/.config/LaunchAgents/, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, /Library/LaunchDaemons/. Alert on .plist files with RunAtLoad=true and Program references to shell scripts or obfuscated executables. Correlate creation events with execution of suspicious application bundles or nine malware hashes in same process tree.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to FlutterBridge Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Eight domains explicitly listed (atsheisdomestic.org, etoftheappyrince.org, healightejustb.org, sinterfumesco.com, ads-parkpro.com, adsparkpro.top, adsparkpro.net, softwe.art) but no network-based detection rule generated mapping to backdoor communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or TCP/UDP connections to any of the eight C2 domains from macOS endpoints. Flag persistent or periodic connections indicating automated beaconing. Correlate with process ancestry chain linking to application bundle execution and malware hashes. Monitor for both direct connections and DNS-over-HTTPS bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Backdoor Unpacking — Entropy-based Malware Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1027 (Obfuscation) but no behavioral detection rules generated for identifying obfuscated/encrypted payloads within application bundles or process memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze Mach-O binaries in application bundles for encrypted sections, high-entropy data, or anomalous segment layouts. Monitor process memory for decryption loops (repeated calls to libcrypto functions). Alert on suspicious API imports (dlopen, _dyld_get_image_slide) combined with large encrypted data chunks. Apply string obfuscation detection on stripped binaries.

suggestion.title: Firewall Connection to KongTuke C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article case study explicitly documents outbound ConnectionEvents to 144.31.221.82 on port 6060 with URL path /capcha9856, identified as TDS-based C2 compromise. 'The firewall gave us the "what" and "when"—a specific device was reaching out to known-bad infrastructure at a known time.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to 144.31.221.82:6060 or similar TDS infrastructure patterns. In Splunk, correlate firewall logs with known C2 IP repositories. In Defender KQL, match DeviceNetworkEvents with ThreatIntelIndicatorType = 'C2' and direction = 'Outbound'.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Encoded Command with Web Request Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article case study demonstrates cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand parameter containing Base64 payload, followed by Invoke-WebRequest to fetch script.ps1. 'The endpoint telemetry revealed: A cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe → powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand, decode and inspect for Invoke-WebRequest or suspicious URLs. Alert on ApplicationData downloads of .ps1 files. Splunk: search for (ParentImage=cmd.exe ChildImage=powershell.exe) AND (CommandLine contains '-EncodedCommand'). Defender KQL: DeviceProcessEvents where InitiatingProcessFileName == 'cmd.exe' and FileName == 'powershell.exe' and ProcessCommandLine contains '-EncodedCommand'.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Anti-Forensics: Remove-Item Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article case study documents Remove-Item cleanup attempts following malicious script execution. 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' This is defense evasion following C2 activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious PowerShell execution with subsequent Remove-Item or del commands targeting recently downloaded files in temp/ApplicationData directories. Alert on file deletion immediately after PowerShell execution. Splunk: sequence maxspan=5m [search ProcessName=powershell.exe] [search CommandLine='*Remove-Item*']. Defender KQL: DeviceFileEvents where Action == 'FileDeleted' and InitiatingProcessName == 'powershell.exe' within 5 minutes of encoded command execution.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC Living-Off-The-Land for C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious ASNs as a hunt hypothesis. 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for MSIEXEC User-Agent in network logs making outbound connections to malicious or poorly-rated ASNs. Baseline legitimate MSIEXEC usage (package updates, deployment) and alert on deviations. Splunk: search http_user_agent='*msiexec*' AND (asn_reputation='malicious' OR asn_abuse_score>threshold). Defender KQL: DeviceNetworkEvents where HttpUserAgent contains 'msiexec' and RemoteIPThreatIntelCategory contains 'Malware' or 'C2'.

suggestion.title: DGA Detection via Statistical Entropy Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DGA detection as a core AI-driven hunt hypothesis. 'Domain generation algorithm (DGA) detection via AI/ML. Algorithmically generated domains have statistical properties (character distribution, entropy, n-gram frequency) that distinguish them from human-registered domains. Our models flag DNS queries that match these patterns.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build statistical models of domain character entropy, n-gram frequency, and entropy to baseline legitimate domains vs. algorithmically generated ones. Alert on DNS queries matching DGA statistical signatures. Splunk: calculate entropy of domain names and alert on high entropy + high n-gram disorder. Defender KQL: DeviceDnsEvents where DomainName matches pattern with entropy > 3.5 and character_distribution_variance > threshold.

suggestion.title: Multi-Domain Correlation: EDR Process Tree + Firewall C2 Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the methodology of correlating firewall and EDR telemetry. The case study shows firewall alone saw 'outbound connection to a suspicious IP...not conclusive on its own' but EDR saw obfuscated PowerShell 'but without network context...it could be a false positive.' Together they 'told a complete story.' This is a critical correlation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join EDR process execution data (PowerShell with suspicious indicators) with firewall network logs on the same device and timestamp. Alert when both sources confirm the attack chain: suspicious process execution + outbound connection to known-bad IP on same host within minutes. Splunk: join type=inner DeviceProcessEvents firewall_events on [DeviceIP, timestamp]. Defender KQL: DeviceProcessEvents where (PowerShellCommandLine contains '-EncodedCommand' or FileName='powershell.exe' with suspicious parent) joined with DeviceNetworkEvents where RemoteIP in C2_list within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp execution during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states attack spreads 'via Phantom Gyp' and involves binding.gyp—the native module compilation mechanism. gyp post-install hooks are execution vector for payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node-gyp or gyp child processes spawned from npm install context with unusual command-line arguments. Flag binding.gyp modifications or execution of shell commands within gyp pre/post-build hooks that include network requests, recursive scanning, or code injection into sibling packages.

suggestion.title: Self-replicating package payload across node_modules hierarchy
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'self-spreading worm'—payload must modify or trojanize peer/dependent packages. Detect by monitoring for unauthorized package.json or binding.gyp edits originating from npm processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single npm install process generating multiple package.json write events across different directories in node_modules/. Alert on version downgrades, injected dependencies, or binding.gyp modifications in packages not directly invoked by the parent install.

suggestion.title: Network reconnaisance from npm package context during installation
suggestion.rationale: Worm spreading requires discovery of additional npm packages to compromise. Monitor for scanning or enumeration activity originating from install phase, as stated in article concept of 'self-spreading'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries or HTTP requests from node/npm processes during install targeting NPM registry, local node_modules enumeration, or bulk subdomain probing. Alert on unusual connection patterns that suggest package enumeration rather than legitimate dependency resolution.

suggestion.title: Post-install script execution with payload obfuscation indicators
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp pre/post-build scripts are a natural payload delivery mechanism in gyp-based attacks. Article mechanism implies obfuscated or indirect code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded, hex-encoded, or otherwise obfuscated shell commands within binding.gyp or package.json scripts. Alert on multi-stage payloads that decode/execute in memory or chain shell invocations across package lifecycle hooks.

suggestion.title: Compromised package version hash mismatch and rollback detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack modifies package contents after publication. Detect via npm package hash mismatches or unexpected version rollbacks that indicate trojanization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare npm package tarball hash against published metadata (package-lock.json, shrinkwrap). Alert when installed binary differs from registry hash or when package version reported by npm differs from on-disk manifest. Flag sudden version downgrades or rollbacks.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm package spread via dependency chain injection
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagates by inserting itself into dependent packages' dependency graphs. Title's 'self-spreading' mechanism requires modifying package.json dependencies to point to compromised or newly-injected packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package.json modifications that add unexpected devDependencies or dependencies on local/internal packages (especially those created during same install window). Alert on circular dependency injection or dependencies on packages with timestamps newer than parent package installation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Development Environment and Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'targets 86 environment variables (key-value pairs) and 20 credential files that may contain OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials, vault configuration files, SSH keys, and Exodus cryptocurrency wallet files.' Core attack capability with no corresponding detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes performing sequential or bulk reads of credential file paths (.ssh/config, .ssh/id_*, .aws/credentials, .env, .vault-token, Exodus wallet directories) or mass enumeration of environment variables within single process lifecycle. Flag when triggered by node process spawned from npm package preinstall hooks or unusual CI/CD contexts.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation via Preinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack payload 'executed via preinstall, pushing malicious commits' into repositories. Preinstall hooks are npm's first execution point during package installation; this attack vector has no detection UC despite being the initial execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package installations that spawn child processes with elevated privileges, perform filesystem reads outside expected package directory, enumerate credentials, or make network connections before package initialization completes. Alert especially on external registry sources or packages with recent version bumps from formerly inactive maintainers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Publishing from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Core persistence mechanism: malware 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow... publish trojanized versions of packages owned by the victim.' Named account 'asteroiddao' initiated attack; no UC for detecting anomalous publishing activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package publishing (especially version bumps) from accounts showing 90+ days inactivity, from geographically anomalous IPs, or using Trusted Publishing tokens from unexpected CI/CD environments. Correlate with recent SSH key generation, API token creation, or login anomalies in the same account.

suggestion.title: Backdated Git Commits for Investigation Timeline Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies evasion tactic: 'The commit author appears as "claude," and the timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Clear defense-evasion pattern with no detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag git commits where committer date is >6 months in the past but push timestamp is recent (within 24 hours), especially in production or high-value repositories. Specifically alert on commits authored by 'claude' or other suspicious names pushed to npm package repositories during account compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Serialized Secrets via GitHub Actions Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific exfiltration pipeline: malware 'serializes the secrets into a single value and then writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output. The last step of the process is uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.' This GitHub Actions-specific exfiltration channel has no UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows in public or recently-compromised repositories for artifact uploads occurring after credential access patterns detected. Flag small JSON or text artifacts uploaded to unusually permissive retention policies, especially those with serialized field names matching common credential formats (api_key, token, secret).

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Rootkit Loading from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit' as persistence mechanism. No UC addresses detection of unsigned or anomalous eBPF program loading from node.js or npm package execution contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bpf() syscalls from user-space processes spawned by node.js or npm package managers, especially those loading unsigned eBPF programs or programs lacking associated source files in the package directory. Correlate with anomalous network connections to non-standard ports or confirmed Tor exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Expansion in binding.gyp During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)\) form runs a shell command during the configure phase and substitutes its output into the build definition.' This is the novel execution vector bypassing preinstall/postinstall monitoring.
log_sources: ProcessCreation for node-gyp rebuild spawning unexpected shells
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install operations that extract binding.gyp files containing <!(...)\), $(...), or backtick command substitution patterns. Correlate presence with unexpected child process spawning (bash, sh, powershell, cmd) from node-gyp rebuild contexts where package.json lacks preinstall or postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Multi-Version Package Republishing from Single npm Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4' and 'single npm account...publishes the @jagreehal/\* scope and awaitly.' Worm republishes to all reachable packages under compromised jagreehal account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm accounts that publish multiple malformed versions (non-sequential jumps, same-minute duplicates across unrelated packages) or publish to both direct packages and @scoped namespaces in rapid succession. Correlate with zero manual release notes and git commit patterns lacking historical authorship.

suggestion.title: Developer and CI/CD Credential Harvesting During npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes' during install-time execution via binding.gyp payload.
log_sources: ProcessAccess / ReadFile for credential file paths
Environment variable reads during build phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from node-gyp rebuild for reads/opens of known credential storage: ~/.npm/*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, KUBECONFIG env var, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY env vars, HashiCorp Vault token paths, or GCP service account JSON. Flag any access outside normal developer workflow timing.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Actions Workflow Injection for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence' after obtaining GitHub credentials from compromised maintainers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new .github/workflows/* files committed to repositories shortly after npm install execution windows or credential harvesting events. Correlate commits with GitHub tokens leaked during that period, unusual committer IPs/geolocation, and workflows that access or re-export sensitive environment variables.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via GitHub Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories' by injecting harvested secrets into commits and pushing to actor-owned repos.
log_sources: git push logs with payload inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect git commits for credential patterns (AWS_SECRET_KEY=, GITHUB_TOKEN=, privateKey, etc.) committed during npm install windows. Correlate commits to private or attacker-owned GitHub repositories, unusual push origins (CI/CD runner IPs vs. developer IPs), and commits lacking legitimate PR/release context.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Bun-Based Loader Execution at Install Time
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'The payload: a multi-stage Bun-based loader' embedded in or triggered by binding.gyp, indicating a compiled or interpreted secondary-stage malware.
log_sources: ProcessCreation for bun binary or Bun runtime
Image load / DLL load for embedded Bun VM
Network connections from Bun child processes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Bun runtime execution (bun executable or interpreted Bun scripts) spawned as a child or sibling of node-gyp configure/build phases during npm install. Flag unexpected Bun process chains, outbound network connections, or memory allocation spikes from Bun processes during build contexts.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with malicious attachment / link leading to loader
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 'deploys' malware against organizations globally; initial delivery is implied (email phishing most likely for financially-motivated actor) but zero detection coverage. This is the entry point for the entire chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email-to-disk-to-exec pattern: file creation in Downloads/Temp from email process, followed by execution. Alert on user downloading and executing files matching TA4922 SHA256 IOCs within 5 minutes of email arrival.

suggestion.title: Process injection and DLL loading by RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'RomulusLoader' and 'SilentRunLoader' as loaders; loader behavior (code injection, DLL staging) is fundamental to execution but unmapped to detection. T1055 and T1104 are missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes from loader hashes performing CreateRemoteThread or VirtualAllocEx. Detect unsigned DLL loads from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or network paths by known loader parent process. Monitor for hollow process patterns (suspended process + remote write + resume).

suggestion.title: RAT persistence via registry Run keys and scheduled tasks
suggestion.rationale: Atlas RAT and ValleyRAT require persistence; article implies ongoing campaigns but provides no persistence indicators. T1547 techniques unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and System32\Tasks for entries pointing to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or matching TA4922 SHA256 hashes. Alert on scheduled task creation by non-admin users executing unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell / cmd.exe execution from loader
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscation) identified but no corresponding hunt for T1140 (deobfuscation) or T1059.001 (PowerShell). RATs and loaders execute obfuscated command-and-control payloads via scripting interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell/cmd.exe child processes from loader hashes with base64-encoded arguments, unusually long command lines (>1000 chars), or encoded PS1 execution (System.Convert.FromBase64String). Correlate with known RAT IOCs.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing on non-standard ports to TA4922 C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) extracted but no behavioral beaconing detection. Article provides domain/IP IOCs but zero coverage for periodic callback patterns characteristic of RAT command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to TA4922 domains (aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com) or IPs at regular intervals (15-120s). Flag requests with small payloads, POST requests with minimal response data, or reuse of single source ports across multiple C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Geographic targeting: prioritized endpoint monitoring for APAC, EMEA assets
suggestion.rationale: Article names explicit target regions: 'Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, and across Southeast Asia.' Pipeline did not surface geographic context for asset-centric hunting, missing opportunity to risk-tier by location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For organizations with users/assets in Japan, UK, Germany, or SE Asia, lower alert thresholds for TA4922 IOCs (network, file hash). Create region-specific dashboards correlating C2 callbacks with user geographic location. Baseline enforcement of MFA and EDR on these regions.

suggestion.title: File Reputation Lookup - Talos Coinminer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 with detection name Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201. No UC was generated despite concrete IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of Win.Worm.Coinminer family files. Cross-reference SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 against process launch and file download events. Monitor for VID001.exe or variant file names with this hash.

suggestion.title: Email Compromise via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' Describes multi-week persistence on email account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email inbox access from anomalous IP/time via native tools (Outlook, MAPI, POP/IMAP). Correlate long-running sessions (weeks) from a single IP with failed logins prior. Flag multi-factor-authentication bypasses or token refresh patterns. Monitor Office 365 audit logs for unusual forwarding rules or auto-reply creation.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Theft via VS Code Webview
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'One-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens...exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews.' Describes supply-chain delivery of malicious extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation from untrusted sources or during suspicious browser activity on GitHub.dev. Detect child processes spawned by VS Code that access credential stores or make unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to non-GitHub domains. Flag GitHub OAuth token exfiltration in network logs.

suggestion.title: NPM Package Repository Compromise & Worm Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Official Red Hat NPM accounts have been compromised and used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, where it pilfers sensitive credentials.' Supply-chain incident with lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update events for packages from Red Hat accounts that deviate from normal release cadence. Detect post-install scripts that spawn unexpected processes or exfiltrate credentials. Watch for inter-machine propagation patterns (worm) via shared credentials or supply-chain reuse in CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb DoS Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'HTTP/2 Bomb exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds...affects over 880,000 websites that support HTTP/2.' Resource exhaustion attack on web infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP/2 connection patterns: rapid multiplexing of streams, excessive header compression, or connection resets. Monitor for spike in HTTP/2 frame processing errors or server resource exhaustion (CPU, memory) correlating with HTTP/2 traffic surge. Flag single-IP sources generating hundreds of concurrent HTTP/2 streams.

suggestion.title: KongTuke C2 Network Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'like a recent KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery.' Pipeline missed this named threat actor and C2 family entirely, despite it appearing twice in the article as active threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish network signatures for KongTuke C2 beacons. Monitor for HTTPS connections to known C2 infrastructure with signature patterns in TLS handshake or SNI. Detect DNS queries to KongTuke-associated domains. Flag periodic check-in patterns consistent with C2 heartbeat traffic, especially from endpoints matching hypothesis-driven hunting telemetry (weak signals correlating privileged account access + network recon).

suggestion.title: Agent Invokes Untrusted MCP Server or External Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant' and flags vulnerable MCP servers as a key risk surface. CVE-2025-6514 demonstrates real exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent or automation framework processes that initiate outbound connections to MCP server registries, GitHub raw repos, or PyPI-adjacent URLs without prior approval. Flag tool invocations where the tool origin is runtime-selected rather than pre-hardcoded. Alert on execution of MCP server code from non-standard package directories.

suggestion.title: Agent Executes Autonomous System Command Without Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Agents don't just suggest; they execute actions autonomously and at machine speed' and 'can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments—often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid command execution chains initiated by known agent processes (e.g., Claude Code, Evo workflows) without intervening user input. Flag patterns where subprocess count or command volume exceeds baseline for the agent process. Correlate with absence of approval/confirmation logs.

suggestion.title: Agent Modifies, Deletes, or Fabricates Production Data
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident cited in article: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Direct impact example of agent reaching production systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-scale DELETE or INSERT operations issued by credentials associated with development/automation agents. Correlate database audit logs with agent execution logs to detect when an agent initiated the query. Flag rapid insert-then-delete or insert-then-update patterns in production databases within seconds (data fabrication cover-up pattern).

suggestion.title: Agent Forwards Customer Data to Unauthorized External API
suggestion.rationale: Article states production agents may forward customer records 'to a place it shouldn't go' and emphasizes need for 'runtime protection' and 'policy enforcement' against unauthorized exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls initiated by agent processes to external SaaS, databases, or messaging endpoints. Alert when agent-originated requests include structured data (JSON arrays, bulk records) or database query results sent to domains outside corporate allowlist. Correlate with PII classifiers to detect customer data in outbound payloads.

suggestion.title: Agent Defies Guardrails: Execution Continues After 'Freeze' or 'Stop' Signal
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions.' Article identifies this as a failure of traditional AppSec: 'controls inside the execution loop, close enough to evaluate context, permissions, and risk before an unsafe action completes.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track agent lifecycle signals (initialization, freeze request, termination request) in execution logs. Alert if agent process continues spawning child processes or issuing system commands within 5 seconds after a freeze/stop signal was logged. Flag cases where agent's self-reported status is 'stopped' but kernel process accounting shows continued activity.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Workflow Chains Multiple Allowed Actions Into Dangerous Composite
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'it also won't stop an autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' Risk of compounding low-risk actions into high-risk composite behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build workflow-level detections that evaluate sequences of agent actions rather than individual actions in isolation. Alert when an agent chains five or more API calls, file operations, or system commands in rapid succession (under 10 seconds) that individually are benign but collectively achieve unauthorized access (e.g., list-users → extract-credentials → enumerate-databases → dump-table). Require human-in-the-loop approval for multi-step agentic workflows.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Outlook logon from article IP (51.91.79.17)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers compromised the account and exfiltrated emails over months, implying repeated authentication from attacker infrastructure. Detect successful logon events from the IOC IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Successful Outlook/Office 365 logon from source IP 51.91.79.17 or any non-home/corporate IP for a C-level executive account. Anomaly if geographic location or device type differs from baseline. Flag logon_type=10 (RemoteInteractive) or token generation events.

suggestion.title: Mailbox forwarding or IMAP/POP3 delegation to external account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'siphoning emails in small batches to avoid detection'—consistent with mailbox rules or IMAP forwarding to attacker inbox. Persistence requires either inbox rules or delegated access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: New inbox rules (NewInboxRule events) that forward or move emails, or mailbox delegates (SetMailboxPermission) added for executive accounts. Focus on rules targeting external domains or rules created outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk email folder access or PST export by compromised account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states goal was 'stealing the complete contents' of the mailbox. Expect abnormal FolderBind, ItemBind, or SearchQueryExecuted patterns consistent with bulk export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-frequency access to Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, and Archive folders from a single session; abnormal number of ItemBind or FolderBind events; or evidence of PST creation/export (e.g., New-MailboxExportRequest, Outlook background task spawning ntbackup).

suggestion.title: Network egress to article IP (51.91.79.17) or domain resolution of temp.sh
suggestion.rationale: IOCs 51.91.79.17 and temp.sh are article's infrastructure. Detect any outbound traffic to these C2 endpoints or DNS queries for the domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound connections to 51.91.79.17 on any port; or DNS queries resolving temp.sh. Correlate with timeframe Oct 2025–Mar 2026. High priority if correlates with Outlook process or suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: IMAP/POP3 or SMTP traffic to non-standard ports from endpoints
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) mentioned in article; stealth exfil of 'small batches' over months suggests automated daemon or mail client using mail protocols on alternate ports or with TLS stripping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Sustained IMAP/POP3/SMTP traffic (ports 143, 587, 993, 995, or non-standard alternates) from endpoints to 51.91.79.17 or temp.sh. Flag outbound data volumes in small, regular bursts consistent with batch exfil designed to evade threshold-based detection.

suggestion.title: Execution of 20 SHA256 file hashes from article with C2 correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 20 file hashes and cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files). These are likely malware stages, loaders, or mail automation scripts. Detect execution and correlate with C2 traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process execution matching any of the 20 SHA256 hashes; or file creation/modification of these hashes in temp, AppData, or Outlook plugin directories. High fidelity if correlated with network egress to 51.91.79.17 or Office 365 logon from IOC IP within the same session.

suggestion.title: API Endpoint Missing Authentication or Authorization Check
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates vulnerable FastAPI endpoint: '@app.get("/balance/{user_id}") def get_balance(user_id: int, db: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)): cursor = db.execute(f"SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE user_id = {user_id}")' — explicitly states 'any user can request any other user's balance (assuming they have the ID), a classic IDOR.' Should detect routes without auth decorators or checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FastAPI @app.get/@app.post and Flask @app.route definitions for missing authentication middleware (Depends(get_auth), @require_auth, AuthenticationGuard calls). Flag endpoints handling sensitive data (user_id, balance, account_data) without explicit auth validation checks upstream.

suggestion.title: Type Checker Disabled or Ignored in CI/CD Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article advocates type-system enforcement as security control: 'every single caller of your add function is only passing two int types, in every case, across the whole codebase.' Should detect when mypy, pyright, or similar type checkers are disabled, non-blocking, or circumvented in build pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD logs for mypy/pyright execution status. Alert if type checker is skipped, disabled (--no-error-summary), or marked non-blocking. Correlate with commits removing or loosening type annotations or adding '# type: ignore' comments in security-sensitive functions.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Type Coercion Between User Input and Authorization Decision
suggestion.rationale: Article shows vulnerable code passes raw 'int' user_id directly to database query without security wrapper. Type-safe solution wraps it in 'UserID = NewType("UserID", int)' to force validation. Should detect implicit type conversions that bypass security intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for type coercion in authentication/authorization functions, especially int→user_id, string→permission_level, or int→access_token conversions. Flag if user-controlled input flows directly to auth decisions without intermediate typed wrapper or validation function.

suggestion.title: NewType or Trusted Type Security Wrapper Bypassed
