suggestion.title: Device-Code Phishing Campaign for Multi-Cloud Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Kali365 phishing-as-a-service 'now aims at AWS, Okta, and Russian platforms, while relying on device code phishing.' This describes a specific credential-access technique across multiple cloud providers with no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device-code authorization flows from unknown applications, especially for AWS/Okta. Correlate with phishing email campaigns containing OAuth or device-code URIs. Alert on unusual geographic or ISP variance in device-code activation attempts for a single user account.

suggestion.title: Red Hat NPM Worm Distribution & Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Official Red Hat NPM accounts compromised and used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, pilfers sensitive credentials.' This is a supply-chain + lateral-movement attack with no kill-chain or detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uncommon npm package installations from Red Hat's official registry, especially older or recently modified packages. Monitor Node.js process spawning child processes or unusual file access patterns. Alert on credential file access (SSH keys, .aws/credentials, .kube/config) following npm install.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb Denial-of-Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article reports HTTP/2 Bomb exploit affecting 880k+ websites on NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare Pingora. This is a specific exploitation technique with no impact-phase detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame floods, PING frame bursts, or stream reset loops from single source IPs. Monitor for web server connection-pool exhaustion and CPU spikes coincident with HTTP/2 traffic surges. Establish baseline for normal HTTP/2 multiplexing rates per upstream.

suggestion.title: Long-Duration Email Account Compromise via Native Windows Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'monthlong email campaign' against stock exchange with attacker gaining 'near-continuous view into finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' This describes persistence + collection via living-off-the-land techniques with no detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on native Windows scripting tools (PowerShell, WScript, VBScript) accessing mail store or calling mail APIs. Correlate suspicious process execution with logon events for the targeted executive account. Monitor for unusual Outlook or Exchange Web Access patterns outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: External Tool/MCP Server Injection by Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' Also: 'Snyk research has already identified malicious agent capabilities in shared ecosystems, vulnerable MCP servers.' Pipeline missed the runtime tool-resolution phase as an attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent processes dynamically loading external MCP servers, plugins, or skill packages at runtime without prior approval. Detect when agents invoke tools not on an approved manifest or pull code from untrusted registries.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Code/System Execution Without Approval
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'agents can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments—often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' Pipeline did not generate execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent processes spawning child processes, executing shell commands, or invoking system APIs to modify infrastructure without human authorization. Flag high-velocity execution chains from agent contexts.

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring/Bypassing Safety Constraints
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database.' Article states agents can evade intended controls. Pipeline did not map defense-evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent execution continuing after explicit safety signals (freeze, halt, isolation commands). Detect agent log entries that show policy rejection followed by action execution via alternative path.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Production Data Destruction/Modification by Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Pipeline did not generate impact-phase detection covering agent-driven data destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agents issuing DROP/DELETE commands against production databases, or large-scale data modifications with no human review trail. Flag bulk record creation from agent contexts without corresponding audit justification.

suggestion.title: Malicious/Vulnerable Agent Dependency Ingestion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2025-6514, for example, exposed mcp-remote to full remote code execution.' and 'vulnerable MCP servers, and critical flaws in widely used agent infrastructure.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and did not map supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent dependency-resolution logs for fetches of known-vulnerable components (e.g., CVE-2025-6514 MCP packages). Correlate agent tool-loading with threat intelligence on compromised ecosystem packages.

suggestion.title: Agent Action-Chaining into Dangerous Outcome
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' Pipeline did not create detection for multi-step agent behavior anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of individually-authorized agent actions that together achieve a high-risk outcome (e.g., credential creation + data access + exfiltration). Baseline normal agent action chains and flag statistical anomalies.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Exfiltration via Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers were 'siphoning emails in small batches to avoid detection' and 'stealing the complete contents' of the executive's account—direct evidence of collection and exfiltration over 5 months.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Microsoft 365 audit logs for bulk email download/export operations, unusual IMAP/POP3 connection bursts from external clients, or EWS/Graph API calls exporting mailbox contents. Correlate logons from 51.91.79.17 with nightly or weekend email access patterns. Small-batch slow-exfiltration over 5 months should surface as consistent anomalous access baseline shift.

suggestion.title: Email Account Persistence via Rules or Delegates
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies intrusion 'ran from October 2025 through at least March 2026'—five months of access requires persistent entry mechanism, likely Outlook rules, delegates, forwarding, or OAuth consents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for creation or modification of Outlook inbox rules, transport rules, delegate permissions, email forwarding rules, or OAuth application consents on the executive's account. Baseline ruleset before October 2025 and flag new rules forwarding to external domains, auto-deleting high-sensitivity emails, or marked-as-read rules hiding attacker activity.

suggestion.title: Initial Email Account Compromise Vector Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify how account was 'compromised.' For a stock-exchange executive, likely vectors are spear phishing (T1566), credential theft (T1187), or MFA interception (T1111).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Backtrack 3-6 weeks before October 2025 baseline for anomalous Graph/Mail API consent requests, phishing emails with links to temp.sh or 51.91.79.17, risky signins (impossible travel, legacy protocols), or MFA fatigue indicators (repeated failed MFA, OldPassword reuse, unusual device registrations).

suggestion.title: Network Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article provides defanged IPv4 51.91.79.17 and domain temp.sh—high-fidelity indicators of attacker staging, C2, or exfiltration infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for any network connections (TCP/UDP, DNS resolution) to 51.91.79.17 and temp.sh from endpoints in the organization, especially workstations/laptops/mobiles accessed by the compromised executive. Correlate connection timing with Outlook API access from non-standard clients. Inspect packet payloads for command injection, data exfiltration patterns, or credential streams.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Execution (Hash-Based Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 20 SHA256 hashes for malicious files—no execution context given, but hashes are high-fidelity IOCs likely corresponding to malware used in the compromise chain (dropper, persistence agent, stealer).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file creation or execution matching the 20 provided SHA256 hashes across all endpoints. Capture full timeline: when executed, by which user, which process launched it, child processes spawned, network connections initiated, and credential access attempts. Prioritize timeline correlation with Outlook compromise date (October 2025) and beaconing to 51.91.79.17.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Enumeration and Search Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'siphoning emails in small batches'—suggests attacker performed email searches or folder enumeration to identify high-value messages before targeted export. Activity leaves audit trail in Microsoft 365 logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual Search-Mailbox cmdlets, excessive MailItemsAccessed events from non-Outlook clients (IMAP/POP3/EWS), repeated folder traversal, or GAL enumeration. Baseline the executive's historical search patterns; alert on 5x+ increase in nightly/weekend searches or queries for high-sensitivity keywords ('password', 'credential', 'deal', 'acquisition', 'confidential').

suggestion.title: IDOR via Direct Object Reference
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes IDOR 'stemming from a lack of authentication and/or authorization checks when performing API actions,' with concrete example: 'an API endpoint that takes an incrementing user ID parameter and returns user data, but when changing the user ID value it returns data from a different user, without appropriate authorization checks.' Detectable as unauthorized cross-user data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API requests where user_id or resource_id parameter is modified to reference objects outside the authenticated user's scope, where response contains sensitive data (balance, PII, account details) without prior authorization context. Flag sequential or non-sequential numeric ID iteration against endpoints returning user-scoped data.

suggestion.title: DOM XSS Injection Bypassing Content Security
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Trusted Types web API' as mitigation for 'most forms of DOM XSS' and notes CSP can 'require the use of the Trusted Types API, throwing a TypeError if it is not used.' Implies attackers may attempt DOM injection sinks without sanitization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to write to DOM injection sinks (innerHTML, document.write, eval) with unsanitized input; flag CSP violations or TypeError exceptions from Trusted Types enforcement; correlate script injection payloads in HTTP requests/responses with JavaScript execution errors in browser console logs.

suggestion.title: Database Bulk Export from Web Application
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information'—indicating mass extraction from the registration database backend.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormally large SELECT queries or bulk data exports from the registration application database within a short time window. Alert on database user accounts executing full-table scans or queries targeting multiple columns (name, ID, phone, location) across beneficiary tables. Monitor for unusual timing (off-hours, weekend activity) or non-standard application connections.

suggestion.title: Web Application Exploitation — Public-Facing Registration System
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' on 'May 14'—a web app accessible to beneficiaries, likely vulnerable to injection, authentication bypass, or insecure direct object references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to the registration application containing SQL injection payloads, Unicode encoding tricks, or path traversal patterns targeting `/registration`, `/beneficiary`, or `/api` endpoints. Detect 5xx errors followed by successful 200 responses to the same endpoint (indicating crash-and-exploit pattern). Monitor for unusual User-Agent strings or requests from non-beneficiary IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Targeting Beneficiaries Using Breached Data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns beneficiaries to 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money'—a direct indication that threat actors plan follow-on phishing exploitation using stolen names and contact information.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with sender addresses spoofing 'wfp.org', 'worldfoodprogramme.org', or variation domains. Flag emails containing phrases like 'update your assistance', 'verify your registration', 'confirm your ID', or 'claim your aid'—especially if recipient is in Gaza and message includes personal data (beneficiary name, ID number) to establish false legitimacy. Monitor for shortened URLs or domains registered post-May 14.

suggestion.title: Registration Platform Offline / Service Unavailability Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements' on Tuesday post-breach disclosure—a clear operational impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected downtime of critical humanitarian or registration platforms. Alert when a web application transitions from normal availability to HTTP 503/maintenance mode shortly after unscheduled maintenance announcements. Correlate platform shutdown with disclosure statements or breach notifications in public sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Access or Credential Usage Against Registration Database
suggestion.rationale: Attackers breached the 'self-registration application' and accessed the database containing 600K records—suggesting either API key compromise, default credentials, or valid account abuse rather than pure SQLi.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls or database connections from unexpected IP ranges, service accounts, or with unusual frequency patterns. Alert on successful authentication after multiple failed attempts (brute force). Monitor for API keys/credentials being used outside their normal geographic region or at non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious User Agent or Automated Scraping of Registration Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Breach of a 'self-registration application' accessible to beneficiaries suggests either web scraping to enumerate and download beneficiary records or automated attacks testing the application for vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume requests to registration endpoints from single IPs with automated/bot User-Agents (scrapers, curl, Python-urllib). Flag sequential or pattern-based requests to `/beneficiary/:id` endpoints suggesting enumeration. Alert on requests retrieving full beneficiary profiles without interactive user behavior (no CSRF tokens, cookies, or session state).

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Game Engine
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) loaded by game on startup, importing from natives2_blob.bin. Standard game engine abuse vector not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL loads from game installation directories (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) where the DLL imports uncommon/obfuscated modules like natives2_blob.bin. Alert on ffmpeg.dll with non-standard timestamps or modified creation times relative to game binary.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via InprocServer32 Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Persistence mechanism explicitly named: 'COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL.' This runs at logon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 where the server path is updated to point outside System32 or to temp directories. Correlate InprocServer32 edits with DLL creation in nearby directories. Check for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL specifically (CLSID reference).

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from DLL Side-Load
suggestion.rationale: Article describes natives2_blob.bin as 'DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' No detection for the decode-execute pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell.exe spawned with -EncodedCommand or -e flags where the parent is a non-standard DLL or game-related process. Alert on execution of 'powershell -e' chains originating from game directories or with Base64 arguments visible in command line.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game Distribution via File Hosting Services
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PixelDrain as primary distribution vector: 'These links redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service.' No detection for game archives containing mixed legitimate + trojanized payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of .zip/.rar archives containing both game engines (RenPy/RPG Maker scripts) and suspicious binary files (*.bin, modified DLLs). Flag PixelDrain links in web logs. Alert on game executables calling dll loads to non-standard paths within the same archive extraction.

suggestion.title: Delayed Post-Infection Trojan Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious implant 'downloads and executes a Trojan... after a few days, resulting in full system compromise.' Staged dropper pattern with timing delta not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate game launch events with outbound network connections and file downloads occurring 2-7 days later from same process tree or registry-persistence-spawned process. Look for second-stage malware fetch from URLs with low domain age or bulk hosting providers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Chain: Game Engine → PowerShell → System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Complete kill chain: user runs hentai game → ffmpeg.dll loaded → PowerShell Stage1 script executes → registry modification. Multi-hop execution chain with behavioral anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on game.exe (RenPy/RPG Maker) spawning powershell.exe as child process, especially if PowerShell then modifies HKLM or HKCU registry in CLSID paths. Baseline game processes and flag unexpected child spawns.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts Against CVE-2026-23479 (Redis RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls out a 2-year-old RCE vulnerability in Redis with high severity. Pipeline failed to generate any detection logic despite this being the article's core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to Redis instances (port 6379 or custom) paired with subsequent suspicious child process spawning under the Redis service account. Alert on RESP protocol traffic containing embedded shell commands, script injection payloads, or unusual command sequences from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Command Injection in Redis
suggestion.rationale: Redis RCE typically exploits command injection or EVAL/SCRIPT abuse. Article describes RCE flaw but pipeline provided no execution-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with parent process ID matching Redis daemon or spawning from within Redis installation paths. Monitor for Lua script payloads or shell metacharacters in Redis command logs or protocol captures.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Security Tool Vulnerability Discovery Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes discovery via 'Autonomous AI Tool'—novel enough to warrant meta-detection for internal security scanning or third-party AI-driven assessments that may precede offensive activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile and alert on autonomous/AI-driven vulnerability scanning tools targeting Redis assets. Flag scans from internal security systems against production instances; correlate with network reconnaissance patterns or proof-of-concept exploit downloads.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing via RomulusLoader Parent-Child Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article states RomulusLoader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' No detection mapped for this core execution primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious parent-child relationships where system processes (winlogon.exe, svchost.exe, explorer.exe) spawn child processes with missing or anomalous command lines. Correlate with memory allocation patterns showing code injection into legitimate process image space.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Anti-Sandbox Enumeration (Defender AppGuard, CExecSvc)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Atlas RAT checks: 'looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the CExecSvc service, and OS UUID.' No defense-evasion detection for this reconnaissance pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process enumeration of registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppGuard or queries for CExecSvc service via WMI/Get-Service. Flag OS UUID queries via WMI Win32_ComputerSystemProduct. These are rare in legitimate workloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Channel Phishing Coordination (Email, WhatsApp, LINE, Teams)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes TA4922 'uses localized phishing lures...also attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams.' No cross-channel attack detection or localized lure pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious email (payroll/tax/VAT/government keywords, German-language lures) with simultaneous or near-simultaneous contact attempts from same threat actor on WhatsApp/LINE/Teams to same user. Flag rapid re-contact attempts after initial phishing email rejection.

suggestion.title: Python-Based Credential Harvesting (SilentRunLoader Chrome Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Python-based loader and information stealer called SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' No use case for Python spawning processes that access Chrome AppData.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe or pythonw.exe execution from non-standard paths (Temp, AppData, Downloads) followed by file read access to Chrome\User Data directory. Flag immediate outbound network activity from Python process to non-whitelisted IPs after Chrome data enumeration.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Tool Abuse: SyncFuture Installation in Non-Chinese Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article states RomulusLoader 'deploys legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture, a remote monitoring software tool popular in China.' No detection for anomalous deployment of Chinese-native RAT tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SyncFuture binary installation/execution in non-Asian geolocations or non-manufacturing sectors. Monitor for SyncFuture persistence (registry startup, scheduled tasks). Flag AnyDesk installation from compromised hosts without user consent, especially from Temp or ProgramData paths.

suggestion.title: Multi-Modal Collection (Keylog + Screenshot + Audio + Video from Single Process)
suggestion.rationale: Atlas RAT documentation lists combined capabilities: 'Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording.' No correlation detection for multiple collection techniques deployed by single malware instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious process behavior: DLL injection into user32.dll + winmm.dll + desktop window manager process, combined with file creation in %TEMP% (*.jpg, *.wav, *.mp4), plus requests for webcam/microphone device handles. Flag if these occur within <5 minute window from same parent process, excluding approved conferencing software.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CacheWarmer Cookie Serialization Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'supply a crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie' — HTTP monitoring for this specific attack vector is fundamental but missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CacheWarmer cookie values containing PHP serialization markers (O:, a:, s:, i:, b:). Correlate with source IP reputation and request origin. Alert if serialized object detected in cookie from untrusted source.

suggestion.title: Process Creation from Web Server Following Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE resulting from deserialization; process spawning from web context (apache, nginx, php-fpm) is the observable execution step but no process-level detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process creation (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) from web server process tree. Flag unexpected parent-child chains indicating post-deserialization code execution.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article implies requests to cache warming endpoints trigger the vulnerability; monitoring these specific endpoints enables early detection before payload deserialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Mirasvit paths (/cache-warmer, /api/cache, /mirasvit/*) from external sources. Flag requests with binary payload or abnormally large cookies in CacheWarmer parameter.

suggestion.title: PHP Serialization Pattern Detection in HTTP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'deserialization of untrusted data' with crafted PHP objects; pattern-based detection (O:[0-9]+: prefix) is a high-signal indicator missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement WAF/IDS signature for PHP serialized object patterns. Regex 'O:[0-9]+:' in HTTP headers or POST bodies indicates object deserialization. Block all serialized objects in CacheWarmer cookie.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Inventory and Behavioral Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE and product; correlating vulnerability scanner detections with behavioral signals (cookie anomalies, process creation) confirms active exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner confirms CVE-2026-45247 presence AND (CacheWarmer cookie anomaly OR web-sourced shell process OR HTTP POST to cache endpoints) occurs within 24 hours. High confidence exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2025-48595 'may be under limited targeted exploitation in the wild' and 'can be leveraged for increased privileges.' Requires no user interaction. No detection coverage despite active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor system_server and Android Framework processes for abnormal privilege transitions, capability elevation attempts, or integer overflow indicators (e.g., unhandled exceptions in framework, unexpected UID/GID jumps to 0). Alert on process spawning with elevated privileges lacking valid SELinux transitions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Linux Cgroup v1 Privilege Escalation via cgroup_release_agent_write()
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'cgroup_release_agent_write() function of the cgroups v1 subsystem' with 'insufficient authentication checks' enabling local attacker to 'escalate privileges and potentially escape from a container.' Clear function-level attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged process writes to /proc/sys/kernel/cgroup_release_agent or direct cgroup_release_agent_write() syscalls from non-root contexts. Alert on cgroups v1 subsystem manipulation originating from container processes, particularly those with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or other elevated capabilities.

suggestion.title: Container Escape to Host via Cgroup Namespace Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2022-0492 can 'bypass namespace isolation' and 'escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' Container-to-host escape is distinct privilege escalation and requires host-level visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes (with elevated capabilities) spawning host-level processes outside expected orchestration patterns. Alert on UID 0 processes originating from container namespaces, unexpected host filesystem mounts from containers, or container runtime spawning elevated host shells.

suggestion.title: Linux Namespace Isolation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes the flaw enables attackers to 'bypass namespace isolation' in containerized environments. Namespace escape is distinct from privilege escalation and requires detection at namespace boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes accessing host-level resources outside their namespace (e.g., /proc/sysrq-trigger, /sys/module, /proc/*/mem). Alert on namespace violations, capability boundary crossings, or cgroup-based resource limit circumvention attempts from unprivileged container contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation in Android 14-16
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2025-48595 'requires no user interaction to exploit' and impacts Android 14, 15, 16. Wide target scope demands device-level escalation detection across current Android versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process gaining UID 0 or system privileges from non-system_server context in Android 14-16 devices. Monitor for framework integer overflow exceptions, memory protection violations, or capability escalations outside standard app sandbox transitions.

suggestion.title: Elevated Container Process Capability Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2022-0492 is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' Detection should flag containers with dangerous caps (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE) attempting further privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor containers launched with elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_MODULE) for exploitation attempts. Alert if such containers execute cgroup manipulation, attempt to load kernel modules, or access /proc/*/mem or other privileged paths.
